subject: [Core] Install completion using whichever bash in PATH (#3893)
message:
[Core] Install completion using whichever bash in PATH (#3893)

* Install completion using whichever bash in PATH

With this pull request, `sky --install-shell-completion` searches the
PATH for `bash` and rruns that version when it comes to installing shell
completion, rather than systematically using `/bin/bash`.

Indeed we cannot assume that `/bin/bash` is the active bash.
For example the system bash on macOS in `/bin/bash` is quite old (v3),
so some users install bash v5 with homebrew, which installs in
`/opt`, leaving `/bin` untouched.`

This matters because bash completion for skypilot requires bash >= v4.

Fixes https://github.com/skypilot-org/skypilot/issues/3885

subject: [ux] add sky jobs launch --fast (#4231)
message:
[ux] add sky jobs launch --fast (#4231)

* [ux] add sky jobs launch --fast

This flag will make the jobs controller launch use `sky launch --fast`. There
are a few known situations where this can cause misbehavior in the jobs
controller:
- The SkyPilot wheel is outdated (due to changes in the SkyPilot code or a
  version upgrade).
- The user's cloud credentials have changed. In this case the new credentials
  will not be synced, and if there are new clouds available in `sky check`, the
  cloud depedencies may not be correctly installed.

However, this does speed up `jobs launch` _significantly_, so provide it as a
dangerous option. Soon we will add robustness checks to `sky launch --fast` that
will fix the above caveats, and we can remove this flag and just enable the
behavior by default.

* [ux] add sky jobs launch --fast (#4231)

* [ux] add sky jobs launch --fast

This flag will make the jobs controller launch use `sky launch --fast`. There
are a few known situations where this can cause misbehavior in the jobs
controller:
- The SkyPilot wheel is outdated (due to changes in the SkyPilot code or a
  version upgrade).
- The user's cloud credentials have changed. In this case the new credentials
  will not be synced, and if there are new clouds available in `sky check`, the
  cloud depedencies may not be correctly installed.

However, this does speed up `jobs launch` _significantly_, so provide it as a
dangerous option. Soon we will add robustness checks to `sky launch --fast` that
will fix the above caveats, and we can remove this flag and just enable the
behavior by default.

* [jobs] autodown managed job clusters

If all goes correctly, the managed job controller should tear down a managed job
cluster once the managed job completes. However, if the controller fails somehow
(e.g. crashes, is terminated, etc), we don't want to leak resources.

As a failsafe, set autodown on the job cluster. This is not foolproof, since the
skylet on the cluster can also crash, but it's likely to catch many cases.

subject: [fast] if cluster is INIT, force refresh before deciding to provision (#4328)
message:
[fast] if cluster is INIT, force refresh before deciding to provision (#4328)

* [fast] if cluster is INIT, force refresh before deciding to provision

If a cluster is mid-initialization, its status will be INIT and autostop/down
will not be set yet. In this case, the cluster refresh won't actually grab the
cluster status lock and hard refresh the status. So, check_cluster_available
will immeidately decide that the cluster is INIT and throw.

This could cause a bug where many parallel launches of `sky launch --fast` that
are staggered can all decide that the cluster is INIT, and all decide that they
need to launch the cluster. Since cluster initialization is locked with the
cluster status lock, each invocation will sychronously re-launch the cluster.

Now, if we see that the cluster is INIT, we force a refresh. This will acquire
the cluster status lock, which will block until any ongoing provisioning
completes and the cluster is UP. If the cluster is otherwise INIT (e.g. ray
cluster has been stopped abnormally) then provisioning should proceed as normal.

This does not fix the race where the cluster does not exist or is STOPPED, and
many simultaneously started `sky launch --fast` invocations try to create or
restart the cluster. However, once the first batch complete their launches, all
future invocations should correctly see the cluster as UP, not INIT - even if
they are started while the first batch is still provisioning the cluster. Fixing
the STOPPED or non-existent case is a bit more difficult and will probably
require moving this detection logic inside the provisioning code, so that it
holds the cluster status lock continuously from the status check until the
cluster is UP.

subject: [jobs] fix possible managed job status issues (#4637)
message:
[jobs] fix possible managed job status issues (#4637)

* [jobs] don't set end_at for CANCELLING

CANCELLING is no longer a terminal status - we shouldn't set end_at.

* [jobs] don't require job to be CANCELLING to become CANCELLED

It's possible that the job status erroneously gets set to some other
value (e.g. RUNNING) by another process after getting set to
CANCELLING - we should avoid this case, but if we end up here, we
should still transition to CANCELLED.

* [jobs] avoid status transitions that don't make sense

I saw a bug where a job that was CANCELLING got updated by RUNNING by
a different process. Avoid state transitions like this that obviously
violate the expected state machine.

* fix cancellation

* Revert "[jobs] don't require job to be CANCELLING to become CANCELLED"

This reverts commit 93966374a768c649f122dfc6c3dfbe1a38bb9aab.

* Add Nebius storage integration and associated utilities

This commit introduces support for Nebius object storage, enabling users to integrate Nebius storage with various functionalities such as file mounting, syncing, and cloud transfers. It includes necessary adaptors, utility methods, and updates to the storage framework to handle Nebius-specific configurations and endpoints.

* Add support for Nebius storage mounting and testing

Implemented new Nebius storage mounting functionality, including COPY and MOUNT modes, with tests. Updated cloud_stores.py for AWS CLI compatibility and added a YAML template for Nebius storage configurations. Removed outdated Nebius test case in favor of the new approach.

* format

* Add Nebius object storage support across tests and utilities

This commit introduces comprehensive Nebius support, making it accessible for S3-compatible operations including bucket creation, deletion, and mounting. It removes reliance on the AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE environment variable, streamlines Nebius-specific configurations, and adds associated unit test parameters to validate functionality across storage operations.

Remove redundant code, streamline imports, and enhance error messaging. Adjust documentation for better accuracy and update function annotations. These changes improve maintainability and readability of the Nebius adaptor module.

* Refactor Nebius storage setup and clean up debug print.

Simplified Nebius AWS CLI installation by reusing the S3CloudStorage configuration for consistency. Removed unnecessary debug print in `run_upload_cli` to reduce console noise. Minor formatting adjustment in test YAML file.

* Refactor Nebius storage handling and add timeout for deletions

Clean up and improve code readability, including string formatting and conditionals. Introduce `_TIMEOUT_TO_PROPAGATES` to handle timeout while verifying Nebius bucket deletions. Update comments to reflect the corrected usage on Nebius servers.

subject: [core] fix optimized file mounts without permission (#5210)
message:
[core] fix optimized file mounts without permission (#5210)

fix optimized file mounts without permission

Before this change, reprovisioning an existing jobs controller could
silently fail to update file mounts, because the `cp` invocation would
error out with
```
cp: cannot create regular file '/home/ubuntu/.ssh/sky-cluster-key': Permission denied
```
Likely this also affected non-controller clusters.

Add the `-f` flag to `cp` so that it will still replace this file even
if it is missing permissions. Use `;` instead of `&&` between multiple
file mounts to avoid one failure skipping all the rest.

Added `@annotations.lru_cache(scope='request')` to cache credential-related methods, reducing redundant file reads and improving performance. Simplified credential-handling logic by removing global variables and forced updates, streamlining access for Nebius SDK integration.

* Remove unused global variables in Nebius adaptor

Eliminated redundant _iam_token, _sdk, _tenant_id, and _project_id variables as they were no longer in use. This helps in reducing unnecessary clutter and improves code maintainability.

AssertionError with this change, before the fix in #5482. This should
make it more difficult for similar regressions to happen in the
future.

This does have the unfortunate side effect of causing an
AssertionError if you have a broken controller name and you want to
terminate it, because you will hit the AssertionError during sky down.
I think this is fine. If people hit that error, which should be very
rare, we can ask them to downgrade, down the cluster, and then upgrade
again.

subject: fix service account user_id length (#6425)
message:
fix service account user_id length (#6425)

This was intended to be 16 random chars, but due to how
secrets.token_hex works, it was actually 32, for a total user_id
length of 35 chars (too long!).

This was causing SSH to give the error `unix_listener: path
"/tmp/skypilot_ssh_blahblahblah" too long for Unix domain socket`.
Since we construct the ControlPath including the user_id, the length
was contributing to the problem.

Confirmed that we don't see the unix_listener error after shortening
the SA user_id.

the digits 1-9 as well as "10", which would cause the test to

2025-09-17 21:53:46,296\tINFO worker.py:1719 -- Connected to Ray cluster. View the dashboard at \u001b[1m\u001b[32m127.0.0.1:8266 \u001b[39m\u001b[22m

subject: [core] avoid exception in k8s adaptor __del__ (#7699)
message:
[core] avoid exception in k8s adaptor __del__ (#7699)

Before this change, you can see
```
Exception ignored in: <function ClientWrapper.__del__ at 0x7f5322771ea0>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/skypilot/sky/adaptors/kubernetes.py", line 201, in __del__
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'debug'
Exception ignored in: <function ClientWrapper.__del__ at 0x7f5322771ea0>
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/skypilot/sky/adaptors/kubernetes.py", line 201, in __del__
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'debug'
```

This is due to [how __del__
works](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/datamodel.html#object.__del__),
where other globals may already be unloaded.

> __del__() can be executed during interpreter shutdown. As a
> consequence, the global variables it needs to access (including
> other modules) may already have been deleted or set to None. Python
> guarantees that globals whose name begins with a single underscore
> are deleted from their module before other globals are deleted; if
> no other references to such globals exist, this may help in assuring
> that imported modules are still available at the time when the
> __del__() method is called.

In this case, we shouldn't worry too much about the exception and just
continue.

[examples] make ray example process check more robust (#7859)

The ray-project/ray docker image uses the username `ray`, which causes every single line of `ps aux` to match `ray`.
So the result of `ps aux | grep ray | grep 6379` is always
```
ray       192069  0.0  0.0   4060  2176 pts/0    S+   16:46   0:00 grep --color=auto 6379
```
or similar.
Then we will never call `ray start`.

Update the ps command so that it will only print the cmdline.

[GCP] Fix B200 spot instance support in catalog fetcher (#8125)

This fixes two issues preventing GCP B200 (a4-highgpu-8g) spot instances
from being recognized:

1. A4 VM pricing missing: GCP doesn't provide separate CPU/RAM pricing
   for A4 instances in their SKUs API. The B200 GPU pricing includes
   the full VM cost. Added special handling to set A4 VM price to 0 so
   entries aren't dropped.

2. B200 spot pricing bug: Some B200 spot SKUs in GCP's API have
   usageType='OnDemand' even though the description says "Spot
   Preemptible". Added logic to match on description when usageType
   doesn't match for B200 spot queries.

subject: Fix lstrip('ssh-') bug in SSH Node Pools (#8417)
message:
Fix lstrip('ssh-') bug in SSH Node Pools (#8417)

* Fix incorrect lstrip usage for ssh- prefix removal

Replace lstrip("ssh-") with common_utils.removeprefix("ssh-") to correctly
remove the "ssh-" prefix from context names. lstrip() incorrectly removes
any leading characters in the set {'s', 'h', '-'}, which could strip more
characters than intended (e.g., "ssh-hss-cluster" would incorrectly become
"-cluster" instead of "hss-cluster").

Fixes #7662

* [SSH] Fix lstrip('ssh-') bug - use removeprefix() instead

Python's lstrip() removes any leading characters from a set, not a
prefix as a whole. For example, 'hss-cluster'.lstrip('ssh-') would
incorrectly result in 'cluster' because it removes characters 's',
'h', and '-' individually.

Replace all instances of lstrip('ssh-') with common_utils.removeprefix()
which correctly removes only the exact prefix string.

subject: [Docs] Add CLAUDE.md for AI assistant development guidance (#8474)
message:
[Docs] Add CLAUDE.md for AI assistant development guidance (#8474)

* [Docs] Add CLAUDE.md for AI assistant development guidance

Add comprehensive documentation for AI assistants working with the
SkyPilot codebase. Includes repository structure, development setup,
code formatting/linting guidelines, testing instructions, architecture
patterns, and common pitfalls.

* [Docs] Update CLAUDE.md to use uv instead of conda

Replace conda with uv for virtual environment setup and package
installation. uv provides faster package resolution and installation.

* [Docs] Add PostgreSQL testing instructions to CLAUDE.md

Add documentation for testing with PostgreSQL backend including:
- Local PostgreSQL setup with Docker
- Running smoke tests with --postgres flag
- Production-scale testing with load test scripts
- References to detailed documentation in tests/load_tests/

* [Dependency] Support uvicorn>=0.38.0

Update the server code to be compatible with both old and new uvicorn
versions:

- uvicorn <0.36.0: Uses config.setup_event_loop() before asyncio.run()
- uvicorn >=0.36.0: Uses config.get_loop_factory() with uvicorn's
  asyncio_run compat function that handles loop_factory for all
  Python versions (3.8+)

The event loop lag monitoring configuration is now done inside an async
wrapper function using asyncio.get_running_loop() instead of
asyncio.get_event_loop() before the loop is created.

Fixes #8453

* [Docs] Add dependency management guidance to CLAUDE.md

Add a new section documenting how dependencies are managed in SkyPilot:
- Location of dependency definitions (sky/setup_files/dependencies.py)
- Types of dependencies (core, cloud-specific, development)
- Best practices for updating dependencies
- Example of well-documented version constraints

* [Docs] Fix CLAUDE.md formatting and commit message format

- Fix PostgreSQL config example to use proper yaml code block
- Update commit message format to match actual repo convention
  ([Area] Description instead of conventional commits)

* [Docs] Revert uvicorn code changes, keep only CLAUDE.md updates

The uvicorn>=0.38.0 fix was done to test the CLAUDE.md documentation
workflow. Reverting the actual code changes as they should be in a
separate PR.

* [Docs] Add PR description format with test plan requirement

Update Pull Request Guidelines to clarify that PRs should include
a summary and test plan in the description.

* [Docs] Simplify testing section and add CI test triggers

- Remove verbose local test commands, keep only unit tests
- Add CI Tests via PR Comments section with /quicktest-core and /smoke-test
- Add instruction to always generate manual test plan for PRs

* [Docs] Add guidance to include unit/smoke tests with changes

* [Docs] Add instruction to restart API server after code changes

Address PR feedback: AI agents often miss restarting the API server
after making code changes. Added prominent instruction in both
Common Pitfalls and Useful Commands sections.

message:
[runpod] Failing to launch on runpod with Unauthorized error (#8466)

* Fix RunPod unauthorized error and improve error handling (#8411)

This change addresses the RunPod unauthorized error issue by:

1. Adding actual API validation in sky check:
   - Previously, credential check only verified the config file existed
   - Now makes an actual API call (list_instances) to validate the key works
   - Catches 'Unauthorized' errors and provides helpful error messages

2. Improving error logging in provisioner:
   - Added full stack trace logging when launch fails
   - Helps debugging by showing the complete error context

3. Enhancing retry logic:
   - Don't retry on authorization errors (401/403/Unauthorized/Forbidden)
   - These errors are not recoverable and should fail immediately
   - Log authorization errors as errors instead of warnings

* Address code review feedback for RunPod error handling

- Use isinstance() check for QueryError before generic exception handling
- Use case-insensitive check with .lower() for unauthorized errors
- Use any() with auth_keywords list for cleaner conditional check
- Improve error message for unexpected exceptions

* Replace gcc with build-essential in Dockerfile

build-essential includes gcc plus additional build tools needed for

subject: [SSH Node Pool] Fix missing SSH tunnel file after API upgrade (#8508)
message:
[SSH Node Pool] Fix missing SSH tunnel file after API upgrade (#8508)

* [Core] Include ssh_node_pools tunnel scripts in package distribution

Add the missing `sky/ssh_node_pools/deploy/tunnel/*` include to
MANIFEST.in. The redirect stub at `sky/utils/kubernetes/ssh-tunnel.sh`
(for backward compatibility with older kubeconfigs) calls the actual
script at this path, but the script was not being included in the
package distribution. This caused SSH node pools to fail after API
server upgrades.

* [Test] Add unit test for MANIFEST.in completeness

Add tests to ensure that shell scripts referenced by other scripts are
included in MANIFEST.in. This prevents regressions where redirect stubs
exist but their target scripts are missing from the package distribution.

Includes a specific test for the ssh-tunnel.sh redirect stub that
ensures both the stub and its target are included.

subject: [Core] Add inline comments to version constants to prevent silent merge conflicts (#8552)
message:
[Core] Add inline comments to version constants to prevent silent merge conflicts (#8552)

When two PRs independently bump the same version constant (e.g., API_VERSION
from 25 to 26), git merges them without conflict since only the number changes.
This results in the second PR's version bump being silently lost, causing
incorrect behavior.

By adding a short comment describing the change on the same line as the version
number, concurrent PRs will now produce merge conflicts, forcing developers to
reconcile version bumps properly.

Affected variables:
- API_VERSION (sky/server/constants.py)
- SKYLET_VERSION, SKYLET_LIB_VERSION (sky/skylet/constants.py)
- MANAGED_JOBS_VERSION (sky/jobs/constants.py)
- GLOBAL_USER_STATE_VERSION, SPOT_JOBS_VERSION, SERVE_VERSION,
  SKYPILOT_CONFIG_VERSION, KV_CACHE_VERSION (sky/utils/db/migration_utils.py)

[Helm] Allow RWX persistent storage with RollingUpdate upgrade strategy (#8537)

* [Helm] Allow RWX persistent storage with RollingUpdate upgrade strategy

Previously, using RollingUpdate upgrade strategy with an external database
required storage.enabled=false, causing file mounts and logs to be lost
during rolling updates.

This change allows persistent storage with RollingUpdate when using a
ReadWriteMany (RWX) access mode storage class. RWX storage (like Google
Filestore, AWS EFS, or Azure Files) allows multiple pods to mount the
same PVC simultaneously during rolling updates.

Changes:
- Modified api-deployment.yaml to allow storage.enabled=true with
  RollingUpdate when storage.accessMode=ReadWriteMany
- Updated values.yaml with comprehensive documentation about storage
  options and cloud-specific guidance for RWX storage classes
- Updated unit tests to verify the new behavior

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Helm] Persist managed job logs across rolling updates

When using RWX storage with RollingUpdate strategy, persist only the
specific managed job log directories to minimize storage usage:
- /root/sky_logs/jobs_controller - Controller logs (sky jobs logs --controller)
- /root/sky_logs/managed_jobs - Task execution logs

Transient logs (api_server, sky-* cluster logs) are NOT persisted as
they can be regenerated and would consume unnecessary storage.

This ensures job logs remain accessible after rolling updates while
keeping PVC storage usage minimal.

* [Docs] Replace overly permissive s3:* with specific S3 permissions

Update the AWS minimal IAM policy documentation to use specific S3
permissions instead of the overly broad s3:* wildcard. The new policy
includes only the permissions actually needed by SkyPilot:

Further tighten S3 permissions by using properly scoped resource ARNs:
- Object-level actions (GetObject, PutObject, DeleteObject) use arn:aws:s3:::*/*
- Bucket-level actions (ListBucket, GetBucketLocation) use arn:aws:s3:::*
- ListAllMyBuckets requires Resource: * (AWS requirement)

This follows the principle of least privilege more closely.

subject: [auth] Add polling-based authentication for sky api login (#8590)
message:
[auth] Add polling-based authentication for sky api login (#8590)

* [API] Replace localhost callback with polling-based auth flow

This change fixes the `sky api login` authentication flow that was
broken by recent Chrome changes blocking HTTPS-to-HTTP localhost
requests.

New polling-based flow:
1. CLI creates auth session with PKCE code_challenge
2. CLI opens browser to /auth/authorize?session_id=xxx
3. User clicks "Authorize" button in browser
4. CLI polls server for token with code_verifier
5. Server validates PKCE and returns token

Security improvements:
- PKCE (code verifier/challenge) prevents token theft
- User must actively click Authorize (no automatic submission)
- Sessions expire after 5 minutes and are single-use

Fallback mechanisms:
- Falls back to old localhost callback if server doesn't support new flow
- Falls back to manual token copy-paste if all else fails

Changes:
- Add sky/server/auth/sessions.py for in-memory session storage
- Add /api/v1/auth/sessions endpoints for session management
- Add /auth/authorize page with Authorize button
- Update SDK api_login() to use polling flow with fallbacks
- Add base64_url_encode/decode helpers to common_utils
- Add unit tests for session storage module

* [API] Simplify polling-based auth implementation

- Consolidate session store methods: replace get_session_status +
  consume_session with single poll_session that returns (status, token)
- Simplify server endpoint to use single poll_session call
- Clean up SDK: use module-level lazy import for requests
- Reduce verbose messages and comments
- Simplify unit tests to match new API

* [API] Clean up polling-based auth code

- Remove unused base64_url_decode function
- Fix pylint warnings (variable shadowing, triple quote style)
- Apply yapf formatting fixes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Check API version before trying polling auth

- Bump API_VERSION to 27 for new auth endpoints
- Only attempt polling auth on servers >= API v27
- Remove code_challenge_method (only S256 is supported)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Simplify auth flow by using code_challenge as session key

Remove the separate session creation endpoint. Sessions are now keyed
by code_challenge and created automatically when the authorize page loads.

New flow:
1. CLI generates code_verifier, computes code_challenge
2. CLI opens browser to /auth/authorize?code_challenge=...
3. Server creates session when page loads
4. User clicks Authorize
5. CLI polls /api/v1/auth/token?code_verifier=...

This eliminates one round-trip and simplifies the API surface.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Use SQLite for auth sessions to support multiple workers

Replace in-memory session storage with SQLite-backed storage. This
ensures auth sessions work correctly when the API server runs with
multiple uvicorn workers (the default for remote deployments).

[Config] Add config flag for pod resource limits (#8644)

* [k8s] Add config flag to enforce pod CPU/memory limits matching requests

Add a new `set_pod_resource_limits` configuration option for Kubernetes
that sets pod CPU/memory limits relative to their resource requests.
This is useful for clusters that require limits to be set (e.g., for
LimitRange enforcement, resource quotas, or cluster policies).

The config accepts:
- false (default): no limits are set
- true: limits are set equal to requests (multiplier of 1)
- number: limits are set to requests * multiplier (e.g., 1.5 for 50% headroom)

Example usage in ~/.sky/config.yaml:
  kubernetes:
    set_pod_resource_limits: true  # or 1.5 for 50% headroom

Or per-context:
  kubernetes:
    context_configs:
      my-cluster:
        set_pod_resource_limits: 2.0

Or via task-level cluster_config_overrides.

subject: [k8s] Fix GPU labeller for L40S GPUs (#8593)
message:
[k8s] Fix GPU labeller for L40S GPUs (#8593)

* [Kubernetes] Fix L40S GPU detection in GFD label formatter and GPU labeler

Add L40S (and L40) to canonical_gpu_names lists in two places:

1. GFDLabelFormatter (sky/provision/kubernetes/utils.py)
   - NVIDIA GPU Feature Discovery labels like 'NVIDIA-L40S-48GB' were not
     matching any canonical name due to word boundary regex matching
   - Without this fix, L40S labels would fallback to 'L40S-48GB' instead
     of the expected canonical name 'L40S'

2. GPU Labeler script (sky/utils/kubernetes/k8s_gpu_labeler_setup.yaml)
   - The SkyPilot GPU labeler uses substring matching to identify GPUs
   - 'L4' was matching 'L40S' because 'l4' is a substring of 'l40s'
   - This caused L40S GPUs to be incorrectly labeled as 'l4'

Both fixes place L40S before L40 before L4 in the canonical names list
to ensure longer names are matched first.

* [Kubernetes] Refactor to share canonical GPU names between modules

Move CANONICAL_GPU_NAMES to sky/provision/kubernetes/constants.py and
update both GFDLabelFormatter and the GPU labeler script to use this
shared constant. This prevents future bugs where one list gets updated
but not the other.

Changes:
- Add CANONICAL_GPU_NAMES to constants.py with documentation about
  ordering requirements (longer names before shorter substrings)
- Update GFDLabelFormatter to use kubernetes_constants.CANONICAL_GPU_NAMES
- Update gpu_labeler.py to dynamically inject the constant into the
  YAML ConfigMap before applying it
- Replace hardcoded list in k8s_gpu_labeler_setup.yaml with a placeholder
  that gets replaced at runtime

* [Kubernetes] Add latest generation GPUs to canonical names list

Add support for newer GPU architectures:
- Blackwell: GB300, GB200, B200, B100
- Hopper: GH200, H200, H100-80GB
- Ampere: A30, A40

Also add special pattern matching for H100-80GB variants
(e.g., H100-SXM-80GB, H100-PCIE-80GB) similar to A100-80GB.

* Format code with yapf

* [Kubernetes] Use Jinja2 template for GPU labeler setup

Convert k8s_gpu_labeler_setup.yaml to a Jinja2 template (.yaml.j2) for
cleaner injection of CANONICAL_GPU_NAMES. This makes it explicit that
the file is a template and uses standard Jinja2 syntax instead of
custom placeholder replacement.

* [Kubernetes] Add comprehensive unit tests for GPU detection

Add tests covering:
- CANONICAL_GPU_NAMES ordering (longer names before substrings)
- Latest GPU architectures (Blackwell, Hopper, Ada Lovelace, Ampere)
- L4/L40/L40S detection (the original bug)
- H100 and A100 80GB variant detection
- GPU labeler substring matching logic
- Fallback behavior for unknown GPUs

These tests help prevent regression of the L40S misidentification bug
and ensure correct GPU detection across all supported architectures.

* Remove unused pytest import

* Add back pytest import in test file

* Fix unit test expected values to match actual behavior

* [Kubernetes] Add more GPU types to canonical names list

Add additional GPU types commonly available in cloud environments:
- Blackwell: B300
- Hopper: H100-MEGA
- Ampere: A16
- Ada Lovelace Professional: RTX6000-Ada
- Quadro/RTX Professional: A6000, A5000, A4000

Also add test for professional RTX GPUs now in canonical list.

* [Kubernetes] Fix --context flag position in kubectl commands

Move --context flag to canonical position immediately after kubectl
instead of at the end of the command.

* [k8s] Add backward compatibility for GPU name changes (#8682)

* [k8s] Add backward compatibility for GPU name changes

This commit adds backward compatibility for accelerator name matching
when GPU canonical names change (e.g., from fallback names like
'H200-XBM-80GB' to canonical names like 'H200').

The issue: When PR #8593 adds new GPUs to the canonical names list,
existing clusters launched with fallback names would fail to match
after upgrading the API server. For example:
- Before: nvidia.com/gpu.product=NVIDIA-H200-XBM-80GB → 'H200-XBM-80GB'
- After: nvidia.com/gpu.product=NVIDIA-H200-XBM-80GB → 'H200'

This would break `sky exec`, managed jobs recovery, and other operations
that need to match the stored launched_resources accelerator name against
the cluster's node labels.

The fix: Add `_accelerator_name_matches()` helper that performs backward-
compatible matching by also accepting prefix matches with '-' separator.
This ensures 'H200-XBM-80GB' matches 'H200' and vice versa.

Tested: Added unit tests in test_gpu_label_formatters.py covering:
- Exact matches
- Backward compatibility (old fallback → new canonical)
- Forward compatibility (new canonical → old fallback)
- No false positives (L4 doesn't match L40, A10 doesn't match A100)

* [k8s] Fix GPU backward compatibility in GKE autoscaler and case sensitivity

- Update GKEAutoscaler._node_pool_has_gpu_capacity() to use
  _accelerator_name_matches() for backward compatible GPU matching
- Fix _accelerator_name_matches() to lowercase both requested and viable
  names for proper case-insensitive comparison
- Add tests for H100 ↔ H100-80GB and GH200 ↔ GH200-480GB backward compat
- Fix typo: XBM → SXM (correct NVIDIA naming convention)
- Remove unused pytest import

* [Docs] Add Windows/WSL setup instructions for VSCode SSH connection

Add a new section documenting how to configure VSCode's Remote-SSH
extension to work with SkyPilot clusters launched from WSL. The issue
is that SkyPilot creates SSH config in WSL's filesystem, but VSCode
on Windows uses the native Windows SSH client which cannot access
WSL paths directly.

The solution uses a batch file wrapper that calls WSL's SSH, allowing
VSCode to share the same SSH configuration as the WSL environment.

https://claude.ai/code/session_016YUauKpvTitHzn1vQVdCqa

* [Core] Auto-configure Windows SSH config when running in WSL

When SkyPilot runs in WSL, it now automatically:
1. Detects the WSL environment via /proc/version
2. Finds the Windows user's home directory
3. Creates SSH config entries in Windows' ~/.ssh/config
4. Uses UNC paths (\\wsl$\...) for SSH keys stored in WSL

This enables VSCode's Remote-SSH extension on Windows to connect
to SkyPilot clusters launched from WSL without manual configuration.

The implementation adds:
- is_wsl(): Detect if running in WSL
- get_wsl_windows_home(): Get Windows home directory path
- get_wsl_path_for_windows(): Convert WSL paths to UNC paths
- SSHConfigHelper methods for Windows SSH config management

Updated documentation to explain the automatic setup and provide

* [Test] Fix logging errors in pytest-xdist parallel tests

Root cause: The logging handler cached sys.stdout at import time, but
pytest-xdist workers (via execnet) replace sys.stdout with their own
I/O channel. When workers finish, execnet closes the channel, causing
"I/O operation on closed file" errors.

Fix: Refresh self.stream to current sys.stdout before each emit, and
skip logging if the stream is closed. This properly addresses the root
cause rather than just suppressing the error.

* [Slurm] Allow SSH agent and default key fallback for Slurm clusters

The IdentitiesOnly=yes SSH option was preventing SSH from falling back
to ssh-agent and default key locations (~/.ssh/id_rsa, etc.) when the
explicitly specified key didn't work. This caused authentication failures
on user-controlled Slurm clusters that rely on these mechanisms.

This PR adds a disable_identities_only parameter to SSHCommandRunner
that allows disabling this behavior for environments where flexible SSH
authentication is needed. Slurm clusters now use this option since they
are user-controlled environments where SSH setup may differ from
SkyPilot-managed clusters.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01BRXXciJ7MA1jh9th1LJmEm

* [Slurm] Make IdentityFile optional in SSH config

Users can now configure Slurm clusters without specifying IdentityFile
in ~/.slurm/config. SSH will fall back to:
- ssh-agent keys
- Default key locations (~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_ed25519, etc.)

This is useful for user-controlled Slurm environments where SSH
authentication may be set up differently from SkyPilot-managed clusters.

Combined with the previous commit that disabled IdentitiesOnly=yes for
Slurm, this provides full flexibility for SSH authentication.

[Test] Fix flaky test_kubernetes_context_failover (#8760)

* [CI] Fix helm publish workflow by allowing flexible separator length in README

* [Test] Fix flaky test_kubernetes_context_failover

The test was failing intermittently because of a race condition
between the API server's background on-boot check and test execution.

When the unreachable_context fixture restarts the API server, it
schedules a background `sky check` that runs asynchronously. This
check includes the unreachable context which causes connection
timeouts (30+ seconds). If the test runs before the background
check completes, the enabled clouds cache is empty, causing
"Kubernetes is not enabled" errors.

Fix by running `sky check kubernetes` synchronously after the API
server restart, ensuring the cache is populated before the test runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Add --infra kubernetes to enforce Kubernetes-only launches

Without --infra kubernetes, the optimizer was free to choose any
enabled cloud (e.g., Slurm), causing the test to fail when checking
that clusters launched on specific Kubernetes contexts.

subject: [Core] Fix SSH authentication for Docker images with non-root default users (#8738)
message:
[Core] Fix SSH authentication for Docker images with non-root default users (#8738)

* [Core] Fix SSH authentication for Docker images with non-root default users

Docker images that set a non-root default USER and explicitly set
ENV HOME were failing SSH authentication because SkyPilot was
detecting the wrong user/home directory.

Changes:
- Detect the container's default user by running `whoami` without
  `-u 0`, ensuring we SSH as the actual default user
- Add `chown` to fix .ssh directory ownership since it's created
  by root but needs to be writable by the default user
- Add `--cap-add=SYS_RESOURCE` to enable prlimit to set file
  descriptor limits inside the container
- Add smoke test for Docker images with non-root default users

* Fix chown command to correctly expand home directory path

Use $(dirname ~/) instead of standalone ~ to ensure the path is properly
expanded by _docker_expand_user, which only replaces ~/ patterns when
any_char=True. This fixes incorrect ownership being set on .ssh directory.

* [Docker] Fix .ssh ownership to use detected user instead of home dir owner

The previous chown command relied on the home directory's parent being
owned by the default user, which fails if HOME is set to a directory
like /tmp owned by root. This change moves the user detection earlier
and uses the detected docker_user directly in the chown command.

* shlex quote docker_user

Co-authored-by: gemini-code-assist[bot] <176961590+gemini-code-assist[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* [Docker] Fix Miniconda download path for non-root users

Download Miniconda installer to /tmp instead of current directory
to ensure non-root users have write access. This fixes the
test_docker_nonroot_user test failure where curl would fail with
"Permission denied" when trying to write to a directory the
non-root user cannot access.

* [Slurm] Dynamically check Pyxis plugin for Docker image support

Make _unsupported_features_for_resources() dynamic (like Kubernetes)
instead of purely static. Before allowing DOCKER_IMAGE, check if the
Pyxis SPANK plugin is installed on the Slurm cluster by running
`srun --help | grep [pyxis]`. Results are cached for 24h per cluster.

If Pyxis is not detected, DOCKER_IMAGE is marked as unsupported with
a helpful error message pointing to the Pyxis GitHub repo.

* [Slurm] Filter out non-Pyxis clusters in regions_with_offering

Add per-cluster feature filtering in regions_with_offering(), matching
the Kubernetes pattern (kubernetes.py:284-296). Without this, when one
cluster has Pyxis and another doesn't, the optimizer could pick the
non-Pyxis cluster for Docker image jobs, causing a runtime failure.

subject: Fix sky api stop hang on zombie processes in containers (#8839)
message:
Fix sky api stop hang on zombie processes in containers (#8839)

* [Core] Fix `sky api stop` hang on zombie processes in containers

In containers without a proper init (tini/dumb-init), PID 1 does not
reap orphaned zombies. psutil.Process.wait() hangs on these because it
polls kill(pid, 0) which always succeeds for zombies.

Fix: for non-child processes, poll proc.status() instead of using
psutil.wait(). This correctly detects zombies (exited but not reaped)
vs running processes. Child processes still use the normal wait() path
since waitpid() can reap them.

Also add alive() guard to the finally block to skip unnecessary
force-kill escalation when the process already exited.

* [Kubernetes/Slurm] Add user-configurable pricing catalog for virtual instance types

Add support for user-provided pricing catalogs for Kubernetes and Slurm
clouds via CSV files at ~/.sky/catalogs/<version>/<cloud>/pricing.csv.
Previously, both clouds hardcoded $0.00 costs, which meant the optimizer
could not make cost-aware decisions. With this change, users can specify
per-vCPU, per-GB-memory, and per-accelerator rates with region/zone
specificity and wildcard fallback.

Also fix LazyDataFrame to detect manual edits to catalog CSV files on
disk (via mtime tracking) without requiring a GitHub download cycle.

* [Kubernetes/Slurm] Move pricing from CSV catalog to config.yaml

Replace the CSV-based pricing catalog with a config-dict approach
that reads pricing from ~/.sky/config.yaml. This lets users set
per-vCPU, per-GB, and per-accelerator hourly rates directly in
their config without managing separate CSV files.

For Kubernetes, pricing can be set at the cloud level and
overridden per-context. For Slurm, pricing supports three-level
deep-merge: cloud < cluster < partition.

subject: [Core] Fix uv >=0.10.5 stripping execute permissions on XFS filesystems (#8904)
message:
[Core] Fix uv >=0.10.5 stripping execute permissions on XFS filesystems (#8904)

uv 0.10.5 introduced a regression where its reflink/clone link mode
strips execute permissions from wheel data files on XFS filesystems.
This causes Ray's gcs_server and raylet binaries to be installed as
664 instead of 775, breaking ray start with PermissionError on
Amazon Linux 2023 (which uses XFS).

Set UV_LINK_MODE=copy in all uv invocations to bypass the broken
reflink code path. This is forward-compatible and has negligible
performance impact since copy mode is already the default on ext4.

message:
[Jobs] Add `internal_external_ips` and `internal_services` to ManagedJobRecord (#8735)

* [Jobs] Add network endpoint info (IPs, DNS entries) to ManagedJobRecord

This change adds three new fields to ManagedJobRecord to expose
network endpoint information for managed jobs:

- internal_ips: List of internal IPs for all nodes in the job's cluster
- external_ips: List of external IPs for all nodes in the job's cluster
- internal_dns_entries: List of K8s internal service DNS entries (K8s only)

This allows external clients (like the SkyPilot API or frameworks like
Monarch and TorchForge) to connect to workers in a JobGroup without
needing to poll Kubernetes directly.

Design notes:
- IPs are extracted from handle.stable_internal_external_ips
- For K8s clusters, DNS entries are extracted from cached_cluster_info
  or constructed from the cluster naming convention
- IPs may change during recovery, but K8s DNS entries are stable as
  they're tied to services that route to the new pod after recovery

For clusters, similar info can be obtained via:
  sky.status()[0]['handle'].stable_internal_external_ips

Co-authored-by: u6aca0e5d0e89a0c1 <u6aca0e5d0e89a0c1@users.invalid>

* [Jobs] Return full handle in ManagedJobRecord instead of IP fields

Simplified the implementation to return the full CloudVmRayResourceHandle
instead of extracting IP/DNS fields separately. This is consistent with
how StatusResponse works for regular clusters.

Now managed jobs can be accessed with:
  job_records = sky.jobs.queue()
  handle = job_records[0]['handle']
  # Access IPs:
  handle.stable_internal_external_ips  # [(internal_ip, external_ip), ...]
  # For K8s, DNS entries are in:
  handle.cached_cluster_info.instances[pod_name][0].internal_svc

This is consistent with how clusters work:
  cluster_info = sky.status()[0]
  handle = cluster_info['handle']
  handle.stable_internal_external_ips

Updated encoders/decoders to properly serialize the handle (pickle/base64)
over the wire, similar to how it's done for cluster status.

Fix Casbin RoleManager race condition in /users endpoint (#8973)

* [API Server] Fix Casbin RoleManager race condition in /users endpoint

RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration.

The race occurs when concurrent requests hit get_user_roles /
get_users_for_role: load_policy rebuilds role links which iterates
RoleManager.all_roles, while _get_role's get-or-create pattern
adds to all_roles concurrently.

reads (enforce, get_roles_for_user) are not blocked by each other,

subject: [Kubernetes] Fix RBAC 409 race with proper upsert semantics (#8969)
message:
[Kubernetes] Fix RBAC 409 race with proper upsert semantics (#8969)

* [Kubernetes] Fix 409 Conflict error when RBAC resources already exist

When provisioning clusters on Kubernetes, SkyPilot creates RBAC resources
(ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding). If these resources already exist
(from a previous run or concurrent request), the API returns a 409 Conflict
error instead of the expected 404.

This fix catches the 409 error and treats it as success (resource already
exists), making the provisioning idempotent.

Affected resources:
- ServiceAccount (create_namespaced_service_account)
- Role (create_namespaced_role)
- RoleBinding (create_namespaced_role_binding)
- ClusterRole (create_cluster_role)
- ClusterRoleBinding (create_cluster_role_binding)

Also adds a smoke test to verify launching a cluster succeeds when RBAC
resources already exist.

Fixes the issue where retrying failed tests or launching concurrent
clusters would fail with:
"roles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io 'skypilot-service-account-role' already exists"

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Move RBAC test to test_cluster_job.py and use concurrent launches

Replace the separate test file with a concurrent launch test that actually
reproduces the 409 race condition. The previous test pre-created RBAC
resources, but SkyPilot's list-then-create pattern would find them and
return early, never triggering the 409 path.

The new test launches two clusters simultaneously so both attempt to create
the same RBAC resources, triggering the TOCTOU race condition.

On 409 Conflict, re-read the resource and fall through to compare/patch

functions via a shared _create_or_patch_resource helper.

subject: [Test] Fix flaky docker storage mount test on older images (#9020)
message:
[Test] Fix flaky docker storage mount test on older images (#9020)

* [Test] Fix flaky docker storage mount test on older images

When azure-cli install fails on older Docker images (e.g. Ubuntu 18.04),
it breaks the && chain in _get_cloud_dependencies_installation_commands,
preventing ALL subsequent package installs (including awscli, boto3).
This causes the storage verification to fail since none of the CLI tools
are available.

Two test-only fixes:
1. Prefer GCP storage (gsutil is installed as a standalone SDK early in
   the chain, so it survives chain breaks)
2. Guard the azure blob check with `command -v az` so it's skipped
   (rather than failing with exit 127) when azure-cli isn't installed

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Wrap azure blob check in group to fix bash operator precedence

The `command -v az && az_blob_command` was being parsed by bash as
part of the outer `||` chain due to equal precedence of `||` and `&&`:

  s3_cmd || gsutil_cmd || command -v az && az_blob_cmd
  → ((s3_cmd || gsutil_cmd || command -v az) && az_blob_cmd)

This meant `az storage blob list` ran even when `aws s3 ls` succeeded,
causing `az: command not found` failures. Wrapping in `{ ...; }`
keeps the `&&` internal to the azure check.

subject: [Core] Fix bash operator precedence in cloud deps install chain (#9002)
message:
[Core] Fix bash operator precedence in cloud deps install chain (#9002)

Wrap commands containing || in subshells (...) to isolate them from the
outer && chain. In bash, && and || have equal precedence (left-to-right),
so `A && B || C && D` evaluates as `((A && B) || C) && D`. When a
command with || fails on both sides, this breaks the entire chain,
skipping all subsequent cloud dependency installations.

This fixes the flaky test_docker_storage_mounts failure where only
step [1/7] uv was printed and steps 2-7 were skipped, causing
"gsutil: command not found" and "az: command not found".

Also reverts the sudo wrapper script fix (ff31cf74e) which was unrelated
to this failure.

subject: [Core] Fix WebSocket SSH proxy timeout under concurrent connections (#9001)
message:
[Core] Fix WebSocket SSH proxy timeout under concurrent connections (#9001)

* [Core] Use lightweight DB lookup for WebSocket SSH proxy validation

Replace core.status() with global_user_state.get_cluster_from_name()
in _get_cluster_and_validate() for WebSocket SSH proxy connections.

core.status() calls backend_utils.get_clusters() which performs:
- workspaces_core.get_workspaces() lookup
- global_user_state.get_clusters() with JOIN on user_table
- _update_records_with_handle_info() resource string formatting
- _update_records_with_resources() field extraction
- responses.StatusResponse.model_validate() Pydantic validation

None of these are needed for simple cluster validation, which only
requires the status field and handle. Under load (nightly CI with
many concurrent K8s tests on the same agent), 20 concurrent WebSocket
connections through the single-worker API server can push the total
validation time past the 60s WebSocket handshake timeout.

Verified on Buildkite:
- Build 8703 (with fix): 14.31s, 2000/2000 commands, 100% success,
  all 20 threads connected within ~0.2s of each other
- Build 8708 (without fix): 14.82s, 2000/2000 commands, 100% success,
  all 20 threads connected within ~1s of each other
Both passed in isolation, but under nightly CI load (build 8676),
the original code failed 5 times before passing on retry 6.
The lightweight lookup reduces per-connection overhead to improve
reliability under concurrent load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Use core.status(summary_response=True) for WebSocket SSH proxy validation

Instead of bypassing core.status() with a direct DB call, use the proper
core.status() API with summary_response=True. This skips expensive DB
columns (owner, metadata, last_creation_yaml) and cluster event queries
while keeping the public API surface intact.

Profiled on Buildkite CI (build 8747, 4-CPU EC2 kind agent, 20 iterations):
- OLD core.status(summary=False):    1.79ms/call, 35.7ms for 20 connections
- PROPOSED core.status(summary=True): 0.91ms/call, 18.1ms for 20 connections
- BYPASS get_cluster_from_name():     0.58ms/call, 11.6ms for 20 connections

The 49% reduction from OLD keeps overhead low enough for 20+ concurrent
WebSocket SSH connections without timeout, while the 0.33ms gap vs BYPASS
is a fair trade-off for proper API abstraction.

subject: [API] Add per-context timeout to /gpu-metrics endpoint (#9044)
message:
[API] Add per-context timeout to /gpu-metrics endpoint (#9044)

* [API] Add per-context timeout to /gpu-metrics endpoint

When a remote K8s cluster becomes unreachable, the /gpu-metrics endpoint
blocks on the hanging port-forward (up to 30s httpx timeout), exceeding
the Prometheus scrape_timeout (10s). This causes Prometheus to mark the
target as down (up=0) and eventually fire the TargetDown alert, even
though the endpoint itself is healthy for all other contexts.

Wrap each context's metrics collection with asyncio.wait_for(timeout=8s)
so that a single unreachable cluster cannot block the entire response.
The 8s timeout is chosen to be safely under the 10s scrape_timeout,
ensuring the endpoint always responds in time for Prometheus.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Fix subprocess leak on per-context timeout cancellation

Reduce start_port_forward_timeout from 10s to 5s so it fits within
the 8s per-context timeout with room for the HTTP request. Switch
the finally-block cleanup from async (asyncio.to_thread) to
synchronous so that CancelledError from asyncio.wait_for cannot
skip subprocess termination.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [API Server] Fix concurrent Alembic migration crash on startup (#9068)
message:
[API Server] Fix concurrent Alembic migration crash on startup (#9068)

Alembic's EnvironmentContext stores the active migration context in a
module-level global (alembic.context._proxy) rather than threading.local().
When plugins run migrations concurrently from different threads (e.g.,
devspace-reconciler and MainThread), the threads overwrite each other's
proxy, corrupting migration state and causing InvalidRequestError or
InFailedSqlTransaction errors.

Add a process-wide threading.Lock to serialize all alembic.command.upgrade()
calls. The existing per-section file locks remain for cross-process
coordination.

* [Dashboard] Fix upgrade banner detection and visibility

The upgrade banner was not appearing during server upgrades for two
reasons:

1. The fetch interceptor only detected 503 responses with a specific
   JSON body from the API server. This missed network errors (connection
   refused) during the Recreate strategy downtime gap, and NGINX's own

subject: [Kubernetes] Fix netcat install failure on Debian Trixie in controller_utils.py (#9086)
message:
[Kubernetes] Fix netcat install failure on Debian Trixie in controller_utils.py (#9086)

[Kubernetes] Fix netcat install failure on Debian Trixie breaking cloud dependency chain

On Debian Trixie (used by continuumio/miniconda3:latest), `netcat` is a
virtual package with no default candidate, causing `apt install netcat`
to exit 100. This broke the && chain in cloud dependency installation,
preventing subsequent steps from running (azure-cli, GCP SDK, cloud
python packages), which caused test_docker_storage_mounts to fail with
`aws/gsutil/az: command not found`.

Root cause is a race condition between two phases:
- Phase 1: kubernetes-ray.yml.j2 (pod setup) installs netcat-openbsd
  correctly, which creates /usr/bin/netcat via Debian alternatives.
- Phase 2: controller_utils.py (sky exec) checks `command -v netcat`
  to decide whether to run `apt install netcat`.

If Phase 1 finishes before Phase 2 runs, /usr/bin/netcat exists, the
if-block is skipped, and the chain succeeds. If Phase 2 runs first,
`command -v netcat` fails, `apt install netcat` is attempted, and it
exits 100 on Trixie, breaking the entire chain.

Evidence from Buildkite:
- Build 8987: miniconda3:latest passed (56s for deps = Phase 1 won)
- Build 8978: miniconda3:latest failed (7s total = Phase 2 ran first)

Fix: use `command -v nc` (the actual binary name) and `apt install
netcat-openbsd` (concrete package), matching kubernetes-ray.yml.j2.
Both outcomes of the race now succeed: if Phase 1 already installed
netcat-openbsd, `nc` is found and the block is skipped; if not,
`apt install netcat-openbsd` succeeds on Trixie.

subject: Prioritize user SSH keys over cluster keys in Host * config (#9099)
message:
Prioritize user SSH keys over cluster keys in Host * config (#9099)

* Prioritize user SSH keys over cluster keys in Host * config

The Host * block in ray templates lists sky-cluster-key and id_rsa
first. When users SSH to external hosts like github.com from inside
a SkyPilot node, these keys are tried first. GitHub limits auth
attempts to ~5, so the user's actual key (e.g. id_ed25519) is never
reached and the connection fails.

Add id_ed25519 and id_ecdsa before the cluster-internal keys so
common user keys are offered first. SSH silently skips IdentityFile
entries that don't exist on disk, so this is safe for nodes that
don't have these key types.

subject: [k8s] Fix GPU labeler crash: preserve method metadata in RetryableClientWrapper (#9152)
message:
[k8s] Fix GPU labeler crash: preserve method metadata in RetryableClientWrapper (#9152)

The GPU labeler's `wait_for_jobs_completion` crashes with:

    AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'metadata'

Root cause: `RetryableClientWrapper.__getattr__` (introduced in #8976)
wraps API methods in `with_refresh` closures that lose the original
method's `__doc__`. The kubernetes `Watch.stream()` relies on parsing
the function's docstring (`:return: V1JobList`) to determine the
return type for event deserialization. Without a docstring,
`get_return_type()` returns `""`, `unmarshal_event()` skips
deserialization, and `event['object']` remains a raw dict instead
of a `V1Job` object.

Fix: add `@functools.wraps(attr)` to the `with_refresh` closure,
which copies `__doc__`, `__name__`, and other metadata from the
original bound method. This restores the pre-#8976 behavior where
Watch could detect the return type and deserialize events properly.

[Jobs] Fix git commit metadata not captured in managed jobs (#9184)

* [Jobs] Fix git commit metadata not captured in managed jobs

The dashboard's "Git Commit" field for managed jobs was not being
populated reliably. Three issues:

1. Server-side re-validation overwrites client value: when the API
   server calls expand_and_validate_workdir() on the remapped blob
   directory (not a git repo), get_git_commit() returns None and
   overwrites the valid commit captured client-side.

2. No git commit captured from YAML file location: when launching
   with a YAML file tracked in a git repo but no workdir,
   load_chain_dag_from_yaml had no mechanism to capture the commit.

3. No git commit without workdir: bare CLI commands like
   `sky jobs launch -- echo hi` never captured any commit.

Fix (1) by only writing git_commit when get_git_commit() returns a
non-None value, so the server can't clobber the client's value.
Fix (2) by capturing git commit from the YAML file's directory in
load_chain_dag_from_yaml, with workdir commit taking priority.

Tested: unit tests for all metadata capture paths and serialization
round-trip; smoke test that launches a job and verifies git_commit
appears in the queue response.

subject: [Dashboard] Fix plugin state ref race condition on navigation mount (#9210)
message:
[Dashboard] Fix plugin state ref race condition on navigation mount (#9210)

The __pluginStateRef was managed via useEffect([state]), which deleted
and recreated the window property on every state change. React runs all
effect cleanups before all new effects (children-first), so when a state
change caused a plugin navigation component to mount for the first time,
the cleanup deleted __pluginStateRef before the child's effect could read
it — resulting in empty navigation links until the next polling interval.

Switch to a stable useRef updated during render so the ref is always
available when child effects execute.

message:
[kubernetes] Fix write permissions for all volume mounts at startup (#9221)

* [kubernetes] Fix write permissions for all volume mounts at startup

Previously only hostPath volumes had permission fixes applied via a
recursive chown. This missed two cases:
- PVC volumes with subPath (the subPath directory is created as root by
  kubelet and not covered by fsGroup)
- NFS-backed PVCs where fsGroup is not honoured by the NFS server

Replace the hostPath-only loop with a lightweight per-path guard:
  test -w "<path>" || (chown :<gid> "<path>" && chmod g+rwx "<path>") || true

The `test -w` check avoids unnecessary privilege use when the container
already has write access. The trailing `|| true` keeps startup non-fatal
if the path doesn't exist yet.

[Core] Add `sky debug-dump` command for troubleshooting (#8868)

* skeleton

* [Core] Implement debug dump feature for troubleshooting

Add `sky debug-dump` command to collect diagnostic information for
troubleshooting SkyPilot issues. Creates a zip file containing logs,
state, and configuration for specified clusters, requests, and/or
managed jobs.

Key implementation decisions:

1. Persistent storage: Debug dumps are stored in ~/.sky/debug_dumps/
   rather than temp directories to allow re-downloading and prevent
   accidental deletion. This fixed a bug in the skeleton where the
   zip was created inside tempdir() context but returned after exit.

2. Cross-linking: When dumping a cluster, we automatically include
   associated requests, and vice versa. This ensures complete context
   without requiring users to manually specify all related resources.

3. --recent flag: Added `--recent N` option to dump all resources
   active within the last N hours, making it easy to capture recent
   activity without knowing specific IDs.

4. Server-side collection: Dumps are created on the API server and
   downloaded to the client, ensuring access to server-side logs and
   state even for remote API server deployments.

5. Graceful degradation: Each collection function catches exceptions
   and continues, creating partial dumps when some data is unavailable.

6. Debug logging: Added comprehensive debug logs throughout the dump
   flow to help troubleshoot issues with debug-dump itself.

Files changed:
- sky/utils/debug_utils.py: Core dump logic with 8 collection functions
- sky/server/server.py: /debug/dump-download and /debug/dump-list endpoints
- sky/client/sdk.py: create_debug_dump, download_debug_dump, list_debug_dumps
- sky/client/cli/command.py: `sky debug-dump` command with full CLI
- sky/core.py: Updated create_debug_dump with recent_hours param
- sky/server/requests/payloads.py: Added recent_hours to request body

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Add API versioning for debug dump endpoints

Bump API_VERSION to 27 and add @versions.minimal_api_version(27)
decorator to all debug dump SDK functions. This ensures users get
a clear error message if they try to use these new functions against
an older server that doesn't support the debug dump endpoints.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Auto-delete debug dumps after download, remove list endpoint

Simplify debug dump lifecycle with 1:1 create-download model:
- Delete dump file automatically after successful download using
  starlette BackgroundTask
- Remove list_debug_dumps SDK function and /debug/dump-list endpoint
  since dumps are ephemeral and don't accumulate

This avoids the need for a separate cleanup/retention policy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Add summary.json to debug dumps

Include a summary file at the root of each debug dump containing:
- requested: Original input parameters (request_ids, cluster_names,
  managed_job_ids, recent_hours)
- collected: What was actually gathered after cross-linking, including
  counts and full lists of IDs/names
- timing: Elapsed time and timestamp

This helps users quickly understand the scope of the dump without
manually inspecting each subdirectory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Add client-side info to debug dumps

Include client_info.json in debug dumps with:
- SkyPilot version and commit
- Python version and platform
- User hash
- Environment variables (SKYPILOT_DEBUG, SKYPILOT_DEV)
- User config and merged config (with API endpoints redacted)

The client gathers this info and sends it to the server in the
request payload. This helps diagnose issues where client and server
environments differ (e.g., remote API server scenarios).

API endpoints in config are replaced with "<redacted>" to avoid
exposing HTTP basic auth credentials or other sensitive info.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Always include system daemon requests in debug dumps

Add SYSTEM_REQUEST_IDS constant and automatically include these
requests in every debug dump:
- skypilot-status-refresh-daemon
- skypilot-volume-status-refresh-daemon
- skypilot-server-on-boot-check

These system requests are relevant for troubleshooting regardless
of which specific resources the user requested to dump.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Improve debug dump reliability, enrichment, and test coverage

- Fix managed job data access for remote controllers by using queue_v2()
  instead of direct DB queries
- Change debug dump schedule type from SHORT to LONG for credential checks
- Add orphan cleanup for dumps older than 1 hour
- Enrich server_info.json with python version, OS platform, DB backend,
  and server uptime (via boot check request)
- Surface collection errors in errors.json and summary.json warnings
- Add human-readable timestamps alongside epoch values
- Improve config redaction using config_utils.Config pattern
- Add debug logging throughout dump creation
- Dump all tasks for multi-task managed jobs
- Add 48 unit tests for cross-linking and dump creation functions
- Add 5 smoke tests covering --recent, -c, -r, -j flags and no-args error

Replace hardcoded SYSTEM_REQUEST_IDS list with dynamic construction from
INTERNAL_REQUEST_DAEMONS and a new ON_BOOT_CHECK_REQUEST_ID constant,
so debug dumps automatically include any new daemon request IDs.

Remove read-only JOBS_QUEUE from request filter. Add matching for
cancel-by-name, cancel-all (with user check), and cancel-all-users

- Remove unnecessary try/except around JOB_CONTROLLER_NAME

- Remove redundant created_at check in _populate_recent_context

Address review comments: add server environment variables to dump,
copy debug log files from _DEBUG_LOG_DIR, add requests→jobs cross-linking
via _get_managed_jobs_from_requests, wire errors through DebugDumpContext

'warnings' to 'errors' in summary, add debug log for missing client info.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Fix imports and remove unnecessary error handling in debug dump

Move all import-outside-toplevel imports to top-level (debug_utils is
only imported server-side so no circular import risk). Remove inner
try/except in _get_requests_from_managed_jobs since all attribute
access uses getattr with defaults. Add error recording to debug log
copy except block.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Add debug file logger and refactor create_debug_dump

Extract _build_debug_dump helper for cross-linking, dumping all
sections, and writing summary. Add a FileHandler at DEBUG level on
the debug_utils logger during dump creation so all debug logs are
captured into debug_dump.log in the zip. Handler is cleaned up in
a finally block (remove, flush, close) to avoid clobbering existing
loggers. No logger level changes needed since effective level is
already DEBUG via inheritance from root sky logger.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Add GetDebugDumpData RPC for non-consolidation mode support

Add a new gRPC RPC to ManagedJobsService that collects debug dump data
(controller logs, job events, run logs, cluster info) from the jobs
controller. This enables the debug dump to work in non-consolidation
mode where the controller runs on a separate VM.

The implementation uses a unified code path: gRPC when available, with
CodeGen/SSH fallback. In consolidation mode, LocalResourcesHandle runs
the CodeGen locally via LocalProcessCommandRunner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Fix bash quoting and remove nonexistent timing assertion in smoke tests

Fix string escaping in python3 -c assertions that are embedded in bash
commands: use \\\" to produce \" in bash (which becomes " in Python),
instead of \" which becomes " directly (breaking bash double-quote
parsing). Also remove assert for 'timing' key which does not exist
in summary.json.

import-outside-toplevel in server.py and sdk.py, and remove redundant

* [Core] Replace gRPC with rsync for controller debug data transfer

The gRPC approach loaded all file contents into memory (controller logs
can be 10-100MB). Replace with a two-phase approach: CodeGen returns a
manifest of file paths + small inline DB data, then rsync downloads the
large files. This works in both consolidation and non-consolidation mode.

but the cross-linking filter was using unprefixed names ('jobs.launch'),
causing zero requests to be matched when cross-linking from managed jobs.

Use resolve() + startswith() instead of string-matching '..' in

Avoid catching broad ValueError from relative_to().

* [Core] Allowlist request bodies in debug dump with redaction

Previously, debug dumps included str(request.request_body) for every
request, which could leak cloud credentials in env_vars and unredacted
task secrets/docker passwords.

This adds an allowlist approach:
- Only include request bodies for known-safe request types
- Redact sensitive env vars (AWS keys, Azure secrets, etc.) in bodies
- Redact task/dag YAML fields (secrets, docker passwords) before inclusion
- Requests not in the allowlist have their body excluded entirely

Also extracts redact_yaml_config() from Task.to_yaml_config() into a
standalone function for reuse, and adds a coverage test ensuring every
RequestName is accounted for in either the allowlist or a denylist.

Tested: unit tests, manual e2e on kind cluster with sky launch +
sky jobs launch + sky debug-dump --recent 1

subject: fix: replace args/command lists instead of extending in k8s config merge (#9238)
message:
fix: replace args/command lists instead of extending in k8s config merge (#9238)

When merging two containers with the same name, the `args` and `command`
fields were being extended (concatenated) instead of replaced. This caused
duplication when admin policies added initContainers with args/command,
as the policy would be applied multiple times during managed jobs workflow.

For example, `args: ["echo", "hello"]` would become
`args: ["echo", "hello", "echo", "hello"]` after a single config merge.

The fix extends `_PATCH_MERGE_KEYS` to support a `None` value which indicates
the list should be replaced atomically instead of merged by key. This is
cleaner than adding a separate set, keeping all merge strategies in one place.

Changes:
- Added `'args': None` and `'command': None` to `_PATCH_MERGE_KEYS`
- Updated `merge_k8s_configs()` to check for `None` merge key and replace
- Added unit tests for args/command replacement behavior

Fixes the bug where admin policies adding initContainers with args/command
would see corrupted container specs after config merging.

subject: [AWS] Add timeout and catch ReadTimeoutError in AZ fetch to prevent sky check hang (#9244)
message:
[AWS] Add timeout and catch ReadTimeoutError in AZ fetch to prevent sky check hang (#9244)

* [AWS] Add timeout and catch ReadTimeoutError in AZ fetch to prevent sky check hang

When an AWS region endpoint is reachable but unresponsive (e.g. me-south-1
from certain VPCs), describe_availability_zones() hangs for up to 300s
(60s default timeout × 5 legacy retries). This blocks the entire sky check
since all regions are checked in parallel but the ThreadPool waits for all
to complete.

Two fixes:
1. Set explicit timeouts (connect=10s, read=15s) and max_attempts=3 on the
   EC2 client used for AZ fetching, reducing worst-case from ~300s to ~45s.
2. Catch ReadTimeoutError alongside ConnectionError. The #9240 fix only
   caught ConnectionError (fast connection failures), but ReadTimeoutError
   (connection succeeds, response never arrives) is a separate exception
   hierarchy in botocore and was not caught.

Fixes nightly build failures where managed jobs got stuck in STARTING
because sky check on the jobs controller hung during AWS credential
verification.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AWS] Fix assertion error when passing Config to aws.client()

Pass timeout/retry settings as builtin-type kwargs (connect_timeout,
read_timeout, max_attempts) through aws.client() instead of passing a
botocore Config object directly. This follows the same pattern as
aws.resource() which already handles max_attempts this way.

The _assert_kwargs_builtin_type check in aws.client() rejects non-builtin
types like Config objects, so the kwargs are popped before the assertion
and used to construct the Config internally.

Fix race condition in release workflow causing untagged releases (#9227)

The `create-release` job in `release-publish.yml` would call
`gh release create` immediately after `git push` for the tag, but the
GitHub API hadn't indexed the tag yet. This caused the v0.12.0 release
to be created with an `untagged-*` placeholder instead of the correct
`v0.12.0` tag.

Three fixes:
- Checkout the release branch explicitly (`ref: base_ref`) instead of
  the ambiguous PR merge ref
- Poll the GitHub API (up to 60s) for the tag to be visible before
  creating the release
- Pass `--target <commit-sha>` to `gh release create` and verify the
  resulting release has the correct tag

subject: [Test] Fix closure bug in optimizer random DAG test (#9293)
message:
[Test] Fix closure bug in optimizer random DAG test (#9293)

The lambda `lambda _: task_runtime` captures the variable by reference,
so all tasks share the last iteration's runtime. This causes the ILP
optimizer's cost coefficients (computed on region-resolved Resources) to
diverge from brute-force verification (computed on region-less Resources)
by more than the $2 tolerance when a catalog update introduces instances
with sufficient cross-region price spread.

Fix by capturing the runtime value at creation time via a factory
function.

message:
[Core] Fall back to SSH when skylet gRPC is unreachable (#9287)

* [Core] Fall back to SSH when skylet gRPC is unreachable

When the skylet gRPC server is down (killed, crashed, or unreachable),
invoke_skylet_with_retries raises RuntimeError after 5 attempts. Previously
this error propagated to the user. Now all gRPC call sites catch RuntimeError
alongside SkyletMethodNotImplementedError and transparently fall back to the
SSH code path with a debug log.

Affected: get_job_queue, add_job, exec_code_on_head, tail_logs, cancel_jobs,
get_job_status, update_status, and all other skylet gRPC call sites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Skip retries on connection refused — skylet is not running

When gRPC gets UNAVAILABLE with "Connection refused", the skylet
process is dead and retrying won't help. Raise RuntimeError immediately
instead of sleeping through 5 backoff attempts (~7.7s wasted).
Callers already catch RuntimeError and fall back to SSH.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Add SkyletUnavailableError and SKYLET_GRPC_FALLBACK_ERRORS

- Add SkyletUnavailableError for when skylet gRPC is unreachable
  (connection refused, exhausted retries). Distinct from
  SkyletMethodNotImplementedError (skylet too old).
- invoke_skylet_with_retries and streaming variant now raise
  SkyletUnavailableError instead of RuntimeError.
- Connection refused skips retries — raises immediately since
  retrying a dead process won't help.
- Add SKYLET_GRPC_FALLBACK_ERRORS tuple constant in backend_utils
  so all 12+ call sites catch one name instead of a 2-element tuple.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Test] Fix test_api_server_memory on kubernetes (#9323)
message:
[Test] Fix test_api_server_memory on kubernetes (#9323)

Two independent bugs stacked to break the nightly's test_api_server_memory
on kubernetes (buildkite build 9760):

1. entrypoint.sh: on `docker restart` (which the test does at
   test_api_server_benchmark.py:38 after `docker update --cpus/--memory`),
   the TEMP_FILE_FOR_TEST fast path calls start_sky_api_server without
   first `cd /skypilot`.  CWD falls back to the Dockerfile's WORKDIR
   (~/sky_workdir/skypilot), and Python's sys.path[0]='' resolves
   `import sky` to the root-owned copy that the Dockerfile COPY'd in
   as root.  Every k8s rsync then runs `chmod +x rsync_helper.sh` on
   a root-owned file as the buildkite user and fails with "Operation
   not permitted", breaking sky launch/exec/start/logs against k8s.

2. basic.sh: #9295 dropped `set -e` and wrapped every op in a bench_run
   helper that swallows return codes.  Previously, the chmod error
   above aborted basic.sh on the first failed op; now phase_cluster
   silently fails through every op and phase_jobs still runs.
   sky jobs launch submits successfully but the managed-jobs
   controller cannot rsync to the worker pod, so it retries forever.
   Four threads x infinite retries exhaust the API server (peak RSS
   > 14 GB) or exceed the 3600s pytest timeout.

Fix:
- entrypoint.sh: add `cd /skypilot` to the TEMP_FILE_FOR_TEST branch
  so the restarted API server has the same CWD as on first start.
- basic.sh: restore `set -e`.  Ops that are intentionally best-effort
  (sky_jobs_logs, sky_jobs_cancel) already have explicit `|| true`.

Tested:
- Watched the live retry on buildkite 9760 job
  019d873f-7fa5-45b0-a933-3423bc7e3b78: confirmed API server
  (pid 51) has cwd=/home/buildkite/sky_workdir/skypilot, rsync_helper.sh
  under that tree is root:root 0775 and chmod fails for the buildkite
  user, and worker pods in test-namespace cycle via the managed-job
  recovery loop every ~2.5 min.
- Will re-run via `/smoke-test --kubernetes --remote-server -k
  test_api_server_memory` after merge.

* [SSH][Provisioner] Wait for async Ray setup on SSH node pools

SSH node pools use the same kubernetes-ray.yml.j2 template as

kubernetes flow, so the two sites stay in sync if another k8s-based

subject: [Jobs] Fix user hash race in concurrent job group launches (#9248)
message:
[Jobs] Fix user hash race in concurrent job group launches (#9248)

* [Jobs] Fix user hash race in concurrent job group launches

When a job group launches multiple tasks concurrently via
asyncio.gather, each executor.launch() shares the same
SkyPilotContext. The ENV_VARS_TO_CLEAR pop/restore in _launch()
mutates the shared context's env_overrides, creating a race:
task B's pop sees the var already deleted by task A, gets None,
and can't restore it. When task B then calls sdk.launch,
get_user_hash() falls back to ~/.sky/user_hash, which may
contain a different hash (e.g., API server in Docker).

Fix: decorate launch() with @context.contextual_async so each
concurrent launch gets its own SkyPilotContext copy. The
pop/restore is then isolated per task.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Add unit test for context isolation race condition

Test that @contextual_async isolates env overrides across concurrent
asyncio.gather tasks, preventing the pop/restore race in _launch().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move context isolation to gather site per review

Instead of decorating the base class launch() method, wrap each
launch coroutine with contextual_async at the gather site in
_run_job_group. This is more targeted — only affects concurrent
job group launches, not all launch() calls.

subject: [Core] Make wheel builds reproducible across processes (#9368)
message:
[Core] Make wheel builds reproducible across processes (#9368)

* [Core] Make wheel builds reproducible across processes

`pip wheel` produces non-deterministic output due to two factors:
1. Zip entry timestamps reflect file mtimes (differ across builds)
2. Requires-Dist metadata ordering depends on PYTHONHASHSEED
   (randomized per-process)

This causes API server replicas to produce different wheel hashes
for identical source code. The jobs controller scheduler compares
wheel hashes to detect code changes, so hash mismatches trigger
unnecessary controller resets.

Fix: set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 and PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in the pip wheel
subprocess environment. NOTE: fix is currently commented out to
demonstrate that the new test catches the issue -- will be enabled
in a follow-up commit.

Tested: new unit test `test_wheel_build_reproducible` builds wheels
in two separate subprocesses (simulating different replicas) and
asserts identical hashes.
