[Telemetry] Add CPU/Memory panels to cluster and job details and rename gpu metrics section to telemetry (#9324)

* [Dashboard] Add CPU/Memory panels to cluster and job telemetry section

The cluster detail and managed job detail pages embed Grafana panels
for GPU utilization, memory, temperature, and power. With node-exporter
metrics already shipping in the bundled DCGM Kubernetes Cluster
dashboard (CPU Utilization at panel 22, Memory Utilization at panel
21), users can now see host-level CPU and memory alongside GPU charts
without leaving the page — useful for debugging OOMs and CPU-bound
workloads in user programs.

Renames `GPUMetricsSection` → `TelemetrySection` since the section now
covers more than GPU metrics. The heading reads "Telemetry" and panels
from both `skypilot-dcgm-gpu` (GPU) and
`skypilot-dcgm-cluster-dashboard` (CPU/Memory) render in a single grid.
"Open in Grafana" now points at the cluster dashboard, which contains
both panel families.

The localStorage keys for the expanded state are renamed accordingly
(`skypilot-*-telemetry-expanded`); users with a previously expanded
section will need to re-expand once.

Tested:
- `npm run build` in `sky/dashboard` succeeds with no type errors.
- Verified iframes load CPU/Memory panels in addition to existing GPU
  panels on the cluster detail page when Grafana is enabled.
- Verified managed job and task detail pages render the same
  consolidated section.
- Verified the "Open in Grafana" button opens the cluster dashboard
  with the correct cluster filter applied.

* [Dashboard] Hide GPU panels in Telemetry for CPU-only clusters/jobs

CPU-only clusters and managed jobs were rendering the four GPU panels
in the Telemetry section even though no GPU data exists for them,
producing four empty/no-data charts before the relevant CPU and Memory
charts. Detect GPU presence from the resources string and hide GPU
panels when none is requested — only CPU Utilization and Memory
Utilization render in that case.

Adds a `resourcesHaveGpu()` helper to gpuUtils that scans for any
canonical GPU model name (or generic "gpu"/"nvidia" fallback) in a
resources or requested_resources string. Threaded through to
`TelemetrySection` via a new `hasGpu` prop (default true preserves
previous behavior).

Tested:
- `npm run build` in `sky/dashboard` succeeds.

* [Dashboard] Use K8s context for host CPU/Mem panels in Telemetry

The host CPU/Memory panels in the Telemetry section were filtering
by var-cluster=<sky_cluster_name_on_cloud>, which matches DCGM's
cluster label but not node_exporter's. node_exporter labels metrics
with the Kubernetes context name, so the panels rendered "no data"
even when host metrics existed for the cluster.

Extract the Kubernetes context name from the SkyPilot infra string
(e.g. "Kubernetes (coreweave-dev)" -> "coreweave-dev") and pass it as
a separate prop. The URL builder uses it for host-family panels and
keeps the SkyPilot cluster name for GPU-family panels.

Note: this surfaces cluster-wide host metrics, not per-Sky-cluster
metrics. Per-Sky-cluster CPU/Memory would require new Grafana panels
that query cAdvisor and filter by pod-name pattern.

Tested:
- `npm run build` in `sky/dashboard` succeeds.

* [Dashboard] Per-Sky-cluster CPU/Mem panels via cAdvisor join

The host CPU/Memory panels in the Telemetry section were filtering by
var-cluster against node_exporter's cluster label, which produced "no
data" because node_exporter labels by Kubernetes context name, not
SkyPilot cluster name. Falling back to the K8s context would only have
shown node-wide metrics, mixing in unrelated workloads.

Fix: add CPU/Memory panels to the existing skypilot-dcgm-gpu
cluster-filter dashboard using cAdvisor metrics
(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total, container_memory_working_set_bytes)
joined with kube_pod_labels{label_skypilot_cluster_name=~"$cluster"}
on (pod, namespace) — exactly the pattern the GPU panels in this
dashboard already use. This gives true per-Sky-cluster CPU and Memory
without conflating other workloads on the same node.

Frontend simplifications:
- TelemetrySection now points all panels at one dashboard
  (skypilot-dcgm-gpu); var-cluster=cluster_name_on_cloud drives both
  GPU and host panels.
- Drop the kubernetesContext prop and extractKubernetesContext helper
  — no longer needed.
- Cap panel grid at 4 columns (grid-cols-1/2/3/4 responsive) to keep
  charts readable on wide screens.

Tested:
- `npm run build` in sky/dashboard succeeds.

* [Dashboard] Use node_exporter for per-Sky-cluster CPU/Mem panels

cAdvisor metrics aren't exported by SkyPilot's /gpu-metrics scrape path,
so the previous cAdvisor-based queries returned no data. Switch CPU and
Memory Utilization panels (id 6, 7) in the skypilot-dcgm-gpu cluster
filter dashboard to node_exporter metrics joined with kube_pod_labels
on the `node` label — kube_pod_labels already carries `node`, so we
filter node_cpu_seconds_total / node_memory_* to nodes that host any
pod of the selected SkyPilot cluster.

This gives node-wide host metrics scoped to the cluster's nodes, not
strictly per-pod usage. For single-tenant nodes (typical SkyPilot
launches with reserved CPU/RAM) the two converge; for shared nodes the
chart will include other workloads on those nodes. True per-pod usage
would need cAdvisor metrics in the scrape path.

Tested:
- Tilt env, managed CPU job on coreweave-dev: panels now render real
  data (e.g. CPU 13.1%, Memory 18.2% on g****b24).
- `npm run build` in sky/dashboard succeeds.

* [Dashboard] True per-pod CPU/Memory in Telemetry via cAdvisor

The CPU/Memory Telemetry panels were node-level and would over-count on
shared nodes. Switch to true per-pod metrics by:

1. Federating cAdvisor `container_cpu_usage_seconds_total` and
   `container_memory_working_set_bytes` from each cluster's Prometheus
   in sky/metrics/utils.py, alongside the DCGM, node_*, and
   kube_pod_labels metrics already pulled.
2. Updating panels 6 and 7 in the cluster-filter dashboard to query
   the cAdvisor metrics joined with kube_pod_labels on (pod, namespace)
   — the same join shape the GPU panels use to filter by SkyPilot
   cluster.
3. Using a 5m rate window to absorb gaps in the 30s federate scrape
   interval. 2m was too tight and intermittently produced "no data".

Tested:
- Local Tilt against coreweave-dev with a managed CPU job and a Sky
  cluster on the same context: panels render real per-pod CPU (~1.28
  cores) and memory (~700 MB) for `telemetry-test-1-328062be-head`,
  scoped strictly to the SkyPilot cluster's pod.
- `npm run build` in `sky/dashboard` succeeds.

* [Dashboard] Address review: case-insensitive Kubernetes check

Use toLowerCase().includes('kubernetes') for the full_infra check on
jobs and task pages, consistent with the cluster detail page.

The var-datasource and var-node comments were already addressed in the
current state (var-datasource removed, var-node present).

* [Dashboard] Rename gpuMetrics* variables to telemetry*

All internal state, memos, and comments in the cluster, job, and task
pages still used the "gpuMetrics" prefix despite the section now
covering CPU/Memory too. Rename to "telemetry" for clarity:

- gpuMetricsRefreshTrigger → telemetryRefreshTrigger
- gpuMetricsTaskIndex → telemetryTaskIndex
- allTasksForGpuMetrics → allTasksForTelemetry
- tasksWithGpuMetrics → tasksWithTelemetry
- hasAnyTaskWithGpuMetrics → hasAnyTaskWithTelemetry
- gpuMetricsTask → telemetryTask
- gpuMetricsClusterName → telemetryClusterName

No behavioral change — purely internal variable/comment renames.

* [Dashboard] prettier format

* [Dashboard] Label CPU Usage panel with (cores) unit

* [Dashboard] Replace resources-string GPU regex with structured accelerators check

Instead of regex-matching the free-form resources string against a hard-coded
list of GPU model names, check the structured `accelerators` field SkyPilot
already exposes on clusters and managed-job tasks. An accelerator is requested
iff the dict is non-empty (or, for the stringified form, not 'None'/'{}').

Robust to new GPU model names without needing to update CANONICAL_GPU_NAMES.

subject: [Core] Skip re-install of unchanged plugin wheels (#9367)
message:
[Core] Skip re-install of unchanged plugin wheels (#9367)

* [Core] Skip re-install of unchanged plugin wheels

On every controller launch (`sky jobs launch`, `sky serve up`, etc.), the
controller's `run` phase would unconditionally `uv pip install` every plugin
wheel listed in `controller_wheel_path`. Two problems:

1. It's wasted work when the wheel hasn't changed since the last launch.
2. Parallel launches can race through the install step and briefly leave
   site-packages in a half-rewritten state, causing transient ImportError
   in other plugin-using processes on the same controller.

This change rewrites `get_plugin_mounts_and_commands()` to emit a guarded
install script that:

- Takes an exclusive `flock` on `~/.sky/plugins/.install.lock`, serializing
  concurrent launches through the install critical section.
- Checks a stamp file (`~/.sky/plugins/.installed_wheels`) containing the
  filenames of already-installed wheels; if the current wheel's filename is
  listed, the install is skipped.
- On install, replaces any prior stamp entry for the same package and
  `find`-deletes older wheels of that package so the wheel directory
  doesn't grow unbounded across upgrades.

Idempotency relies on the wheel filename encoding the build identity (via
the PEP 440 version, including any local-version segment such as
`+<sha>`), which is how plugin producers already distinguish builds.

The two controller templates are updated to pipe the commands through
`| indent(2)` so the now-multiline install block preserves YAML
block-scalar indentation.

Tested:
- `python -m sky.server.plugin_utils` helpers: `_wheel_name_prefix` parses
  both plain (`pkg-1.2.3-...`) and local-version (`pkg-1.2.3+abc-...`)
  wheel filenames correctly.
- Rendered `jobs-controller.yaml.j2` with a representative wheel and
  confirmed the output parses as valid YAML via `yaml.safe_load`.
- `bash format.sh` passes (black/yapf/isort/mypy/pylint).

* Address review: atomic stamp rename + simpler wheel-name parsing

- mktemp now uses the stamp file's own directory as the template
  (`mktemp "$_sky_stamp.XXXXXX"`) so the subsequent mv is an atomic
  same-filesystem rename. Previously mktemp defaulted to /tmp, which
  on many cloud VMs is a tmpfs separate from $HOME, turning the mv
  into copy+delete and reopening the atomicity gap the stamp file
  was meant to close.
- `_wheel_name_prefix` now splits on the first '-' directly. PEP 427
  guarantees the distribution name portion contains no hyphens (they
  are replaced with underscores), so the regex was overkill. Dropped
  the `re` import.

* Simplify: shared _sky_record shell function + 2-tuple API

- Extract the per-wheel stamp-file-rewrite + stale-wheel-prune tail
  into a `_sky_record` bash function defined once inside the flock
  subshell. Each per-wheel block collapses to `_sky_record <prefix>
  <wheel>`.
- Compute the package prefix inside `_build_guarded_install_script`
  instead of precomputing it at the caller. The helper now accepts
  `List[Tuple[wheel_filename, remote_path]]`, dropping the third
  tuple element that leaked `_wheel_name_prefix` into the caller's
  vocabulary.
- Drop the 4-line block comment on `_REMOTE_INSTALL_LOCK`; the same
  rationale already lives in `get_plugin_mounts_and_commands`'s
  docstring.

* [Test] Update test_get_plugin_mounts_and_commands for guarded install

The install script is now a flock-wrapped bash block with per-wheel
stamp-file guards rather than an && chain of uv-pip-install commands.
Replace the ' && ' assertion with assertions that exercise the new
guarantees: flock is present, installs are gated on the stamp file,
and the per-wheel check uses grep -Fxq.

subject: [Dashboard] Fix filter bar expanding to full width on page navigation (#9350)
message:
[Dashboard] Fix filter bar expanding to full width on page navigation (#9350)

* [Dashboard] Fix cluster filter bar expanding to full row width on re-renders

The input wrapper div inside FilterDropdown had `flex-1` (flex: 1 1 0%),
which made the FilterDropdown container's CSS max-content intrinsic size
unbounded. The parent `sm:w-auto` flex item uses this intrinsic size: on
initial render the browser picks min-content (~480px, narrow/correct), but
after React re-renders triggered by auto-refresh or navigation the browser
picks max-content (unbounded), expanding the filter bar to fill the full row.

Fix: add `sm:flex-none` to the input wrapper div. On sm+ screens this
disables flex-grow so the div sizes to its content (the `sm:w-96` input =
384px), giving the container a deterministic ~480px intrinsic size.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Dashboard] Fix filter bar expanding to full width on page navigation

Add `max-w-[520px]` to the filter wrapper div on the Clusters and Jobs
pages. Without a hard max-width, the `w-full sm:w-auto` wrapper in a
flex-wrap container has no upper bound — browsers inconsistently resolve
the flex base size between initial render and re-render, sometimes
choosing max-content (unrestricted width) instead of min-content.

The previous fix (sm:flex-none on the inner wrapper) was insufficient
because it only bounded the inner element's flex growth, not the outer
wrapper's intrinsic size. This matches the existing pattern in users.jsx
which uses max-w-md for the same reason.

subject: [CI] Lowercase branch slug when triggering ReadTheDocs build (#9385)
message:
[CI] Lowercase branch slug when triggering ReadTheDocs build (#9385)

ReadTheDocs slugifies version names by replacing slashes with dashes
AND lowercasing all letters (Django-style slugify). The
readthedocs-manual-pr-build workflow only does the slash -> dash
replacement, so any PR branch with an uppercase letter in its name
(e.g. `claude/slurm-to-skypilot-converter-fggF9`) fails the
`PATCH /versions/<slug>/` lookup with 404 and /build-docs comments fail
with "Failed to trigger ReadTheDocs build".

Add `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'` (and `.toLowerCase()` in the JS step
that builds the preview URL) so the slug used in the RTD API matches
the one RTD actually creates. Also applied to the cleanup job so
deactivation on PR close uses the correct slug.

subject: [Core] Improve user-facing error messages for launch misconfigurations (#9403)
message:
[Core] Improve user-facing error messages for launch misconfigurations (#9403)

* [Core] Improve 'did you mean' suggestions in config errors

Three small improvements to the suggestions shown when a user supplies
invalid infra / cloud / field names in launch YAMLs or CLI flags:

- Unknown-field suggestions now join with a space separator. Previously,
  two typos at the same level produced a concatenated string like
  "...did you mean 'setup'?Instead of 'env'..." with no whitespace.
- The cloud registry now suggests a close match when the user typos
  a cloud name (e.g. --infra gpc -> "Did you mean 'gcp'?"), matching
  the existing UX for region / zone typos.
- Lowered the region/zone fuzzy-match cutoff from 0.9 to 0.6. The old
  cutoff required near-identical strings and missed common typos such
  as 'us-east' (user forgot the numeric suffix) matching 'us-east-1'.

* [Core] Clean up user-facing error messages for memory, local_disk, and k8s instance types

Three user-facing error paths were leaking internal implementation
details or chained tracebacks when a user passed an invalid value:

- parse_memory_resource: the error message interpolated the raw
  MEMORY_SIZE_PATTERN regex into the user-facing string, producing a
  garbled '"memory" field should be a ^[0-9]+(kb|ki|...)?$+?, got xyz'.
  Replace with a human-readable message that names accepted formats.
  Also wrap the three raise sites with print_exception_no_traceback.
- normalize_local_disk: chained 'could not convert string to float'
  traceback leaked above the user-friendly message for inputs like
  --local-disk foo. Use 'raise ... from None' and wrap the remaining
  two raise sites with print_exception_no_traceback.
- Kubernetes.get_vcpus_mem_from_instance_type: the underlying
  KubernetesInstanceType.from_instance_type raised a regex-mismatch
  ValueError that was not wrapped, so a non-Kubernetes instance type
  (e.g. --instance-type m5.large --infra k8s) produced a Python
  traceback during dryrun YAML serialization. Catch and re-raise with
  a targeted message documenting the expected name format.

* [Core] Unwrap anyOf/oneOf schema errors to surface the real problem

When a config field is validated against an anyOf or oneOf schema,
jsonschema's default top-level ValidationError is the unhelpful
"X is not valid under any of the given schemas" with json_path
truncated at the branch boundary. This hides the real issue from
users for fields like resources.autostop, workdir (str vs dict),
and resources.accelerators.

Use jsonschema.exceptions.best_match to recurse into the branch
context and surface the deepest, most-specific sub-error. For
example, a misspelled type inside resources.autostop.idle_minutes
now reports:

  Invalid resources YAML: 'ten' is not of type 'integer'.
  Check problematic field(s): $.autostop.idle_minutes

instead of the old:

  Invalid resources YAML: {'idle_minutes': 'ten'} is not valid under
  any of the given schemas. Check problematic field(s): $.autostop

subject: [Pools] Fix pool consolidation under deploy-mode auto-enable (#9342)
message:
[Pools] Fix pool consolidation under deploy-mode auto-enable (#9342)

* [Pools] Fix pool consolidation under deploy-mode auto-enable

serve_utils.is_consolidation_mode(pool=True) read config only, while
managed_job_utils.is_consolidation_mode() reads the signal file written
by setup_consolidation_mode_on_startup. Under deploy-mode auto-enable
(PR #9090), the signal file is created without setting config, so the
pool and managed-jobs readers diverged: pool apply launched a separate
controller cluster while pool status routed to the in-pod handle and
returned "Pool not found".

Read the signal file for pool=True to match managed jobs. Serve
(pool=False) remains config-driven since serve has its own controller.
Add cross-module invariant comments and parametrized tests.

* [Pools] Mirror managed-jobs warnings in pool consolidation reader

Address review feedback on #9342: the pool=True branch of
serve_utils.is_consolidation_mode now mirrors the warning and
validation logic from managed_job_utils.is_consolidation_mode so both
readers give users identical guidance. Specifically:

- Warn when explicit config disagrees with the effective signal-file
  state (user needs to restart API server for config to take effect).
- Validate against the intended config_value when set, falling back to
  the effective value when config is unset.

Reinforces the invariant that the two readers behave identically.

* [Pools] Fix line-length violations in invariant comments

* [Pools] Add test coverage for IS_SKYPILOT_SERVER validation path

Address review comment on #9342: existing test_pool_follows_signal_file
did not exercise the config-read + warning + validator block because
IS_SKYPILOT_SERVER was unset. Add:

- Explicit assert_not_called() on config.get_nested in the existing
  test to prove the env-guard skips config reads when unset.
- New test_pool_warns_and_validates_with_server_env parametrized over
  signal × config × mismatch, verifying the jobs config key is read,
  validator is called with the intended config_value (or effective
  when unset), and the restart warning fires only on mismatch.

* [Pools] Delegate to managed-jobs reader instead of duplicating logic

Address review feedback on #9342: the pool branch of
serve_utils.is_consolidation_mode now delegates to
sky.jobs.utils.is_consolidation_mode via a function-local import,
eliminating ~20 lines of duplicated signal-read + restart-warning
logic. Function-local import justified by the module cycle:
sky.jobs.utils -> sky.backends.backend_utils -> sky.serve.serve_utils.

The pool-specific validator is still called on top of delegation
because the jobs validator warns about leftover managed jobs, not
leftover pools; pool callers need both warnings to fully unblock a
consolidation flip.

Unit tests rewritten to mock managed_job_utils.is_consolidation_mode
directly, since pool delegates to it rather than reimplementing.

* [Pools] Skip pool validator when consolidation is on

The jobs validator (called during delegation to
managed_job_utils.is_consolidation_mode) already warns about the
leftover controller cluster when consolidation is enabled. Running the
pool validator on top duplicated that warning.

Only call the pool validator when consolidation is off — its unique
contribution is warning about leftover pools, which the jobs validator
does not cover.

Test parametrization updated to cover both branches: pool validator
runs only for arg=False cases, skipped for arg=True cases.

* [Test] Use assert_called_once_with for serve config key assertion

Stricter assertion catches future regressions where the serve branch
of is_consolidation_mode accidentally grows additional config reads.

* [Test] Make is_consolidation_mode tests hermetic against shell env

Use monkeypatch.delenv to remove IS_SKYPILOT_SERVER and
IS_SKYPILOT_JOB_CONTROLLER at test start, preventing a stale shell env
var from flipping test behavior (e.g. the OVERRIDE short-circuit
bypassing the pool or serve branches entirely). Auto-restored on
teardown, follows the pattern in tests/unit_tests/test_mithril.py.

* [Test] Simplify test_override_env_forces_true; clean up imports

Address review observations:

- test_override_env_forces_true used a TemporaryDirectory and signal-file
  patch that the OVERRIDE short-circuit never consults. Removed; kept
  only the skypilot_config mock as a defensive guard against a future
  regression that breaks the short-circuit and falls through to config.

- Tried the inline form of pylint disable for the function-local import
  in serve_utils. yapf strips the trailing comment, so kept the
  block-form on its own line above the import (working baseline).

* [Pools] Extract shared consolidation reader into controller_utils

Address Lloyd's follow-up on #9342: extract the jobs-consolidation
signal-read + config-vs-signal warning + jobs validator into a single
helper owned by sky/utils/controller_utils.py, which both readers now
route through.

- controller_utils.is_jobs_consolidation_mode(extra_validator=None) is
  the single source of truth. Internal
  _effective_jobs_consolidation_with_warnings is cached per request so
  the jobs validator and restart warning fire at most once per request
  even when multiple readers resolve in the same request.
- controller_utils.warn_jobs_consolidation_mode_intent moved over from
  sky/jobs/utils.py (where it was the jobs half of
  _validate_consolidation_mode_config).
- sky/jobs/utils.py::is_consolidation_mode becomes a thin wrapper.
- sky/serve/serve_utils.py::is_consolidation_mode(pool=True) becomes a
  thin wrapper that passes a pool-specific extra_validator. The extra
  validator calls the pool-only _validate_consolidation_mode_config
  only when consolidation is off (the jobs validator already covers
  the consolidated case via the shared helper).
- setup_consolidation_mode_on_startup updated to call the moved
  validator.

Tests:
- New tests/unit_tests/test_controller_utils.py::TestIsJobsConsolidationMode
  covers OVERRIDE short-circuit, no-server-env path, server-env matrix
  (signal x config x warn x validator arg), and extra_validator
  plumbing.
- test_serve_utils.py tests rewritten to mock the helper directly.
- test_jobs_utils.py restart-warning test updated to mock the moved
  validator and new helper cache.

* [Pools] Clean up typing nits in controller_utils helper

- Import Tuple and use Tuple[bool, Optional[bool]] instead of the
  string-form 'tuple[...]' return annotation, matching the rest of the
  file (Dict, List, etc. are all typing-module forms here).
- Drop the trailing comma on is_jobs_consolidation_mode's single
  parameter so yapf leaves the signature in a readable split form.

* [Pools] Update signal-file comment for post-refactor reader layout

After extracting the shared helper into controller_utils, the direct
signal-file readers are the helpers there, not the jobs/serve wrappers.
Clarify which functions actually read the file and which are thin
wrappers routing through the shared helper.

subject: [Docs] Speed up incremental docs build (~15x on no-op, ~10x on one-line edit) (#9396)
message:
[Docs] Speed up incremental docs build (~15x on no-op, ~10x on one-line edit) (#9396)

* [Docs] Speed up docs build by ~15x on incremental rebuilds

Root causes of slow docs builds:
- build.sh did "rm -rf build docs" on every invocation, throwing away
  Sphinx's incremental build cache.
- generate_examples.py bumped mtimes of ~130 generated example pages on
  every run, even when their content was unchanged, causing Sphinx to
  re-read them.
- dynamic_llms_txt rewrote source/llms.txt on every build, invalidating
  that source file.
- markdown_export ran pandoc over all ~216 pages on every build (32s of
  35s incremental wall time), regardless of whether any page changed.
- generate_examples.py ran "git ls-files --error-unmatch" per file
  (~545 subprocess invocations, ~12s).

Fixes:
- build.sh: only clean build/ on explicit --clean/-c; otherwise let
  Sphinx do incremental.
- Makefile: pass -j auto for parallel reading/writing.
- generate_examples.py: batch tracked-file lookup into one git ls-files
  call; write generated .md files only when content changes; filter
  untracked example paths so local remnants don't leak into the build;
  remove stale outputs whose sources are no longer present.
- dynamic_llms_txt: skip source llms.txt write when content unchanged.
- markdown_export: skip pandoc re-export for pages whose .html.md is
  already newer than their .html.

Timings (local, 218-page build):
  Clean build:      80s -> 50s
  No-op rebuild:    60s -> 3.5s
  One-line edit:    60s -> 6s

Test plan:
- Run "bash docs/build.sh" twice in docs/. Second run should complete
  in a few seconds and report "0 added, 0 changed, 0 removed".
- Edit any .rst/.md source file and rerun; only that page and its
  dependents should rebuild.
- Run "bash docs/build.sh --clean" for a from-scratch build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Docs] Declare extension.linting parallel-safe

The linting extension only hooks source-read and reads text — no shared
mutable state — so it's safe under -j auto. Without this declaration,
Sphinx emits a warning and falls back to serial reading, which trips
build.sh's error-on-warning check.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Docs] Fix yapf formatting in speedup changes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Docs] Make docs watch mode use the incremental doctree cache

sphinx-autobuild defaults its doctree dir to <outdir>/.doctrees, i.e.
build/html/.doctrees, while `make html` writes to build/doctrees. On
startup, watch mode saw an empty cache and rebuilt from scratch — none
of the incremental-build savings applied. Pass -d build/doctrees so
both paths share the cache, and -j auto to match the Makefile default.

Timings after the fix:
  Watch-mode startup (cache warm):  full rebuild -> sub-second
  One-line .rst edit under watch:   full rebuild -> ~6s

subject: [Slurm] Preserve SLURM_CONF* env vars when launching task srun (#9425)
message:
[Slurm] Preserve SLURM_CONF* env vars when launching task srun (#9425)

* [Slurm] Preserve SLURM_CONF* env vars when launching task srun

The task codegen strips all SLURM_* environment variables before invoking
the inner srun, to avoid the parent step's allocation constraints
(SLURM_CPU_BIND, SLURM_NNODES, SLURM_NODELIST) leaking into the child and
causing "CPU binding outside of job step allocation" errors.

Stripping everything is too broad: it also removes SLURM_CONF and
SLURM_CONF_SERVER, which srun needs to locate slurmctld on sites that
distribute the Slurm config via an env var rather than
/etc/slurm/slurm.conf. When unprivileged users cannot write to
/etc/slurm/, they rely on SLURM_CONF, and losing it causes srun to fall
through to DNS SRV discovery and fail with:

  srun: error: resolve_ctls_from_dns_srv: res_nsearch error: Unknown host
  srun: error: fetch_config: DNS SRV lookup failed
  srun: fatal: Could not establish a configuration source

This surfaces as "Job N's setup failed with return code 1" in SkyPilot's
driver output, regardless of whether the user defined a setup: block,
because both the exclusive-allocation srun and the --overlap setup srun
go through the same codegen path.

Change the awk filter to exclude names matching /^SLURM_CONF/, preserving
both SLURM_CONF and SLURM_CONF_SERVER while still stripping the
step/layout variables the original unset was targeting.

Tested:
- Updated snapshot tests in tests/unit_tests/test_sky/backends/testdata/slurm_codegen/
- Manual test plan: on a Slurm site that exports SLURM_CONF (with no
  /etc/slurm/slurm.conf), run sky launch against a Slurm infra; task
  should run to completion instead of failing with the DNS SRV error.

* [Slurm] Regenerate slurm_codegen snapshots to include comment block

The preceding commit only updated the awk line in the slurm_codegen
snapshots, but the added SLURM_CONF* preservation comment also lives
inside the codegen's textwrap.dedent block and is therefore part of the
generated driver script. Regenerate the snapshots so they match what
task_codegen.SlurmCodeGen now emits.

Tested:
- pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/backends/test_task_codegen.py (18 passed)
- bash format.sh (pylint 10.00/10, yapf/mypy/isort clean)

subject: [Test] Add streaming smoke tests for `sky logs` edge cases (#9435)
message:
[Test] Add streaming smoke tests for `sky logs` edge cases (#9435)

* [Test] Add streaming smoke tests for `sky logs` edge cases

`sky logs <cluster> <job>` (streaming mode, not `--status`) is how users
normally watch training output, but the existing smoke tests only
exercise it with a handful of short `echo` lines per run. Two patterns
that show up routinely in real workloads have no coverage today:

  1. A single log line much larger than a reasonable fixed-size scanner
     buffer. JSON configs, dataset/tokenizer summaries, tensor dumps,
     and image-mode progress snapshots easily clear 256 KB on one line.

  2. `\r`-only progress bar updates (tqdm, keras, rich.progress). The
     server emits a single log "line" (server-side split is on `\n`),
     so a client that splits the received stream on `\n` only will
     visually hang until the bar is eventually replaced by a
     `\n`-terminated summary line.

Clients that split the stream with a fixed line-size cap (for example
Go's `bufio.Scanner`, which caps at 64 KB by default) will either
silently truncate on case (1) or deterministically fail the whole
command if they treat buffer-full as a transient scanner error that
triggers a retry — every retry re-hits the same stalled byte.
Python's SDK uses `iter_content` + `str.splitlines` which has neither
limitation, so when another client implementation hits case (1) the
gap doesn't surface in OSS CI until a user reports it.

Adds:

* `tests/test_yamls/long_log_line.yaml` — runs a task that prints a
  300 KB line bracketed by short START/END markers.
* `tests/test_yamls/cr_progress_bar.yaml` — runs a task that emits
  five `\r`-terminated progress frames followed by a `\n`-terminated
  summary marker.
* `tests/smoke_tests/test_basic.py::test_cli_logs_streaming_long_line`
  — launches the long-line task, then `sky logs <cluster> 1` and asserts
  the captured output (a) contains both bracket markers and (b) that
  its longest line is ≥ 300 KB.
* `tests/smoke_tests/test_basic.py::test_cli_logs_streaming_progress_bar`
  — launches the progress-bar task, then `sky logs <cluster> 1` and
  asserts every frame and the summary reached the client.

Both tests run end-to-end against `generic_cloud`, use
`LOW_RESOURCE_ARG` so they stay cheap, and locally verify in a couple
of seconds.

* [Test] Add real-time streaming smoke test for `sky logs`

The existing log smoke tests (`test_cli_logs`, `test_cli_logs_streaming_*`)
all observe `sky logs` *after* the underlying job has finished — they
either run `--status` or capture the whole output via `$(sky logs ...)`.
None of them can tell the difference between a real streaming pipeline
and one that just hands the entire log file over at the end. A
regression that broke incremental streaming (e.g. a too-large
server-side flush buffer, or a client that reads the body in one shot
after EOF) would look identical to the user when running `sky logs
<cluster> <job>` mid-run: no errors, just dead air for the entire job
runtime.

Adds:

* `tests/test_yamls/streaming_logs.yaml` — runs a 30-second task that
  prints six STREAM_TICK_N lines five seconds apart. Uses `python3 -u`
  so each tick is written through the kernel pipe immediately;
  otherwise the OS-level pipe buffer would hold every tick until the
  script exits and the test would pass even without real-time
  streaming.
* `tests/smoke_tests/test_basic.py::test_cli_logs_streaming_realtime`
  — provisions a cluster, submits the streaming task detached, and
  immediately starts `sky logs` against it. Each received line is
  timestamped via `while IFS= read -r line; do printf "%d %s\n"
  "$(date +%s)" "$line"; done` (a `while read` loop instead of `awk`
  because awk block-buffers its stdin and would mask the very property
  this test is checking — confirmed locally: piping through awk
  collapses the receive timestamps to a single second). The first and
  last STREAM_TICK receive timestamps must differ by ≥ 15 seconds;
  with a 25-second emit spread this gives a 10-second margin for
  scheduling slop while still failing loudly if every tick arrives in
  one burst.

Verified locally end-to-end against a real Kubernetes cluster:
sky logs received the six ticks at the same five-second cadence the
job emitted them, spread = 25s, assertion PASS.

Extract Core Logic for Jobs (#9420)

* Extract out core logic.

* [Plugin] Add ExternalManagedJobRunner extension point

Introduces a singleton-registry extension (modeled on
ExternalFailureSource) that lets plugins supply an alternative
implementation for the three managed-job controller operations:

- fetch_managed_job_table
- cancel_managed_jobs
- tail_managed_job_logs

When a plugin registers, the three _*_via_controller helpers in
sky.jobs.server.core delegate to the registered functions instead of
the default codegen+subprocess path. No change to default behaviour
when no plugin is registered.

* [Plugin] Unified cancel dispatch via inspect.getsource

Extract the cancel-variant selection (job_ids/name/pool/all/all_users)
into a single cancel_managed_jobs() dispatcher in managed_job_utils.
Add a matching ManagedJobCodeGen method that ships the dispatcher's
source into the generated Python via inspect.getsource, so the
subprocess codegen path runs the same function bytes as direct callers.

No duplicate dispatch implementation, no managed_job_version gating for
the dispatcher itself. Collapse _cancel_managed_jobs_via_controller to
a single codegen call.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Plugin] Replace ExternalManagedJobRunner with ManagedJobRunner registry

Invert the extension point: instead of core having a default inline path
plus an optional plugin override, both paths register a runner and core
just calls the currently-registered runner.

- New sky/jobs/runner.py defines the ManagedJobRunner Protocol plus
  register()/current(). Last registration wins.
- sky/jobs/server/core.py defines _DefaultManagedJobRunner (the old
  codegen+run_on_head logic) and registers it at module import.
- queue_v2 / cancel / tail_logs call managed_job_runner.current().<method>
  instead of the ex-_*_via_controller wrappers.
- Remove sky/utils/plugin_extensions/external_managed_job_runner.py —
  replaced by sky/jobs/runner.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Plugin] Simplify cancel_managed_jobs codegen

Replace the inspect.getsource-based codegen with a direct call to
utils.cancel_managed_jobs, gated on managed_job_version. Addresses
three review points:

1. Drop the three now-unused individual cancel codegen methods
   (ManagedJobCodeGen.cancel_jobs_by_id/name/pool) — nothing calls
   them after we consolidated to cancel_managed_jobs.
2. Drop inspect.getsource: the codegen's _PREFIX already imports
   sky.jobs.utils as ``utils``, so we can reference
   utils.cancel_managed_jobs directly on new controllers.
3. Add managed_job_version gating: controllers running version < 18
   don't have cancel_managed_jobs. Client-side picks one of
   utils.cancel_jobs_by_id / cancel_job_by_name / cancel_jobs_by_pool
   based on the selector args and embeds just that call.

Bump MANAGED_JOBS_VERSION to 18 for the new dispatcher.

* [Plugin] Restore per-version gating in cancel codegen legacy branch

The legacy branch (managed_job_version < 18) of
ManagedJobCodeGen.cancel_managed_jobs previously hard-coded the latest
signatures of cancel_jobs_by_id / cancel_job_by_name — passing
graceful/graceful_timeout to controllers that don't support them (< 16),
current_workspace to controllers that don't support it (< 4), and
all_users to controllers that don't support it (< 2).

Restore the multi-tier gating from the deleted individual codegen
methods so old controllers receive only the args their signatures
accept:

- cancel_jobs_by_id: 4 tiers (< 2, < 4, < 16, else)
- cancel_job_by_name: 3 tiers (< 4, < 16, else)
- cancel_jobs_by_pool: unchanged (no historical gating)

[Jobs] Add --tail to sky jobs logs (#9449)

* [Jobs] Add --tail to sky jobs logs

Matches the existing --tail on `sky logs` (cluster jobs) and the
dashboard's 5000-line tail for the managed-jobs log viewer. Useful for
large logs where downloading the full file is slow, especially via
-s/--sync-down.

The server/backend/codegen already accept `tail`; this wires it through
the download_logs path that was previously hard-coded to "all lines":

  CLI --tail N
    -> managed_jobs.tail_logs(tail=N)         (already accepted)
    -> managed_jobs.download_logs(tail=N)     (new)
       -> JobsDownloadLogsBody.tail           (new payload field)
       -> core.download_logs(tail=N)          (new)
       -> backend.sync_down_managed_job_logs(tail=N)   (new)
       -> ManagedJobCodeGen.stream_logs(tail=N)        (already accepted)

This reaches backend.tail_logs(tail=N) on the worker, which translates
to the underlying log reader's tail parameter, keeping the response
bounded at the source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Address review: normalize tail<=0 in SDK, support --tail for controller logs

- SDK: normalize tail <= 0 to None in both tail_logs and download_logs,
  matching the CLI. Prevents a remote AssertionError in
  utils.stream_logs (which asserts tail > 0) when callers pass 0 directly.
- sync_down_managed_job_logs: when --tail is set together with
  --controller, route through ManagedJobCodeGen.stream_logs(controller=True,
  tail=N) instead of rsyncing the full controller log. Keeps the rsync
  fast-path for the default (no --tail) case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Drop --tail support for --sync-down

Per review: --tail + --sync-down combines poorly. A user who wants a
bounded tail can use \`sky jobs logs --no-follow --tail N <id>\` and
redirect stdout to save it. The sync-down path is for full-log
downloads with the managed-jobs dir layout, which is an orthogonal use
case.

- CLI: reject --tail + --sync-down with a UsageError that points users
  to the --no-follow + --tail workflow.
- Revert the download_logs tail plumbing (SDK, core, payload, backend
  signature, ManagedJobCodeGen.stream_logs tail pass-through on the
  sync-down path, and the controller-logs routing via stream_logs).

Kept: --tail CLI flag for the non-sync-down path, and the SDK-side
tail<=0 normalization in tail_logs (prevents remote AssertionError).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Raise on invalid tail in SDK instead of silent normalization

The previous change silently normalized tail<=0 to None, which hides
caller bugs. The CLI already normalizes its 0=all-lines convention
before reaching the SDK, so an SDK caller passing 0 or negative is
passing an invalid value and should see a clear error rather than
silently getting the full log.

Launches a managed job that prints 20 tagged lines, then verifies:

subject: [Core] Pin click<8.3.0 in controller runtime ray install (#9459)
message:
[Core] Pin click<8.3.0 in controller runtime ray install (#9459)

* [Core] Pin click<8.3.0 in controller runtime ray install

click 8.3.0+ breaks Ray CLI on the controller (skypilot-runtime venv) due
to deepcopy failures on Click's Sentinel values:

  ValueError: <object object at 0x...> is not a valid Sentinel
    File ".../site-packages/ray/scripts/scripts.py", line 2440, in <module>
      add_command_alias(up, name="create_or_update", hidden=True)
    File ".../scripts.py", line 2430, in add_command_alias
      new_command = copy.deepcopy(command)

This crashes ray on import, which makes any sky jobs / serve launch on the
controller fail with 'Failed to start ray on the head node'.

The skypilot wheel install pins click<8.2.0 (sky/setup_files/dependencies.py),
but the controller's RAY_INSTALLATION_COMMANDS installs ray *before* the
skypilot wheel and ray 2.9.3 only requires click>=7.0, so uv can resolve
click to 8.3.x. Pin click at the ray-install step, mirroring what was done
for sky_templates/ray/start_cluster (#7985) and pydantic-core (#7611).

See: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/56747

* Force pin click<8.3.0 even when ray install is skipped

The previous commit's pin was bypassed because the SkyPilot-baked AMI
(sky/catalog/images/provisioners/skypilot.sh) installs ray==2.9.3 without
a click constraint, so click 8.3.x ends up baked into the AMI's
~/skypilot-runtime venv. When a controller VM boots from this AMI,
RAY_INSTALLATION_COMMANDS' idempotency guard ('ray==2.9.3 already installed
-> skip') skips the install and leaves the broken click in place.

Fix:
- constants.py: add an unconditional 'uv pip install "click<8.3.0"' before
  the ray guard, so we always downgrade click on existing controllers.
- skypilot.sh: pin click<8.3.0 alongside ray in the AMI provisioner so
  freshly baked images don't ship the broken click in the first place.

* [Plugins] Pin click<8.3.0 in plugin wheel install

Reproduced the buildkite CI failure on a real environment: when a plugin
wheel transitively pulls click>=8.3.0 (or has it as a hard requirement),
'uv pip install <plugin.whl>' silently upgrades click in the controller
runtime venv. ray 2.9.3 then fails to import because click 8.3+'s
Sentinel objects don't survive copy.deepcopy, breaking Ray's
add_command_alias.

This is exactly the AWS smoke-test failure path: the local-dev
controller install (RAY_INSTALLATION_COMMANDS + skypilot wheel) leaves
click at 8.1.8 and ray works, but plugin install runs after and bumps
click to 8.3.3 -> RuntimeError: Failed to start ray on the head node.

Add "click<8.3.0" alongside the plugin install so uv resolves to an
older click instead of upgrading. If a plugin truly hard-pins click>=8.3
the install will fail with a clear error message - that combination
genuinely can't run with ray 2.9.3 anyway.

See: https://github.com/ray-project/ray/issues/56747

* [Controller] Pin click<8.3.0 in cloud-deps install (real buildkite fix)

Reproduced exactly on a fresh venv: 'uv pip install <combined cloud
extras>' with all enabled clouds (aws, azure, gcp, lambda, nebius,
runpod, slurm, kubernetes, ssh) silently upgrades click from 8.1.8 to
8.3.3. The trigger is typer 0.25.0 (transitive dep of fastapi-cli, which
is itself transitive from one of the cloud SDKs): typer 0.25 requires
'click>=8.2.1' with no upper bound, so uv picks the latest = 8.3.3.

After this install completes, any subsequent 'ray ...' on the controller
fails with 'ValueError: ... is not a valid Sentinel' (ray 2.9.3's
add_command_alias does copy.deepcopy on Click commands, which Click 8.3+
breaks). This matches the buildkite log timeline exactly:

subject: [Helm] Add SkyPilot History Grafana dashboard (#9447)
message:
[Helm] Add SkyPilot History Grafana dashboard (#9447)

* [Helm] Add Compute Overview Grafana dashboard

Adds a new cluster-level dashboard with three panels for fleet-wide
GPU tracking:

- Utilization gauge: avg DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL over the selected
  time range
- Allocation gauge: sum of nvidia.com/gpu pod requests / sum of
  allocatable nvidia.com/gpu capacity over the selected time range
- Timeseries: both metrics plotted on a shared 0-100% axis

Thresholds on both gauges: 0-30 red, 30-50 amber, 50-100 green —
higher is better (indicates the fleet is being used / allocated).

The dashboard exposes a hidden `cluster` template var (textbox with
regex `.*`) so external pages can scope via `var-cluster=<name>` in
the URL. Layout is 6x20 gauges on the left + 18x20 timeseries on the
right, mirroring a KPI-style compute overview card.

Tested: helm template, dashboard renders in Grafana with
threshold arcs and dual-line timeseries.

* [Helm] Add GPU pod-request and node-allocatable to federate

Extend the match-patterns set in get_metrics_for_context() to pull
kube-state-metrics series for GPU capacity + demand:

- kube_pod_container_resource_requests filtered to
  resource=~"nvidia.com/gpu|amd.com/gpu"
- kube_node_status_allocatable with the same filter

These are required for fleet-wide GPU-allocation % panels (added in
the compute-overview dashboard in this branch). Without them, the
API server's local Prometheus only sees DCGM utilization — it can't
compute allocation because KSM is not directly scraped.

The federate function adds a `cluster=<context>` label to each
series, so downstream dashboards can filter by cluster via the
existing `$cluster` template var.

Tested: federate response verified to include the two new metrics
when a remote cluster has GPU pods scheduled; allocation gauge
renders data after rollout.

* [Helm] Scrape in-release kube-state-metrics

The chart ships kube-state-metrics as a subchart dependency
(kube-state-metrics.enabled=true in values.yaml) but the Prometheus
server never had a scrape job for it, so kube_pod_container_resource_requests
and kube_node_status_allocatable were never stored. That also meant the
/gpu-metrics federate had nothing to match for those series even after
they were added to the federate match-pattern set.

Add a static scrape target for the KSM service at
{release}-kube-state-metrics.{namespace}.svc.cluster.local:8080. Once
this rolls out, the compute-overview dashboard's Allocation gauge and
timeseries finally have data to plot.

* Revert "[Helm] Scrape in-release kube-state-metrics"

This reverts commit cb8b1a6e33a51f8a27eddb744ab56f992ae2e6f1.

* [Helm] Fix GPU resource label — use nvidia_com_gpu (KSM-sanitized form)

kube-state-metrics sanitizes K8s resource names by replacing '.' and '/'
with '_' when emitting them as Prometheus label values. So the running
series on every cluster is:

    kube_pod_container_resource_requests{resource="nvidia_com_gpu", ...}
    kube_node_status_allocatable{resource="nvidia_com_gpu", ...}

Queries using resource="nvidia.com/gpu" match zero series. The scrape
itself succeeds, which hid the bug — nothing flags "label mismatch".

Fixed locations:
- Federate match patterns in sky/metrics/utils.py (the /gpu-metrics
  endpoint's allowlist) — was silently forwarding zero KSM samples.
- compute-overview-dashboard.json — both the Allocation gauge (panel 2)
  and the stacked-area timeseries (panel 3) queries.

After rollout, the Compute Overview allocation panels should finally
render non-zero values wherever KSM is healthy on the remote cluster.

Note: coreweave-dev's Prometheus is separately stuck on a full PVC
(/data 50G/50G, WAL writes failing). That's a tenant-side recovery,
not part of this change.

* [Helm] Compute Overview: add Power + Temperature stat panels

Adds panels 4 (Power Draw) and 5 (Temperature) to the
skypilot-compute-overview dashboard. Both are Stat panels with
graphMode=area (sparklines behind the big number):

- Panel 4 — Power Draw:
  sum(DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE) / 1000, unit kW, teal #0891B2.
- Panel 5 — Temperature:
  avg(DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP), unit °C,
  thresholds green<65 amber 65-75 red>=75.

Both honor the dashboard's hidden `cluster` template var so external
pages can scope by context via `var-cluster=<name>`.

These replace the left-column Util/Alloc gauge iframes in the Compute
Overview React section — Util/Alloc are already shown in the top
strip, so the gauges were redundant. Power and Temperature trends
are novel and complement the Util/Alloc timeseries next to them.

* [Helm] Blank panel 3 title so React can render it with inline controls

The timeseries panel's title was showing as 'Utilization & Allocation
Over Time' inside the iframe. To let the consumer (feature-plugin's
Compute Overview panel) render its own title+filters on a single row
above the chart, blank the panel title so the iframe header doesn't
duplicate it.

The dashboard still has a meaningful dashboard title; only the
single panel header line is removed.

* [Helm] Compute Overview chart: order Allocation before Utilization

Swap target order in panel 3's timeseries so GPU Allocation is the
first/front series and GPU Utilization is second. Aligns with the
top-strip ring order (Allocation comes before Utilization).

* [Helm] Restore Compute Overview chart title (the React wrapper now uses 'Compute Overview' as its own collapsible-section title)

* [Helm] Reorder chart title and tooltip to Allocation, Utilization

* [Helm] Compute Overview: dedupe duplicate KSM series in allocation math

When two kube-state-metrics instances are scraped on the same cluster
(e.g. coreweave-dev currently has both 'skypilot-prometheus-kube-state-
metrics' and 'skypilot-gpu-view-kube-state-metrics'), the same pods and
nodes are emitted with different 'instance' labels. A naive
sum(kube_pod_container_resource_requests) double-counts.

Symmetry between numerator and denominator is fragile — a single node
briefly disappearing from one KSM (e.g. cordon, scrape failure) blows
the ratio past 100% (saw 108% on rohan dev).

Wrap each side in a 'max by (cluster, namespace, pod, container)' (and
'max by (cluster, node)' for allocatable) before summing. This collapses
duplicate series to a single value per real entity regardless of how
many KSMs report it.

* [Helm] Compute Overview: trim legend to mean only, 1-decimal precision

Drop the lastNotNull calc (the asterisk in 'Last *' was confusing) and
keep just the mean. Add decimals: 1 so values render as XX.X% instead
of full-precision floats.

* [Helm] Rename Compute Overview dashboard to Usage Trends

* [Helm] Rename Usage Trends to Trends

* [Helm] Address review: $datasource var + simplify gauge queries

- Use $datasource template var instead of hardcoded 'prometheus' UID in
  all 6 panel targets, so the dashboard works against any Prometheus
  datasource in the target Grafana instance.
- Drop the redundant avg_over_time(...[$__range:]) wrapper from the
  GPU Utilization and GPU Allocation gauge queries — the gauges already
  use calcs: ['mean'] which averages the range query results, so the
  outer aggregation was double-counting work.
- Update the timeseries panel description: legendFormat is hardcoded so
  the 'in-cluster' note about per-cluster labels was misleading.

* [Helm] Rename Trends dashboard to History

subject: [o11y] Better Kubernetes provisioning failure reasons (#9389)
message:
[o11y] Better Kubernetes provisioning failure reasons (#9389)

* feat(k8s): add _condensed_pod_reason() for single-line failure summaries

Part of SKY-4555: better provisioning failure reasons.

* fix(k8s): clean up redundant exit code in _condensed_pod_reason()

When terminated.reason is None, the old code produced
"exit(137) (exit code 137)". Now returns
"Terminated with exit code 137" instead. Adds a test for this case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(k8s): include condensed failure reason in pod termination exception

Replaces generic 'Pod terminated unexpectedly' with specific reason
(OOMKilled, ImagePullBackOff, preemption, etc.) in KubernetesError.

Part of SKY-4555.

* feat(k8s): carry error reason through retry loop into final message

Stores KubernetesError message as last_error_reason and passes it
through _insufficient_resources_msg() into the ResourcesUnavailableError.

Part of SKY-4555.

* feat: replace provision failure table with block format and hints

Switches from a PrettyTable to block-formatted output that handles
multi-line reasons cleanly. Adds hints for ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled,
and Insufficient resources.

Part of SKY-4555.

* test(k8s): add end-to-end integration tests for provision failure reasons

Verifies OOMKilled and ImagePullBackOff flow from KubernetesError
through the retry loop into block-formatted output with hints.

Part of SKY-4555.

* refactor(k8s): use V1Pod type hint for _condensed_pod_reason

Replaces `Any` with `kubernetes.client.V1Pod` via TYPE_CHECKING guard.
Gives static type checkers visibility into pod fields without triggering
the lazy-loaded kubernetes import at runtime.

Part of SKY-4555.

* fix(k8s): use waiting.reason as error prefix for container failures

The error path for non-init containers in waiting state used waiting.message
but dropped waiting.reason. This meant keywords like "ErrImagePull" never
reached the final output, and the hint map (which keys off those substrings)
couldn't fire. Prefix the message with waiting.reason so category labels
survive to the CLI.

Part of SKY-4555.

* fix(k8s): scope hints to k8s blocks and dedupe sky logs trailer

Two follow-ups from code review:

1. Strip the `Run \`sky logs --provision <cluster>\`` trailer from the
   KubernetesError message. Previously this got embedded in every block
   (once per failing infra) since it flowed through last_error_reason.
   The wrapper already prints `View logs: sky logs --provision` once
   above the blocks via _RESOURCES_UNAVAILABLE_LOG, so the per-block
   repetition was noise.

2. Scope the failure hints to Kubernetes blocks only by checking
   `isinstance(resource.cloud, clouds.Kubernetes)`. The substring
   matcher was too loose (e.g., AWS "InsufficientInstanceCapacity"
   would falsely trigger the k8s `kubectl describe nodes` hint).
   Renamed `_PROVISION_FAILURE_HINTS` → `_KUBERNETES_FAILURE_HINTS`
   and `_get_provision_hint` → `_get_kubernetes_hint` to make the
   scope explicit.

Also tidied a trailing blank line in the block output via rstrip().

Tests:
- Renamed test_no_hint_for_unknown → test_no_hint_for_unknown_k8s_failure
  with a less-fragile generic message.
- Added test_no_hint_for_non_k8s_cloud verifying AWS messages with
  matching substrings don't trigger k8s hints.
- Refactored mock-resource setup into shared helpers.

Part of SKY-4555.

* fix(k8s): improve provision failure formatting and hint quality

Address review feedback on PR #9389:

1. Use textwrap.indent for multi-line reasons in the block format
   (Gemini): the previous f'  {reason}' only indented the first line,
   so multi-line reasons (common for k8s image pull / scheduling
   errors) lost the visual structure.

2. Put the appended Reason on its own line in _insufficient_resources_msg
   (Gemini): improves readability when the error reason is long.

3. Insufficient-resources hint now links the dashboard infra page,
   scoped to the failing context (e.g.,
   <server>/dashboard/infra/<context>), and keeps the
   `kubectl describe nodes` fallback (Michael).

Implementation note: hints can carry a {dashboard_url} placeholder
that _get_kubernetes_hint() substitutes with a context-scoped URL via
server_common.get_dashboard_url. Pattern matches existing dashboard
URL usages in sky/client/cli/command.py.

Tests: added test_hint_for_insufficient_includes_url_and_kubectl,
which monkeypatches get_server_url and asserts both the URL and the
kubectl pointer appear in the hint.

Part of SKY-4555.

* fix(k8s): harden hint placeholder substitution against edge cases

Address two robustness concerns from code review on the prior commit:

1. Use str.replace() instead of str.format() for the {dashboard_url}
   token. .format() would raise on any future hint that contains a
   literal `{...}` (e.g., a YAML/JSON snippet, or a Python f-string
   pattern). .replace() does the single substitution we actually need
   and has no such failure mode.

2. Wrap server_common.get_server_url() / get_dashboard_url() in
   try/except. This is failure-rendering code — if URL resolution
   ever raises (malformed config, surprising env state), we'd swallow
   the original provision error in the renderer, which is exactly the
   bug class this PR is trying to fix. On failure, fall back to
   "the SkyPilot dashboard infra page" so the hint still renders.

Tests: added test_hint_falls_back_when_url_resolution_fails which
makes get_server_url raise and asserts the hint still renders with
the generic fallback string and no leaked {dashboard_url} placeholder.

Part of SKY-4555.

subject: [fusermount-server] Close /dev/fuse fd after passing to client via SCM_RIGHTS (#9463)
message:
[fusermount-server] Close /dev/fuse fd after passing to client via SCM_RIGHTS (#9463)

* [Fuse] Close /dev/fuse fd after passing to client via SCM_RIGHTS

The fusermount-server leaked one /dev/fuse fd per mount operation.
After SendMsg passed the fd to the client (rclone shim), the server's
local copy stayed open. This prevented the kernel from firing
fuse_conn_kill when rclone died (dev_count never reached 0), leaving
FUSE requests wedged in request_wait_answer and making pods
un-killable on `sky down`.

     append "click<8.3.0" to the ray[default]==... pydantic-core==...
     install line. The unconditional pre-install protects controllers
     booting from a SkyPilot AMI where ray is already baked in.
  2. sky/utils/controller_utils.py: add 'click<8.3.0' to

in parallel and race on the same pool: one test sees

and fails its grep assertion; the other test's managed job gets
CANCELLED mid-run when the shared pool is torn down.

Make the example's pool name configurable via BATCH_POOL_NAME env
var (default unchanged for demo users), and have each test pass a
test-unique name so they no longer collide.

``usage_lib.send_heartbeat``: ``cloud``, ``region``, ``zone``,

new fields as ``None`` (env vars unset).

* [Core] Carry user, use_spot, instance_type in heartbeat

Extend the orchestrator-to-skylet env var pattern from the parent commit
to cover three more launch-time fields:

  - SKYPILOT_HEARTBEAT_USER (orchestrator's user hash; the head node has
    no user_hash file of its own and would otherwise generate a fresh
    one)
  - SKYPILOT_HEARTBEAT_USE_SPOT (1/0)
  - SKYPILOT_HEARTBEAT_INSTANCE_TYPE

UsageHeartbeatReportEvent reads these and forwards to send_heartbeat,
which sets the corresponding optional fields on HeartbeatMessageToReport.
All fields default to None — backward compatible with collectors that
only read the existing fields.

This makes the heartbeat self-contained for downstream consumers that
attribute clusters to a launching identity, distinguish on-demand vs
spot, or price by instance_type.

* [Core] Fix mypy: narrow Optional[str] before int() in heartbeat env helpers

the int(value) call in _int_env hits 'incompatible type Optional[str]'.
