subject: [Core] Speed up log download and tailing for large jobs (#9464)
message:
[Core] Speed up log download and tailing for large jobs (#9464)

* [Core] Plumb tail_offset to cluster-side log_lib

Adds tail_offset to log_lib.tail_logs / tail_logs_iter, the gRPC
TailLogsRequest, the codegen path (gated on SKYLET_VERSION 37), and
backend.tail_logs. Older skylets (v<37) keep the existing call
shape — codegen detects the version at runtime.

This makes the dashboard backfill behave correctly at multi-GB scale:
scrolling up now actually fetches a window of older lines instead of
silently re-tailing the same last 5000.

Adds streaming download endpoint:
- POST /download?mode=link returns {zip_id, filename}; the zip is
  prepared on disk and the client navigates to GET /download_zip,
  which streams via FileResponse with Content-Disposition: attachment.
- Dashboard switched to that flow so the browser streams to the OS
  Save dialog instead of buffering the whole zip via resp.blob().
  Multi-GB downloads no longer OOM the tab. CLI keeps using the inline
  POST stream.

* [Jobs] Add tail_offset to /jobs/logs for paginated backfill

Lets the dashboard fetch a fixed-size window of older lines instead of
re-tailing the whole file from EOF on every scroll-up. Used by the
consolidation-mode live-tail UI; bounded server-side work per backfill
regardless of file size.

Behavior is opt-in: tail_offset defaults to None and the existing
collections.deque(f, maxlen=tail) path is unchanged. ManagedJobsService
bumped to v20; older controllers still get the v15 codegen branch.

* [Jobs] Tail managed-job logs via backward seek

The previous `collections.deque(f, maxlen=tail)` approach iterates the
whole file in Python. For a 10 GB log that's ~10 s of CPU per /jobs/logs
request — every dashboard tab open, every backfill scroll-up. The seek
helper reads ~64 KB blocks from EOF until it has enough newlines, so
cost is O(tail × line-length) regardless of file size. Benchmarked on a
1 GB log: 1.04 s -> 0.3 ms.

Same change powers tail_offset: we read tail+offset lines via the same
backward scan, then drop the last offset of them. follow=True still
works because the seek read records EOF position and the follow-loop
seeks there.

Validated with deque cross-checks for tail, tail+offset, files smaller
than tail, files without trailing newline, and lines that span block
boundaries.

* [Core] Tail cluster job logs via backward seek

Same fix as for managed-job controller logs: switch
sky.skylet.log_lib.tail_logs / tail_logs_iter from
collections.deque(f, maxlen=tail) (O(file_size)) to a backward block
read (O(tail * line_length)). On a 1 GB log this is 1.04s -> 0.3ms; for
multi-GB customer logs the dashboard tab open / scroll-up no longer
costs many seconds of cluster CPU per request.

Helper now lives in log_lib so both controller and worker code paths
share it. Result is byte-identical to the deque path for all tail
values (cross-checked on 100K-line files; offset variants verified
separately for the managed-job path).

* [Test] Pin tail_lines_from_end behavior

Cross-checks the seek-based reader against the deque reference for tail
sizes 1..100K and offsets 0..5K, plus edge cases (file smaller than
tail, no trailing newline, lines spanning multiple read blocks, offset
past file, empty file). 23 cases, all green.

* [Dashboard] Retry download_logs poll on Cloudflare 524

For multi-GB running jobs sync_down_managed_job_logs takes minutes
(rsync of the live worker log file). The dashboard's apiClient.fetch
issues a single GET /api/get?request_id=... and throws on any
non-2xx — Cloudflare cuts the request at ~100s with a 524, well
before sync_down completes, so the user sees an immediate error
toast and the download never starts.

Replace the apiClient.fetch wrapper for the download_logs step with
a small loop that re-issues GET /api/get with the SAME request_id on
524/502/503/504. The server's long-poll just resumes waiting; the
work continues in the background queue. follow=False is already set
in sync_down (cloud_vm_ray_backend.py:4913), so the call does
terminate — we just need to keep waiting through edge timeouts.

* [Server] Stream managed-job log downloads inline

Replace the rsync-then-zip-then-serve flow with direct streaming so
the user sees the OS save dialog immediately:

  1. POST /jobs/logs (tail=0, follow=false) dispatches the existing
     streaming tail_logs path. The codegen runs on the controller and
     pipes worker bytes back over SSH/gRPC into the request's
     log_path file as they arrive.
  2. Browser navigates (<a download>) to GET /api/stream with the new
     download=<filename> query param. The endpoint adds
     Content-Disposition: attachment, forces plain text, and serves
     the request log_path as it grows.

Net effect for a multi-GB running job: bytes start flowing within a
second instead of minutes, no temp zip on disk, no memory pressure
from buffering the whole zip in JS.

* [Server] Gzip-stream log downloads inline

Text logs compress 10-30x, so a 5 GB run.log download becomes
~200-500 MB on the wire. /api/stream gains a compress=gz query
param that wraps the chunk iterator in a streaming gzip compressor
(payload-encoding, not transport — the browser saves the .gz file
verbatim instead of decompressing on the way down).

Dashboard download button now uses compress=gz; the saved file ends
in .log.gz. macOS Finder and most Linux file managers auto-extract;
`gunzip foo.log.gz` works everywhere.

* [CLI] Default --tail to 1000 lines for log commands

Both `sky logs` (cluster) and `sky jobs logs` (managed) defaulted to
fetching the entire log file, which means a multi-GB run.log dumps
to the terminal and takes minutes to transfer. Most invocations are
'what's the tail look like?' — fetching 1000 lines covers that case
in <1s.

  - `sky [jobs] logs <id>`: now tails last 1000 lines.
  - `sky [jobs] logs --tail 0 <id>` or `--tail -1 <id>`: full log,
    matching the previous default.
  - `sky [jobs] logs --tail N <id>`: last N lines (unchanged).

Side effect: removes the 'tail must be non-negative' check on
`sky jobs logs` — -1 is now a valid alias for 0 (= all).

* [CLI] Streaming gzipped sync-down for managed jobs

`sky jobs logs --sync-down` now tries the streaming /api/stream
path first, saving a .log.gz file. For RUNNING jobs this avoids
the rsync of the entire worker log to the API server's tmp dir
before bytes can flow back, and gzip cuts a multi-GB log to a few
hundred MB on the wire.

Falls back to the existing sync-down (rsync) path when the
streaming download yields zero bytes — that happens for terminal
jobs whose worker cluster is already torn down (the underlying
tail_logs has no source). The fallback path also handles errors
gracefully (e.g., older API server without /api/stream gzip
support).

The dispatched /jobs/logs response body is drained on a background
thread; cancelling/closing it would tell the server the client
disconnected and the running tail_logs task would be killed
mid-stream, leaving /api/stream with only a partial log.

* [CLI] Sniff Content-Type before naming streaming sync-down

FastAPI silently drops unknown query params, so an older API server
without the compress=gz handler would return plain text — saved under
a .gz filename, the user's gunzip would fail. Pick the extension based
on the Content-Type header (application/gzip → .log.gz, else .log).

* [Dashboard] Add jobs.detail.logs and jobs.detail.controllerlogs plugin slots

The job detail page's Logs and Controller Logs tabs are now
PluginSlot-wrapped, so a plugin can fully replace the default
LogFilter-based panel with a custom log viewer (e.g. a live-tailing
implementation). When no plugin is registered, the existing rendering
runs unchanged via the slot's `fallback`.

Also gates the OSS useLogStreamer with `usePluginComponents` so plugin
overrides do not pay for a redundant fetch.

Default behavior is unchanged for OSS users.

* [Dashboard] Hide "Logs are not streaming" hint when plugin owns slot

When a plugin component is registered for jobs.detail.logs (or
jobs.detail.controllerlogs), the plugin owns log rendering and may be
streaming live — the OSS "(Logs are not streaming; click refresh ...)"
hint is then both misleading and visually competes with the plugin's
own status badge. Hide it conditionally; OSS users with no plugin
registered see the same UI as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Dashboard] Move Logs section above Telemetry / Infra Nodes

Users opening a job page expect to see the live tail at the top —
they're typically here to watch progress, not the GPU/CPU
telemetry panel. Hoist the Logs section to render right under the
job-summary cards (and the Tasks table for multi-task jobs), then
Telemetry, Infra Nodes, Events, Controller Logs in that order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Dashboard] Loading state for log download buttons

Clicking the download icon previously gave no feedback — the button
stayed plain while the server zipped up the logs, then a moment
later the file appeared in the browser's download bar. Users
naturally re-clicked thinking nothing happened.

Track in-flight state for both the per-task Logs download and the
Controller-Logs download. While downloading: disable the button,
swap the icon to a small CircularProgress spinner, and update the
tooltip to "Preparing zip… download will start shortly". Re-enable
once the promise settles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Dashboard] Pass onNodesExtracted into jobs.detail.logs slot context

Plugins that own the logs slot replace the OSS useLogStreamer, so OSS
no longer parses chunks for `(head|workerN, ...` prefixes — the
"All Nodes" dropdown above the log pane stays empty regardless of
what's streaming. Forward the same `onNodesExtracted` callback the
OSS streamer used to receive into the plugin context, letting the
plugin populate the dropdown by parsing its own stream.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Dashboard] Add jobs.detail.downloadbutton plugin slot

Wraps both download buttons (Logs section + Controller Logs section)
in PluginSlot. OSS default behavior is unchanged — falls back to the
existing zip-via-/download_zip flow which works for both running and
terminal jobs.

Plugins can register a richer handler (streaming, gzip, status-aware
fallback) at this slot without OSS rebuilds. Reverts the
streaming/gzip/terminal-fallback logic that briefly lived in
downloadManagedJobLogs back to the simple zip flow — that logic now
lives in the consolidation_optimizer plugin.

* [Dashboard] Branch download path on job status

The streaming /jobs/logs path only works for RUNNING jobs — once a
managed job reaches a terminal state, the worker cluster is auto-down
and tail_logs has no source to read from, so /api/stream returns an
empty file (just rich-payload boilerplate).

Pass the job's status into downloadManagedJobLogs and:
  - Running / starting / recovering: use the new streaming path so
    the OS save dialog appears within ~1s of click.
  - Terminal (succeeded / failed / cancelled): fall back to the
    sync_down -> zip -> /download_zip path. sync_down reads the
    cached log that was synced to the controller before the worker
    was torn down. With the recent retry-on-524 logic, this still
    works for multi-GB historic logs.

* [Dashboard] Fix jobData not-defined in ControllerLogsSection

The jobs.detail.downloadbutton plugin slot context referenced
`jobData` from the outer JobDetailPage scope, which is not in
scope inside ControllerLogsSection (it receives `detailJobData`
instead). Triggered a 'ReferenceError: jobData is not defined' on
the job detail page render.

Use detailJobData?.status — the per-job record already passed in.

* [Server] Drop /download_zip and mode=link branch

These were added alongside the streaming-download primitives but only
benefit dashboards that want a single-shot link; the OSS dashboard's
managed-job download reverts to the plain blob+createObjectURL pattern
that cluster-jobs already uses. Skips the dual-API surface (sync_down
+ /download_zip) that the OSS managed-job flow no longer relies on.

Also fix tail_logs_iter signature to accept tail_offset (lost in a
cherry-pick conflict resolution).

* [CLI] Stderr hint when default --tail is truncating

Print a one-line stderr hint when 'sky logs' / 'sky jobs logs' would
truncate output to the new 1000-line default. Suppressed when the user
explicitly passed --tail (any value, including 0/-1) so existing
pipelines stay quiet.

Also fix 'sky jobs logs --sync-down' to silently treat the default
--tail as 'all'. Without this the new default would raise a
UsageError on every existing 'sky jobs logs --sync-down <id>'
invocation that didn't pass --tail.

* [CI] Fix unit tests, pylint, prettier, regen reference docs

- Update test_cli_jobs_logs_tail.py to match new --tail semantics:
  default 1000 truncates (was 0=all), --tail 0/-1 means all, mock
  download_logs_streaming so sync-down fallback exercises legacy path.
- sky/server/server.py: hoist 'import zlib' to module top-level
  (pylint C0415); silence W0621 redefined-outer-name on the /api/stream
  download query param (URL contract requires the literal name).
- sky/dashboard: prettier-format jobs.jsx and [job].js.
- agent/skills/skypilot/references/cli-reference.md: regen for new
  --tail default + help text.

* [Cleanup] Apply review findings: bug fixes + dead code removal

- /download: BackgroundTasks().add_task(...) returned None, so the
  prepared zip was never deleted after download (disk leak). Use
  starlette.background.BackgroundTask (singular) instead.
- download_logs_streaming: drop the leaky _JobLogStreamingEmptyError
  exception (private class crossing module boundary forced the CLI
  caller to use # pylint: disable=protected-access). Return None
  instead to signal 'empty stream, fall back'; CLI checks for None.
- _is_default_tail: replace 'except Exception' with a hasattr guard
  for click<8 ParameterSource. Real bugs in the call now surface
  instead of silently disabling the hint.
- /api/stream filename: replace ad-hoc replace().replace().replace()
  + UTF-8-unsafe truncation with re.sub(r'[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+', '_').
  Prevents CRLF header injection via download=foo%0d%0aX-Injected.
- [job].js: remove dead controllerDownloading state + the unused
  downloadControllerLogsZip function (controller download is owned
  by ControllerLogsSection's own state).
- jobs.jsx: 524-retry loop adds linear backoff capped at 5s so a
  502/503 hiccup doesn't hammer back-to-back.

* [Jobs] Use backward-seek tail in stream_logs_by_id

The terminal-job dashboard log loader was 10+ s for multi-GB cancelled
jobs because stream_logs_by_id used collections.deque(f, maxlen=tail)
to keep the last 200 lines — that scans the entire cached log file.
The new tail_lines_from_end (already used by log_lib.tail_logs) reads
backward in 64 KB blocks, making the same call milliseconds.

Net: cancelled-job /jobs/logs goes from ~10 s to <100 ms on the
dashboard's first paint.

* [CI] Drop unused Deque/TextIO imports from jobs/utils.py

* [CLI] Drop _is_default_tail; use None/'all' for tail sentinel

Replace the click.ParameterSource gymnastics with a simpler contract:
- --tail not given (= None at the handler) → apply 1000 default and
  print a one-line stderr hint that truncation is in effect.
- --tail all (string) / 0 / -1 → 'no limit' (None at the SDK).
- --tail N (positive int) → that count.

Implemented via a Click callback that normalizes the str/int value at
parse time. Removes the helper functions and inlines the hint.

Behavior preserved:
- sync-down with default --tail still silently means 'all' (no break
  for existing 'sky jobs logs --sync-down <id>').
- sync-down with explicit positive --tail still raises UsageError.

* [CLI] Type hints for _parse_tail callback

* [Test] Update smoke tests for new --tail semantics

- --tail -1 / 0 / 'all' are now valid synonyms for 'no limit'; the
  smoke test that expected --tail -1 to be rejected as 'non-negative
  integer' now uses --tail xyz (non-numeric) instead.
- Default --tail (no flag) is 1000 lines, not 0; on a 20-line log
  both still return all 20 — comment updated to match the new
  semantics.

* [CLI] Dedup --tail option + accurate error message

Review follow-ups:
- Extract _tail_option(verb) decorator + _apply_default_tail() helper
  so 'sky logs' and 'sky jobs logs' share the --tail surface and the
  default-applies-with-stderr-hint logic. Future tweaks (e.g. accept
  human-friendly counts like '1k') touch one place.
- _parse_tail error message said 'must be a non-negative integer or
  "all"' but the function accepts any int <= 0 as 'all'. Update the
  message to 'must be an integer or "all"' so it matches behavior;
  test + smoke-test grep updated to match.

* [Review] Address CR comments: codegen indent bug, gzip eof, version

Three real bugs flagged by reviewer + a version-check + a CLI nit.

1. sky/skylet/job_lib.py — JobLibCodeGen.tail_logs joins entries
   with ';' in _build, so the post-tail status check + sys.exit got
   pasted onto the same physical line as the last 'else:' suite line
   and were absorbed into the else branch. Net: when SKYLET_VERSION
   < 37 (old skylet), the if-branch ran tail_logs(...) and silently
   fell off the end without sys.exit — the exit code was always 0
   regardless of job status. Fix: prepend '\n' to the post-tail
   entries (the same pattern already used for tail_logs_call) so
   they reset out of the else block.

2. sky/server/server.py — /api/stream gzip wrapper had two bugs:
   (a) yielded compressor.flush() from a finally block; PEP 525
   forbids yielding while GeneratorExit is propagating, so every
   client cancel raised 'async generator ignored GeneratorExit'.
   (b) gzip framing always emits ~10-20 bytes even on an empty
   source stream, which defeated the SDK's bytes_written == 0
   fallback for terminal jobs. Track 'saw_payload' and skip the
   trailer entirely on empty input; move the flush yield out of
   finally so it only fires on natural EOF.

3. sky/jobs/utils.py — managed_job_version cutoff was '< 20' but
   we bumped MANAGED_JOBS_VERSION to 21; should be '< 21'.

4. sky/client/cli/command.py — drop the 'all' string sentinel for
   --tail; just '0' (or any non-positive int) means all lines, and
   we use -1 internally as the no-flag sentinel. Simpler. Also
   collapse the now-trivial _parse_tail callback into a plain
   default=-1 + type=int.

* [CLI] Don't streaming-first --sync-down (output shape regression)

The streaming variant of sync-down (download_logs_streaming) produces
a single .log.gz file, whereas the legacy download_logs returns a
directory of per-task logs. Scripts and our smoke test
(test_managed_jobs_logs_sync_down) depend on the directory shape —
they do '[ -d $path ]' and 'cat $path/controller.log'.

Revert the CLI sync-down branch to always use download_logs. The
streaming SDK function stays exported for users who want the gzipped
.log.gz file directly via sky.jobs.download_logs_streaming(...).

* [Review] Marker-filter on tail path + drop _tail_option verb arg

- sky/jobs/utils.py:stream_logs_by_id: my earlier change to use
  tail_lines_from_end set start_streaming=True unconditionally for
  the tail>0 path, bypassing the LOG_FILE_START_STREAMING_AT marker
  filter that hides Ray INFO boilerplate. With the new --tail 1000
  default this leaks pre-marker lines into output, breaking smoke
  tests that 'head -n2 | grep "Waiting for"'. Apply the same
  _should_stream_the_whole_tail_lines heuristic that
  log_lib.tail_logs_iter uses.
- sky/client/cli/command.py: drop verb param on _tail_option per
  reviewer nit; both 'logs' and 'jobs logs' now share a single
  _TAIL_OPTION constant with 'print the entire log' verb.

* [CI] Pylint disable on bare-raise + regen reference docs

* [CLI] --no-follow defaults --tail to all (snapshot mode)

The --tail 1000 default was too aggressive for snapshot mode: scripts
running 'sky jobs logs --no-follow | grep <marker>' for markers near
the start of the log got truncated output and the grep failed
(test_managed_jobs_inline_env, test_job_group_primary_auxiliary, and
several other smoke tests).

Differentiate by mode: live-tail (--follow, default) keeps the 1000
cap so opening a multi-GB log doesn't dump the whole thing upfront;
snapshot mode (--no-follow) reverts to all-lines so existing
grep-based scripts continue to work.

* [CI] Move pylint disable to except line

* [CLI] download_logs_streaming: client-side gunzip + dir-shape output

Re-enable streaming-first --sync-down with output that matches
legacy download_logs:

- Decompress gzipped chunks on the client via
  zlib.decompressobj(16 + zlib.MAX_WBITS) (gzip mode), so the saved
  file is plain text. Wire bandwidth still benefits from gzip;
  on-disk we hand the user a regular .log file.
- Save into a per-job directory <managed_jobs/managed-{controller|job}-
  {label}>/{controller.log|run.log} so callers walking the path with
  '[ -d ]' / 'cat <path>/controller.log' (the smoke tests) keep
  working unchanged.
- Empty stream now also rmdir's the per-job directory before
  returning None.
- Drop the 'job_id is None and name is None' guard — the server's
  /jobs/logs handler already resolves to the latest job, so this
  case is valid and lets sync-down without --name/--job-id stream
  too.

subject: [Test] Bump test_cancel_pytorch wait-for-RUNNING timeout 150s -> 360s (#9496)
message:
[Test] Bump test_cancel_pytorch wait-for-RUNNING timeout 150s -> 360s (#9496)

[Test] Bump test_cancel_pytorch RUNNING-wait timeout 150s -> 360s

The test waits up to 150s for job 1 to leave SETTING_UP after `sky launch
-d` returns. The setup script downloads ~1.7GB (torch==1.12.1+cu113 wheel)
plus ~170MB (CIFAR-10) on each of 2 g4dn.xlarge nodes. On healthy AWS
instances setup completes in ~28s and the wait detects RUNNING at ~35s,
but on slower instances (cold EBS / noisy neighbor / transient PyPI
slowness) setup can exceed 150s and the test times out.

This is genuine flake: same commit, same code, same instance type — two
back-to-back attempts can fail at 150s and a third sail through at 35s.
The outer Test(timeout=20*60) easily absorbs the larger per-step budget.

Diagnosed by SSHing into a passing retry's cluster on smoke-tests/10174
and timing the actual setup (28s) and downloads (pytorch wheel 71 MB/s,
cifar-10 52 MB/s) — bottleneck is per-instance variability, not network.

subject: [Dashboard] Stabilize settings header and allow extending Tailwind content paths (#9497)
message:
[Dashboard] Stabilize settings header and allow extending Tailwind content paths (#9497)

* [Dashboard] Stabilize settings header and allow extending Tailwind content paths

Two related fixes in sky/dashboard/.

1. Settings header alignment (src/components/config.js). The API Server
   settings header clamps its row to h-5 (20px) and centers content with
   flex items-center. The 16px title rendered with default text-base
   line-height (24px) is taller than the 20px row, so the title sits
   clipped above its natural baseline. Right-side controls (loading
   spinner, action buttons) mount one frame after the title; as the row
   grows from 20px to ~38px, the title is re-centered downward, producing
   a visible post-paint vertical shift.

   This pins the row to h-8 (32px), adds leading-none to the title span
   so it renders at exactly 16px, and shrinks the "View API Server
   Metrics" button from py-2 (~38px) to h-8 (32px) so it fits without
   bleed. Title position is stable from first paint.

2. Tailwind content extension hook (tailwind.config.js). Tailwind purges
   any utility class not referenced inside a path matched by the content
   array. Today the dashboard scans only its own source tree. Builds that
   bundle external React source alongside the dashboard lose any utility
   class used only outside this tree -- those classes are purged from the
   compiled CSS, leaving the external UI unstyled.

   This adds SKYPILOT_DASHBOARD_TAILWIND_CONTENT: a comma-separated list
   of glob patterns appended to content at config-load time. Empty by
   default, so behavior is unchanged for users not bundling external
   sources.

Tested: visited /dashboard/settings/config; "SkyPilot API Server" title
appears immediately at a fixed vertical position and does not shift when
the loading spinner or action buttons render. Verified
title.getBoundingClientRect().top is constant at 32px from first frame
through settle (was 35px, shifting to 32px at ~30ms).
Verified npm run build with the env var unset produces a CSS bundle
byte-identical to pre-change. Verified
SKYPILOT_DASHBOARD_TAILWIND_CONTENT='../my-extra/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx}'
npm run build picks up classes referenced only in ../my-extra/.

* [Dashboard] Fix prettier format

* Update sky/dashboard/tailwind.config.js

subject: [Dashboard] Don't cache error responses on /dashboard/_next paths (#9498)
message:
[Dashboard] Don't cache error responses on /dashboard/_next paths (#9498)

* [Dashboard] Don't cache error responses on /dashboard/_next paths

CacheControlStaticMiddleware sets Cache-Control: max-age=3600 on every
response under /dashboard/_next, including 4xx/5xx. When an upstream
auth middleware returns 401 for a static asset request from an
unauthenticated browser, a CDN in front of the API server will cache
that 401 for the full TTL on the asset URL. Subsequent authenticated
requests for the same fingerprinted URL hit the cached 401, the browser
refuses to interpret JSON as CSS/JS, and the dashboard breaks for all
users until the CDN cache expires.

Only attach the cacheable Cache-Control header to 2xx responses; for
non-2xx, set Cache-Control: no-store so CDNs and browsers cannot cache
auth failures or other transient errors on static asset paths.

* Address review: keep 304 cacheable

Use status_code >= 400 to identify error responses instead of
narrowing to 2xx. This preserves Cache-Control: max-age=3600 on
304 Not Modified responses, which are common when a browser or
CDN revalidates a previously cached static asset and should not
trigger no-store (which can purge an otherwise valid cache entry).

* Set Cache-Control: no-store on auth-middleware 401 responses

Auth middlewares (BasicAuthMiddleware, BearerTokenMiddleware) sit
outside CacheControlStaticMiddleware in the middleware stack, so
their short-circuit 401 responses for /dashboard/_next/* paths
never reach the cache middleware on the way out. Without an
explicit Cache-Control header, a CDN can apply its default
static-extension cache TTL to the 401, poisoning the dashboard
for all subsequent users.

Set Cache-Control: no-store directly on these 401 responses, and
update CacheControlStaticMiddleware to respect any Cache-Control
header already set by downstream rather than overriding it.

subject: [Core] Make usage_lib.messages per-context (#9503)
message:
[Core] Make usage_lib.messages per-context (#9503)

[Core][Jobs] Make usage_lib.messages per-context

Wrap the module-level MessageCollection in a ContextVar-backed proxy so
each contextvars Context lazily gets its own instance. Concurrent async
tasks — e.g. JobController coroutines that share a process — no longer
stomp on shared message state.

Existing call sites continue to use ``usage_lib.messages.usage.foo``
unchanged; the proxy forwards reads and writes to the MessageCollection
associated with the current Context. Synchronous callers in the same
Context still share one collection.

Forward the request's SKYPILOT_USAGE_RUN_ID into the controller's env
file via controller_utils.controller_only_vars_to_fill, so the
controller process inherits the client's run id and the per-context
MessageCollection picks it up at lazy init time.

Add usage_lib.install_fresh_messages_for_current_context() and call it
from sky.jobs.controller.run_job_loop after the per-job env file is
loaded into the JobController's ctx. This is required because class-body
decorators (``@usage_lib.messages.usage.update_runtime('provision')`` in
sky/backends/backend.py) trigger lazy MessageCollection creation at
module import time, against the controller subprocess's startup env;
without an explicit reset, every JobController coroutine would inherit
that one MessageCollection and its run id. The helper also clears the
request-level cache so the freshly-initialized UsageMessageToReport's
``__init__`` re-reads identity fields from the (now-overridden) env,
mirroring the order ``server.common.reload_for_new_request`` already
uses.

Tested:
- New unit tests in tests/unit_tests/test_sky/usage/test_usage_lib.py
  cover lazy creation idempotency, isolation between concurrent
  @contextual_async coroutines, scoped reset, the collection protocol
  surface, and install_fresh_messages_for_current_context.
- New tests in tests/unit_tests/test_controller_utils.py verify the
  client's run id is forwarded into controller_envs and that an unset
  run id is not propagated as an empty string.
- End-to-end: launched two concurrent managed jobs in consolidation
  mode with distinct SKYPILOT_USAGE_RUN_ID values; each worker
  cluster's ~/.sky/usage_run_id file ended up with the correct
  per-job value.

message:
[Test] Skip batch tests on shared API server pipelines (#9507)

The batch tests all run `sky jobs pool apply`. On the shared GKE
nightly pipeline the API server pod is small (4GB), and in
consolidation mode that caps concurrent services at 1. Multiple
Buildkite jobs run in parallel against the same shared API server,
so they race for that single slot — whoever calls `pool apply`
first wins and the others fail with `RuntimeError: Max number of
services reached: 1/1` (presented as `Failed to wait for pool
initialization`).

In nightly build #25209242019, build 328 had:
- test_batch_custom_formats — 4/4 attempts failed
- test_batch_cancel — 3/3 attempts failed

Mark all four batch tests as `no_remote_server` so they only run on
pipelines with a per-test API server. The marker also skips
`--env-file` runs whose env file contains `api_server` config (i.e.
the shared-gke pipeline).

Mirrors the equivalent note in tests/smoke_tests/test_pools.py for
the pool tests that hit the same constraint.

subject: [CI Fix] test_cli_auto_retry: track progress for non-resumable streams (#9506)
message:
[CI Fix] test_cli_auto_retry: track progress for non-resumable streams (#9506)

* [CI Fix] Fix test_cli_auto_retry: track progress for non-resumable streams

Two bugs caused all 6 variants of test_cli_auto_retry to fail in nightly
(aws/kubernetes/dependency/jobs-consolidation/remote-server/shared-gke):

1. Pattern A (ChunkedEncodingError on `sky jobs logs --controller`):
   `retry_transient_errors` detects forward progress between attempts
   by comparing `RetryContext.line_processed`, which only stream_response
   updates when `resumable=True`. After PR #9449 added a default
   `--tail 1000` for managed-job log streaming, `tail_logs` calls
   stream_response with `resumable=False`, so line_processed never
   advances and the consecutive-failure counter never resets. Three
   chaos-proxy disconnects in a row exhaust the retries and the CLI
   fails despite the stream making real forward progress.

   Fix: introduce `RetryContext.progress_count`, a monotonic counter
   incremented per streamed line by stream_response and
   stream_response_async regardless of `resumable`. The retry decorator
   now uses progress_count for forward-progress detection. line_processed
   keeps its original meaning (high-water mark used to skip
   already-printed lines on resumable retries).

2. Pattern B (ApiServerConnectionError on `sky launch`):
   The chaos proxy is launched with `&` and the next sky command runs
   immediately. On slower CI workers, the first sky command races the
   proxy startup and fails before any connection ever establishes.

   Fix: in the smoke test, wait until the proxy port is reachable
   before kicking off `sky launch`.

Adds unit tests:
- test_stream_response_non_resumable_reports_progress: verifies
  progress_count is bumped per streamed line in non-resumable mode.
- test_progress_via_line_processed_alone_does_not_reset: regression
  guard ensuring the decorator no longer keys off line_processed.

Buildkite failure: https://buildkite.com/skypilot-1/smoke-tests/builds/10200#019de34c-ba7a-4a7e-a97a-5ba7e7777af3
Classification: UNKNOWN
Confidence: MEDIUM

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

- Add `test_stream_response_resumable_retry_skips_replayed_lines`:
  end-to-end test combining `retry_transient_errors` with
  `stream_response(resumable=True)`. First attempt prints lines 1-2 then
  raises ChunkedEncodingError; on retry the server replays from line 1
  and the client must skip already-printed lines via `line_processed`.
  Verifies no duplicate output and that both `line_processed` and

  - `stream_response` (sync + async): drop redundant

subject: [Dashboard] Persist layout settle state across LayoutContent remounts (#9505)
message:
[Dashboard] Persist layout settle state across LayoutContent remounts (#9505)

[Dashboard] Persist pluginsSettled across LayoutContent remounts

LayoutContent guards initial render with a `pluginsSettled` state, gated to
`true` by the navigation-ready / plugins-loaded events (or a 1 s timer). On
the first commit, `pluginsSettled` is `false`, and the component renders a
blank `<div className="min-h-screen bg-gray-50" />` until one of the unblock
signals fires.

That state lives entirely inside the component instance. If a plugin uses
PluginWrapperSlot to register an app-level wrapper component (slot:
'app.providers') after first mount, the wrapper insertion changes the tree
shape at PluginWrapperSlot's child position -- React unmounts and remounts
the descendant subtree, including Layout. The fresh LayoutContent re-enters
the gate at `pluginsSettled = false` and renders the gray div again until
the timer or events fire a second time.

Visible result on hard refresh: page paints, briefly flashes bg-gray-50
(~150 ms), then the page paints again.

Persist `pluginsSettled` on a window flag once it's true, and read it back
in useState's lazy initializer on each mount. After the first settle, any
remount of LayoutContent skips the gate immediately and renders directly,
without a second flash.

Tested: in a build with a plugin that registers an `app.providers` wrapper,
hard-refreshed /dashboard/settings/notifications and instrumented the
iframe-loaded DOM to sample every animation frame. Before the change, the
empty `bg-gray-50` div appears twice (at ~30 ms and again ~300 ms after
LayoutContent remounts) with the page rendering between and after. After
the change, the gate appears once and the page renders without a second
flash. With no app.providers wrapper registered, behavior is unchanged --
gate appears once at first paint and clears on the navigation-ready event.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Core] Turn silent launch misconfigurations into explicit errors (#9423)
message:
[Core] Turn silent launch misconfigurations into explicit errors (#9423)

* [Core] Reject obviously-invalid disk_size / accelerator count / --num-jobs

Three user-facing validation gaps where a misconfiguration was either
silently accepted or surfaced as a misleading downstream error:

- disk_size <= 0 was accepted by `Resources.__init__` and only failed
  at provision time (often with a generic cloud-API error). Add an
  explicit positive-integer check alongside the existing parse step.

- Accelerator counts of zero or negative numbers ('V100:0', {V100: -1})
  reached the optimizer and produced an unhelpful
  "Catalog does not contain any resource satisfying ..." message; on
  Kubernetes it could launch a pod with zero GPUs. Reject the value
  at parse time with a message naming the bad accelerator entry.

- `sky jobs launch --num-jobs 0 / -N` was accepted silently; the
  controller later handed back a confusing "0 jobs submitted" state.
  Enforce `>= 1` as a click UsageError before reaching the server.

Also split comma-separated `--ports` entries (e.g. '8000,9000') into
individual tokens before validation so the common CLI form is accepted
and a mixed list '8000,9000,abc' reports 'abc' as the bad entry
instead of echoing the full string as a single invalid port range.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Validate file inputs and reject empty tasks

Three user-facing gaps where a misconfiguration was either accepted
silently (and the user learned about it only after provisioning) or
surfaced as a confusing downstream error:

- `--env-file` / `--secret-file` wrapped `dotenv.dotenv_values` directly.
  That function returns {} when the path does not exist, so a typo'd
  path was silently equivalent to passing no env file at all. Route
  both flags through a small wrapper that errors up-front if the path
  is not a file, with a message that names the path.

- `file_mounts` with a relative remote destination (e.g.
  `file_mounts: {relative/path: /etc/hosts}`) used to be stored
  verbatim and later produce unintuitive behavior on the remote node
  because cloud storage semantics also assume absolute paths. Reject
  non-absolute destinations with a targeted error that names the path
  and tells the user to prefix it with `/`. Cloud-store URIs
  (`s3://...`) continue to be accepted.

- `Task.validate_run` now also fails when both `run` and `setup` are
  empty/None. An otherwise-empty task previously launched a cluster
  or managed-job controller that had nothing to execute, wasting
  cloud resources before the user noticed. Setup-only tasks (useful
  for pre-warming environments) remain valid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Harden YAML parsing for launch/jobs launch

Three failure modes where a malformed task YAML produced either silent
wrong behavior or a raw Python traceback:

- Duplicate YAML keys were silently accepted (PyYAML default: later
  value wins). A repeated `name:` or two `/remote:` entries in
  `file_mounts:` would drop the earlier value and mask the real typo.
  Add `yaml_utils.check_no_duplicate_keys` that walks the YAML node
  graph with `yaml.compose_all` and raises a ValueError naming the
  duplicate key and the two line numbers. Call it from
  `Task.from_yaml_str` and `dag_utils.load_chain_dag_from_yaml` so
  both single-task and pipeline YAMLs are covered.

- A non-UTF-8 (e.g. binary) file passed as an entrypoint leaked a raw
  `UnicodeDecodeError` traceback from deep inside PyYAML. Catch the
  error explicitly in `_check_yaml_only` and in the chain DAG loader,
  surfacing a clear "file is not valid UTF-8" message.

- A YAML file containing only `null`, an empty body, or `---\n---`
  previously produced an internal
  `AssertionError: If you see this, please file an issue; tasks: []`
  because `_load_chain_dag` returned an empty DAG and the CLI
  unpacked `dag.tasks[0]` unconditionally. Reject the empty-document
  case at the DAG-load layer with a targeted error that tells the
  user to add at least a `run:` field.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Address review feedback on launch-validation-hardening

Three corrections from the review of #9423:

- Empty-task check: downgrade from hard error in `validate_run()` to a
  one-time warning in `from_yaml_config`. Rejecting empty tasks at
  `validate()` time broke legitimate workflows that construct a Task
  programmatically with no run/setup (e.g. `sky launch -c mycluster`
  to pre-provision a bare cluster, or YAMLs with only `resources:` set
  to spin up a typed cluster). The warning still nudges users whose
  pipeline YAML split into an empty trailing document, which was the
  motivating case.

- `_validate_mount_dest_is_absolute`: replace `os.path.isabs()` with an
  explicit `path.startswith(('/', '~'))` check. `os.path.isabs` uses
  the host OS's rules (on Windows, 'C:/foo' is absolute) but the remote
  side is always POSIX. Also accept paths starting with `~` as a
  shorthand for the remote home directory, matching the existing
  examples in the `Task` docstring.

- `validate_run`: the empty-task guard previously called `.strip()` on
  `self.run` before the isinstance check — safe today because `run`
  must be a string, but fragile if callable-run support is ever
  enabled. Removed along with the downgrade above.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Harden duplicate-key walker against edge-case YAML

Follow-up from code review of #9423. Three small robustness
improvements to the duplicate-key detection added in the previous
commit, plus a couple of test/type cleanups:

- `check_no_duplicate_keys` previously assumed all mapping keys were

  so SkyPilot schemas (which only use scalar keys) keep full coverage

  walker.

  (unclosed quote, etc.). Previously that exception leaked before the
  regular `safe_load` error path could fire. Swallow it in
  `check_no_duplicate_keys` so the user-facing parse error comes from
  the main loader, not from our duplicate-detection helper.

  original audit bug was specifically that `--gpus H100:0` on k8s
  launched a zero-GPU pod, and the existing test only exercised the
  AWS path.

  'UTF-8' wording and the file path, rather than an `or` clause that
  could pass on unrelated errors.

subject: [Dashboard] Default Managed Jobs table sort to ID descending (#9522)
message:
[Dashboard] Default Managed Jobs table sort to ID descending (#9522)

The Managed Jobs table previously used the API default sort
(submitted_at desc). When many jobs are submitted within the same second
(batch submissions, load tests, etc.), the secondary order from Postgres
is non-deterministic, so paging through the table can show ID 1533 next
to ID 1535 next to ID 1532 — confusing and hard to scan.

Sort by ID descending by default to give a stable, monotonically
decreasing scan that matches what users get after a single click on the
ID column header. Manually clicking a different column still works.

subject: [Dashboard] Skip unpaginated full-jobs preload when pagination plugin loaded (#9532)
message:
[Dashboard] Skip unpaginated full-jobs preload when pagination plugin loaded (#9532)

* [Dashboard] Skip unpaginated full-jobs preload when pagination plugin loaded

cachePreloader.preloadForPage('jobs') registers getManagedJobs via the
client-side wrapper getManagedJobsWithClientPagination, which fetches
the entire job set unpaginated and slices client-side. With a
server-side pagination plugin in play (window.__skyJobsPaginationFetch),
the Managed Jobs table reads its own paginated cache through that
plugin and never touches the wrapper's cache entry — so the wrapper's
26-second / 110 MB fetch on a 50k-row backend is wasted work, and it
also saturates the executor pool so subsequent page-click fetches sit
in queue behind it. Net symptom: at scale, "Showing 1-10 of 50022"
flips to "11-20 of 50022" instantly while the rendered rows hang on
page 1 for many seconds.

Skip the entry in both _loadPageData (foreground) and
_backgroundPreloadOtherPages (background-from-other-pages) when
window.__skyJobsPaginationFetch is present. Falls through to the
existing behavior when the plugin is absent, so OSS deployments without
the pagination plugin keep the warm cache.

subject: [Core] Add extension points for managed-job runtime and provisioner (#9510)
message:
[Core] Add extension points for managed-job runtime and provisioner (#9510)

* [Core] Add extension points for managed-job runtime and provisioner

- Provisioner registry (sky.provision.register_provisioner) backed by a
  Provisioner dataclass: routed lifecycle module + optional
  TemplateOverrideFn for launch-time template override.
- ProvisionManifest on ProvisionRecord, surfacing has_ray and the
  runtime/workdir/file-mounts/setup/run-started state so the backend
  can skip work the provisioner has already done.
- ManagedJobRuntime Protocol (sky.jobs.runtime) with module-level
  dispatch for get_job_status / get_exit_codes / download_logs /
  cleanup / tail_logs / get_node_addresses, plus an is_registered()
  fast-path predicate. Replaces the per-feature controller_hooks /
  log_reader / networking_provider split with one runtime adapter.
- Launch-context plumbing: _extra_launch_context flows from sdk
  through payloads / execution into RetryingVmProvisioner so plugins
  can carry side-channel data without polluting the public Task.
- register_sensitive_fields() for provider-config keys.
- fill_template() accepts absolute .j2 paths so plugins can register
  templates outside the package tree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Thread _extra_launch_context through execution.launch()

The LaunchBody payload sends _extra_launch_context to the server's
/launch endpoint, but execution.launch() didn't accept it, so the
server-side call raised TypeError: launch() got an unexpected keyword
argument '_extra_launch_context'.

Add the kwarg to launch() and pass it down to _execute().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Serialize provision_manifest as a plain dict in handle pickle

ProvisionManifest is a new class on sky.provision.common (added in
this PR). Pickling a CloudVmRayResourceHandle with a live
ProvisionManifest instance bakes the class reference into the bytes,
so any code that doesn't yet have the class (an older server reading
the cluster-state DB after a downgrade, or an older client decoding
an API response that pickles the handle) raises:

  AttributeError: Can't get attribute 'ProvisionManifest' on
  <module 'sky.provision.common'>

before __setstate__ ever runs, defeating the version<13 upgrade path.

Convert the field to a plain dict in __getstate__ and reconstruct it
in __setstate__. Both the cluster-state DB and the API response wire
format (encoders.encode_handle is base64(pickle.dumps(handle))) inherit
the fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Add pre-provision networking hook for managed-job runtimes

Some runtimes can predict a task's internal DNS names before its
cluster is provisioned (e.g. workloads with stable hostnames). Today
all DNS-mapping work happens after the handle exists, which means a
task can't resolve its peers until provisioning is complete.

- Add `ManagedJobRuntime.get_node_addresses_for_task(task, *,
  cluster_name, cluster_name_on_cloud)` to the Protocol and the
  module-level dispatch in sky.jobs.runtime, returning Optional addresses.
- In job_group_networking, add generate_pre_provision_networking_script
  which asks the registered runtime for predicted addresses and emits
  a base64-encoded in-pod DNS updater. Returns '' when no runtime is
  registered, preserving the OSS post-provision networking behavior.
- In the JobController, prepend the pre-provision script alongside the
  existing wait-for-networking script.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Skip _execute when provisioner reports run already started

When a registered provisioner already started the user's run command,
skip _execute instead of raising. Mirrors the existing skip behavior
for runtime_ready / file_mounts_ready / setup_done on the same manifest.

* [Jobs] Plug runtime adapter into more of the managed-job lifecycle

- ManagedJobRuntime gains get_job_submitted_at / get_job_ended_at slots,
  with module-level dispatch parallel to get_job_status.
- recovery_strategy._wait_until_job_starts_on_cluster,
  utils.try_to_get_job_end_time, and utils.stream_logs_by_id consult the
  runtime adapter before falling through to the skylet-over-SSH defaults,
  so clusters whose pods don't host a skylet (e.g. pods that *are* the
  job and Succeed quickly) don't hard-fail when kubectl exec on the
  completed pod returns non-zero.
- K8s query_instances accepts an optional status_map_overrides kwarg so
  callers whose pods don't follow the ray-cluster lifecycle
  (Succeeded != cluster gone) can selectively remap a subset of phases
  without duplicating the function body.
- New build_managed_job_streaming_header helper for runtimes that write
  their own saved-log files, so headers stay byte-identical to the
  legacy skylet header (LOG_FILE_START_STREAMING_AT marker preserved).

* [Core] Always cache cluster_info / docker_user / IPs on handle after provisioning

The post-provision block in CloudVmRayBackend was gated on
`not manifest.runtime_setup_done`, but the calls inside (cached_cluster_info
and docker_user assignments, update_cluster_ips with cluster_info,
update_ssh_ports) are pure derivations from cluster_info — none of them
issue Ray/SSH queries when cluster_info is provided.

When the gate fires (e.g. a provisioner returns runtime_setup_done=True),
handle.cached_cluster_info stays None. Downstream consumers then see None
even though cluster_info was correctly produced — most notably
FailoverStrategyExecutor._launch reads cached_cluster_info to populate
node-name lineage, and silently writes NULL when the handle is empty.

Master never had this gate; it was introduced on this branch. Drop it so
the handle is always populated when cluster_info is available.

* [Jobs] Fix isort import ordering in controller / job_group_networking

Mechanical isort fix; no behavior change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Fetch cluster_info when runtime_setup_done=True to fix UnboundLocalError

The previous commit (002fd940a4) dropped the `if not manifest.runtime_setup_done:`
gate around `handle.cached_cluster_info = cluster_info` and friends, so the handle
gets populated for V1 / fast-path provisioners. But `cluster_info` was only
assigned inside the `else` branch (from `provisioner.post_provision_runtime_setup`),
so when `runtime_setup_done=True` the un-gated consumers hit:

  UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'cluster_info' where it is
  not associated with a value

Fix: when `runtime_setup_done=True`, fetch cluster_info via
`provision_lib.get_cluster_info()` — same call `_post_provision_setup` makes
internally at provisioner.py:449. Cheap (no SSH/Ray work), gives the handle
the populated `cached_cluster_info` it needs for downstream lineage tracking.

* [Core] Add has_job_queue and ssh_available to ProvisionManifest

The launch site in CloudVmRayBackend was gating three behaviors on
``not manifest.runtime_setup_done``:

  1. Refresh stale ray-job state via skylet after re-attaching to a
     previously INIT cluster.
  2. Fail in-progress jobs via skylet after restarting a STOPPED
     cluster.
  3. Add the cluster to the SSH config file.

These predicates describe different cluster capabilities, but
``runtime_setup_done`` was being used as a coincidence proxy for all
three. Sites 1 and 2 are really gated on whether the cluster has a
multi-job queue (ray + skylet bookkeeping); site 3 is gated on
whether the cluster is reachable via SSH.

Add two semantic fields to ``ProvisionManifest``:

  - ``has_job_queue``: cluster runs a job queue that accepts multiple
    ``sky exec`` submissions over its lifetime.
  - ``ssh_available``: cluster is reachable via SSH using the
    credentials in its cluster YAML.

Both default to ``True``, so existing behavior is unchanged. A
provisioner that materializes a single-use, non-SSH-reachable cluster
(e.g. a pod that runs the job and exits) can now express that
directly via the manifest.

Also clarified the ``template_override`` comment at the launch site
("override the cluster config template" rather than "claim the
launch") and added field-level docstrings to the rest of
``ProvisionManifest`` for consistency.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Remove unused build_managed_job_streaming_header helper

This helper has no callers in the OSS tree. The header it produces
is byte-compatible with the legacy skylet streaming header so that
external runtimes that write their own saved-log files can match
it, but that out-of-tree use does not justify keeping the helper
in OSS — those callers can render the same lines themselves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Guard managed-job runtime calls with is_registered()

Three call sites were dispatching through the managed-job runtime
registry without first checking ``is_registered()``:

- ``recovery_strategy.StrategyExecutor`` (async): paid two
  ``asyncio.to_thread`` round-trips on every poll — one to fetch a
  handle, one to call the runtime that immediately returned ``None``.
- ``utils.try_to_get_job_end_time`` (sync): paid a DB lookup for a
  handle that the runtime would never use.
- ``utils.stream_logs_by_id`` (sync): negligible cost but
  inconsistent with the other guarded sites.

Wrap each in ``if managed_job_runtime.is_registered():`` — the cheap
synchronous guard the registry exposes precisely for this purpose
(see its docstring). When no runtime is registered (the default),
the OSS fallback path runs immediately with no thread-pool or DB
overhead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Add pre_provision_k8s_dns_addresses runtime hook

Replace the prior pair of Protocol methods (``get_node_addresses`` and
``get_node_addresses_for_task``) with a single, narrower hook on
``ManagedJobRuntime``:

  pre_provision_k8s_dns_addresses(*, cluster_name_on_cloud)

A non-None return means the runtime contributes pre-provision DNS for
the task: addresses are baked into the in-pod DNS updater script that
runs at task start, and the post-provision SSH-based DNS updater is
skipped on the initial Phase 3 setup for that task.

The skip is driven from a single shared predicate
``job_group_networking.pre_provision_addresses_for_task`` called both
at injection time AND at the controller's Phase 3 skip filter, so the
two ends stay structurally in sync rather than relying on coincident
correlation.

Returned addresses for K8s targets may use ``$POD_NAMESPACE`` as a
literal placeholder; the in-pod shell expands it from the Kubernetes
Downward API at task start. This avoids resolving the namespace from
the controller's kubeconfig, which can disagree with the namespace
the pod actually ends up in (workspace overrides, etc.).

The recovery callback (``on_recovery``) re-runs
``setup_job_group_networking`` for all tasks unconditionally so peer
address changes propagate even to tasks that pre-provisioned their
own DNS initially.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Rename generate_pre_provision_networking_script for clarity

The function returns a bash prelude that gets prepended to ``task.run``
to start the JobGroup DNS updater locally. The old name described its
relationship to the broader pre-provision concept; the new name
describes what the function actually returns and where the bash gets
delivered (inline, via task.run) — symmetric with Phase 3's SSH-based
delivery of the same updater script.

Also adds a comment at the controller call site explaining the
relationship between this prelude and the Phase 3 SSH-based path.

No behavior change — pure rename + comment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Tighten Phase 3 skip-filter comment

Drop the "pre-provision networking" / "self-configure at task start"
phrasing — neither matches anything concrete in the code. Replace with
language that mirrors generate_inline_networking_setup_script and points
at where the work actually happens (task.run).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Revert _generate_k8s_dns_mappings to master form

The intermediate ``addresses = [...]`` list was added when this
function had a runtime override branch (``managed_job_runtime
.get_node_addresses(handle)`` short-circuit). That branch was later
dropped, leaving the restructure vestigial — pure cosmetic churn vs
master with no remaining purpose. Revert to the simpler form.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Rename pre_provision DNS helpers; add k8s_dns_addresses_for_handle

Rename the pre_provision_* identifiers — callers don't care about
timing, they just need K8s DNS names:

- pre_provision_addresses_for_task -> dns_addresses_for_task
- pre_provision_k8s_dns_addresses -> k8s_dns_addresses_for_task
- _generate_pre_provision_k8s_dns_mappings -> _generate_k8s_dns_mappings_from_runtime

Move _task_targets_kubernetes and _cluster_name_on_cloud_for_task

Phase 3 skips tasks that inline the DNS mapping — they self-start the

[Core] Allow relative file_mounts destinations again (#9537)

* [Core] Allow relative file_mounts destinations again

PR #9423 added _validate_mount_dest_is_absolute(), which rejected any
file_mounts destination not starting with `/` or `~`. But the backend
(cloud_vm_ray_backend.py) has explicit support for relative
destinations: it resolves them against ~/sky_workdir at provision time
(added in PR #1315, "Set relative dir root to workdir"). The example
examples/using_file_mounts.yaml documents this as a feature, and the
test_file_mounts smoke test exercises it — that test went red on the
first nightly after #9423 (build #10301 vs. previously-passing #10289).

Move the absolute-path check out of the shared _validate_mount_path()
and into the volumes site only. Volumes still require absolute paths
(no workdir-relative handling), but file_mounts no longer rejects
relative destinations. Other validation tightening from #9423
(disk_size, accelerator counts, --num-jobs, env-file existence,
duplicate YAML keys, UTF-8) is unrelated and preserved.

subject: [Dashboard] Show torn-down cluster on detail page when URL holds the name (#9513)
message:
[Dashboard] Show torn-down cluster on detail page when URL holds the name (#9513)

* [Dashboard] Find torn-down clusters in history by name on the cluster page

The cluster detail page loads with the URL parameter as either the
cluster name (when navigated from the active list) or the cluster hash
(when navigated from the historical list). When an active cluster is
torn down via `sky down` and the page is refreshed, the URL still
contains the cluster name, but the history lookup only filters by hash
on the backend, so the page incorrectly shows "Cluster not found in
active clusters or history."

Fall back to scanning recent history by name and re-fetch the full
record by hash so YAML/command fields remain populated.

* [Core] Add cluster_names filter to cost_report for dashboard name lookup

The dashboard cluster detail page receives the URL parameter as a
cluster name when navigated from the active list, and as a cluster
hash when navigated from the historical list. Filtering only by hash
on the backend meant a torn-down cluster's page (where the URL still
holds the name) couldn't be resolved without scanning all of history,
which doesn't scale on deployments with tens of thousands of records.

Add an optional cluster_names filter to /cost_report (and the
underlying core.cost_report / get_clusters_from_history). When both
cluster_hashes and cluster_names are provided, rows matching either
are returned (logical OR), so the dashboard resolves the URL param
in a single round trip regardless of whether it's a hash or name.

The new field is optional and silently ignored by older servers
(payloads use extra='ignore'), so no API_VERSION bump is required.

subject: [CI] Fix shell injection in pytest.yml via untrusted github.event interpolation (#9531)
message:
[CI] Fix shell injection in pytest.yml via untrusted github.event interpolation (#9531)

The set_env steps in both unit-test and failover-test jobs interpolate
${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}, ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }},
${{ github.head_ref }}, and similar untrusted contexts directly into bash
run scripts. When the value contains backticks around a valid CLI command,
bash performs command substitution on the runner.

This is the script injection pattern documented in GitHub's Security
Hardening guide:
https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-an-intermediate-environment-variable

Replace each interpolation with the intermediate environment variable
pattern: assign the expression to an env: entry, reference it as $VAR
in the script. Same set_env outputs (branch, message); same downstream
consumer (TEST_ANALYTICS_COMMIT_MESSAGE); only the path from ${{ ... }}
to bash literal is replaced.

Verified with zizmor v1.24.1 (template-injection audit):
- Before: 5 findings (4 High confidence)
- After:  0 findings

Closes #9530.
