subject: [Dashboard] Add plugin extension slots for infra page (#9475)
message:
[Dashboard] Add plugin extension slots for infra page (#9475) * [Dashboard] Add useAllDataProviders hook Adds a small hook that returns the list of all registered data providers, enabling host pages to discover plugins exposing a particular hook by name without knowing any specific plugin id. Companion to the existing useDataProvider(id) lookup. * [Dashboard] Add plugin extension slots for infra page Adds 8 generic plugin slots to the Infra page and detail pages, and wires useExtraInfraRows merging so plugins can contribute extra rows + status data without OSS knowing any specific plugin id. Slots added: - infra.headerActions: page header right-side actions - infra.attentionBanner: above the kubernetes / cloud / ssh cards - infra.row.namePrefix: inside row name cell, receives {id, kind, status} - infra.row.actions: trailing row cell, receives {id, kind} - infra.cloudRow.link: wraps the cloud row to make it a link - infra.contextDetail.statusPanel: top of k8s context detail page - infra.sshDetail.statusPanel: top of SSH node pool detail page - infra.emptyState: replaces the default "no infrastructure" hint Also extends PluginWrapperSlot to accept a context object (passed as props to each wrapper) and a fallback element. Adds useAllDataProviders helper for host pages that want to discover plugins exposing a particular hook by name. OSS users without any plugin loaded see no behavior change — every slot renders nothing (or the existing OSS fallback) when no plugin is registered. * [Dashboard] Polish header spacing and empty-state behavior - Add a small left margin to the infra.headerActions slot so plugin-injected buttons (e.g. an "Add infra" CTA) don't sit flush against the Refresh button. - When all infrastructure is disabled, render only the empty-state hint — hide the otherwise-empty Kubernetes/Slurm/Cloud/SSH cards underneath. This makes the OSS empty page (and any plugin-replaced empty card via infra.emptyState) the singular CTA when nothing is configured. * [Dashboard] Trigger infra-page refresh on plugin-emitted event The Infra page now listens for a 'skydashboard:infra:refresh' window event and re-fetches its data when the event fires. This lets plugins that mutate infra (e.g. an Add/Remove flow) request a host-page refresh without needing to know any details of the host page's data plumbing. * [Dashboard] Fix ReferenceError: statusByKey is not defined Inside GPUs.renderCloudInfrastructure() the row-prefix slot context was reading from \`statusByKey\` but the local in scope is \`extraStatusByKey\` (\`statusByKey\` is the prop name InfrastructureSection receives, not a variable in GPUs). The crash only fired once a cloud row actually rendered — i.e. once a credential was uploaded — which is why it appeared after the AWS upload, not on initial empty-state load. * [Dashboard] Isolate plugin hook calls in their own components The Infra page previously enumerated plugin-provided hooks via \`extraInfraRowHooks.map((useHook) => useHook())\` directly inside the GPUs component's render. That meant adding or removing a data provider changed the number of hooks called per GPUs render, which React reports as 'Invalid hook call' (error #311). Each provider's hook now runs inside its own ProviderInfraRowsLoader child component. Each loader has a stable hook count for its lifetime and pushes results back to GPUs via callback. GPUs's own hook count no longer depends on how many plugins are registered. Triggered when any plugin registers a useExtraInfraRows hook (e.g. the credential_manager plugin) — without this fix the page crashes once the plugin loads. * [Dashboard] Cloud row blue link styling, hide redundant warning icon - Cloud rows in the Cloud card now use the same blue + underline-on-hover styling as the Kubernetes context rows so it's clear they're clickable. - The yellow context-unreachable warning icon next to Kubernetes context names is hidden when a plugin is contributing per-row status data via the infra.row.namePrefix slot — the plugin's status dot and per-context detail page cover that information already, so the icon was redundant. * [Dashboard] Add infra.contextDetail.headerActions slot Allows plugins to inject right-aligned header actions (e.g. a Remove button) into the Kubernetes context detail page. * [Dashboard] Cloud row only renders as a link when a plugin wraps it Pure OSS has no per-cloud detail page, so unconditionally styling the cloud name as a blue clickable link would be misleading. Now we check whether the infra.cloudRow.link wrapper slot has any registered components — if yes (a plugin like a credential manager has wired the wrapper), the cell renders blue + underline-on-hover. If no, it falls back to the original plain dark-grey styling. * [Dashboard] Detail-view heading: small back link + large h1 The Infra detail view (selectedContext set) previously rendered a small breadcrumb (Infrastructure › Kubernetes › name) for the entire header. Now we render a small grey '← Infrastructure' back link on its own line, and a separate large h1 row below carrying the leaf identifier — same treatment used by other detail-style pages in the dashboard. K8s context names render in the monospace font that matches the row-name styling; SSH and Slurm names use the default sans-serif. The Refresh + workspace + plugin headerActions controls stay on their own row to the right of the back link, unchanged. * [Dashboard] Don't manually clear plugin route container on unmount The catch-all plugin route pages (\`pages/[...path].js\` and \`pages/plugins/[...slug].js\`) called \`container.innerHTML = ''\` right after invoking the plugin's cleanup function. When a plugin uses \`ReactDOM.createRoot(container).render(...)\`, React 18 manages the container's children itself; manually wiping innerHTML after \`root.unmount()\` races with React reconciliation and produces \"Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node'\" errors that abort the in-flight Next.js navigation. Removing the manual clear lets React handle its own DOM teardown, so back-button clicks and sidebar navigation away from a plugin route now work as expected. * [Dashboard] Polish detail-page chrome and Cloud-card loading state - Hide the workspace selector, "Updated …" indicator, Refresh button, and infra.headerActions slot when viewing a specific infra detail page. The per-page chrome (back link + heading + per-page Refresh inside the status panel) handles its own controls; keeping the page-level controls visible at the top right is redundant and conflicts with the new heading layout. - Cloud card no longer flashes "No enabled clouds available." while cloud data or plugin-contributed extra rows are still loading. The message is suppressed in favor of a small inline spinner until at least one of the data sources resolves. * [Dashboard] Fix render-loop in ProviderInfraRowsLoader The data-provider hook caller had a useEffect with no dependency array — it called onResult after every render. Plugin hooks that return a fresh object literal each render (the common pattern) would trigger an infinite re-render loop: onResult → parent setState → re-render → useEffect fires again with a new result reference → ... Chromium happens to recover from the loop, but Firefox ends up locked: navigation clicks (Next.js Link, sidebar links, the back link on detail pages) appear to do nothing because the router never gets a chance to commit while the loop is in flight. Now the effect depends on the result, so it only fires when the plugin's returned object reference actually changes. Plugins are expected to memoize their hook returns to keep the reference stable. * [Dashboard] Render context detail header actions inline with the h1 Plugin-injected detail-page actions (e.g. Remove) used to render above the heading because the slot lived inside ContextDetails. Now the slot renders on the same row as the h1 in the GPUs return:

{contextName}

The slot context now also forwards isSsh/isSlurm flags so consumers can opt out for non-k8s detail flavors. The headerActions slot inside ContextDetails has been removed. * [Dashboard] Skip the list-view top bar entirely on detail pages On a detail page the back link above already serves as the leaf navigation, and the page-level workspace selector / Refresh / plugin headerActions don't apply when viewing one infra. Hiding the whole row instead of just its inner controls also closes the ~36px empty space (h-5 + mb-4) that was sitting between the '← Infrastructure' back link and the h1. * [Dashboard] Make /infra/ a catch-all route Context names containing slashes (e.g. EKS ARNs like arn:aws:eks:.../cluster/) survive a page refresh now: the dashboard handler decodes %2F back to /, which the single-segment dynamic route could not match, so the page fell into the global plugin catch-all and got stuck on "Loading plugin resources…". Convert pages/infra/[context].js to a catch-all pages/infra/[...context].js that tries plugin routes first (preserving /infra/cloud/ and /infra/ssh/) and falls through to otherwise. Wait for skydashboard:plugins-loaded before falling through so a refresh on a plugin route doesn't briefly mount while the plugin's registerRoute call is still in flight. Update infra.jsx to join the catch-all array back into a context name instead of taking only the first segment. * [Dashboard] Run OSS + plugin refresh in parallel on Infra page The Refresh button awaited the OSS data fetch (sky check, slow) before kicking off the plugin's status fetch, so the row status dots stayed frozen on stale data until the much slower OSS pass finished. Run both in parallel via Promise.all — the dots refresh as soon as the plugin call returns, without waiting on sky check. * [Core] Add check_results accessors to global_user_state Adds get_cached_check_results / set_check_results keyed by workspace. Supports full-workspace overwrite and per-cloud merge modes via the is_full_workspace_run flag. JSON-encoded value, stored alongside the existing enabled_clouds rows in config_table. Will be populated by sky.check.check in a follow-up commit. * [Core] Persist cloud2ctx2text from sky.check.check After each workspace check completes, write the per-(cloud, context) enabled bool + reason string to check_results_. Strings are ANSI-stripped at the persist site so consumers don't have to. Full-workspace runs (clouds=None) replace the row; scoped runs merge at cloud granularity so a single-cloud refresh doesn't erase other clouds' leaves. This unblocks the credential_manager plugin's /check_output rewrite, which becomes a thin DB read against this row. * [Dashboard] Pass force=true through plugin refresh The Infra page's Refresh button calls refreshExtraInfra, which fans out to each plugin data provider's refresh() callback. Pass true so plugins can distinguish a manual refresh from initial mount and bypass any caches accordingly. * [Dashboard] Hoist row id/kind out of PluginSlot context props Compute id and kind once per row in the kubernetes/SSH row map and reuse them across the namePrefix and actions PluginSlot context props. Removes the triple-ternary and quadruple-evaluated \`isSSH ? ... : context\` chain from the JSX — same data, fewer copies. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) * [Dashboard] Memoize handleRefresh and drop redundant fallback prop Two follow-ups from the gemini review on this PR: - Wrap handleRefresh in useCallback([refreshExtraInfra]) and add it to the dependency arrays of the keyboard-shortcut and infra-refresh event listeners. Previously both effects had empty deps and an eslint-disable, so they captured first-render handleRefresh which closed over an empty extraInfraResults array; the listeners would fire but never refresh the plugin-contributed data that resolves after first paint. - Remove the duplicate fallback prop on the cloud-row PluginWrapperSlot. PluginWrapperSlot already renders children when no plugin is registered (see fallback ?? children in the slot impl). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) * [Core] Tolerate persist failures in sky check + correct race-safety doc Two fixes from review feedback on the check_results persistence path: - sky/check.py: wrap the set_check_results call in try/except + log a warning. The persisted row is a cache; the source-of-truth enabled_clouds__ rows are written above it. A transient DB failure or unsupported dialect must not fail the user-visible `sky check` command. - sky/global_user_state.py: rewrite the docstring on the scoped-run read-modify-write to match what the code actually does. orm.Session does not acquire row locks under default isolation, so two concurrent scoped writes for different clouds in the same workspace can clobber each other's per-cloud updates. The blast radius is bounded (one scoped run's leaves get overwritten until the next write) and the source-of-truth enabled_clouds rows are unaffected, so we accept the race here rather than serialize through an advisory lock. Documented with the upgrade path (with_for_update / BEGIN IMMEDIATE) for if/when this row becomes load-bearing. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) * [Dashboard] Cut detail-page navigation latency by ~6 seconds Three independent changes that together reduce the time from clicking a context row on the Infra page to a populated detail view from ~9s to ~3s on a typical multi-context tenant: - sky/dashboard/src/components/infra.jsx: drop the \`kubeLoading && !kubeDataLoaded\` spinner gate around the context-detail view. Plugin-contributed slots (status panels, etc.) shouldn't wait for OSS's per-cloud kube data load — which can take 5-10s on tenants where some K8s contexts time out at the API. The inner sections handle empty gpus/nodes arrays gracefully and render their own skeletons. - sky/dashboard/src/components/infra.jsx: in handleContextClick, drop the local setSelectedContext(context) — let the URL effect on the destination page set it. Setting it locally caused the source /infra page to render the detail view briefly (firing all its data fetches and mounting plugin slots) right before router.push unmounted it. That doubled every fetch on navigation, and the destination's mount lost the race for HTTP connection slots against OSS's own enabled_clouds calls — so the user only saw the slow second wave even when the first wave was a fast cache hit. - sky/dashboard/src/plugins/PluginProvider.jsx + sky/dashboard/src/pages/infra/[...context].js: expose plugin-loaded state via a synchronously-readable global flag (\`window.__skyDashboardPluginsLoaded\`). The catch-all page now initializes its useState from that flag, eliminating the 2-second safety-net timeout that previously gated every detail-page navigation (the \`skydashboard:plugins-loaded\` event always fires during initial app bootstrap, so by the time a detail page mounts the listener never receives it; only the timeout did). Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) * [Core] Merge per-context within a cloud on scoped check_results writes A scoped `sky.check.check(clouds=(,))` run currently replaces the entire cloud entry in `check_results_` with whatever the scoped run produced, dropping leaves for sibling contexts that weren't re-probed. For a multi-context Kubernetes cloud, a per-context lookup that only iterates one context (or only succeeds on one) clobbers every other context's status until the next full-workspace run rewrites the row. Switch the non-full path to per-context merge: scoped writes only update the individual leaves under each cloud_repr, preserving sibling contexts. Stale leaves for contexts that were since removed from the cloud will linger until the next full-workspace run, which is acceptable for a status cache. The existing `enabled_clouds__` rows remain the source of truth and are not affected by this change. Test: added a per-context merge case to test_global_user_state_check_results — a scoped Kubernetes write touching one of three contexts must leave the other two intact. * [Dashboard] Invalidate getEnabledCloudsBatch on Infra Refresh `getWorkspaceContexts` resolves its workspace -> contexts mapping by calling `dashboardCache.get(getEnabledCloudsBatch, [...])` internally. The Infra page's Refresh button invalidates `getWorkspaceContexts` itself but not the batch fetcher it reads through, so re-running `getWorkspaceContexts` after Refresh keeps returning the stale batch result and the rendered context list lags whatever change just happened upstream. Add `dashboardCache.invalidateFunction(getEnabledCloudsBatch)` to the Refresh handler so every (workspaces, expand) variant is cleared in one call and the next read goes to the network. * [Core] Per-Kubernetes-context scope on sky check `sky check` accepts cloud names but not per-context scopes, so a gesture like `sky check k8s/` warned and ignored the context, iterating every allowed context anyway. Add a real scope that flows from CLI all the way down to the cloud's check path: - New `--context` CLI flag on `sky check` (repeatable). Equivalent to passing `kubernetes/` as an infra arg. - `sky.client.sdk.check` accepts `kubernetes_contexts`. Infra strings of the form `kubernetes/` (and the alias `k8s/`) parse the path component as a context instead of warning and dropping it. - `payloads.CheckBody.kubernetes_contexts` carries the scope to the server; existing `extra='ignore'` keeps the field invisible to older servers. - `sky.check.{check, check_capabilities, check_capability}` accept the same kwarg. - New `Kubernetes.scoped_allowed_contexts()` contextmanager: while active, `existing_allowed_contexts()` returns the requested list intersected with what's actually in kubeconfig instead of consulting `allowed_contexts`. Class-level (not thread-local) so the scope propagates to the ThreadPool workers `subprocess_utils.run_in_parallel` spawns inside the check. - The persisted `check_results_` row is updated only at the leaves the scoped run probed, thanks to the per-context merge in `set_check_results` already on this branch. Bump `API_VERSION` 49 → 50 and add `MIN_KUBERNETES_CONTEXTS_API_VERSION = 50`. The SDK warns at request time when a per-context scope is set and the server is older — the field would otherwise be dropped silently by the older server's `extra='ignore'` config. Test plan: - pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/test_global_user_state_check_results.py tests/unit_tests/test_sky/test_check_persistence.py — passes - `sky check kubernetes --context ctx-a`: enables only ctx-a, no warning - `sky check k8s/ctx-a`: same, no "ignoring" warning - After scoped run, /check_results retains sibling-context leaves (per-context merge confirmed) * Revert "[Core] Per-Kubernetes-context scope on sky check" This reverts commit 31bcfb90927dee11106fcb9b61ca1dbeae072c28. * [Test] Fix yapf formatting in scoped check_results test Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) Co-authored-by: u78f0bdd0e5c20ed2

[CI] Stabilize 3 smoke tests against curl 8.18 and HF Xet CDN (#9543)

* [CI] Stabilize 3 smoke tests against curl 8.18 and HF Xet CDN

Three independent failures in the nightly --aws build (#10325) all
caused by external environment changes, not code regressions:

1. test_skyserve_https
   curl 8.18+/OpenSSL 3.5+ (e.g. on Ubuntu 26.04) emits
   "SSL: unable to obtain common name from peer certificate" for an
   empty-subject (-subj "/") cert, instead of the older
   "self-signed certificate" wording. Exit code is unchanged (60).

   Fix: assert curl exit==60 (CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION) rather
   than grepping the message text. Verified across curl 7.81 (Ubuntu
   22.04) and 8.18 (Ubuntu 26.04) and across 3 cert variants
   (empty CN, mismatched CN, matching CN — all return 60).

2. test_skyserve_llm
   HuggingFace's Xet CDN (us.aws.cdn.hf.co) is returning ~25-40%
   HTTP 403 Forbidden to AWS workers, stalling vLLM's
   Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B download until the 1800s initial_delay_seconds
   times out and the replica goes FAILED_INITIAL_DELAY.

   Verified directly on the live worker:
     - default (xet):    260 MB cached after 120s, 16x 403 vs 8x 206
     - HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1: full 1.5 GB downloaded in 6.1 seconds

3. test_batch_diffusion (examples/batch/diffusion/pool.yaml)
   Same Xet CDN issue, this time stalling Stable Diffusion v1.5
   weight downloads on the pool workers; the 45-min test timeout
   expires before all workers finish setup.

Both (2) and (3) get HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 to fall back to the
direct-S3 LFS path, which is reliable from AWS.

Failing build evidence:
https://buildkite.com/skypilot-1/smoke-tests/builds/10325

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Batch] Set HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET inside the remote function, not pool.yaml

The first attempt put HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET=1 in pool.yaml's `envs:`, but
that env doesn't reach the worker process that runs the remote function.
sky.batch.Dataset.map submits a brand-new managed-job task internally
(sky/batch/dataset.py:262: `task = sky.Task(name=..., run=None)`; then
`sky.jobs.launch(task, pool=pool_name)`), and pool.yaml's envs are not
copied onto that submitted task. The remote function further runs in
a fresh Python namespace per sky/batch/utils.py:102, so module-level
imports/env writes in generate_images.py don't reach it either.

Verified directly on a live diffusion-pool worker (ami-0ba50db9...,
test build 10350): HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET unset on every Python process,
xet log still showing 28×403, .incomplete blob sizes identical to
the failing baseline.

Move the env-var write into the remote function body, before the
diffusers import, so it lives in the actual download process. Drop
the pool.yaml entry now that we know it's a no-op.

subject: [Nebius] Stabilize tempfile path in get_credential_file_mounts (#9555)
message:
[Nebius] Stabilize tempfile path in get_credential_file_mounts (#9555)

* [Nebius] Stabilize tempfile path in get_credential_file_mounts

#9432 introduced a fresh `tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile` per call inside
`Nebius.get_credential_file_mounts`. Because `Cloud.get_credential_file_mounts`
runs on every launch for every enabled cloud (see
`sky/check.py::get_cloud_credential_file_mounts`), and its return value feeds
the file-mounts hash that SkyPilot uses to (a) dedupe rsync uploads to
controllers and (b) decide whether `sky launch --fast` may skip re-setup, the
unstable path made every launch look like a config change.

Visible symptoms on master with Nebius among the enabled clouds (e.g. on the
nightly Buildkite agents that have aws+azure+gcp+lambda+nebius+runpod
enabled):

  * `test_pools_num_jobs_speed --aws`: `timeout 70 sky jobs launch --pool ...
    --num-jobs 10 -d -y` killed mid-submit (warm-controller submission slowed
    from ~88s baseline to ~150s).
  * `test_multi_tenant_managed_jobs --aws`: 60s wait for the cancel-1 job to
    leave PENDING expires.
  * `test_pool_autoscaling_scale_up_to_max_then_down_to_zero --aws`: same
    family.
  * `test_launch_fast --aws` and `test_launch_fast_with_cluster_changes --aws`:
    `--fast` re-runs setup because the file-mounts comparison sees the path
    "changed" since the previous launch.

Bisect (warm 10-job submit time, AWS pool, single replica):

  * 36afaeea (last green nightly): 96s
  * 0de83381 (parent of #9510 / #9538 / #9545): 89s
  * b7a9653f (#9510): 87s
  * e7e5da1b (#9538): 87s
  * 8ffce113 (right before #9432): 88-98s
  * eff7a163 (#9432): 128s, 150s ← regression starts here
  * a8deb9ae (#9545): 129s
  * f1d53a0d (master tip) with sky/clouds/nebius.py reverted to 8ffce113: 95s

Confirmation that the change is the cause:

    >>> n = Nebius()
    >>> for _ in range(3):
    ...     print(n.get_credential_file_mounts()['~/.nebius/NEBIUS_TENANT_ID.txt'])
    /tmp/nebius-tenant-id-frg_ebgn
    /tmp/nebius-tenant-id-bg5l0bix
    /tmp/nebius-tenant-id-n0ouhu78

This patch makes the tempfile path deterministic in `value` (sha1[:16]) and
writes idempotently. Repeated calls now return the same path, restoring the
file-mounts hash stability the rest of the launch path expects. Other
intent of #9432 (workspace/region-config-driven tenant_id materialization,
managed-disks support) is preserved.

After the fix:

    >>> for _ in range(3):
    ...     print(n.get_credential_file_mounts()['~/.nebius/NEBIUS_TENANT_ID.txt'])
    /tmp/nebius-tenant-id-9f3d24c46bfc2ee3
    /tmp/nebius-tenant-id-9f3d24c46bfc2ee3
    /tmp/nebius-tenant-id-9f3d24c46bfc2ee3

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Nebius] Namespace tempfile path by UID for shared /tmp safety

Per gemini-code-assist review on #9555: on Linux, ``tempfile.gettempdir()``
is shared (``/tmp``), so a content-hash-only filename can collide across
users. If user A wrote the file with a restrictive umask, user B would
hit ``PermissionError`` when trying to read or rewrite it.

Prepend ``os.getuid()`` to the filename so each user gets a distinct path
while keeping content stability per user. ``hasattr(os, 'getuid')`` guards
non-POSIX hosts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Skylet] Fix autostop ignoring active SSH after stop/start (#9539)
message:
[Skylet] Fix autostop ignoring active SSH after stop/start (#9539)

* [Skylet] Fix autostop ignoring active SSH after stop/start

When skylet's first AutostopEvent tick runs with no SSH connected
(e.g. right after `sky stop` + `sky start`), psutil's module-global
@haa41c44cc609e0f7 cache for get_terminal_map() freezes with no /dev/pts/*
entries. devpts is dynamic, so any PTY allocated afterwards stays
invisible to the daemon: Process.terminal() returns None,
has_active_ssh_sessions() returns False, and the cluster autostops
despite an active interactive session.

Clear psutil._psposix.get_terminal_map's cache on each tick so newly-
allocated PTYs are visible. Wrapped in try/except AttributeError so a
future psutil refactor of the private path cannot crash skylet.

Fixes #9524.

subject: [AWS] Add support for `aws login` (2026 AWS CLI command) (#9526)
message:
[AWS] Add support for `aws login` (2026 AWS CLI command) (#9526)

* [AWS] Add support for `aws login` (2026 AWS CLI command)

`aws login` is the browser-based OAuth 2.0 + PKCE auth flow released
by AWS in early 2026. It writes short-term credentials to
~/.aws/login/cache/ and auto-rotates them every 15 minutes; boto3
picks these up via the standard credential provider chain. The
~/.aws/credentials file is not used.

Before this change, `sky check aws` rejected setups using `aws login`
because the identity-type detection fell through to
SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE and required the legacy file to exist:

  AWS: disabled
    Reason [compute, storage]: ~/.aws/credentials does not exist...

Changes:
- Add AWSIdentityType.LOGIN matching the 'login' Type column in
  `aws configure list` output
- Recognize LOGIN in _check_credentials_exist and skip the legacy
  static-credentials-file existence check (LOGIN behaves like SSO,
  IAM_ROLE, CONTAINER_ROLE, etc. — credentials live elsewhere and
  boto3 resolves them via the standard provider chain)
- Include LOGIN in non_static_types in should_use_env_auth_for_s3
  so that S3 mounts use env-based auth instead of embedding the
  (temporary) credentials in rclone config

Reference:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli-configure-sign-in.html

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AWS] Add unit tests for `aws login` identity type detection

Two tests covering the new AWSIdentityType.LOGIN:
- test_aws_login_detected_as_LOGIN_identity_type: verifies that
  `aws configure list` output with 'login' in the Type column is
  classified as AWSIdentityType.LOGIN.
- test_login_credentials_do_not_auto_expire: verifies that
  AWSIdentityType.LOGIN.can_credential_expire() returns False, since
  `aws login` auto-rotates credentials via the refresh token.

[Test] Fix self-kill on managed-jobs recovery test with long user hash (#9567)

* [Test] Fix self-kill on managed-jobs recovery test with long user hash

`test_managed_jobs_recovery_kubernetes_multinode` was killing the
cloud-cmd helper pod and failing with exit code 137 when run under a
user hash long enough (e.g. 19-char service-account hashes) to push
`<test>-cloud-cmd` past the K8s 42-char pod-name limit. Once the
cluster name is truncated, the trailing `-cloud-cmd` suffix is dropped
from the pod name, so `grep -v -- "-cloud-cmd"` against pod names no
longer excludes the helper pod, and `kubectl delete` on the result
kills the very pod running `sky exec`.

Switch the filter to match against the `skypilot-cluster-name`
annotation, which always holds the full untruncated cluster name, so
the `-cloud-cmd` exclusion is reliable regardless of user-hash length.

All SkyPilot pods carry the `skypilot-cluster-name` label, so adding
`-l skypilot-cluster-name` lets kubectl pre-filter by the label's
existence. This avoids returning unrelated pods in busy namespaces

subject: [Test] Make CIFAR-10 wget fall back to wayback when primary mirror is slow (#9572)
message:
[Test] Make CIFAR-10 wget fall back to wayback when primary mirror is slow (#9572)

* [Test] Make CIFAR-10 wget fall back to wayback when primary mirror is slow

The setup script in examples/resnet_distributed_torch.yaml downloads
CIFAR-10 from cs.toronto.edu, with a wayback-machine fallback chained
via `||`. But with no `--timeout` flag, a slow primary mirror does not
make wget exit non-zero — it just keeps draining bytes — so the
fallback is unreachable in the most common failure mode.

This is the root cause behind the recurring `test_cancel_pytorch`
flake. The cs.toronto.edu mirror serves the 162 MB tarball at
~350 KB/s on bad days, which puts the SETTING_UP phase right at the
360 s wait-for-RUNNING budget. Smoke build 10440 (passed) took 350.6 s
in SETTING_UP; build 10461 (failed) took 367 s. The 360 s budget was
itself bumped from 150 s only nine days ago (#9496) — bumping it
again would just push the cliff edge a bit further.

Adding `--timeout=30 --tries=2` makes wget abort after 30 s of read
stall, triggering the `||` branch and letting the wayback mirror
actually serve as a fallback. The wayback copy is generally faster
and more consistent than the toronto mirror under load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Address Gemini review: use `timeout` for hard wallclock cap

Per review feedback: `wget --timeout=30` is an *inactivity* (read)
timeout — it only fires if no bytes arrive for 30 s. The actual
failure mode is a slow-but-steady ~350 KB/s stream, which never
trips inactivity. The `||` fallback was therefore still unreachable.

Wrap each wget with the GNU `timeout` command so a hard wallclock
limit kills the process (rc=124) and triggers `||` to the wayback
mirror. Keep `--timeout=30` on wget itself so genuine stalls fail
faster than the wallclock cap.

- Primary (toronto): 90 s wallclock — fast days finish in <60 s,
  slow days fail over after 90 s
- Fallback (wayback): 120 s wallclock — same idea, more headroom
  since archive.org throughput is more variable

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(vast): fix 5 API compatibility issues with vastai-sdk v6+ (#9314)
message:
fix(vast): fix 5 API compatibility issues with vastai-sdk v6+ (#9314)

* fix(vast): fix 5 API compatibility issues with vastai-sdk v6+

The Vast.ai Python SDK was updated (v6+) breaking several assumptions
in the SkyPilot Vast provider. Fixes verified against Vast.ai API in
production (tested with vLLM deployment on RTX 3090, 2026-04-11).

Fixes:
1. api_key_access renamed: vast.vast().api_key_access no longer exists;
   use vast.vast().client.api_key instead.

2. direct/ssh params removed: create_instance() no longer accepts
   'direct' or 'ssh' keyword arguments, causing 400 Bad Request.

3. bid_price renamed to price: the instance creation parameter was
   renamed from bid_price to price in the Vast.ai API; normalize the
   old name for backwards compatibility.

4. env must be a dict: the Vast.ai API now requires env as a dict
   {'KEY': 'VAL'} instead of the old CLI-style string "-e KEY=VAL".
   Port mappings via -p are also no longer accepted in this field.
   Added backwards-compat parsing for legacy string env values.

5. ssh_host vs public_ipaddr: Vast.ai routes all SSH through a gateway
   host (e.g. ssh3.vast.ai) rather than the instance's public IP.
   Using public_ipaddr causes connection timeouts. Use ssh_host with
   fallback to public_ipaddr. Also add fallback for ports['22/tcp']
   being None (use ssh_port field instead).

Tested with:
  sky launch / sky exec on RTX 3090 and A100 instances
  vLLM inference server deployment via sky serve YAML
  SDK version: vastai-sdk 0.4.x (pip install vastai-sdk)

* fix(vast): add query_ports() with correct ssh_host:(ssh_port+1) mapping

Vast.ai exposes container ports via SSH reverse-proxy:
  container:22   → ssh_host:ssh_port   (SSH access)
  container:8080 → ssh_host:(ssh_port+1) (service endpoint)

Without query_ports(), sky serve uses query_ports_passthrough() which
constructs the readiness probe URL as http://ssh_host:8080 — this fails
because the Vast.ai SSH gateway does not expose port 8080 of the gateway
node itself; it only exposes the container's port 8080 via the gateway
port ssh_port+1.

Implement query_ports() in the Vast provider to return the correct
SocketEndpoint(host=ssh_host, port=ssh_port+1) for container port 8080.
Sky serve then probes the correct URL: http://ssh_host:(ssh_port+1)/health

This is analogous to RunPod's query_ports() implementation which also
maps container private ports to public gateway ports.

subject: [GCP] Pin gcloud SDK version in Dockerfile (#9587)
message:
[GCP] Pin gcloud SDK version in Dockerfile (#9587)

#9535 bumped _GCLOUD_VERSION in sky/clouds/gcp.py to 567.0.0 so the
wget-installed gcloud on remote VMs picks up gsutil 5.37 (which replaced
OpenSSL.crypto.sign with the cryptography library after #8070 dropped
the pyopenssl<24.3 cap). The Dockerfile's apt-install path was left
unpinned, so it kept resolving to whatever apt's `cloud-sdk` repo
considered current on the first build that ever populated the buildx
cache. Since the RUN command's content hash is the cache key, every
subsequent build with `--cache-from` reused that initial stale layer
indefinitely — even after Google released newer gcloud.

In practice this means anyone consuming `berkeleyskypilot/skypilot{,
-nightly}` or building from a Dockerfile-based fork still gets the
pre-May-5 gcloud (564.0.0 / gsutil 5.36), which still hits the
crypto.sign AttributeError on GCS storage operations under pyopenssl
24.3+.

Pin both `google-cloud-cli` and `google-cloud-cli-gke-gcloud-auth-plugin`
to 567.0.0-0 via a top-of-stage ARG, with a comment cross-referencing
_GCLOUD_VERSION so future bumps move both in lockstep. Exact-pin (not a
floor) because apt's CLI doesn't natively support `>=` and exact pins
buy reproducibility across all consumers.

Tested:
- `docker build -f Dockerfile --target gcloud-apt-install -t test .`
  succeeds; apt resolves both packages to 567.0.0-0 as expected.
- `docker run --rm test gcloud version` → `Google Cloud SDK 567.0.0`.
- `docker run --rm test gsutil version` → `gsutil version: 5.37`.

subject: [Jobs] Add daemon to sweep expired managed-job API access tokens (#9588)
message:
[Jobs] Add daemon to sweep expired managed-job API access tokens (#9588)

* [Jobs] Add daemon to sweep expired managed-job API access tokens

Add an internal server daemon that periodically deletes expired
service-account tokens issued for managed jobs with api_server_access.
The controller already revokes tokens on normal job completion (PR #8900),
but tokens can leak if the controller crashes mid-cleanup or if older
code paths skipped the controller-side revoke. Without a sweep, these
expired tokens accumulate in the service_account_tokens table forever.

The daemon scans for tokens whose name matches the managed-job shape
(prefix "managed-job-" plus a trailing 8-hex-char dag_uuid suffix) and
whose expires_at is in the past. Driving the sweep off the name shape
catches leaked tokens regardless of whether the api_access_tokens
mapping row was written.

Also reduce the managed-job token TTL from 7 to 3 days so any leaks
are shorter-lived.

Limitation: a custom user-created token whose name happens to match
managed-job-<anything>-<8 hex> would be removed once expired. The
prefix+suffix shape makes this unlikely in practice.

* [Jobs] Promote managed-job token TTL to a constant

Address Gemini review feedback on PR #9588: replace the hardcoded
`expires_in_days=3` with `MANAGED_JOB_TOKEN_TTL_DAYS` in
sky/jobs/constants.py for maintainability.

* [Jobs] Make expired-token-cleanup interval configurable

Read the sweep interval from `daemons.expired-token-cleanup-daemon.
interval_seconds` in skypilot config on each iteration so operators
can dial the cadence down (e.g., for testing on an existing
deployment) without rebuilding the API server. The default stays at
3600 seconds.

Also add `interval_seconds` to the daemon config schema; it is only
honored by daemons whose event functions opt in to reading it.

* [Jobs] Register expired-token-cleanup in debug_utils allowlist

CI fix: test_all_request_names_covered requires every RequestName to
appear in _REQUEST_BODY_ALLOWLIST or the denylist. Add the new
sky.expired-token-cleanup name introduced in this PR.

* [Test] Bump test_config expectations for the new cleanup daemon

The expired-token-cleanup daemon is unconditionally counted by
_get_min_short_workers, which raises the floor on short-worker
parallelism by 1 in low-memory configurations. Update the two
assertions that pin the floor (test_compute_server_config_low_resources
and test_parallel_size_short) from 4 to 5.

Same pattern as the heartbeat daemon PR (#8984).

subject: [DB] Use async_creator to hand asyncpg the libpq DSN (#9483)
message:
[DB] Use async_creator to hand asyncpg the libpq DSN (#9483)

* [Core] Use async_creator to hand asyncpg the libpq DSN

When the Postgres connection URI contains libpq query params (most
commonly `sslmode`, but also `sslcert`/`sslkey`/`sslrootcert`/`sslcrl`),
the async engine fails at connect time with:

    connect() got an unexpected keyword argument 'sslmode'

asyncpg recognizes those names only when parsing them out of a DSN
string itself; its keyword-arg path accepts only `ssl=`. SQLAlchemy's
asyncpg dialect parses the URL into kwargs and calls
`asyncpg.connect(**kwargs)`, so the libpq params end up as unknown
kwargs and asyncpg rejects them.

Instead of translating the URL ourselves (sslmode -> ssl, plus
SSLContext construction for cert-bearing URIs), use SQLAlchemy's
`async_creator` hook to bypass URL disassembly and hand asyncpg the
original DSN. asyncpg then handles every libpq URI param natively, no
translation table required.

Refs:
- https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6275#issuecomment-820227148
- https://github.com/MagicStack/asyncpg/issues/737

* [Test] Cover async_creator wiring for libpq sslmode in DB URI

Adds a regression test that asserts:
- the async engine wires an `async_creator` kwarg
- the creator, when awaited, calls `asyncpg.connect` with the original
  libpq DSN as a positional arg (so asyncpg's own DSN parser handles
  sslmode/sslcert/sslkey/sslrootcert/sslcrl)
- no libpq query param is leaked as a kwarg (which would trigger
  `connect() got an unexpected keyword argument 'sslmode'` from asyncpg)

Mock-based per existing convention in this file; no Docker/postgres
container needed.

* Don't rewrite conn_string; key engine cache by sync/async instead

asyncpg engine is built via async_creator and never uses conn_string for
connection params, so the postgresql+asyncpg:// rewrite was unnecessary.
Drop it and use a separate cache_key prefixed with 'async:' to keep sync
and async engines from colliding in the cache.

subject: [Test] Fix scale-test injection breaking on populated JSON columns (#9592)
message:
[Test] Fix scale-test injection breaking on populated JSON columns (#9592)

* [Test] Fix scale-test injection breaking on populated JSON columns

The managed-job sample row read back by ``inject_managed_jobs`` is fetched
via psycopg2's ``RealDictCursor``, which auto-deserializes ``spot.full_resources``
(and ``spot.links``) into Python ``dict``s. Passing those values back into
``cursor.execute`` raises ``can't adapt type 'dict'`` because no adapter is
registered for ``dict``, so injection silently returned 0 rows while
``main()`` still printed ``Data injection completed successfully!``.

That latent bug was masked because pre-#9483 the async DB engine could not
connect to URIs carrying libpq query params (``?sslmode=require``, which
AWS RDS always requires), so ``set_starting_async`` — the only writer of
``full_resources`` — silently failed and the column stayed NULL on the
sample. Once #9483 made async writes against SSL postgres URIs actually
work, ``full_resources`` started being populated and the injection
deterministically broke (Buildkite smoke-tests build 10525,
``test_large_production_performance@serial_kubernetes``).

Wrap dict/list values with ``psycopg2.extras.Json`` on the postgres path
so they're written back as JSON, and stop swallowing the exception in
``inject_managed_jobs`` so the bash harness fails loudly instead of
proceeding into Step 5 with zero rows.

* [Test] Mark scale-test managed-job clones as scheduler-INACTIVE

After fixing the dict-adapt bug, the injected managed-job rows started
carrying realistic per-row data cloned from the live template (including
schedule_state ALIVE, full_resources JSON, and current_cluster_name).
The consolidation-mode scheduler then treated each of the 12,500 clones
as a live managed job that needs reconciliation: per generated cluster
name, it tried to spawn a worker pod, blowing past the kind cluster's
4-CPU budget and causing Step 1 ("Creating sample terminated cluster")
to time out with "Insufficient cpu" (Buildkite build 10534).

These injected rows are synthetic, used for sky status / sky jobs queue
scale-perf tests; they have no real cluster behind them. Set
schedule_state = 'INACTIVE' (per ManagedJobScheduleState docstring:
"The job should be ignored by the scheduler") on every clone, and null
out current_cluster_name / full_resources so cluster-recovery and pool-
aware capacity accounting don't fire either.

Sky status still counts these rows as in-progress (the count comes from
non-terminal status, which we preserve), so the 12,501-in-progress
assertion in Step 5 continues to work — without the controller spawning
12,500 worker pods.

subject: [Jobs] Remove unused cleanup() hook from ManagedJobRuntime Protocol (#9595)
message:
[Jobs] Remove unused cleanup() hook from ManagedJobRuntime Protocol (#9595)

The cleanup() hook on ManagedJobRuntime was intended for runtimes that
need to release runtime-specific state on the cluster before cluster
termination. In practice, terminate_cluster (via
provision.terminate_instances) already deletes the underlying instances,
so any runtime that exposes its cluster-equivalent resources through the
provisioner ends up doing the same work twice.

Drop the hook from the Protocol, drop its module-level dispatcher, and
remove the call site in JobController._cleanup_cluster. Teardown now
runs exclusively via terminate_cluster.

If a future runtime needs a pre-teardown hook, it can be reintroduced
with a clearer contract that distinguishes runtime-state cleanup from
instance termination.

subject: [Test] Raise sky-status SLA in scale test from 18s to 25s (#9599)
message:
[Test] Raise sky-status SLA in scale test from 18s to 25s (#9599)

A survey of the last 30 same-config nightly builds (`nightly-build-pypi
--kubernetes --no-resource-heavy`, builds 10177..10560) recorded these
sky-status durations after the test injects 12,501 in-progress managed
jobs and queries `sky status`:

    12, 12, 13, 13, 15, 16, 16, 16, 17, 17, 17, 17, 17, 17,
    18, 18, 18, 18, 18, 18, 18, 18, 18,            ← old SLA
    19, 19, 21, 21, 21, 22

  min 12s  |  median 18s  |  max 22s

The median sat exactly on the 18s threshold and 52% of runs landed at
or above it, with 21% (6 / 29) outright exceeding it. The SLA was
mathematically a coin flip — Step 5 accounts for 8 of the 9 real test
failures in this window, not because sky status regressed but because
the threshold was chosen against a buggy baseline.

Why the baseline was buggy: until #9592 / commit d36889e72, the inject
script silently left `full_resources` NULL on every cloned row (the
sample's value came back as a Python dict via psycopg2 RealDictCursor
and the raw tuple insert failed with "can't adapt type 'dict'"; the
exception was swallowed and main() still printed "successfully"). With
that bug fixed the cloned rows now carry a populated JSON blob each,
sky status does strictly more JSON deserialization work per row, and
the distribution is expected to shift up by ~1-2s. The first three
post-fix nightlies already show 18s / 19s / 19s — 2 of 3 over the old
threshold.

25s covers 100% of historical observations with ~15% headroom while
still catching real regressions — e.g. the ~38s outlier observed
during #9592 debugging, when the controller was accidentally
reconciling every cloned managed-job row.

sky jobs queue (10s SLA, observed max 10s, never failed) and
sky jobs queue --all (30s SLA, observed max 24s, never failed) are
unchanged — they have margin.

   python_path, ray_path). When `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` is set, catalogs
   live at `$SKY_RUNTIME_DIR/.sky/catalogs/<version>/` (typically a
   per-runtime writable location, e.g. local disk inside a SkyPilot
   pod). When it isn't set, `runtime_utils.get_runtime_dir_path()`
   falls back to `~`, so laptops and plain VMs are unchanged.

2. Remove all filesystem side effects at `import sky`. Previously,
   `import sky` triggered three eager `os.makedirs` calls:
   - `catalog/common.py:35` at module load.
   - `read_catalog()` mkdirs the meta-dir on every call, fired
     transitively at module load by per-cloud catalog modules
     (aws_catalog, gcp_catalog, etc.) that call `read_catalog()`
     at module top level.
   - `get_catalog_path()` mkdirs on every call, used eagerly by
     `read_catalog()` and various module-level path stores.
   On environments where `~/.sky/catalogs` exists but is owned by a
   different user (shared NFS home setups), any of these would
   crash `import sky` with `PermissionError`, breaking even
   read-only commands like `sky status`.

Together (1) eliminates the bad-perm scenario for environments with
`SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` set (the catalog dir is on the running user's
writable location), and (2) makes `import sky` robust even on
environments WITHOUT `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` (the dir is created lazily by
`_update_catalog` only when something actually needs to write).

Changes:

- `sky/catalog/common.py`:
  - `_ABSOLUTE_VERSIONED_CATALOG_DIR` resolves via
    `runtime_utils.get_runtime_dir_path('.sky/catalogs/<version>')`.
  - Drop the module-level `os.makedirs` call.
  - `get_catalog_path()` becomes a pure path getter (no side
    effects). Documented in a comment.
  - Move the eager `os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(meta_path))` out of
    `read_catalog()` and into `_update_catalog`, right before the
    filelock + md5 file write. The eager call was firing on every
    `read_catalog()` invocation, including module-level ones.
  - `get_modified_catalog_file_mounts()` computes `local_path` from
    the SKY_RUNTIME_DIR-aware `_ABSOLUTE_VERSIONED_CATALOG_DIR`,
    not `os.path.expanduser(remote_path)`. `remote_path` stays
    `~/.sky/catalogs/<version>/<catalog>` so the file_mounts upload
    lands at the controller pod's `$HOME` (controllers that don't
    set `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` resolve to `$HOME` via the same
    `runtime_utils` default).
- `sky/catalog/aws_catalog.py`: `_get_az_mappings()` used to rely
  on `get_catalog_path()`'s mkdir side effect. With the pure-getter
  change, add explicit `os.makedirs` for both the catalog path and
  the meta path before the writes.
- `sky/clouds/aws.py`: `get_user_identities()` had the same
  implicit dependency on `get_catalog_path()`'s mkdir for the AWS
  user-identity cache write. Added explicit `os.makedirs` for the
  cache parent dir before the open-for-write.

`constants.CATALOG_DIR` (`'~/.sky/catalogs'`) is intentionally
unchanged. It is used only by `get_modified_catalog_file_mounts()`'s
`remote_path` computation, where the `~` is expanded by the
receiving controller pod's shell.

Tested:

- `import sky` with `chmod 555 ~/.sky/catalogs` (read-only dir) and
  no `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` set: succeeds. Without these changes it
  crashed with `PermissionError` at `catalog/common.py:35`.
- `import sky` with `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/runtime` set and a
  bad-perm `$HOME/.sky/catalogs`: also succeeds.
  `_ABSOLUTE_VERSIONED_CATALOG_DIR` resolves to
  `/tmp/runtime/.sky/catalogs/v8` as expected.
- `get_modified_catalog_file_mounts()` with `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` set
  and a fake locally-modified catalog: returns
  `{'~/.sky/catalogs/v8/aws/vms.csv': '/tmp/runtime/.sky/catalogs/v8/aws/vms.csv'}`
  with remote `$HOME`-relative and local SKY_RUNTIME_DIR-rooted as
  intended.
- End to end on a SkyPilot pod with `SKY_RUNTIME_DIR` set and
  `$HOME` on shared NFS with deliberately permission-corrupted
  `~/.sky/catalogs/`: `sky check`, `sky show-gpus`, and the
  `sky launch` optimizer step all succeed. Catalog files land at
  the SKY_RUNTIME_DIR-rooted location; `$HOME/.sky/catalogs/` is
  not touched.
- `format.sh`: 10.00/10. mypy passes.

subject: [Core] Add register_config_update_hook for post-update cache invalidation (#9616)
message:
[Core] Add register_config_update_hook for post-update cache invalidation (#9616)

* [Core] Add register_config_update_hook for post-update cache invalidation

Plugins that derive memoized state from the loaded config (e.g. a TTL-cached
query whose result depends on `get_nested(...)`) currently have no way to
react when the API server config changes through a path they don't control
(the dashboard's settings page, `workspaces.update_config`, etc.). The
result is stale plugin-side caches until the TTL expires.

Add a small hook mechanism in skypilot_config:

- `register_config_update_hook(fn)`: callable registry, populated at
  single-threaded server startup during plugin loading.
- After `update_api_server_config_no_lock` persists the new config and
  calls `reload_config()`, each registered hook is invoked once. Hook
  exceptions are caught and logged so a misbehaving hook cannot fail the
  config update itself.

This is the natural choke point — every API-server-side config write
funnels through `update_api_server_config_no_lock`, so a single hook
registration covers all write paths (current and future).

Test plan:
- Register a no-op hook at startup, edit the config via the dashboard's
  settings page, and confirm the hook fires exactly once after the
  config is reloaded.
- Replace the hook with one that raises; confirm the config update still
  completes and the exception is logged at WARNING.

* Apply suggestions from code review

subject: [Kubernetes] Surface truthful launching reason on cluster status badge (#9615)
message:
[Kubernetes] Surface truthful launching reason on cluster status badge (#9615)

* [Kubernetes] Add _unmask_crashloopbackoff_reason helper

Returns the underlying termination reason for a container in CrashLoopBackOff,
so callers can surface OOMKilled/Error etc. instead of the bare backoff state.
Will be consumed by the launch-time pending-reason logic in a follow-up commit.

* [Kubernetes] Add tier-1 container-status sweep for pending reason

New helper _get_pod_pending_reason_from_container_status walks a pod's
container_statuses to derive an authoritative pending reason for failure
modes that live on the container status (ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled hidden
behind CrashLoopBackOff, non-zero terminations). Not yet called from the
launch wait loop -- wired up in a follow-up commit.

* [Kubernetes] Replace event deny-list with tiered Warning + Normal allow-list

_get_pod_pending_reason now does a two-pass scan: Warning-type events win
unconditionally over Normal events, then a small allow-list of slow Normal
events (Pulling, Provisioning, WaitForFirstConsumer) is consulted. Drops
deceptive Normal events like SuccessfulAttachVolume that the old deny-list
let through. Caller signature unchanged.

* [Kubernetes] Wire tier-1 container-status sweep into _inspect_pod_status

Tier 1 now runs unconditionally before the phase-based branches. For
phase=Running pods with a CrashLoopBackOff container (today: silently
return None), the loop now surfaces the underlying OOMKilled / Error
reason in the LAUNCH_PROGRESS event. For phase=Pending pods that raise on
a bad waiting state, the raise message is enriched: CrashLoopBackOff is
unmasked to the underlying termination reason while the waiting.message
body (registry URL, back-off duration) is preserved.

Raise control flow is unchanged -- the set of pod states that produce
KubernetesError is identical to today; only the message string differs.

* [Kubernetes] Enrich _check_init_containers raise with unmasked reason

When an init container is in CrashLoopBackOff, the raised KubernetesError
now surfaces the underlying termination reason (e.g. OOMKilled) instead of
the bare 'CrashLoopBackOff' text. The waiting.message body is preserved.
Non-CrashLoopBackOff init failures get an explicit reason prefix in the
'Error details:' line, replacing the implicit reason-in-message-body
convention.

* [Test] Smoke test for ImagePullBackOff launch error

Verifies that a Kubernetes launch with an unresolvable image fails with
the kubelet's ImagePullBackOff/ErrImagePull reason in the error output --
regression guard for the truthful-launching-reason refactor.

* [Test] Drop internal spec path from test_launch_image_pull_back_off docstring

The docstring referenced a planning doc that doesn't ship with the OSS
repo. Replace with a code-anchored pointer.

* [Test] Smoke test for CreateContainerConfigError launch failure

Verifies that a Kubernetes launch with a missing-Secret envFrom reference
fails with CreateContainerConfigError (or CreateContainerError on older
k8s) in the error output -- covers the non-CrashLoopBackOff path of the
tier-1 container-status sweep.

* [Test] Smoke test for OOMKilled visibility during launch

Verifies that an OOM during a Kubernetes launch surfaces 'OOMKilled' in
the LAUNCH_PROGRESS cluster event (which powers the dashboard tooltip),
even though the launch itself does not raise -- the wait loop continues
on a Running-but-CrashLoopBackOff pod. Polls cluster_events for up to
3 minutes, then tears down the stuck cluster unconditionally.

* [Kubernetes] Wrap long docstring line in tier-1 helper

Fix pylint C0301: line 2255 was 82/80 cols. Reflow the bare-reason note
across two lines.

* [Test] Fix smoke-test pod-config YAML key + container name

Two bugs in the two new pod_config-using smoke tests:

1. Top-level `experimental:` is not a valid task-YAML key — SkyPilot rejects
   with InvalidSkyPilotConfigError. The correct key is `config:` (which
   maps to `_cluster_config_overrides` per task.py:904). The `config_overrides`
   nesting level is also dropped — `config:` already addresses that scope.
2. Container name `ray-head` doesn't match the SkyPilot k8s template
   (sky/templates/kubernetes-ray.yml.j2 uses `ray-node`). Overrides match
   by container name, so the wrong name silently no-ops.

Pattern verified against tests/test_yamls/test_k8s_ephemeral_storage_eviction.yaml.

* [Test] Fix OOM smoke test memory request/limit ordering

Previous attempt failed at sky-launch time with ResourcesUnavailableError
because the task requested 0.3 GiB (307 MiB) but the pod_config override
capped the limit at 256 MiB — request > limit is invalid for Kubernetes
memory, so SkyPilot couldn't acquire resources at all and the pod was
never created.

Adjust:
- request: 0.1 GiB (102 MiB) — comfortably below the limit, fits on kind
- limit: 256 MiB unchanged — tight enough that bytearray(1 << 30) OOMs
  immediately after Python startup (~30-50 MiB), with margin for the
  interpreter to actually start.

* [Test] Drop test_launch_oom_killed smoke test

The OOMKilled path is hard to trigger reliably as an end-to-end smoke
test: SkyPilot's default pod restartPolicy is 'Never', so an OOM moves
the pod straight to phase='Failed' (handled by the existing
_condensed_pod_reason path), never producing a LAUNCH_PROGRESS event
for the wait-loop's Tier-1 sweep to see.

The Tier-1 OOMKilled-unmask logic is fully covered by the unit tests
in TestUnmaskCrashloopbackoffReason and
TestGetPodPendingReasonFromContainerStatus; the other two K8s smoke
tests (ImagePullBackOff and CreateContainerConfigError) exercise the
end-to-end Tier-1 sweep on more reliably-reproducible failure modes.

* [Kubernetes] Defensive null-guards in pod status inspection

Address PR #9615 review feedback (gemini-code-assist):
- guard container_status.state before reading .waiting
- guard pod.status before reading .container_statuses
- fall back to 'Unknown' when waiting.reason is None in error messages

* [Kubernetes] Tighten tier-1 sweep docstring + ordering test + minor fixups

Address senior-reviewer feedback on PR #9615:
- Clarify in the tier-1 docstring that transient ContainerCreating /
  PodInitializing waiting reasons fall through to checks 2 and 3 on the
  *same* container, so a prior OOMKilled in last_state surfaces before
  advancing to the next container.
- New test pins multi-container ordering: container A transient + prior
  OOM beats container B's ImagePullBackOff.
- Guard last_term.exit_code against None before the != 0 check (k8s-client
  typing allows int | None).
- Align _unmask_crashloopbackoff_reason to the same `if cs.state else None`
  defensive idiom used by the tier-1 sweep.
- Reword the "today" comment near the phase=='Running' fall-through to be
  tense-neutral after merge.

subject: [Core] Cancel in-flight Skylet gRPC calls on SkyPilotContext cancel (#9620)
message:
[Core] Cancel in-flight Skylet gRPC calls on SkyPilotContext cancel (#9620)

* [Core] Cancel in-flight Skylet gRPC calls on SkyPilotContext cancel

When a SkyPilotContext is cancelled (e.g. on API client disconnect),
synchronous gRPC calls to Skylet kept blocking their worker thread inside
threading.Condition.wait() until the call's deadline fired. For streaming
calls like tail_logs the deadline is None, so the worker thread could be
held indefinitely, eventually exhausting the per-process
request_thread_executor pool (cap 128) and rejecting subsequent log /
streaming requests with ConcurrentWorkerExhaustedError.

This change closes the cancel path end-to-end:

- SkyPilotContext.register_cancel_callback / unregister_cancel_callback
  let blocking sync code react to ctx.cancel() (idempotent, race-safe,
  exception-isolated).
- invoke_grpc_unary / invoke_grpc_streaming wrappers in backend_utils use
  the gRPC future / iterator's .cancel() and register it with the active
  context, so a context cancel aborts the in-flight RPC instead of
  leaving the thread blocked.
- SkyletClient wires every stub method through a _CancelAwareStub proxy
  so all 25+ Skylet RPCs gain cancel support with one change.
- invoke_skylet_with_retries / invoke_skylet_streaming_with_retries bail
  on a pre-cancelled context so a cancel during backoff doesn't fan out
  into a new RPC nobody is waiting on.
- get_grpc_channel gains keepalive options (30s ping, 10s timeout,
  permit_without_calls=1) as a backstop for half-dead TCP connections.

Tested:
- pytest tests/unit_tests/test_context_cancel_callbacks.py
  tests/unit_tests/test_skylet_grpc_cancellable.py — 15 passed.
- Repro against a real API server: 900 concurrent streaming POST /logs
  with hard-killed clients leaked 580 stuck threads (never drained)
  pre-fix; same workload leaves 0 stuck threads within 5s post-fix.

* Address review: forward *args/**kwargs and raise CancelledError on ctx-cancel

- invoke_grpc_unary / invoke_grpc_streaming now accept *args, **kwargs
  and forward them to the underlying gRPC method, so callers can pass
  metadata / credentials / wait_for_ready unchanged.
- When the gRPC call is cancelled because the surrounding SkyPilotContext
  was cancelled, the gRPC CANCELLED RpcError is re-raised as
  asyncio.CancelledError. This makes _execute_request_coroutine classify
  the request as CANCELLED rather than FAILED.
- _CancelAwareStub wrappers also use *args, **kwargs.
- Unit tests assert both behaviors and that extra gRPC options
  (metadata, wait_for_ready) are forwarded.

* [Test] Install fresh asyncio loop for cancel-callback tests on py3.9

SkyPilotContext.__init__ constructs asyncio.Event(), which on Python 3.9
calls get_event_loop() in the main thread. If an earlier test in the same
xdist worker has called set_event_loop(None) (or otherwise tripped the
"_set_called" flag), the lazy main-thread loop auto-creation is disabled
and the call raises "There is no current event loop in thread
'MainThread'". Add an autouse fixture that installs a fresh loop per test
so the tests are robust to the worker's prior state.

[metrics] Raise per-context timeout to 20s for large GPU fleets

The /gpu-metrics endpoint port-forwards to skypilot-prometheus-server in
each remote context and runs a /federate query. On large clusters (e.g.

Prometheus that scrapes /gpu-metrics doesn't itself time out.

subject: [Jobs] Speed up pool dashboard with batched query and indexes (#9636)
message:
[Jobs] Speed up pool dashboard with batched query and indexes (#9636)

* [Jobs] Speed up pool dashboard with batched query and indexes

When a job_info table accumulates tens of thousands of finished jobs, the
pool dashboard's per-pool job lookups (called once per pool, then once
per replica) all degrade into full table scans, and the pools page can
take a long time to render. This change cuts that cost in two places:

- N+1 -> 1 query: serve_utils._get_service_status batches the per-replica
  used_by lookups via the new
  managed_job_state.get_nonterminal_job_ids_by_pool_grouped, which
  returns jobs keyed by current_cluster_name in one round-trip. The
  previous code path issued (1 + len(replicas)) queries per pool.

- Add indexes that the existing per-pool / skip_finished queries rely on
  for filtering: ix_job_info_pool, ix_job_info_current_cluster_name,
  ix_spot_status. Alembic migration 020 creates them idempotently inside
  an autocommit_block so SQLite and PostgreSQL deployments both upgrade
  cleanly without blocking writes.

Also fixes a long-standing semantic bug in the pool-level used_by
calculation. The original code intended pool-level jobs to mean "have
pool set but no cluster_name" (e.g. batch coordinators that span every
worker), but the helper it called treated cluster_name=None as "no
filter" rather than "IS NULL", which silently surfaced every other
replica's jobs on every READY worker. The grouped query lets us
implement the intended semantic exactly via jobs_by_cluster.get(None).
This change is normally hidden when a pool has at most one nonterminal
job per replica, which is why the regression was not caught earlier.

Tested:
- pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/jobs/test_state.py
  tests/unit_tests/test_serve_utils.py (39 passed)
- bash format.sh (yapf/isort/mypy clean)

subject: [Kubernetes] Allow excluding in-cluster context from `allowed_contexts: all` (#9637)
message:
[Kubernetes] Allow excluding in-cluster context from `allowed_contexts: all` (#9637)

* [Kubernetes] Allow excluding in-cluster context from `allowed_contexts: all`

When the SkyPilot API server runs inside Kubernetes, the pod's own host
cluster is discoverable as an `in-cluster` context. With
`allowed_contexts: all` (or `SKYPILOT_ALLOW_ALL_KUBERNETES_CONTEXTS=true`),
that in-cluster context is included alongside uploaded kubeconfig contexts,
which is surprising on hosted deployments where the API server's own
cluster shouldn't be a user-facing compute target.

This change adds an opt-in flag to exclude `in-cluster` from the `'all'`
expansion. Default is unchanged (in-cluster included) for backward
compatibility.

Two layers, in resolution order (highest first):
1. env var `SKYPILOT_ALL_KUBERNETES_CONTEXTS_INCLUDES_IN_CLUSTER` —
   operator-level, set on the API server pod by hosted deployments so
   tenant admins can't expose the host cluster by editing config.
2. config field `kubernetes.all_includes_in_cluster` (bool, workspace
   and global scope, default true) — admin-level switch.

Explicit listings (`allowed_contexts: ['in-cluster', ...]`) always honor
the listing regardless of this flag. The `allowed_contexts: None` →
in-cluster fallback path (no kubeconfig present) is also unaffected.

Tested:

  backward-compat behavior, config false, env var overriding config in both

subject: [Dashboard] Quieter upgrade banner: ignore aborts, hidden tabs, single flaps (#9654)
message:
[Dashboard] Quieter upgrade banner: ignore aborts, hidden tabs, single flaps (#9654)

* [Dashboard] Quieter upgrade banner: ignore aborts, hidden tabs, single flaps

The upgrade-aware fetch interceptor currently flips into "deployment
is undergoing upgrades" on any thrown fetch from a non-static request.
That's correct for true outages, but it also fires for benign reasons
that have nothing to do with the server, especially on mobile:

  - Page navigation / React unmount cancels in-flight polls
    (AbortError). The banner flashes whenever the user switches
    routes while a status poll is in flight.
  - iOS Safari aborts pending fetches as `TypeError: Load failed`
    when the user switches apps or the tab backgrounds. Coming
    back to the tab then briefly shows the banner before the next
    poll succeeds.
  - A single dropped request on a flaky Wi-Fi handoff also trips
    it; real upgrades produce a sustained stream of failures
    instead.

Filter those three cases before calling reportUpgrade(): skip
AbortError, skip when `document.visibilityState === 'hidden'`, and
require two thrown fetches within a 4s window. The 503 path is
unchanged, so the GracefulShutdownMiddleware + nginx no-backend
cases still surface the banner instantly. A successful 2xx response
resets the streak counter so an old failure can't team up with a
fresh one minutes later.

Tested:
- Open dashboard, navigate between pages rapidly while a status
  poll is in flight: no banner.
- Hide the tab (cmd-tab away in Safari), wait for in-flight fetches
  to abort, switch back: no banner (was flashing before).
- Stop the API server (simulating an upgrade): banner appears
  within ~one poll cycle once a second consecutive request throws.
- Start the server back up: banner clears on the next 2xx.

* [Dashboard] apiInterceptor: don't prime flap window with benign errors

Address review feedback: the catch handler was updating
_lastFetchErrorAt unconditionally — before applying the AbortError /
static-asset / hidden-tab filters. A benign throw could then "start
the clock" and a single subsequent real error within 4s would
satisfy `sustained` and fire the banner. That's exactly the
false-positive case the flap window was added to prevent.

Move the timestamp update inside the qualifying-error branch so
only real, foreground, non-cancelled failures advance the window.

Also rewrap the tabHidden line so prettier --check passes.

* [Dashboard] apiInterceptor: drop flap window, keep benign-error filters

Addresses review feedback: the 4s flap window was shorter than the
standard 30s dashboard poll interval (sky/dashboard/src/lib/config.js),
so on pages that fire a single fetch per cycle (clusters, jobs, etc.)
the two-failures-in-4s rule could never trigger and reportUpgrade()
never fired through the error path. That regressed detection of
Recreate-strategy deploys where the pod goes connection-refused
without a 503.

The flap window was originally added to absorb single Wi-Fi blips,
but the actual user-visible noise that motivated this change is
already handled by the benign-error filters introduced in the
previous commits (AbortError, static asset, hidden tab). Drop the
window and let any qualifying error fire the banner on the first
failed poll, like before.

Net behavior vs. master:
  - Real outage on a single-fetch page: banner fires on first
    failed poll (same as master).
  - Page navigation cancelling a poll (AbortError): no banner
    (was flashing on master).
  - Backgrounding the tab on iOS: no banner (was flashing on
    master).

subject: [Slurm] Let users override --time and fall back to DefaultTime when MaxTime is UNLIMITED (#9633)
message:
[Slurm] Let users override --time and fall back to DefaultTime when MaxTime is UNLIMITED (#9633)

* [Slurm] Let users override --time and prefer DefaultTime over MaxTime

Today the SLURM provisioner hard-codes #SBATCH --time={partition_MaxTime}.
On partitions with MaxTime=UNLIMITED this becomes --time=UNLIMITED, which
the backfill scheduler refuses to schedule ahead of a maintenance
reservation — the job hangs with "ReqNodeNotAvail, Reserved for
maintenance". Users also could not override --time via sbatch_options
because 'time' was in _SBATCH_PROTECTED_OPTIONS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Slurm] Preserve MaxTime-first dispatch, use DefaultTime only when MaxTime is unset

Pre-existing code always emitted #SBATCH --time={partition.MaxTime} and
ignored DefaultTime entirely. Some users rely on jobs receiving the
partition's MaxTime by default, so DefaultTime is now consulted only
when MaxTime is UNLIMITED — which is precisely the #9370 scenario
where emitting --time=UNLIMITED makes the backfill scheduler refuse
to schedule ahead of maintenance reservations.

Docstring records the rationale for the inverse preference as a
TODO(dev) for a future flip.

* [Slurm] Align _DEFAULT_TIME_REGEX with the strict _MAXTIME_REGEX style

* [Slurm] Trim duplicated test cases per audit

- Replace test_time_accepted_formats (6) + test_time_invalid_format_raises (7)
  with a single test_time_validator_wired smoke test. The exhaustive
  accepted/rejected format grid already lives in TestValidateSbatchTime;

* [Slurm] Fold _compute_time_directive into a single _build_sbatch_directives call

Combine auto-generated --time + user-supplied options into one block at
the bottom of the SBATCH directives instead of threading two separate
substitutions through the script template. Keeps _compute_time_directive
as a standalone helper for focused unit tests; adds a thin wrapper

Also drop the trailing newline from _compute_time_directive's return so
the wrapper can join lines cleanly. Regenerate the two script snapshot
tests to reflect the new directive ordering.
