subject: [Kubernetes] Probe Ray ports when pod has hostNetwork: true (#9644)
message:
[Kubernetes] Probe Ray ports when pod has hostNetwork: true (#9644)

* [Kubernetes] Probe Ray ports when pod has hostNetwork: true

Pods with hostNetwork: true share the host's network namespace, so
Ray's default GCS/dashboard/object/node-manager/etc. ports bind
directly on the host. A second SkyPilot pod scheduled to the same
node (common for fractional-GPU workloads) collides on those ports
and fails to admit.

When hostNetwork: true is detected in kubernetes.pod_config, the
head pod runs a stdlib-only probe that binds ephemeral sockets to
pick a free Ray port set, publishes the chosen GCS/dashboard ports
to a <cluster>-ray-ports ConfigMap, then closes the sockets right
before ray start binds them. Worker pods poll the ConfigMap for the
head's GCS port (the head IP is already discoverable via the
existing headless Service DNS), probe their own local-bind ports,
then TCP-wait for the head's GCS to accept before invoking
ray start --address.

Port flags now use ${VAR:-default} / ${VAR:+--flag=$VAR} shell
substitution so non-hostNetwork clusters see bit-identical
behavior. ~/.sky/ray_port.json schema is unchanged (still ray_port
+ ray_dashboard_port); the dict expression just reads from env vars
with fallback to the SkyPilot constants. No API version bump
needed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Set ownerReference on ray-ports ConfigMap

When the probe creates the <cluster>-ray-ports ConfigMap, point its
ownerReference at the head pod (looked up by HOSTNAME -> pod UID).
K8s garbage-collects the ConfigMap when the head pod is deleted, so
sky down cleans it up automatically — no extra teardown logic.

controller=false (we don't manage the pod), blockOwnerDeletion=false
(deleting the pod doesn't wait on us). If a stale ConfigMap from a
prior head pod still exists, the PUT path refreshes its ownerReference
to the current head pod so cleanup catches it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Quote k8s_env_vars values when rendering pod env

The pod env emit at kubernetes-ray.yml.j2:560 rendered values bare:

    - name: {{ key }}
      value: {{ value }}

For string values like "1" (added by the hostNetwork probe wiring),
the bare emit produced `value: 1` in YAML, which then parses as a
Go int. K8s rejects the pod with:

    Pod in version "v1" cannot be handled as a Pod: json: cannot
    unmarshal number into Go struct field EnvVar.spec.containers.env
    .value of type string

Switch to `value: {{ value | tojson }}` so the rendered YAML always
quotes the value. Strict improvement — also covers `"true"`/`"false"`
and any future int- or bool-looking env var content.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Get pod identity via downward API, not HOSTNAME

The ownerReference probe path read pod identity from $HOSTNAME and
then GET'd the pod by that name to fetch its UID. Under hostNetwork:
true the container inherits the host node's hostname (e.g.
gke-sj-cluster-default-pool-df654ef1-c3cx), so the GET 404'd:

    RuntimeError: Failed to GET pod default/gke-...-c3cx to derive
    the ConfigMap ownerReference: status=404

Inject metadata.name and metadata.uid via the K8s downward API
(SKYPILOT_POD_NAME / SKYPILOT_POD_UID) in kubernetes-ray.yml.j2,
matching the existing SKYPILOT_POD_NODE_TYPE pattern, and read both
from the env. Drops the _get_pod_uid HTTP roundtrip entirely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Make RAY_HEAD_WAIT_INITIALIZED_COMMAND port-aware

constants.RAY_STATUS hardcodes RAY_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:6380. After the
hostNetwork probe binds Ray to a dynamic free port, the post-start
wait loop dials 6380 and prints a noisy connection-refused traceback:

    ray.exceptions.RpcError: failed to connect to all addresses;
    last error: UNKNOWN: ipv4:10.x.x.x:6380: Failed to connect to
    remote host: Connection refused

The probe already exports SKYPILOT_RAY_PORT into the bash env right
before ray start; use it via ${SKYPILOT_RAY_PORT:-DEFAULT} so the
loop dials the actual port. Non-hostNetwork bootstraps keep the same
behavior because the env var stays unset and falls back to
SKY_REMOTE_RAY_PORT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Invoke host_network_probe by file path

The K8s bootstrap template re-installs skypilot from PyPI right after
installing the dev wheel (kubernetes-ray.yml.j2 line ~1067):

    uv pip install skypilot[kubernetes,remote]

with no version pin. uv excludes pre-releases by default, so the
`1.0.0.dev0` wheel just installed gets downgraded to PyPI's latest
stable (`0.12.1`). The resulting install is half-baked — bootstrap's
own `from sky.skylet.ray_patches import patch` happens to take a path
that works, but the host_network_probe was invoked as

    python -m sky.provision.kubernetes.host_network_probe

which triggers a full `sky/__init__.py` import and hits the broken
side:

    ImportError: cannot import name 'common_utils' from 'sky.utils'

The probe module is stdlib-only — it never needed the parent package.
Invoke it by file path via sysconfig.get_paths()['purelib'] (which
doesn't import sky), so the broken __init__ can't take the probe
down. The PyPI-downgrade in the template is a separate latent issue
that this PR does not address.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Read ~/.sky/ray_port.json without importing sky

The health-check poll's port-reading step ran `python -c "from sky.skylet
import job_lib; print(job_lib.get_ray_port())" 2>/dev/null || echo 6379`.
That swallows any import error silently and falls back to legacy port 6379,
which never matches anything modern. On pods where the bootstrap's
unsuppressed PyPI downgrade leaves sky/__init__.py partially importable,
the poll silently targeted 6379, never saw Ray on the probed port, and the
provisioner ate its full 90s timeout before SSH-launching ray start as a
fallback.

Read the file directly with stdlib json — no sky import, no silent
sky/__init__ regression risk. Also bump the fallback from legacy 6379 to
SKY_REMOTE_RAY_PORT (6380) since any cluster after #1790 lands on 6380.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Inline host_network_probe via heredoc

The K8s bootstrap installs stable skypilot from PyPI BEFORE
ray_head_start_command runs in the pod — the dev wheel ships later
in the template via skypilot_wheel_installation_commands (line ~1635
in kubernetes-ray.yml.j2). So at probe time, the probe file from the
dev wheel doesn't yet exist in site-packages:

    can't open file '/.../sky/provision/kubernetes/host_network_probe.py':
    [Errno 2] No such file or directory

Read the probe source once at module import (relative to
instance_setup.py's __file__) and embed it via a single-quoted bash
heredoc in the probe-cmd snippet. The bash command becomes
self-shipping: it writes /tmp/sky_host_network_probe.py from the
inlined content on every run, then executes it. No dependency on
what skypilot version the pod happens to have installed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Base64-encode inlined probe to stay YAML-safe

The previous heredoc form embedded the probe content as multi-line
text in the bash command. When Jinja interpolated that into
{{ ray_head_start_command }} in kubernetes-ray.yml.j2, the column-0
lines from inside the heredoc landed inside a block-scalar at
unexpected indentation, breaking the cluster-yaml parse:

    yaml error (ScannerError): while scanning a simple key
      ...
    could not find expected ':'

Switch to a single-line `echo '<b64>' | base64 -d > /tmp/...` so the
whole inlined payload stays on one bash line — YAML can't misparse a
single line of a block scalar. Adds two tests that pin the
single-line shape and round-trip the b64 payload back to the actual
probe source.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Kubernetes] Drop pod-spec containerPort list under hostNetwork

K8s' NodePorts scheduling predicate treats containerPort declarations
as hostPort reservations when the pod has hostNetwork: true. With the
template's static list of 5 ports (22, ray GCS, 10001, dashboard,
46590), a second SkyPilot cluster on the same node fails to schedule:

    Predicate NodePorts failed: node(s) didn't have free ports for
    the requested pod ports

The Ray ports in that list are also stale under hostNetwork because
the probe assigns them dynamically — the declaration would block
co-scheduling even on ports the first cluster never actually used.

Gate the entire `ports:` block on `not k8s_host_network`. When
hostNetwork is off, containerPort is purely informational and Services
already dial via targetPort, so existing clusters behave the same.

Known follow-up (not in this commit): under hostNetwork, the host's
real port 22 (sshd) and 46590 (skylet gRPC) still genuinely conflict
between sibling clusters; they need probe-driven port selection
similar to Ray's. For workloads that don't need a second cluster's
SSH and only need Ray itself to share the node (the RoCE/RDMA case),
this commit unblocks scheduling.

[Kubernetes] Set dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet under hostNetwork

When a pod has hostNetwork: true, Kubernetes silently downgrades the
default dnsPolicy from ClusterFirst to Default — the pod inherits the
node's /etc/resolv.conf and loses access to cluster DNS. The worker
probe then can't resolve

  ${cluster}-head.${ns}.svc.cluster.local

and blocks forever in _wait_head_gcs_tcp, even though the head pod is
healthy and reachable by node IP.

Render dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet on the pod spec whenever the
detected hostNetwork flag is set. Users who supply their own dnsPolicy
in cluster_config_overrides.pod_config still win — that override is
merged in via combine_pod_config_fields after the template renders.

[Kubernetes] Probe pod sshd port under hostNetwork

Under hostNetwork the K8s node's own sshd already owns host:22, so the
pod's bootstrap `service ssh restart` silently fails to bind and dies.
All in-pod traffic to localhost:22 (kubectl exec... nc, etc.) then
lands on the node's sshd, which has no `sky` user / no SkyPilot
authorized_keys — every subsequent `ssh <cluster>` returns Permission
denied (publickey).

Extend the existing Ray-port probe so each pod (head + each worker)
also probes a free port for its sshd and publishes it back into the
same `<cluster>-ray-ports` ConfigMap under key `sshd_<podname>`:

* host_network_probe.py: add `sshd` to both _HEAD_PORT_NAMES and
  _WORKER_PORT_NAMES, key it as `sshd_<podname>` in the ConfigMap
  data so multiple pods don't clobber each other. Workers GET +
  merge + PUT (with 409 retry) since the head created the ConfigMap.
* instance_setup.py: extend the hostNetwork probe bash snippet to
  delete any existing `Port ...` line from /etc/ssh/sshd_config,
  append `Port ${SKYPILOT_SSHD_PORT}`, and restart sshd. Gated on
  SKYPILOT_SSHD_PORT being set so non-hostNetwork bootstraps are
  unaffected.
* kubernetes/instance.py: read each pod's `sshd_<podname>` from the
  ConfigMap when building InstanceInfo, fall back to 22 if absent.
  Poll the ConfigMap (180s budget) for hostNetwork pods so the
  cached SSH config doesn't lock in 22 right after launch.
* server.py kubernetes_pod_ssh_proxy: use the head pod's recorded
  ssh_port (`handle.cached_external_ssh_ports[0]`) for kubectl
  port-forward instead of hardcoded 22. The inner ssh in the
  ProxyCommand already inherits the right port via `-W [%h]:%p`
  once the SSH config's `Port` directive is right.
* tests: cover the per-pod ConfigMap keying, env-file output for
  SKYPILOT_SSHD_PORT, and the sshd-rebind snippet.

[Kubernetes] Bind raylet to a per-pod loopback IP under hostNetwork

Two SkyPilot pods on the same K8s node under hostNetwork: true share
the host's IP, so both raylets register in GCS with the same
node_manager_address (only node_manager_port differs). The driver's
CoreWorker fetches node info once at startup and caches an
(IP, port) channel per NodeID; when both NodeIDs collapse onto the
same IP, the cached channel can race to the wrong raylet's port and
every subsequent RequestWorkerLease is sent there. Bundle 0's
reservation check never reaches its raylet, pg.ready() never
resolves, and the job hangs in sky_job_1's ray.get(). The race is
why the failure is intermittent — sometimes the driver caches the
right port; sometimes it doesn't.

Probe a deterministic 127.<H1>.<H2>.<rank> per pod (cluster-id hash
in H1/H2, head=.0/worker<N>=.N in the last byte) and pass it via
--node-ip-address. 127.0.0.0/8 routes wholly to lo with no
CAP_NET_ADMIN, so every pod on the same K8s node can dial every
other pod's loopback. Distinct IPs disambiguate Ray's NodeID ->
endpoint cache and the scheduler routes correctly.

The head publishes its loopback in the <cluster>-ray-ports ConfigMap
under head_node_ip; the worker reads it and overrides
SKYPILOT_RAY_HEAD_IP so its --address dials the head over the
loopback.

Non-hostNetwork bootstraps are unchanged: SKYPILOT_RAY_NODE_IP stays
unset, the \${VAR:+...} flag substitution emits nothing, and Ray
falls back to its own IP auto-detection.

Scope note: cross-node hostNetwork is out of scope — host IPs are
already distinct there, so the underlying race doesn't trigger. The
worker's loopback override would break a worker scheduled to a
different K8s node than the head, but that combination is already
broken upstream of this change.

subject: [CI] Fix shell injection in run-python-tests composite action (#9666)
message:
[CI] Fix shell injection in run-python-tests composite action (#9666)

* [CI] Fix shell injection in run-python-tests composite action

The set_env step in .github/actions/run-python-tests/action.yaml
interpolates ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }},
${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}, ${{ github.head_ref }}, and
similar untrusted contexts directly into a bash run script. When the
value contains backticks around what bash treats as a command (or other
shell metacharacters), bash performs command substitution on the runner.

PR #9531 already applied the env-var indirection pattern to
.github/workflows/pytest.yml, but the python-test matrix jobs were later
moved to this composite action, which still carried the original unsafe
pattern. The limited-deps-test and failover-test jobs (still inline in
pytest.yml) were protected; the 6 composite-action jobs were not.

This caused the Python Tests workflow on master to fail with
"syntax error near unexpected token 'only'" on commit 3fc18abcd
([Kubernetes] Probe Ray ports when pod has hostNetwork: true), whose
squashed body contains many backtick-quoted code spans.

Apply the same intermediate-environment-variable pattern as #9531:
lift each ${{ ... }} into the step's env: block and reference it via
$VAR in the script body. Same set_env outputs (branch, message); only
the path from ${{ ... }} to bash literal is replaced.

* [CI] Use printf for untrusted values in set_env heredoc

Address Gemini Code Assist review: echo treats values starting with -n,
-e, -E as option flags, which would drop the trailing newline and
collapse the heredoc EOF onto the same line as the title/message,
breaking the GITHUB_OUTPUT multiline format.

Switch the three untrusted-value emits (PR_TITLE,
MERGE_GROUP_HEAD_COMMIT_MESSAGE, HEAD_COMMIT_MESSAGE) to
printf '%s\n', which prints the string literally regardless of its
leading characters. The literal echo lines (branch=, message<<EOF,
EOF) stay as-is since their content is fixed.

* [Test] Mock get_remote_api_version in api_login user_hash tests

test_api_login_user_hash_needs_auth and
test_api_login_user_hash_needs_auth_both call client_sdk.api_login(),
which since #8590 (polling auth) gates a code path on
versions.get_remote_api_version() >= 30. Neither test mocked
get_remote_api_version, relying on the contextvar default of None to
make the gate False.

Some other unit test in the suite leaves a non-None value behind in
versions.get_remote_api_version (or the underlying _remote_api_version
contextvar). Because of pytest-xdist worksteal, whether these tests
land on the same worker as the polluting test depends on shard
composition. Commit 3fc18abcd added ~76 lines of new unit tests, which
shifted the shard layout and put the polluting test on the same worker
for the first time. The api_login tests then evaluated
`Mock() >= 30` and raised TypeError.

Patch get_remote_api_version to return None inside both tests' with
blocks (matching the fix from PR #9659). The tests now assert the
non-polling path explicitly regardless of cross-test contextvar state.

subject: [API] Skip request env overlay for internal daemon requests (#9663)
message:
[API] Skip request env overlay for internal daemon requests (#9663)

* [API] Skip request env overlay for internal daemon requests

`override_request_env_and_config` overlays `request_body.env_vars` onto
`os.environ` for every dequeued request. For client requests this is
correct — the executor temporarily takes on the client's identity. For
internal daemon requests (e.g. `managed-job-status-refresh-daemon`),
however, the persisted `env_vars` were captured when the daemon was
first scheduled, which may have been by a previous deployment generation
of the API server pod. Overlaying that stale snapshot clobbers the
current pod's actual downward-API values (`SKYPILOT_POD_MEMORY_BYTES_LIMIT`,
`SKYPILOT_POD_CPU_CORE_LIMIT`, `SKYPILOT_APISERVER_UUID`, etc.).

This was observed to make `common_utils.get_mem_size_gb()` inside the
daemon return `0.0977` (the stale 100 MiB) instead of the pod's actual
~300 GiB, breaking `controller_utils.get_number_of_jobs_controllers()`
and downstream controller scaling logic.

Fix: short-circuit the env-vars overlay (and a few client-only steps
like `add_or_update_user` and the workspace permission check) for
daemon request ids. The shared try/finally that restores `os.environ`
on exit is kept for both paths, so daemons that mutate `os.environ`
inside the with block (e.g. `InternalRequestDaemon.run_event` setting
`SKYPILOT_DISABLE_LOGGING=1`) don't leak that mutation to the next
request handled by the same worker.

Tested:
* Unit: 3 new tests in test_executor.py covering (a) daemon path
  doesn't overlay env_vars, (b) client path still does (regression
  guard), (c) env mutations inside the daemon with block are still
  reverted on exit.
* Manual repro: a script that seeds os.environ with current-pod values,
  enters `override_request_env_and_config` with a daemon request id and
  stale env_vars, and calls `common_utils.get_mem_size_gb()`. Without
  the fix it returns 0.0977 GiB; with the fix it returns 300.0 GiB.

-Claude

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Address review: drop unneeded workspace-check gate, set UserType.SYSTEM

Two review comments on PR #9663:

1. Setting `user_type=models.UserType.SYSTEM.value` on the `models.User`
   constructed for daemon requests, matching the convention used in
   `prepare_request_async` for `is_skypilot_system=True` requests.

2. Dropping the `not is_daemon` gate on the workspace permission check.
   The SkyPilot system user has admin role
   (`sky/users/permission.py` line 408 short-circuits to True for
   admins), so the check passes anyway — the gate added complexity
   without functional benefit.

[CLI] sky api login: continue polling when browser cannot be opened (#9676)

[CLI] sky api login: continue polling auth when browser cannot be opened

The polling-based login flow only needs the user to visit the auth URL
and click Authorize — it does not require the browser to be on the same
machine as the CLI. Previously, when `open_browser` failed (e.g. on a
headless server), `_try_polling_auth` bailed out and the CLI fell
through to the localhost-callback flow (which also can't open a
browser) and then to manual token entry.

Now, when the browser can't be opened locally, print the auth URL and
ask the user to open it themselves, then continue polling as usual.

subject: [Jobs] Fix log_tail fork bomb on HA controller pod restart (#9404)
message:
[Jobs] Fix log_tail fork bomb on HA controller pod restart (#9404)

* [Jobs] Fix log_tail fork bomb on HA controller pod restart

On HA jobs controller pod restart, log_tail() treats every file
matching ~/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log as new and spawns a tail+mylsof
loop per file. The PVC retains task logs from all prior jobs
(including completed ones), so thousands of stale logs each get a
monitor_file child. mylsof scans /proc/*/fd/* per tick, and its
cost grows with the process count -- producing runaway fork growth
and CPU saturation on the replacement pod.

Fix:
- Pre-seed already_monitored with every file present at startup so
  they are never tailed. Those jobs are already complete; their
  stdout has already been written.
- Switch already_monitored from a space-separated string checked
  with `echo | grep -q` to a bash associative array, replacing the
  O(n) per-file membership test (O(n^2) across the outer loop) with
  O(1).

New files created after startup are still picked up as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] log_tail: bash-native glob (ARG_MAX-safe, space-safe)

Address Gemini review feedback. The previous version used
`ls $(eval echo $FILE_PATTERN)` and `for f in $(eval echo ...)`,
which had two issues:

1. ARG_MAX: at ~55-60k files the expansion exceeds /usr/bin/ls's
   exec arg limit (3.2 MB on the controller pod), so the pre-seed
   `if ls ...` quietly fails and the next `while ! ls` hangs.
2. Word-splitting: a space anywhere in the expanded path (e.g.
   in $HOME) splits one file into two non-existent entries.

Replace all three call sites with a bash-native glob,
`for f in "$HOME"/sky_logs/*/tasks/*.log`, under `shopt -s nullglob`
so an empty match is a no-op. `log_tail` runs in a `log_tail &`
subshell, so the shopt does not leak. Pass file paths into
monitor_file as a positional arg and quote them throughout.

Verified with shell sims at 60k stale files and with $HOME
containing a space; pre-seed skips all stale files and a new
file created after startup is still picked up.

-Claude

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Kubernetes] Accept dict[K, V] openapi_types from kubernetes>=36 (#9682)
message:
[Kubernetes] Accept dict[K, V] openapi_types from kubernetes>=36 (#9682)

* [Kubernetes] Accept dict[K, V] openapi_types from kubernetes>=36

kubernetes==36.0.0 (released 2026-05-20) switched the dict openapi_types
representation from 'dict(K, V)' to 'dict[K, V]'. PodValidator's regex
only matched the parens form, so every sky launch --cloud kubernetes
fails on metadata.labels with:

  Validation error in metadata.labels:
  No module named 'kubernetes.client.models.dict[str, str]'

(getattr on kubernetes.client.models triggers its lazy importlib loader.)

This affects every fresh PyPI install of skypilot[kubernetes] /
skypilot-nightly[kubernetes] / Docker images built today onwards, on
all SkyPilot releases v0.8.0 -> 0.12.2 + every nightly, because the pin
'kubernetes>=20.0.0,!=32.0.0' is open. Existing installs that already
have kubernetes<36 keep working.

Fix: extend the regex to accept either dict(K, V) or dict[K, V].

Also add a hotpatch (hotpatch_dict_openapi_types.py) that rewrites the
same regex in the installed base wheel during backward-compat tests,
so /quicktest-core --base-branch pypi/skypilot-nightly --kubernetes
passes against published wheels that don't yet contain this fix.

Fixes Buildkite quicktest-core build #3239.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Handle external_ips rename in kubernetes>=36

Second breakage from the kubernetes==36.0.0 PyPI release (2026-05-20):
V1ServiceSpec.external_i_ps was renamed to external_ips. sky/provision/
kubernetes/network_utils.py reads this attribute during `sky serve` to
get the ingress IP, so every `sky serve up` against k8s fails with:

  AttributeError: 'V1ServiceSpec' object has no attribute 'external_i_ps'.
  Did you mean: 'external_ips'?

Read both attributes with getattr fallback so the code works against
both pre-36 (external_i_ps) and 36+ (external_ips) clients.

Also rename hotpatch_dict_openapi_types.py -> hotpatch_kubernetes36.py
and extend it to patch the external_ips call site in the base wheel,
since both issues stem from the same upstream release. The dict[K, V]
patch logic is unchanged.

Fixes Buildkite quicktest-core build #3246 (test_serve_deployment).

subject: [Serve] Fix HA recovery double-spawn, catastrophic cleanup, and init lock race (#9683)
message:
[Serve] Fix HA recovery double-spawn, catastrophic cleanup, and init lock race (#9683)

* [Serve] Fix HA recovery double-spawn, catastrophic cleanup, and init lock race

Follow-up to PR #9578. Three regressions surfaced post-merge:

1. Catastrophic cleanup on boot timeout. When _wait_for_controller_ready
   raised RuntimeError, the comment claimed "DB state untouched" but the
   `raise` fell through to `_start`'s outer `finally`, which called
   `_cleanup` -> `remove_ha_recovery_script` and, on pools with no
   replicas, `remove_service_completely` — silently deleting the
   service row + version_specs. Fix: extract `_bail_on_boot_failure`
   that SIGKILLs the controller subprocess then `os._exit(1)` to bypass
   the finally entirely (mirrors `_orphan_exit`).

2. Recovery double-spawn during boot window. Controller boot can take
   up to SERVICE_REGISTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (60s); the daemon iterates
   every ~20s. During that window DB controller_pid stayed stale, so
   the daemon re-fired the recovery script, piling up multiple `_start`
   processes racing on the same service. Two-layer fix:
   - `_start` pre-claims `controller_pid` to its own pid immediately
     on is_recovery, so `_controller_process_alive` sees it as live
     and the daemon skips redundant recovery. ip+port still flip
     atomically after `_wait_for_controller_ready` succeeds.
   - `ha_recovery_for_consolidation_mode` snapshots in-flight
     `_start` processes via psutil once per iteration (argv exact
     match, zombie-aware) and skips services that already have one.

3. ReplicaManager init lock race. `SkyPilotReplicaManager.__init__`
   started `_job_status_fetcher` (and two other daemon threads)
   BEFORE running `_recover_replica_operations`. If
   `_job_status_fetcher` won the race for `self.lock` and tried to
   SSH a replica whose head node was unreachable, it hung at the
   kernel TCP timeout (tens of seconds to minutes) — main thread
   blocked on `_recover_replica_operations`'s `with self.lock:`,
   never reached `uvicorn.run`, `_wait_for_controller_ready` timed
   out, item (1)'s bailout fired, daemon retried, same race
   forever. Fix: run recovery first, start the daemons after.

Also adds an audit log in `_cleanup` (own pid + DB controller_pid /
ip / status) and in the `_start` finally (normal / SHUTTING_DOWN /
unexpected-exception classification via a local flag, not
sys.exc_info() which returns None after the `except` catches).

Test plan
- New unit tests:
  - tests/unit_tests/test_serve_service.py — TestBailOnBootFailure
    (5 cases: os._exit(1), no _cleanup/remove_service_completely,
    kills controller subprocess, handles None, swallows kill failure);
    TestCleanupAuditLog (2 cases).
  - tests/unit_tests/test_serve_utils.py — TestStartInFlight (7 cases
    incl. exact-argv match, zombie exclusion, per-process
    NoSuchProcess tolerance, no prefix false positive);
    TestHaRecoverySkipsWhenStartInFlight.
  - tests/unit_tests/test_serve_replica_managers.py — ordering
    invariant (verified by git stash + rerun: test fails with the
    pre-fix order, passes after the reorder).
- 84/84 unit tests pass, format.sh clean.
- Manual: dev environment k8s pod restart should now show
  "SkyServe Controller started on http://..." in controller.log
  (uvicorn binds), DB controller_pid/ip/port flip within seconds,
  pool refresh no longer fails on stale ip/port.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Serve] Guard controller_process.pid is not None in boot-failure bailout

Address gemini-code-assist review on #9683 (discussion r3279635364):
`psutil.Process(None)` returns the *calling* process, so if
`controller_process.pid` were ever None (theoretical — start() always
populates pid on success, and start()-raise paths don't reach this
helper), `kill_children_processes(parent_pids=[None], force=True)`
would SIGKILL the current process instead of bailing out cleanly,
defeating the whole point of `_bail_on_boot_failure`.

Adds an explicit `controller_process.pid is not None` guard and a
unit test that mocks a Process with `pid = None` to verify
`kill_children_processes` is not called and `os._exit(1)` still
fires.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Jobs] Lazy-load replica handle in pool/serve status responses (#9673)
message:
[Jobs] Lazy-load replica handle in pool/serve status responses (#9673)

* [Jobs] Lazy-load replica handle in pool/serve status responses

For pools with thousands of replicas, every /jobs/pool_status response
serializes a base64-pickled CloudVmRayResourceHandle per replica
(~8 KB each), producing 40+ MB responses no current consumer reads
(dashboard, CLI, and SDK callers only need a few derived strings).

- Pre-compute infra / cloud / region / resources_str /
  resources_str_full on the controller and ship them in every response.
- Strip the handle to None on the wire for new clients
  (API_VERSION >= MIN_LAZY_REPLICA_HANDLE_API_VERSION). Old clients
  still receive the full handle so existing SDK code does not regress.
- Tighten controller HTTP retry from 3 x 2s connect to 1 x 1s connect.
  An unhealthy controller now costs ~1s per pool instead of ~7s.

CLI _format_replica_table prefers the pre-computed fields and falls
back to the handle path when talking to an old server.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Guard against launched_resources=None in handle access

Defensive None-check on handle.launched_resources before dereferencing
.cloud / .region / .infra. Although the type signature on
CloudVmRayResourceHandle declares launched_resources as non-Optional,
add the guard at the two new access sites to be robust against any
transiently-incomplete handle state.

Addresses gemini-code-assist review comments on #9673.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Fan out get_service_status_pickled across services

For deployments with many pools, the per-service controller HTTP call
(/autoscaler/info) is the dominant cost on /jobs/pool_status. Each
call costs up to 1s on an unreachable controller (after the retry
tightening in this branch); 50 pools serially adds 50s.

Run the per-service loop on a bounded ThreadPoolExecutor
(_STATUS_FANOUT_MAX_WORKERS = 8). Each task gets a fresh
Context.copy() so request_id / user_id contextvars propagate from
the caller while still allowing concurrent Context.run() across
worker threads.

Failure contract is preserved: ex.map() yields in input order and
re-raises the first exception, matching the legacy serial behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [RBAC] support viewer role (#9681)
message:
[RBAC] support viewer role (#9681)

* [API] Add viewer role: enum, allowlist, dispatch, schema

Introduces a strictly read-only "viewer" role to the RBAC system. The
role is allowlist-based (default-deny), distinct from the existing
admin/user blocklist semantics — so any future endpoint added to the
server is denied for viewers unless deliberately allowlisted.

- RoleName.VIEWER + rbac.get_viewer_allowlist() composing
  _DEFAULT_VIEWER_ALLOWLIST + operator overrides + plugin entries.
- PermissionService.check_endpoint_permission dispatches to an
  in-memory allowlist for viewer; admin/user continue to use the
  existing Casbin blocklist with no behavior change. Path matching
  via casbin keyMatch2 (`:name` placeholders + `*` wildcards).
- PermissionService.check_service_account_token_permission rejects
  viewers outright (defense-in-depth) so token mint/rotate/update
  is blocked even if a future allowlist change opens the URL.
- rbac_schema accepts `rbac.roles.<name>.permissions.{allow,block}list`
  (previously rejected by additionalProperties:False), and the
  default_role enum gains "viewer".
- Unit tests in test_rbac.py and test_permission.py covering the
  allowlist composition, dispatch, keyMatch2 patterns, and the
  SA-token guard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Add plugin viewer_allowlist contract + body shim for ambiguous endpoints

* `BasePlugin.viewer_allowlist` (default empty): plugins opt their
  read endpoints in to the viewer role.  Default behavior for any
  plugin endpoint is "denied for viewer" — safe default.
* `plugins.load_plugin_viewer_allowlist()` mirrors
  `load_plugin_rbac_rules()`: collects each plugin's
  `viewer_allowlist` entries at server boot.  Wired into
  `_main()` alongside `load_plugin_rbac_rules()`.
* `sky/server/requests/role_filter.py`: tiny FastAPI `Depends()`
  shims that strip side-effecting body fields (`refresh`,
  `include_credentials`) for viewer callers before the handler
  runs.  Wired into `/status`, `/jobs/queue(/v2)`, `/jobs/logs`,
  `/jobs/download_logs`, and `/volumes`.
* Tests cover the loader (with/without override), each shim
  helper, and the unchanged-for-non-viewer path.

The shim is read-only for admin/user callers — they see no
behavior change.  Viewers, by contrast, will get a sanitized
body server-side regardless of what the client sends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] backend_utils: refuse include_credentials for viewer-role caller

Defense-in-depth complementing the role_filter body shim from the
previous commit. If some future caller bypasses the HTTP layer and
reaches get_clusters() with include_credentials=True on behalf of a
viewer-roled user, suppress the SSH-key embedding outright.

The caller's user ID comes from USER_ID_ENV_VAR, which the executor
propagates into the worker process (executor.py:377). The viewer
check reads the in-memory casbin enforcer state directly to avoid a
DB roundtrip on the hot status path. Failures (env unset, casbin
not yet initialized, lookup error) all fail to "not a viewer" so
admin/user callers see no behavior change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Add route-coverage assertion for viewer allowlist

Walks every registered FastAPI route on the server's app and
fails if any (path, method) is neither in
rbac._DEFAULT_VIEWER_ALLOWLIST nor in this test file's explicit
_KNOWN_VIEWER_DENIED set.  This is the safety net for the
allowlist's main weakness: a new endpoint that the PR author
forgot to classify would otherwise silently 403 for viewers
(harmless) or, worse, slip through with no deliberate decision.

Also includes a reverse check: every allowlist pattern must
match at least one real route, so renamed/removed endpoints
don't leave stale entries that could accidentally cover a
different route in the future.

Adjusts the allowlist to cover the three RBAC-skipped surfaces
the prior commits omitted: /dashboard/*, /api/v1/auth/token,
/api/plugins.  The /dashboard_config entry from the earlier
plan was a stale reference — that endpoint does not exist on
this branch — so it has been removed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] viewer: build allowlist in every process, not just main

The viewer-role allowlist lives in process memory (PermissionService._viewer_allowlist) and was only built inside _maybe_initialize_policies, which is gated on full_initialize=True. That gate is only set when initialize() runs — i.e., once in the main API server process at startup.

uvicorn workers (uvicorn.Config(workers=N)) are separate processes that re-import sky.users.permission from scratch. They reach permission_service via _ensure_enforcer → _lazy_initialize(full_initialize=False), which builds the casbin enforcer but never built the viewer allowlist. Result: viewer-role requests hitting a worker fall through with an empty allowlist and 403 on every path on the allowlist — /dashboard/*, /users/role, /status, /jobs/queue/v2, /workspaces, /volumes, etc.

Admin/user roles weren't affected because they use casbin blocklist semantics: their policies live in the DB and casbin's load_policy() loads them in every process. The viewer allowlist intentionally doesn't sit in casbin, so we have to build it per-process.

Move the build into _lazy_initialize (read-only, no policy lock needed) and have _get_plugin_viewer_allowlist lazy-populate the module-level plugin cache when it's empty — the cache is filled by plugins.load_plugin_viewer_allowlist() in the main process at startup, but worker processes re-import that module and see an empty cache.

* [API] viewer: allowlist /debug/dump_create POST

Operators (including viewers) need to be able to trigger a diagnostic
dump for support. The corresponding download endpoint
(/debug/dump_download/:filename) stays admin-only via the user-role
blocklist — dumps can contain user-scoped data so reads need a higher
bar.

* [API] users: add SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_VIEWER_USER_ID built-in viewer

Adds a built-in viewer-role counterpart to the existing
SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_USER_ID admin user. Created automatically on startup
via the same seeding path so external auth integrations have a stable
user_id to impersonate as when they want to log a user in as a viewer
without materializing the caller's identity on the instance.

- new constant SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_VIEWER_USER_ID = 'skypilot-system-viewer'
- _maybe_initialize_policies seeds it with the VIEWER role
- protect from delete + role update next to the existing system user
- mark it as UserType.SYSTEM in get_user_type
- unit tests updated to cover the new built-in user

* [API] users: seed User row for built-in system users at startup

Without this, an external auth integration that impersonates a caller
as one of the built-in system users (e.g. SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_VIEWER_USER_ID
for a viewer-mode super-admin) gets a session that the session
middleware immediately invalidates: it does
`global_user_state.get_user(session.user_hash)` and on None deletes
the session and bounces the user back to /login.

Previously only the casbin role grouping was added at startup; the
User row was created lazily by other code paths (e.g.
executor.prepare_request_async for SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_USER_ID), which
isn't reached on the login path.

Seed the row for all three built-in users (SERVER_ID,
SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_USER_ID, SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_VIEWER_USER_ID) with
UserType.SYSTEM next to the role grouping so impersonation works
out of the box.

* refine

Signed-off-by: ubda012a9867b6dfc <ubda012a9867b6dfc@users.invalid>

* [API] viewer: keep /debug/dump_create on allowlist, sync tests

Address PR #9681 review comments: /debug/dump_create stays on
_DEFAULT_VIEWER_ALLOWLIST (viewers running on-call need to capture
support dumps; only /debug/dump_download/:filename is admin-only).

The contradictory test assertions are updated to match:
  - test_rbac.py:test_sensitive_reads_NOT_on_default_allowlist now
    asserts only the dump_download endpoint is denied, not dump_create
  - test_viewer_route_coverage.py drops /debug/dump_create from
    _KNOWN_VIEWER_DENIED (it's allowlisted, so the coverage test would
    otherwise flag it as appearing in BOTH lists)

Also add /dashboard_config GET to the allowlist; the viewer dashboard
fetches it on every page load to render external_links labels, and the
coverage test was failing because the route had no viewer decision.

* [API] viewer: admin wins over viewer when both roles are held

A user holding both admin and viewer should keep admin's permissive
behavior; viewer's default-deny semantics must not override admin.
Today's checks fire on viewer regardless of admin, which makes the
combined role strictly more restrictive than admin alone.

Updated four sites:
  - PermissionService.check_endpoint_permission: skip the viewer
    allowlist branch when admin is also present, fall through to
    enforce()
  - PermissionService.check_service_account_token_permission: check
    admin first; admin can manage any token
  - role_filter._is_viewer (force_viewer_status_body etc.): admin
    bypasses the side-effect-stripping
  - backend_utils._caller_is_viewer (refuses include_credentials):
    admin gets credentials even with viewer also assigned

Tests:
  - test_check_endpoint_permission_admin_wins_over_viewer
  - test_sa_token_permission_admin_wins_over_viewer

Addresses #9681 review comment r3279282693.

* [API] users: block password update on all internal user ids

The existing password-update guard only checked
SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_USER_ID, missing SERVER_ID and the newly added
SKYPILOT_SYSTEM_VIEWER_USER_ID — so an admin could set a password on
the system-viewer user. Match the role-update / delete guards which
already check the full _INTERNAL_USER_IDS tuple.

Addresses #9681 review comment r3279433232.

subject: [Server] reap multiprocess prometheus files when worker exits (#9689)
message:
[Server] reap multiprocess prometheus files when worker exits (#9689)

* [Server] reap multiprocess prometheus files when worker exits

Each uvicorn / executor worker writes pid-labelled multiprocess metric
files at $PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR/<type>_<pid>.db. MultiProcessCollector
keeps reading those files until prometheus_client.multiprocess.
mark_process_dead(pid) deletes them. Today nothing calls
mark_process_dead, so a worker that exits (graceful restart, crash,
etc.) leaves its last written gauge value visible to every future
/metrics scrape — and for multiprocess_mode='liveall' gauges this can
pin a stale per-pid value (e.g. an event-loop-lag spike) indefinitely.

Register an atexit hook that calls mark_process_dead(os.getpid()) once
per process, from the two entry points that own writer processes:

  - sky/server/uvicorn.py    : uvicorn worker (Server.run)
  - sky/server/requests/executor.py : executor worker (executor_initializer)

The hook is gated on PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR so single-process / unit
test environments are unaffected.

Tested:
  - pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/server/test_metrics.py

* [Test] add subprocess e2e for atexit multiproc-cleanup

Per @hdf67fd849db16fcd review: codifies the prior throwaway A/B repro as
two unit tests. Spawns a fresh Python subprocess that writes a liveall
gauge and exits — exercises the real prometheus_client + atexit path
end-to-end, not mocked.

- test_atexit_reaps_liveall_file_with_fix: with the fix, the dead
  subprocess's gauge_liveall_<pid>.db is gone.
- test_without_fix_leaks_liveall_file: without the fix, it leaks
  (locks in the bug as a regression test).

Cold `from sky.server import metrics` in a fresh subprocess pulls in
the full sky import chain; bumped the per-spawn timeout to 60s. Each
test runs in ~25s on this machine.

subject: [Serve] Persist SkyletEvent across daemon iterations so consolidation status refresh fires (#9684)
message:
[Serve] Persist SkyletEvent across daemon iterations so consolidation status refresh fires (#9684)

In consolidation mode, `update_service_status` (the function that
transitions a service to CONTROLLER_FAILED when its controller process
is dead) is gated by `ServiceUpdateEvent.run()`. `SkyletEvent.run()`
throttles `_run()` via an internal counter `_n` that accumulates across
calls: with EVENT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300 and EVENT_CHECKING_INTERVAL_SECONDS=20,
`_run()` only fires when `_n` rolls from 14 back to 0 (i.e. every 15
calls).

But `_serve_status_refresh_event` and `managed_job_status_refresh_event`
create a brand-new event instance every iteration of the outer
`InternalRequestDaemon.run_event` loop:

    while True:
        event = events.ServiceUpdateEvent(pool=pool)  # _n = 0
        event.run()                                   # _n = 1, no _run
        time.sleep(EVENT_CHECKING_INTERVAL_SECONDS)

`_n` resets to 0 on every call, `run()` only advances it to 1, the
`_n == 0` trigger never re-fires, and the throttled work is silently
skipped forever. The skylet's `run_event_loop` (where this pattern was
copied from) keeps the event instances at module scope on purpose; the
API server's port lost that.

Observable symptom in consolidation mode: a controller subprocess can
die and the service row stays in READY/NO_REPLICA indefinitely, with
no log line from `update_service_status`. The companion `--purge`
fallback path (PR #9678 / pending) is the only escape, but only because
this one is broken.

Fix: cache the three event instances (`_managed_job_event`,
`_pool_status_update_event`, `_serve_status_update_event`) at module
scope, matching the existing pattern for the consolidation-mode locks.
Lazy-init on first use so the daemon's `should_skip()` short-circuit
in non-consolidation mode does not pay for it.

Tests: new `TestConsolidationEventInstancePersistence` class with four
cases (serve / pool / independence / managed-job). All assert the
event constructor is called exactly once across multiple daemon
iterations and `run()` is invoked on the same instance per iteration.
Revert check: with the fix removed, all four fail with
`Expected '<Event>' to be called once. Called 3 times.` Without the
fixture's getattr-based defaults, the bare module-attribute access
would AttributeError on revert; the fixture is deliberately tolerant so
the failure surfaces as the assertion (a pointed signal at the bug)
rather than a setup error.

Test plan:
- `pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/server/test_daemons.py` — 8 passed
- Revert check (`git stash push sky/server/daemons.py`): 4 new tests
  fail with the expected assertion, then pass after `git stash pop`

subject: [Server] periodically reap multiproc prometheus files from dead workers (#9690)
message:
[Server] periodically reap multiproc prometheus files from dead workers (#9690)

* [Server] periodically reap multiproc prometheus files from dead workers

Companion to #9689: that PR registers `multiprocess.mark_process_dead(pid)`
via `atexit` in each worker so its per-pid live-gauge files are cleaned up
on graceful exit. As that PR's caveats note, `atexit` does not run on
SIGKILL / OOM / hard crash, so a defense-in-depth scan on the read side is
still worthwhile for the cases where the atexit hook never fires.

Without that scan, every `liveall`/`livesum`/etc. gauge that a dead worker
had written keeps being emitted as the dead pid's last value on every
`/metrics` scrape — until the API server pod itself restarts and wipes
`$PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR`. Downstream Prometheus dashboards and probes
see permanent per-PID series for processes that no longer exist.

New `sky.server.metrics.multiproc_reaper_daemon()` coroutine, scheduled
in the API server's existing background event loop alongside the metrics
server and the other `*_daemon` tasks. Once per `interval_seconds`
(default 60s):

1. Glob `$PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR/gauge_live*_*.db` (the exact set of
   files `mark_process_dead` would unlink — counters, histograms,
   summaries, and non-live gauges are intentionally preserved by the
   library to keep aggregate values meaningful across worker exits).
2. For each unique pid, if `psutil.pid_exists(pid)` is False, call
   `multiprocess.mark_process_dead(pid)`.

Runs only in the main API server process — the one place with a stable
event loop and full visibility into the pod's process state.

The membership check is "does this pid currently map to any running
process?", not "is this pid one of my descendants". A strict descendant
filter would have leaked files from legitimate writers that aren't direct
children (e.g. workers reparented to init after an intermediate exits).
The tradeoff: if a dead worker's pid is later reused by an unrelated
process inside the same pod, its files keep being scraped until either
that process also exits, the pid wraps to a fresh value, or a SkyPilot
writer with the same pid overwrites the file. Linux pid_max is large
and pid allocation is sequential, so this is rare in practice.

Per tick: one `glob.glob` + one `psutil.pid_exists` per unique pid in the
dir (typically O(workers) ≈ tens). Scan offloaded via `asyncio.to_thread`
so it never blocks the event loop. The 60s interval keeps per-pid stale
liveall samples bounded to roughly one scrape interval of staleness.

- [x] pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/server/test_metrics.py — added 8
  new tests covering: aggregate-only pids skipped, missing dir, no env
  var, live pid preserved, dead pids reaped exactly once, per-pid error
  isolation, daemon early-return without env, and daemon tick+cancel.
  All 25 tests pass.
- [x] pylint clean on sky/server/metrics.py and sky/server/server.py.
- [x] Manual e2e: started `sky.api_start(metrics=True)`; confirmed
  `Starting prometheus multiproc reaper (interval=60s)` in server log;
  planted `gauge_live*_<fake>.db` for a non-existent pid; SIGKILL'd a
  uvicorn worker and planted `gauge_live*_<that-pid>.db` for it; waited
  for the next reaper tick (~60s); confirmed log line
  `Reaped prometheus multiproc files for 2 dead pid(s).` and that the
  stale live-gauge files were gone while the SIGKILL'd worker's
  aggregate files (counter_*, gauge_all_*, histogram_*) remained — as
  the prometheus_client library intends.

-Claude

* [Server] reaper: use exc_info=True instead of traceback.format_exc()

Addresses Gemini code-review suggestions on #9690: prefer the logging
framework's built-in exception handling over manual traceback string
formatting. Drops the now-unused traceback import.
