subject: [Dashboard] Managed Jobs filter polish: More dropdown, Active/All toggle, default to Mine (#9707)
message:
[Dashboard] Managed Jobs filter polish: More dropdown, Active/All toggle, default to Mine (#9707)

* [Dashboard] Collapse non-primary statuses behind a More dropdown on managed jobs

Show only RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED as primary chips on the managed
jobs page; tuck the other statuses (PENDING, STARTING, CANCELLED,
FAILED_SETUP, FAILED_PRECHECKS, FAILED_NO_RESOURCE, FAILED_CONTROLLER,
etc.) behind a "More" dropdown so the row no longer over-emphasizes
failure variants. Also surface the total job count next to the
"Statuses:" label.

The selected non-primary statuses still show inline as chips so the
applied filter is always visible without opening the dropdown.

* [Dashboard] Show a delayed spinner over the jobs table on slow fetches

When the user clicks an Active/All toggle or status chip and the server
takes >1s to respond, fade in a subtle spinner overlay over the table
body so it's obvious the request is in-flight rather than the click
having no effect. Sub-second fetches stay quiet — no flashing spinner.

* [Dashboard] Refine primary statuses, dropdown highlighting, filter default

- Replace FAILED with STARTING in the primary chip row so the bar reads
  as a lifecycle progression (STARTING → RUNNING → SUCCEEDED). FAILED
  moves into the More dropdown alongside the FAILED_* variants.
- Light up dropdown rows for statuses that are implicitly included via
  the Active/All toggle (PENDING/STARTING/RECOVERING/CANCELLING when
  Active is selected), not only for explicitly-clicked statuses.
- Default the filter dropdown's property to Name instead of ID — users
  typically search jobs by name.

* [Dashboard] Default Managed Jobs to the current user's jobs

Add a "Mine | Everyone" segmented toggle next to the activity toggle
on the managed jobs page, defaulting to Mine. The user's id is
resolved from /users/role; the initial fetch waits for that resolve
so it can already carry userMatch and avoid a one-flash "Everyone"
round-trip.

Coexists with the existing FilterDropdown user filter: an explicit
?user=… filter wins, and the toggle highlights Mine only if the
explicit value matches the current user (otherwise neither segment
is highlighted, signalling that an explicit narrow scope is in
effect). If the role endpoint can't id the caller (unauthenticated
or basic-auth), the toggle is hidden and the table degrades to the
Everyone view.

* [Dashboard] Reflect implicit filtering in the More pill count

When the user is in any narrowed state (Active toggle on, or specific
statuses picked), the More button now shows "N selected" where N is
the count of dropdown items currently included in the filter — same
items that light up inside the dropdown. Previously the button kept
showing the total dropdown count even when Active narrowed the view,
so it gave no hint that filtering was on.

* [Dashboard] Stabilize filter bar layout so toggles don't slide on click

Three things conspired to shift elements horizontally when clicking a
toggle: chip counts changed digit count, the More pill's badge text
changed length ("4 selected" vs "10 selected"), and the toggles
themselves were positioned after all the chips so any width change
upstream pushed them right.

- Move the Active/All and Mine/Everyone toggles BEFORE the primary
  chips so the toggle positions are anchored to the start of the bar
  and never move on click.
- Use tabular-nums on every numeric label so digits occupy equal
  columns (1 and 9 render the same width).
- Reserve a min-width slot for each count badge (chips, More pill,
  dropdown rows) so the chip width is the same whether the count is
  1, 12, or 123.

* [Dashboard] Drop totalNoFilter count from the Statuses label

* [Dashboard] Move toggles back to after the More dropdown

* [Dashboard] Empty-state CTA when Mine has no jobs but Everyone does

When the Mine view comes up empty, fire a one-shot probe for the
Everyone total and surface it in the empty state: "You haven't
submitted any managed jobs yet. N jobs from other users — switch to
Everyone to see them." with a button that flips the toggle. Avoids
leaving first-time users staring at a blank table wondering whether
SkyPilot has any activity at all.

The probe only fires after the initial fetch resolves with 0 user
jobs and only once per session; it goes through jobsCacheManager
like the main fetch.

* [Dashboard] Stop gating initial fetch on /users/role for faster first paint

The earlier change held the initial managed-jobs fetch until the
/users/role round-trip resolved so the first request could already
carry userMatch. On networks where /users/role is slow this left the
table in a long loading state. Fire the initial fetch immediately
with userMatch=undefined; when currentUser resolves shortly after,
fetchData's useCallback recreates (currentUser is in its deps) and
the existing dep-on-fetchData effects refire, narrowing to Mine.

* [Dashboard] Trigger empty-state CTA on rendered row count, not totalNoFilter

The earlier gate used the server's totalNoFilter to decide when to show
the "View everyone's jobs" CTA, but totalNoFilter is the unfiltered
total across the whole deployment — it doesn't honor userMatch — so on
any tenant where other users have jobs the CTA was silently suppressed
for users with zero jobs of their own. Switch to data.length === 0 as
the trigger; it's the same signal that already drives the empty-state
row, and it's unambiguous.

* [Dashboard] Gate initial managed-jobs fetch on currentUser via shared cache

On tenants with tens of thousands of finished jobs the unscoped
"Everyone" query is expensive (full count + status aggregation), and
the previous flow paid it twice — once on the unscoped initial fetch
and again on the narrow Mine refetch when currentUser resolved.

- Export getCurrentUserInfo() from client.js so jobs.jsx can hit the
  same module-level cache that the sidebar / config / etc. already
  populate on dashboard mount. The /users/role round-trip happens at
  most once per page session.
- Gate the initial fetch on currentUser; with the cache warm this is
  effectively synchronous, and on cold load it's a single ~200ms
  /users/role wait rather than the seconds-long Everyone round-trip.
- 1.5s safety-net timeout: if /users/role never resolves (anonymous
  user, role endpoint down) we fall back to the unscoped fetch so the
  page doesn't get stuck.
- Treat the 'local' sentinel from getCurrentUserInfo as null so we
  don't accidentally send userMatch='local' on un-authenticated paths.

* [Dashboard] Default to Everyone when no usable user identity

Previously the Mine/Everyone gate would wait up to 1.5s for /users/role
to resolve before falling back to the unscoped fetch — fine for SSO
tenants, but tenants running anonymous or basic-auth without a logged
user (a common dev/single-user setup) would eat the timeout on every
page load even though getCurrentUserInfo() returns the 'local' sentinel
immediately.

Track a userResolved flag separately from currentUser:
- Real user id → currentUser set, userScope stays 'mine'.
- 'local' sentinel or role-endpoint error → currentUser stays null and
  userScope flips to 'all'.
- Either way userResolved becomes true and the initial fetch fires.

Initial fetch now gates on userResolved (not currentUser), so basic-auth
installs land on Everyone in zero extra wait, while authenticated
tenants still go Mine-first. The Mine/Everyone toggle was already
hidden when !currentUser, so the no-identity UX collapses cleanly to a
single-view Everyone dashboard.

* [Dashboard] Rename Mine/Everyone to My Jobs/All Jobs

The owner-scope segments now read "My Jobs | All Jobs" instead of
"Mine | Everyone" — clearer that the toggle scopes by job ownership,
not by something more abstract. Also updates the empty-state CTA to
say "switch to All Jobs to see them" and the button to "View all
jobs". Internal state ('mine' / 'all') is unchanged.

* [Dashboard] Keep filter toggles visible when Mine is empty

The Active/All and My Jobs/All Jobs toggles were both gated on
totalNoFilter > 0, which hid them whenever the current user had zero
jobs of their own — leaving the empty-state "View all jobs" CTA as
the only way to switch scope, with no way to switch back to Mine
afterward. Show both toggles when there are jobs anywhere we could
switch to (current scope OR the probed everyoneTotal).

* [Dashboard] Address review comments: toggle visibility, CTA gating, z-index

Three fixes from PR review:

1. Active/All and My Jobs/All Jobs toggles were hidden whenever
   totalNoFilter === 0, which stranded users in two scenarios: a Mine
   view with no personal jobs, and an Everyone view with a filter
   that narrowed to zero rows. Both cases left only the empty-state
   CTA (which only switches Mine→All, never the other way) as a way
   out. Show both toggles past the initial-load state — they're
   harmless when the table is empty and indispensable as soon as
   anything else changes.

2. The empty-state CTA ("You haven't submitted any managed jobs yet")
   could fire when a user with only finished jobs clicked Active —
   the message was factually wrong because they had submitted jobs,
   just none currently active. Gate the CTA on
   activeTab === 'all' && showAllMode so it only renders when no
   status narrowing is in effect.

3. Re-word the CTA's body from "N jobs from other users — switch to
   All Jobs to see them" to "N jobs in total — switch to All Jobs
   to see them". The probe fetches totalNoFilter with no userMatch,
   which technically includes the current user's jobs; "in total"
   is accurate regardless.

4. Bump the More dropdown's z-index from z-20 to z-50 to clear
   sticky table headers and other floating UI.

* [Dashboard] Reset status narrowing when toggling My Jobs/All Jobs

The My Jobs/All Jobs toggle handler left selectedStatuses and
showAllMode untouched, so a status chip clicked in one scope (e.g.,
RUNNING in My Jobs) carried over to the other. Combined with a 60K
deployment where most jobs are SUCCEEDED/FAILED, this landed users
in states where the table was empty even though the toggle said All
Jobs — they had implicitly filtered to a status with zero rows under
the new scope.

Mirror the Active/All toggle's reset semantics: clear selectedStatuses
and force showAllMode=true on scope switch. activeTab is intentionally
preserved so users who picked Active in one scope keep that activity
filter when they switch scope.

* [Dashboard] Replace "No active jobs" flash with a loading row during refetch

Three improvements to the empty-state transition UX:

1. Table-body loading row now fires whenever loading && data.length===0,
   not just on isInitialLoad. Clicking "View all jobs" or flipping the
   My Jobs/All Jobs toggle from a zero-row scope used to flash "No
   active jobs" for the duration of the refetch before the new rows
   arrived. The spinner-row now stays until the data lands.

2. Also show the loading row while the Everyone probe is in flight on
   an empty Mine view. Without this the user briefly saw "No active
   jobs" between the empty Mine fetch returning and the probe answering
   (the CTA renders only after everyoneTotal resolves).

3. The "View all jobs" CTA button now mirrors selectScope's reset
   (clear selectedStatuses + force showAllMode=true) so it can't carry
   a stale status narrowing over from the previous scope.

* [Dashboard] Address PR review: send username for Mine filter; memoize chip lists

Two fixes from PR review:

1. Mine scope was sending currentUser.id (the user hash) as user_match, but
   the server resolves user_match via get_user_by_name_match which does a
   LIKE on the name column. On any tenant where id and name differ
   (multi-user / RBAC), the LIKE matches nothing and "My Jobs" silently
   returns zero. Send currentUser.name instead.

2. The non-primary selected-statuses chip list and the More dropdown's total
   count were both recomputed on every render. Hoist them to useMemo.

subject: [Hooks] Generalized lifecycle-hooks framework (config.hooks) + K8s head (#9064)
message:
[Hooks] Generalized lifecycle-hooks framework (config.hooks) + K8s head (#9064)

* [Hooks] Add failing tests for lifecycle-hooks framework

TDD red baseline for PR1. Covers the target API surface:

- `resources.hooks: [{run, events?, timeout?}]` schema with `events`
  optional (defaults to [autostop, preemption, down])
- Schema rejects empty/duplicate/unknown events, non-positive
  timeouts, unknown keys
- Controller resources (jobs.controller.resources,
  serve.controller.resources) reject hooks
- Resources._hooks round-trip through YAML + copy()
- Pickle v32 → v33 migration routes legacy autostop.hook attrs into
  the new _hooks list
- Legacy autostop.hook YAML parses with stderr deprecation warning
- hook_executor: try_claim_teardown CAS, per-event log path,
  sequential run, failure continues, empty/no-match no-ops
- SKYLET_LIB_VERSION bumps to 7

All tests fail on master; subsequent commits turn them green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Hooks] Schema + Resources._hooks + pickle v32→v33 migration

Adds resources.hooks to the schema and storage layer of Resources.

- sky/utils/schemas.py: _HOOKS_SCHEMA + _HOOK_EVENTS. events is
  OPTIONAL (defaults applied at load time, not in schema). Controller
  resources (jobs.controller.resources, serve.controller.resources)
  reject the hooks field — infrastructure lifecycle is not user-
  configurable.
- sky/resources.py:
  - AutostopConfig loses hook/hook_timeout fields. Resources'
    _set_autostop_config consumes them from the legacy YAML shape,
    emits a one-line stderr deprecation warning, and routes them
    into the new _hooks list.
  - New _hooks field + hooks property + round-trip via
    from_yaml_config / to_yaml_config / copy().
  - _normalize_hook_entry fills events default = all three and
    timeout default = DEFAULT_AUTOSTOP_HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.
  - _VERSION bumps 32 → 33 with __setstate__ branch that rehydrates
    legacy AutostopConfig.hook / hook_timeout attrs into _hooks and
    scrubs them from AutostopConfig.
- sky/execution.py + sky/core.py: temporarily synthesize the legacy
  hook/hook_timeout pair from the first autostop-matching entry in
  resources.hooks, preserving the set_autostop wire format until
  the later Proto v7 commit lands.

24 of 32 unit tests now green; remaining failures are hook_executor
(next commit) and SKYLET_LIB_VERSION (proto v7 commit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Hooks] Add hook_executor module + autostop_lib persistence

New sky/skylet/hook_executor.py:
- try_claim_teardown(event): per-node file-lock CAS on
  ~/.sky/hooks/.teardown_claim via fcntl.flock. Lock released
  immediately after claim; not held during hook execution.
- run(event, hooks): filters by event, truncates the per-event log
  (~/.sky/hooks/<event>.log), runs each matching hook with the
  configured timeout, writes output via log_lib.run_with_log.
  Non-zero exit / timeout logs a warning and continues teardown.
- Helpers: current_teardown_event, clear_teardown_claim (boot-time
  cleanup), reset_teardown_state_for_tests.

autostop_lib:
- New _HOOKS_CONFIG_KEY = 'lifecycle_hooks' sqlite key.
- set_hooks(hooks): JSON-persists the hooks list set at cluster launch.
- get_hooks(): loads the list; returns [] if unset.

All 7 hook_executor tests + 1 legacy-routing test now green
(31/32 total; only SKYLET_LIB_VERSION bump remains).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Hooks] Skylet SIGTERM handler + autostop routing + K8s grace-period

- sky/skylet/skylet.py::main: register signal.SIGTERM handler that
  claims the preemption teardown slot via hook_executor file-lock,
  runs matching preemption hooks from autostop_lib.get_hooks(), and
  exits cleanly. Skylet boot also clear_teardown_claim() to unblock
  rescheduled pods or rebooted VMs.
- sky/skylet/events.py::AutostopEvent._execute_hook_if_present:
  re-implemented on top of hook_executor.run('autostop', ...) under
  try_claim_teardown CAS. If another teardown trigger already
  claimed the slot, autostop no-ops on hooks. Matches the per-node
  exactly-once guarantee from the design doc §1.6.5.
- sky/clouds/kubernetes.py::_get_deploy_vars: compute
  preemption_hook_timeout = max(preemption-hook timeouts). Passed
  to the K8s pod template.
- sky/templates/kubernetes-ray.yml.j2: render
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds only when preemption_hook_timeout
  is set. Hook-free pods keep K8s's 30-second default.

Dispatch path for autostop and K8s preemption now matches design
doc §2.1-§2.4. 31/32 unit tests green; only SKYLET_LIB_VERSION
bump remains (next commit).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Hooks] Proto v7 + AutostopCodeGen dual-emit + re-launch propagation

Proto (autostopv1.proto):
- Add Event enum (UNSPECIFIED, AUTOSTOP, PREEMPTION, DOWN).
- Add Hook message { run, events[], timeout }.
- Add SetAutostopRequest.hooks (field 7) for v7+ clients; keep
  legacy hook / hook_timeout (fields 5, 6) for backward-compat.
- Regenerate bindings.

SKYLET_LIB_VERSION: 6 → 7.

autostop_lib.set_autostop: route a pre-v7 client's hook/hook_timeout
payload into the generalized hooks list via set_hooks(). This lets
pre-v7 clients talking to v7+ skylets work seamlessly.

AutostopCodeGen.set_autostop: gain a hooks kwarg and dual-emit:
  - skylet < 4 / < 5: legacy signatures (unchanged)
  - skylet 5–6: flatten first autostop-matching entry to
    hook/hook_timeout on the existing set_autostop call
  - skylet ≥ 7: set_autostop + set_hooks(full list)

Re-launch propagation in _check_existing_cluster: after the
docker_login_config override, also to_provision.copy(hooks=...)
when the new task's list differs from the stored one. The next
SetAutostop RPC carries the updated list via field 7.

SKYLET_LIB_VERSION test now green: all 32 hook unit tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Hooks] Per-event hook logs + core.down() runs down-hook

Client/SDK/server:
- Add `sky logs --hook [event]` with `click.Choice`; `--autostop` kept
  as deprecated alias rewriting to `--hook autostop` with stderr warn.
- Add `sdk.tail_hook_logs(cluster_name, event=None, ...)`; keep
  `sdk.tail_autostop_logs` as a deprecated shim.
- Add `POST /hook_logs` route with `HookLogsBody`; keep
  `/autostop_logs` route as deprecated alias.
- Add `core.tail_hook_logs(cluster_name, event, follow, tail)` and
  `CloudVmRayBackend.tail_hook_logs(handle, event, ...)` with
  auto-select (newest `~/.sky/hooks/*.log`) plus legacy-path fallback
  to `~/.sky/autostop_hook.log` for `event='autostop'`.

Controller-side hook dispatch:
- `backend.set_autostop(..., hooks=...)` is now routed via both
  gRPC (v7+: `Hook` repeated field) and codegen (pre-v7: legacy
  `hook`/`hook_timeout` flatten) paths; skylet `SetAutostop` handler
  persists `request.hooks` via `autostop_lib.set_hooks`.
- `core.down()` now invokes `_maybe_run_down_hooks(handle, backend,
  cluster_name)` before teardown: on VM/Ray backends, runs inline
  codegen on the head that calls `hook_executor.try_claim_teardown`
  then `hook_executor.run('down', hooks)`. Best-effort (warn+proceed
  on failure).

Constants:
- Add `HOOK_LOG_DIR` and `HOOK_EVENTS` to `sky/skylet/constants.py`.

* [Hooks] Add pytest smoke tests for lifecycle hooks (PR1)

Adds `tests/smoke_tests/test_lifecycle_hooks.py` with 13 tests
exercising the PR1 framework surface:

- S1  test_hook_autostop_fires: basic autostop hook retrieval via
      `sky logs --hook autostop`.
- S2  test_hook_events_default_to_all: omitting `events` yields all
      three events in the stored config.
- S3  test_hook_k8s_preemption_sigterm (@pytest.mark.kubernetes):
      `kubectl delete pod` triggers SIGTERM → preemption hook fires
      within grace window; verified via `kubectl logs`.
- S4  test_hook_down_fires: down hook observed during teardown.
- S5  test_hook_multi_event: autostop+down entry only fires autostop.
- S6  test_cli_hook_auto_select: `sky logs --hook` (no event).
- S7  test_cli_autostop_alias_deprecation: stderr warning on alias.
- S8  test_hook_legacy_autostop_hook_backcompat: legacy
      `autostop.hook` routed with stderr deprecation warning.
- S9  test_hook_schema_rejects_unknown_event: `events:[reboot]`.
- S10 test_hook_controller_rejected: `jobs.controller.resources.hooks`.
- S11 test_hook_timeout_kill: partial output + teardown completes.
- S12 test_hook_autostop_down_race: exactly-one exclusive-event fire.
- S13 test_cli_hook_rejects_unknown_event: click error.

All tests use `smoke_tests_utils.Test + run_one_test` to match the
existing framework; `generic_cloud` fixture drives per-cloud runs.

* [Test] Fix no-dep smoke-test shell quoting + SKYPILOT_CONFIG env var

Three issues found by local smoke-test runs:
- test_cli_hook_rejects_unknown_event: `! sky ... | tee && grep` negated
  the whole pipe, so the `&&` short-circuit never ran grep. Switched to
  `out=$(cmd || true); echo "$out" | grep`.
- test_hook_schema_rejects_unknown_event: same pattern.
- test_hook_controller_rejected: heredoc inside f-string collided with
  the shell parser. Switched to Python-side tempfile + plain env var;
  also fixed the env var name SKYPILOT_USER_CONFIG → SKYPILOT_CONFIG.

* [Hooks] Persist hooks at launch even when autostop is disabled

Two fixes found by running K8s smoke tests end-to-end against a local
API server:

1. **execution.py**: The previous code only persisted `resources.hooks:`
   via `backend.set_autostop(..., hooks=...)` when the user had ALSO
   set `autostop.idle_minutes`. Hooks that only target `preemption` or
   `down` were silently lost on clusters without autostop. Now we call
   `set_autostop(idle_minutes_to_autostop=-1, hooks=task_hooks)` in the
   hooks-only case, so the skylet's `SetAutostop` RPC writes the hooks
   list to sqlite without enabling idle-timer autostop.

2. **tests/smoke_tests/test_lifecycle_hooks.py**: The inspect command
   used nested single-quotes that the shell collapsed, so the regex
   `'"events":.*autostop.*down.*preemption'` became bare
   `events:.*autostop.*down.*preemption` — which didn't match the JSON
   output. Replaced with three separate `grep -q` calls.

Verified against a real K8s cluster launch: skylet sqlite now shows
`[{"run": "...", "events": ["autostop", "preemption", "down"],
"timeout": 3600}]` after a hooks-only YAML launch, and the
test_hook_events_default_to_all smoke test passes in ~68s.

* [Hooks] Use SKY_PYTHON_CMD for down-hook codegen on remote

The inline codegen dispatched via `backend.run_on_head` needs to run
in a Python environment that has `sky` installed. The plain
`python3` in PATH on the remote pod points to `/opt/conda/bin/python3`
which doesn't have the SkyPilot library — only `$SKY_PYTHON_CMD`
(resolved via `SKY_PYTHON_PATH_FILE` on the cluster) does.

Previously the codegen silently failed with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sky'`, my broad except caught
it, and teardown proceeded without running any down hooks — so
`test_hook_down_fires` could never observe the hook output.

Verified end-to-end against a real kind-skypilot cluster: a teardown
with a `sleep 5` down hook now takes 11s (vs 4.6s before) and
`test_hook_down_fires` passes in 89s.

* [Test] Fix K8s preemption smoke test: read log during grace via kubectl exec

The previous version used `kubectl logs` to look for the hook's echo,
but `hook_executor.run_with_log` directs subprocess stdout to
`~/.sky/hooks/<event>.log` — not to the container stdout — so
`kubectl logs` couldn't see it. Also the label selector was missing
the `-name` suffix.

Fixes:
- Hook writes the marker to `~/.sky/hooks/preemption.log` then
  sleeps 20s so the pod stays in Terminating.
- Test reads the file via `kubectl exec` during the grace period
  (terminationGracePeriodSeconds is rendered from timeout=60).
- Label selector now `skypilot-cluster-name={name}` (no user hash).

* [Hooks][K8s] Forward SIGTERM to skylet via preStop hook

The skylet isn't PID 1 in a K8s pod (the setup bash script is), so
kubelet's SIGTERM doesn't reach the skylet — the preemption hook
never fires.

Add a preStop lifecycle hook that reads `~/.sky/skylet_pid` and
`kill -TERM`s it, then `sleep`s for `preemption_hook_timeout`
seconds so K8s doesn't SIGKILL the skylet mid-hook. Only rendered
when the task has preemption hooks (same condition as the
terminationGracePeriodSeconds block).

Verified end-to-end on kind-skypilot: without this hook, SIGTERM
never reaches skylet and `~/.sky/hooks/preemption.log` is never
written. With it, the marker appears in the file during the grace
window and `kubectl exec` can read it.

* [Test] Use pod-name grep instead of label selector for K8s preempt tests

The `skypilot-cluster-name` label value includes the user-hash
suffix (e.g. `foo-4b972ab6`), so using `-l skypilot-cluster-name={name}`
matches zero pods. Switched to `kubectl get pods -o name | grep {name}`
which matches by pod-name prefix.

* [Hooks][K8s] preStop pgrep+poll, gracePeriod=sum (review fixes)

Three review-driven fixes to the K8s preemption-hook path:

1. **gracePeriod = sum(preemption_hook_timeouts), not max.**
   hook_executor.run executes matching hooks sequentially, so the
   wall-clock time is the sum. Using max would let kubelet SIGKILL
   the skylet partway through hooks 2..N. Refactored the rendering
   into a module-level helper `_compute_preemption_hook_timeout` so
   the math is testable in isolation.

2. **preStop uses pgrep instead of a cached PID file.** Eliminates:
   - boot-race window between skylet start and PID-file write
   - HA stale-PID after skylet crash + restart
   - PID-reuse on uncleanly-shut daemons
   The pgrep regex matches both `sky.skylet.skylet` (head) and
   `sky.skylet.worker_hook_handler` (worker — added in PR3) so the
   same template works for head and worker pods.

3. **preStop polls for daemon exit instead of unconditional sleep.**
   Old code did `sleep $grace` even when the hook finished in 1s,
   leaving the pod stuck Terminating. New body `kill -0`s the
   discovered PID once per second up to grace.

Unit tests:
- 4 new tests on `_compute_preemption_hook_timeout`: sum semantics,
  ignore non-preemption events, None when no preemption hook,
  default timeout when unset.

Tested locally on `kind-skypilot`: full unit suite (54 tests) green.

EOF

* [Hooks] Senior-review fixes: clear_hooks proto, grace cap, K8s short-circuit

C1 — explicit hook-clear on the wire (proto3 has no presence on
repeated). SetAutostopRequest gets bool clear_hooks = 8. Servicer
treats clear_hooks=True as drop-stored-hooks; otherwise existing
replace-if-non-empty semantics applies. Client backend translates
hooks=None → leave alone, hooks=[] → set clear_hooks=True,
hooks=[...] → replace. Without this, re-launching after removing
all hooks from the YAML would leave stale hooks in skylet sqlite.

C7 — cap rendered terminationGracePeriodSeconds at 600s with warning.
cluster-autoscaler default --max-graceful-termination-sec is 600.
Render-bigger-grace doesn't extend the autoscaler's willingness to
wait. _compute_preemption_hook_timeout caps at
_PREEMPTION_GRACE_CAP_SECONDS and stderr-warns when raw sum exceeds.

S2 — skylet boot skips cloud-detect probe on K8s. EKS pods can
reach EC2 IMDS, so the previous probe-everything strategy
mis-detected EKS pods as aws and started a poller racing the K8s
preStop. Short-circuit when KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST is set in env.

Tests: 4 unit + 3 smoke (kind). 57 unit tests pass total.

* [Hooks] Pass hooks=[] on re-launch to actually clear stored hooks

The proto3 clear_hooks=True plumbing landed earlier was unreachable:
the only call site at execution.py:587 gated on `elif task_hooks:`,
which is false for an empty list. Re-launches dropping `hooks:` from
YAML therefore left skylet's stored hook list intact (regression
caught by test_hook_clear_via_relaunch on kind).

Change PRE_EXEC to compute an explicit `hooks_payload`:
  - task_hooks set → forward as-is (existing behavior)
  - re-launch (cluster_exists) with no hooks → send [] to clear
  - first launch with no hooks → leave stored hooks alone (None)

The autostop-cancel side effect of the elif branch was already present
for re-launches with hooks; extending the branch to fire on
cluster_exists+no-hooks just makes that behavior consistent. K8s and
RunPod treat idle=-1 as a no-op since autostop isn't supported there.

* [Hooks] Drop unused backend.tail_autostop_logs + move misplaced test

Two small cleanups, both PR1 territory:

1. backend.tail_autostop_logs was an orphan. The deprecation chain is
   sdk.tail_autostop_logs → POST /autostop_logs → core.tail_autostop_logs
   → core.tail_hook_logs(event='autostop') → backend.tail_hook_logs.
   The backend-level alias is never reached. Deleting it; the SDK,
   server route, and core handler stay through the deprecation window.

2. test_skylet_cloud_detect_short_circuits_on_kubernetes was committed
   on PR1's senior-review pass but exercises
   skylet._detect_cloud_for_preemption_poller, which only exists on
   PR2. Pre-existing AttributeError on PR1 alone. Removing here; the
   test will be re-added on PR2 alongside the function it tests.

* [Hooks] Fix CI: allowlist sky.hook_logs + yapf + regenerate refs

Three independent CI failures from the previous force-push:

1. Unit test (test_debug_utils.TestRequestBodyAllowlistCoverage):
   sky.hook_logs is a new request name added by this PR but wasn't
   listed in _REQUEST_BODY_ALLOWLIST. Added it (Category 1: metadata
   only), matching the existing sky.autostop_logs entry.

2. yapf (format check): the merge-conflict resolution in `logs`
   command put the deprecation-warning string on three lines; yapf
   wants two. Reflowed.

3. reviewable (Check for diff): agent/skills/skypilot/references/
   {cli-reference.md,python-sdk.md} were stale relative to the new
   --hook CLI option and tail_hook_logs SDK function. Regenerated via
   `python agent/scripts/generate_references.py`.

* [Hooks] Add removal-window TODOs on every transient deprecation surface

Per termination_hook_impl.md §10: every transient deprecation surface
should carry a TODO comment so the eventual cleanup PR can grep for
all of them. Audit-and-add pass.

Surfaces marked "remove ~2 minors after the lifecycle-hooks framework
ships":
  - sky/backends/cloud_vm_ray_backend.py: both legacy-log-path
    fallback branches in tail_hook_logs
  - sky/client/sdk.py: tail_autostop_logs (rewording the existing
    v0.15.0-pinned TODO since we don't lock to a specific version)
  - sky/client/cli/command.py: --autostop flag + handler block
  - sky/core.py: tail_autostop_logs server-side handler
  - sky/resources.py: autostop.hook YAML routing (rewording existing
    TODO)
  - sky/server/requests/payloads.py: AutostopLogsBody
  - sky/server/server.py: POST /autostop_logs route
  - sky/skylet/constants.py: AUTOSTOP_HOOK_LOG_FILE

Surface marked "remove once SKYLET_LIB_VERSION's minimum supported
client is ≥ 7" (different removal trigger):
  - sky/skylet/autostop_lib.py: pre-v7 hook/hook_timeout translation
    in set_autostop

Pickle migration (resources.py v32→v33) intentionally has no TODO —
old pickles on disk exist forever, so the migration shim stays.

* [Hooks] Extract autostop-deprecation warnings to a single module

Three near-identical 'WARNING: ... deprecated. Use ... instead.\n'
messages were inlined at three call sites. Hoist them into
sky/utils/hooks_deprecation.py so the cleanup PR drops a single
module + 4 imports rather than chasing string literals across
sdk.py / command.py / resources.py.

Module-level TODO marks the file for removal ~2 minors after the
lifecycle-hooks framework ships, matching the rest of the
deprecation-surface markers from the prior commit.

Bonus cleanup: the `if autostop:` block in `sky logs` was redundant.
The validation block above it already maps `--autostop` →
`hook_event = 'autostop'` (with the deprecation warning), then
control flows into the existing `if hook_event is not None:` handler
which calls tail_hook_logs(event='autostop'). The duplicate block
was emitting a SECOND warning on every `--autostop` invocation.
Removed.

* [Hooks] Consolidate smoke tests: 13 → 6 tests

Each PR1 smoke test launches a real cluster (~2-3 min on cloud) so
running 13 of them against `--generic-cloud aws/gcp/azure` adds ~30
min to a CI run. Many of them shared the same setup — launch with
hooks YAML, wait for autostop, inspect the log — and only differed
in which sub-feature they asserted on.

Aggregated:

- test_hook_lifecycle_combined (replaces 8 tests):
  test_hook_autostop_fires
  test_hook_events_default_to_all
  test_hook_multi_event
  test_cli_hook_auto_select
  test_cli_autostop_alias_deprecation
  test_hook_legacy_autostop_hook_backcompat
  test_hook_timeout_kill
  test_hook_newline_in_run_survives_resync (sqlite round-trip portion;
    the worker-resync portion is descoped along with worker support)
- test_hook_down_and_race (replaces 2): test_hook_down_fires +
  test_hook_autostop_down_race
- test_hook_invalid_inputs_rejected (replaces 3, all no-cluster):
  test_hook_schema_rejects_unknown_event +
  test_hook_controller_rejected + test_cli_hook_rejects_unknown_event

Kept separate:
- test_hook_clear_via_relaunch — re-launch sequencing is long
- test_hook_k8s_preemption_sigterm — K8s-only failure surface
- test_hook_grace_capped_at_autoscaler_limit — K8s-only failure surface

Each combined test has a leading comment listing every sub-feature
plus per-assertion comments labeling which sub-test the assertion
exercises, so a failure log narrows down quickly.

* [Hooks] Fix CI: --hook auto-select click validation + drop down/race window

Two failures from build 10346 (--aws -k test_lifecycle_hooks):

1. test_hook_lifecycle_combined — `sky logs --hook --no-follow` (the
   "auto-select" form) was rejected by click because `flag_value=''`
   ran through `click.Choice([autostop, preemption, down])`, which
   doesn't accept ''. The earlier --kubernetes build (10331) didn't
   surface this because the `or`-form -k expression silently filtered
   out every test (substring match), so 0 tests actually ran. With
   the file-path form (10345/10346) the tests run for real.

   Fix: replace the `click.Choice` with a `_validate_hook_event`
   callback that accepts None / '' / one of the three valid events
   and raises `click.BadParameter` with the same "is not one of …"
   wording for unknown events. The CLI rejection path
   (test_hook_invalid_inputs_rejected) still passes — the message
   contains "is not one of 'autostop', 'preemption', 'down'".

2. test_hook_down_and_race — the test launched with autostop=1m and
   tried to land `sky down` ~55s later inside the autostop window to
   exercise the per-node CAS race. On real AWS, autostop wins the
   race often enough that the down hook never fires and the grep
   for the down marker fails. The CAS race is already covered by
   unit tests in test_hook_executor.py. Drop the autostop block

a pre-v7 client (e.g. master) sends `hook='sleep 120'` with no
explicit hooks list, the codegen would:

  1. Call `set_autostop(...)` WITHOUT `hook=` — so the skylet's
     legacy-hook → new-hooks-list routing bridge at
     autostop_lib.py:200-206 never fired.
  2. Then call `set_hooks([])` — wiping any stored hooks.

Result: `autostop_lib.get_hooks()` returns `[]` at idle-timer fire,
`_execute_hook_if_present` skips its no-op branch, and the cluster
tears down immediately. Affected the SSH codegen path specifically
(`SKYPILOT_ENABLE_GRPC` defaults False, so this is the default path
on AWS/GCP/Azure). The gRPC handler in
`sky/skylet/services.py:AutostopServiceImpl.SetAutostop` was already
correct — it passes `hook=` to `set_autostop` and only calls
`set_hooks` when the client explicitly opts in via
`request.clear_hooks` or a non-empty `request.hooks`.

Fix: mirror the gRPC handler's semantics in the codegen v7+ branch.

  - Forward `hook=` and `hook_timeout=` to `set_autostop` so the
    bridge runs.
  - Only emit `set_hooks(...)` when `hooks is not None`. `None`
    means "leave stored hooks alone" — exactly what a legacy caller
    that doesn't know about the hooks list intends. `[]` stays
    reserved for explicit clear (re-launch dropping `hooks:`).

Regression coverage (red → green TDD):

  * test_codegen_v7_branch_preserves_legacy_hook_when_hooks_none
    asserts the rendered v7+ branch contains the legacy hook string
    and does NOT emit `set_hooks([])` when `hooks=None`.
  * test_codegen_v7_branch_explicit_clear_hooks_still_works pins
    the corollary: `hooks=[]` MUST still emit `set_hooks([])` so
    re-launches that drop hooks clear the stored list.

Live verification on real AWS c6i.large cluster (hook-test-autostop):

  Before fix:
    UP → UP → UP → UP → UP → STOPPED at t=105s (no AUTOSTOPPING)

  After fix:
    UP → UP → UP → UP → AUTOSTOPPING at t=92s ✅

* [Hooks] Smoke pin: sky exec does NOT clear stored hooks

A reviewer (Devin AI) flagged a hypothetical regression where
`sky exec` on an existing cluster might wipe the stored
lifecycle_hooks list. Reasoning: `_execute`'s PRE_EXEC stage builds a
hooks_payload that becomes `[]` when `task_hooks=None` and
`cluster_exists=True`, which would flow into the
`elif hooks_payload is not None:` branch and call set_autostop with
`hooks=[]` (clear_hooks=True on the wire).

The claim does not match current behavior: `sky exec` calls
`_execute` with `stages=[Stage.SYNC_WORKDIR, Stage.EXEC]`, NOT
including Stage.PRE_EXEC. The `if Stage.PRE_EXEC in stages and not
dryrun:` guard at execution.py:613 gates the entire hooks_payload
computation, so the wipe path is correctly inaccessible from
`sky exec`. Local repro confirmed the stored hooks list survives
a `sky exec` invocation unchanged.

adds Stage.PRE_EXEC to `sky exec`'s stages list would silently
re-introduce the bug — users only discovering it when a hook stops
firing on the next teardown. Add a smoke test that pins the
contract:

  1. Launch with hook A → verify stored = [A]
  2. sky exec name -- "echo hello"

subject: [Kubernetes] Fail fast when cluster has no default StorageClass (#9713)
message:
[Kubernetes] Fail fast when cluster has no default StorageClass (#9713)

* [Kubernetes] Fail fast when cluster has no default StorageClass

When `_apply_pvc_volume` is invoked without an explicit
`config.storage_class_name`, Kubernetes falls back to the cluster's
default StorageClass at PVC-bind time. If no class is annotated default,
the PVC sits in Pending forever with no clear signal — the user sees
"created successfully" and silently waits.

Add a pre-flight check that lists the cluster's StorageClasses, looks
for the current (`storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class`) or
legacy beta annotation, and raises `KubernetesError` with an actionable
message when none is found. The truthy parser matches
`strconv.ParseBool` semantics (`true`/`True`/`TRUE`/`1`/`t`/`T`) to
recognize capitalized values emitted by some Helm charts in the wild.

The empty-default-API-error branch is given a distinct error message
("Failed to list storage classes…") so RBAC or connectivity failures
during the check aren't conflated with the empty-default condition.

Tested: 9 unit tests in
`tests/unit_tests/test_sky/provision/test_kubernetes_volume.py` cover
explicit-SC pass-through, omitted-with-default, legacy beta annotation,
capitalized truthy values, omitted-with-no-default error message,
multiple defaults proceeding, and API-error path. All passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Skip SC validation for use_existing; tolerate 401/403 RBAC

Two follow-ups to address review feedback:

1. When `use_existing=True`, `create_persistent_volume_claim` looks up
   the existing PVC by name/label and never provisions a new one. Both
   the explicit-name `read_storage_class` check and the empty-default
   safety net are irrelevant in that path — the existing PVC already
   has its own SC binding. Skip both. Previously, importing an existing
   PVC on a cluster with no default-annotated StorageClass would
   spuriously fail with the empty-default error.

2. Listing StorageClasses (and `get` on a specific one) requires
   cluster-scoped permissions. Namespace-constrained users on multi-
   tenant clusters often lack these but can still create PVCs in their
   namespace and rely on K8s admission to bind. On 401/403, log a
   warning and proceed instead of raising — K8s will surface a real
   binding error if the SC is actually invalid or missing. 404 still
   raises (catches real typos in user-supplied SC names).

Helper `_is_rbac_permission_error` centralizes the 401/403 check;
`_validate_explicit_storage_class` factors out the explicit-name path
so both API calls go through the same RBAC-tolerance treatment.

Tested: 15 unit tests pass, including 6 new ones — use_existing skips
both checks (with and without explicit SC), 401/403 on either API call
is tolerated, 404 on read_storage_class still raises, and the 500
non-RBAC error still propagates as `KubernetesError`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Skip SC validation for `storageClassName: ""` opt-out

`storageClassName: ""` (empty string) is the K8s convention for "no
storage class" — opt out of dynamic provisioning, used to bind a PVC
to a manually-created PV (static provisioning) or skip the cluster's
default class. Previously, `_apply_pvc_volume` treated `''` as a name
to validate, called `read_storage_class(name='')`, and raised
`KubernetesError`. Regression for the static-binding use case.

Three-way branch the dispatch:
  - non-empty name: validate that the class exists
  - None (omitted): check the cluster has a default StorageClass
  - '' (opt-out):    skip both — let K8s handle binding semantics

Also clean up test docstrings: the O1/O2/... prefixes were internal
trace labels from the design plan and meaningless to anyone reading
the tests without that context. Replaced with descriptive one-liners
that stand alone.

Tested: 16 unit tests pass, including the new
`test_apply_pvc_empty_string_storage_class_skips_both_checks` which
asserts neither SC API is called when `storage_class_name=''`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Move StorageClass default-annotation helpers to utils

Hoist the truthy-annotation parser and the default-StorageClass
annotation check out of `_apply_pvc_volume` into public helpers in
`sky/provision/kubernetes/utils.py`:

- `is_truthy_annotation(value)` — matches `strconv.ParseBool` semantics
  used by K8s admission for boolean annotations.
- `is_default_storage_class(sc)` — checks both the current and legacy
  beta `is-default-class` annotations; robust to missing metadata.
- `DEFAULT_STORAGE_CLASS_ANNOTATION` /
  `DEFAULT_STORAGE_CLASS_ANNOTATION_LEGACY` constants.

`_check_cluster_has_default_storage_class` now calls
`kubernetes_utils.is_default_storage_class(sc)` instead of inlining the
annotation comparison, and the user-facing error message references
`kubernetes_utils.DEFAULT_STORAGE_CLASS_ANNOTATION` so the constant
stays the single source of truth.

No behavior change — the 16 existing unit tests still pass. The
refactor lets other K8s code paths reuse the same default-detection
logic without re-implementing the truthy parser.

message:
[Test] Resolve K8s context dynamically + dual-mode host_network test (#9716)

Build 378 of nightly-build-shared-gke-api-server failed 7 tests on
a real multi-node GKE pipeline. Two root causes, fixed together
because both need the same primitive — a kubeconfig-context lookup
that doesn't assume a Kind-style single-cluster runner.

(1) test_lifecycle_hooks.py — 6 failing tests
    Every kubectl call hardcoded ``--context kind-skypilot`` (42 sites
    in 7 tests, added with the lifecycle-hooks framework in #9064).
    That context only exists on the Kind-based smoke pipelines; on
    pipelines where workloads run elsewhere, the call silently empties
    ``$pod`` and the subsequent ``kubectl delete ""`` aborts.

    Replace with smoke_tests_utils.kubectl_for_cluster(name), a shared
    helper whose returned ``kubectl --context "$ctx"`` resolves <ctx>
    at *shell* runtime by scanning kubeconfig contexts for the one
    that actually owns a pod with the cluster's name. Single-context
    runners (Kind) short-circuit on the first iteration; multi-context
    runners (shared-GKE has both the API server's GKE cluster and the
    workload cluster) pick the right one.

(2) test_kubernetes_host_network_multi_node_same_node
    The test asserted single-node-only behaviour (anti-affinity must
    block the 2nd pod). On the multi-node shared-GKE pipeline that
    launch succeeds — the documented mode-b cross-node happy path —
    and the test failed. Build 367's previous "pass" was a false
    positive: the launch died with a urllib3 ProtocolError, but the
    grep ``-iE "anti-?affinity"`` matched SkyPilot's own debug dump
    of the generated pod spec (``"podAntiAffinity":``), passing for
    the wrong reason.

    Rewrite as a dual-mode test, branched on schedulable-node count
    from sky.kubernetes_node_info():
      - 1 node:  existing fail-loud assertion, with the grep
        tightened to ``didn't match.*anti-?affinity`` (the actual
        kube-scheduler rejection, not the bare substring that also
        appears in SkyPilot's debug logs).
      - >=2 nodes:  assert launch succeeds AND head + worker pods
        land on distinct K8s nodes (mode-b's cross-node happy path,
        which the test never previously covered).

subject: [Core] Pass to_provision into Provisioner.template_override (#9679)
message:
[Core] Pass to_provision into Provisioner.template_override (#9679)

The ``TemplateOverrideFn`` protocol receives only ``task`` today, which
forces plugin implementers to read the user's pre-optimizer
``task.resources[0]`` (whose ``region`` is routinely ``None`` for tasks
that didn't pin one in YAML) or to fall back to ``task.best_resources``
(which is the optimizer's first pick and can drift from the current
attempt during failover).

Add ``to_provision: Resources`` as a positional parameter. The backend
already has it in scope at the call site — it's the same resource passed
into ``Cloud.make_deploy_resources_variables`` immediately afterwards,
with ``region`` asserted non-None at ``cloud_vm_ray_backend.py:1056``.
Surfacing it through the protocol lets implementations read
``to_provision.region`` directly and stay correct across the failover
loop (``template_override`` is re-invoked per attempt).

Test plan:
- Existing call site updated to pass ``to_provision`` positionally.
- No OSS-side plugins implement ``template_override`` today, so no
  tests change. Plugin authors implementing the protocol will see a
  ``TypeError`` at the call site if they don't accept the new arg,
  which is the intended migration signal.

subject: [Kubernetes] Fix owner identity check for scoped kubeconfig names (#9725)
message:
[Kubernetes] Fix owner identity check for scoped kubeconfig names (#9725)

* [Kubernetes] Ignore kubeconfig name-scope suffix in owner identity check

When a context's cluster/user `name` fields are rewritten with a
`__sky__<context>` suffix during kubeconfig assembly, the derived owner
identity string (`<cluster>_<user>_<namespace>`) changes shape. Clusters
whose owner was recorded before the suffix existed then fail the
owner-identity equality check, which aborts status refresh and blocks
management operations (exec/logs/stop/down) on those clusters.

Normalize both sides by stripping the `__sky__<context>` scope segments
before comparing, and self-heal the stored owner to the current identity
on a scope-only match so later checks pass exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Harden kubeconfig name-scope stripping for underscored contexts

The owner-identity normalizer used `__sky__[^_]*`, which strips only up to
the first underscore of the scope token. Context names can contain
underscores (e.g. GKE `gke_<project>_<zone>_<cluster>`), so the suffix was
left partially in place and the owner check still mismatched.

Anchor on the namespace instead: a Kubernetes namespace cannot contain `_`,
so the scope token is the text between the last `__sky__` and the final
`_<namespace>`. Removing every occurrence of that token recovers the
pre-scoping identity regardless of underscores in the context, cluster, or
user names. Add a GKE-style regression test with an underscored context.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Keep cloud identity check enabled in owner-identity scope tests

CI runs unit tests with SKYPILOT_SKIP_CLOUD_IDENTITY_CHECK=1, which makes
_check_owner_identity_with_record return at its first line. The new
Kubernetes owner-identity scope tests therefore never exercised the
comparison: the positive cases saw no self-heal and the negative case did
not raise. Clear the env var in each test so the check actually runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Core] Skip teardown-hook codegen on clusters with no hooks declared (#9728)
message:
[Core] Skip teardown-hook codegen on clusters with no hooks declared (#9728)

`sky down` / `sky stop` on a cluster that never declared any
lifecycle hook still SSHes to the head to run a Python codegen
whose only purpose is to (a) execute user-declared hooks and (b)
claim a per-event teardown slot to block a racing preemption-hook
fire. With no hooks declared, both jobs are no-ops — there's
nothing to run and no competing preemption hook can race. The SSH
itself is pure overhead, and worse, surfaces a misleading warning
whenever the head IP is transiently unreachable (already partway
shut down, stale cached handle, network blip):

  Failed to run down hook on '<cluster>': . Proceeding with teardown.

…on a cluster the user never put a hook on. Reported by a user
who'd never used lifecycle hooks and was confused by the warning
appearing on every teardown.

Fix: bail early when `handle.launched_resources.hooks` is None /
empty. The slot-claim still runs unconditionally as soon as ANY
hook is declared (even just a preemption hook) so the SIGTERM ↔
sky-down race fix from PR #9064 remains intact.

Two test changes:

  - `tests/unit_tests/test_lifecycle_hooks.py`:
    new `test_sky_down_skips_codegen_when_no_hooks_declared` pins
    the no-SSH contract for both `_maybe_run_down_hooks` and
    `_maybe_run_stop_hooks` against `hooks=None` and `hooks=[]`.
    Updated `test_sky_down_claims_teardown_even_without_down_hooks`
    and `test_sky_stop_fires_stop_hook_via_codegen` to give their
    `_FakeHandle.launched_resources` a populated `hooks` list, so
    the contract they pin (codegen MUST run when ANY hook is
    declared) is preserved cleanly under the new guard.

  - `tests/smoke_tests/test_lifecycle_hooks.py`:
    new `test_hook_sky_down_no_hooks_skips_head_codegen` launches a
    cluster from the bare `tests/test_yamls/minimal.yaml` (zero
    hooks anywhere), runs `sky down`, and asserts the output
    contains neither the spinner message ("Running down hook on
    '<cluster>'") nor the failure warning ("Failed to run down
    hook on '<cluster>': …"). Both signals fire pre-fix and are
    absent post-fix.

Verified locally with `conda activate sky`:

  pytest tests/unit_tests/test_lifecycle_hooks.py
  # Pre-fix: test_sky_down_skips_codegen_when_no_hooks_declared FAILS
  #          (run_on_head called twice when hooks=None)
  # Post-fix: 75 passed, 1 unrelated pre-existing failure

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Core] Fix KeyError on restart for clusters predating a nested provider field (#9723)
message:
[Core] Fix KeyError on restart for clusters predating a nested provider field (#9723)

* [Core] Fix KeyError on restart for clusters predating a nested provider field

When restarting a STOPPED cluster, write_cluster_config restores launch
fields from the cluster's stored YAML via _replace_yaml_dicts. The
exception-revert loop walked a multi-level key path (e.g.
('provider', 'security_group', 'GroupName')) assuming every intermediate
dict existed. But 'provider' is restored wholesale from the old YAML, so
for a cluster created before that nested field existed (e.g. Nebius
clusters created before native security groups were added), the old
provider block has no 'security_group' and the traversal raised
KeyError: 'security_group'. New clusters were unaffected because no old
YAML exists to merge.

Recreate missing intermediate keys with setdefault so the new value is
still applied instead of crashing. This is a no-op for existing
well-formed YAMLs (the key is already present), matching the defensive
behavior already used by the sibling exception-finder and hash-removal
loops.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] Harden nested-key revert against null/non-dict intermediates

Address review feedback: dict.setdefault(key, {}) returns the existing
value when the key is present, so an intermediate key present but null
(YAML `key:` parses to None) would yield None and then crash on the next
descent. Treat any non-dict intermediate (missing, null, or scalar) as
absent and rebuild the path. Add a regression test for the null case.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Nebius] Don't mask SG create errors as a race in get_or_create_security_group

When restarting a cluster created before native security groups existed,
bootstrap creates the cluster SG. If that create() fails for a real
reason (bad network, quota, transient VPC error), the except block
assumed it was an ALREADY_EXISTS race and re-fetched with an unwrapped
get_by_name. Since the SG was never created, the re-fetch raised a
misleading "NOT_FOUND: SecurityGroup ... not found" that masked the real
create error and aborted provisioning as ResourcesUnavailableError.

Only recover from an actual ALREADY_EXISTS conflict (checked via the
structured gRPC status code, with a string fallback); re-raise any other
create error so the true cause is visible. The race re-fetch now uses the
wrapped lookup and re-raises the original error if the SG is absent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: [Server] Return 404 for missing dashboard _next/ assets instead of index.html (#9722)
message:
[Server] Return 404 for missing dashboard _next/ assets instead of index.html (#9722)

* [Server] Return 404 for missing dashboard _next/ assets

The dashboard catch-all served index.html (200, text/html) for any
unmatched /dashboard/ path, including missing _next/ build assets. When a
content-hashed .js/.css is absent (e.g. a replica serving a different
build during a rolling update), returning the HTML shell lets a CDN cache
it under the asset URL. The browser then refuses to execute the text/html
response as a script (strict MIME checking) and the dashboard renders
blank until the cache entry expires.

Return 404 for missing _next/ paths so they are never cached as HTML,
while keeping the index.html SPA fallback for client-side page routes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Dashboard] Add Cache-Control: no-store to _next/ 404 and regression tests

Per review feedback: add Cache-Control: no-store header to the 404 raised for
missing _next/ build assets so CDNs that negative-cache 404s by default won't
freeze the bad response. Add two unit tests asserting the 404+header behaviour
and that extensionless client-side routes still fall through to index.html.

subject: [Kubernetes] Per-workspace namespace via `context_configs` (#9640)
message:
[Kubernetes] Per-workspace namespace via `context_configs` (#9640)

* [Kubernetes] Add `namespace` to context-config schemas

Adds the `namespace` field at three layers so workspaces sharing a
single physical Kubernetes cluster can target different namespaces
without synthesizing one kubeconfig context per namespace:

  - global `kubernetes.namespace`
  - global `kubernetes.context_configs.<ctx>.namespace`
  - per-workspace `workspaces.<ws>.kubernetes.context_configs.<ctx>.namespace`

Layer 1 and 2 come "for free" from adding `namespace` to the shared
`_CONTEXT_CONFIG_SCHEMA_KUBERNETES` dict (mirrors #9635's pattern for
`kueue.local_queue_name`). Layer 3 is added by listing `namespace` as
an explicit property of the workspace-level `context_configs.<ctx>`
block, alongside the existing `kueue` and `quota` properties.

The workspace-level shorthand `workspaces.<ws>.kubernetes.namespace`
(without `context_configs.<ctx>`) is intentionally NOT added — the
per-context form covers every workspace with an explicit
`allowed_contexts` list, and keeping a single mechanism avoids two
resolution paths to document and reason about. A test enforces that
the shorthand is rejected on the server. Easy to add later if there
is demand (e.g. for the `allowed_contexts: 'all'` case).

Schema-only change in this commit; resolver and call-site updates
follow in subsequent commits.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* [Kubernetes] Add `get_effective_namespace` resolver

Adds a helper that resolves `kubernetes.namespace` across four
layers, most-specific wins:

  1. workspaces.<ws>.kubernetes.context_configs.<ctx>.namespace
  2. workspaces.<ws>.kubernetes.namespace
  3. kubernetes.context_configs.<ctx>.namespace
  4. kubernetes.namespace

Returns None when unset at every layer; the kubeconfig-default
fallback is left to the caller (see the follow-up commit adding
`get_namespace` in `sky/provision/kubernetes/utils.py`). This keeps
the resolver a pure config lookup with no side effects.

Shape: a small `_lookup(scope)` closure handles the within-scope
precedence (per-context > cloud-level) and the override merge; the
outer flow is two top-level cases — workspace scope, then global —
with early returns. Diverges from `get_effective_queue_name`'s flat
list-of-scopes loop because namespace has a single spelling (no
`_QUEUE_NAME_KEYS` to iterate); the simpler shape matches the
simpler resolution job.

Layer (2) is not currently exposed in the workspace schema (only
`kueue`, `quota`, `context_configs`, plus plugin-registered fields).
It is included in the resolver so plugin-registered or pass-through
workspace-level entries still resolve correctly.

A more general refactor — extending
`config_utils.get_cloud_config_value_from_dict` to consult
workspace-level `context_configs` for any field — would also subsume
the half-implemented workspace-`context_configs` path inside
`get_effective_queue_name`. That refactor is deliberately deferred:
larger blast radius (touches every `get_effective_region_config`
caller) and best handled as its own change so reviewers can evaluate
it on its own merits.

Tests cover full precedence matrix, the `override_configs` regression
scenario (mirrors `test_get_effective_queue_name_workspace_override`),
and the empty-config case.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* [Kubernetes] Add `get_namespace` helper with kubeconfig fallback

Adds `get_namespace(context, workspace=None, override_configs=None)`
in `sky/provision/kubernetes/utils.py` next to
`get_kube_config_context_namespace`. The helper:

  1. Calls `skypilot_config.get_effective_namespace` to resolve the
     namespace from config (workspace per-context > workspace cloud >
     global per-context > global cloud > None).
  2. Falls back to `get_kube_config_context_namespace(context)` when
     no config layer matches, preserving today's behavior for
     configs that don't set `namespace`.

`get_namespace` is a drop-in replacement for
`get_kube_config_context_namespace` at sites that have a workspace
in scope (the actual call-site swaps land in the next commit).

Tests cover: config-value wins over kubeconfig fallback;
`override_configs` are forwarded; `context=None` propagates to the
current-context kubeconfig default; the kubeconfig fallback is
exercised when the resolver returns None.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* [Kubernetes] Switch namespace-resolving call sites to `get_namespace`

Migrates three call sites from `get_kube_config_context_namespace`
to the workspace-aware `get_namespace` helper. After this commit, a
workspace that sets `kubernetes.context_configs.<ctx>.namespace`
sees its pods, volumes, and managed-jobs networking land in that
namespace instead of the kubeconfig context's default.

Switched:

  - `sky/clouds/kubernetes.py:make_deploy_resources_variables` — the
    main `sky launch` path. Sets `provider_config['namespace']` at
    cluster creation, so downstream sites that read it
    (`get_namespace_from_config`, the `network.py` ports/IP lookups)
    automatically pick up the workspace-resolved namespace without
    further changes. Passes
    `override_configs=resources.cluster_config_overrides` to honor
    per-launch overrides.

  - `sky/provision/kubernetes/volume.py:_get_context_namespace` —
    volumes created without an explicit namespace now use the
    workspace's resolved namespace, matching where the workspace's
    pods land.

  - `sky/jobs/job_group_networking.py:_get_k8s_namespace_from_handle`
    — managed-jobs networking uses the workspace's resolved
    namespace instead of the raw kubeconfig default. Reading the
    namespace directly off the cluster handle would be strictly
    more correct (a handle for a cluster created in a different
    workspace would still resolve via the active workspace here);
    out of scope for this PR.

Not switched (intentional):

  - `get_kube_config_context_namespace` itself stays as the
    underlying kubeconfig lookup.
  - `check_credentials` test — no workspace conceptually involved.
  - `get_namespace_from_config` fallback + the `network.py`
    `provider_config.get('namespace', ...)` fallback paths — these
    are the legacy-cluster path: `provider_config['namespace']` is
    set at provisioning time and is the source of truth for the
    cluster's lifetime; the kubeconfig fallback only triggers for
    clusters created before this change. Switching the fallback
    would change the namespace lookup for legacy clusters if the
    user later sets the new config, which would break those clusters.

Pre-existing inconsistency noted during the audit:
`_open_ports_using_ingress` builds an ingress URL path from
`get_kube_config_context_namespace(context)` while the same
function's service creation uses `get_namespace_from_config`. For
new clusters with workspace-namespace overrides these could
diverge. Left for a separate follow-up to keep this PR focused.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* [Kubernetes] Document `namespace` config

Document the new `kubernetes.namespace` field and its per-context /
per-workspace overrides:

- `config.rst`: add a dedicated `kubernetes.namespace` section
  (global form + per-context via `context_configs`), surface the
  field in the top example block, and cross-link to Workspaces for
  per-workspace overrides.
- `admin/workspaces.rst`: show
  `workspaces.<ws>.kubernetes.context_configs.<ctx>.namespace` in

  different namespace per workspace.
- `reference/kubernetes/multi-kubernetes.rst`: add `namespace` to
  the list of per-context configurable fields.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* ci: trigger re-run

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* [Kubernetes] Fix ingress URL namespace divergence

`_open_ports_using_ingress` resolves the Service's namespace from
`provider_config` (set at provisioning time, source of truth for the
cluster's lifetime) but re-resolves the namespace embedded in the
Ingress URL path from `get_kube_config_context_namespace(context)`,
which only reads the kubeconfig context's default. Pre-PR these two
usually agreed because `provider_config['namespace']` was sourced
from the kubeconfig default; with the workspace/per-context override
shipped earlier in this PR they routinely diverge — the Service is
created in the workspace's namespace, but the Ingress URL embeds the
kubeconfig default, so nginx routes to a non-existent service.

Use the local `namespace` variable already resolved a few lines above
(from `provider_config`) for the URL path. The two are now provably
equal — same variable.

Add a regression test in `tests/unit_tests/kubernetes/test_network.py`
that exercises the divergent case (provider namespace `team-a`,
kubeconfig default `kubeconfig-default`) and asserts:
  - the URL path contains the provider namespace,
  - the URL path does not contain the kubeconfig default,
  - `get_kube_config_context_namespace` is not consulted on this path,
  - all ports in a multi-port fan-out share the same namespace.

The other three `get_kube_config_context_namespace` uses in this file
(`_query_ports_for_loadbalancer`, `_query_ports_for_ingress`,
`_query_ports_for_podip`) are intentionally left as-is: they follow
the legacy-cluster fallback pattern
`provider_config.get('namespace', kubeconfig-fallback)` and only hit
the kubeconfig path for clusters provisioned before the
`provider_config['namespace']` field existed.

Addresses review comments from @hdf67fd849db16fcd and @h2387b73fd264574c on

* [Jobs] Read JobGroup namespace from cluster YAML, not active workspace

`_get_k8s_namespace_from_handle` resolved the JobGroup peer-DNS

which (with no `workspace=` arg) defaults to thread-local
`get_active_workspace()`. The handle carries the cluster's context but
not its launch-time workspace, so a JobGroup spanning clusters launched

active workspace different from the cluster's launch one — would

authoritative source for the namespace the pods actually live in and is
workspace-invariant. Mirrors the existing

which would re-introduce the workspace race) for legacy clusters whose
