subject: [Chart] Optional server log mirror via SKYPILOT_SERVER_LOG_MIRROR_DIR (#9754)
message:
[Chart] Optional server log mirror via SKYPILOT_SERVER_LOG_MIRROR_DIR (#9754)

* [Chart] Optional server log mirror via SKYPILOT_SERVER_LOG_MIRROR_DIR

Operators running the API server in containers may want a stable
secondary log file (e.g. NFS-backed, sidecar collector) that survives
the in-container logrotate copytruncate of
/root/.sky/api_server/server.log and pod replacement.

When SKYPILOT_SERVER_LOG_MIRROR_DIR is set, the chart's tee also
writes a per-pod, per-boot mirror file at
<dir>/$HOSTNAME/server-<UTC_ISO>.log alongside the usual local
server.log. Each server process boot creates a new file so log
history persists across logrotate and process restarts; placing
$HOSTNAME in the path keeps replicas from clobbering each other when
the mirror dir lives on shared (RWX) storage.

No behavior change when the env is unset.

* [Chart] Address review: word splitting + graceful mkdir failure

* Drop the `${var:+"$var"}` tee argument: under /bin/sh (dash/busybox)
  the inner quotes aren't preserved by the outer unquoted parameter
  expansion, so a mirror path containing spaces would be word-split.
  Use a clean `if mkdir; then tee a b; else tee a; fi` instead.
* Replace `\${HOSTNAME:-\$(hostname)}` with `\${HOSTNAME:-unknown}`:
  k8s always sets HOSTNAME, so the fallback is purely defensive; running
  `\$(hostname)` would fail under `set -e` on images without the binary.
* Treat mirror as opportunistic: if `mkdir -p` fails (e.g. RO mount,
  permissions, NFS blip), log a warning and fall back to local-only
  logging instead of crash-looping the API server pod under `set -e`.

* [Chart] Support log mirror without serveServerLog

Decouple SKYPILOT_SERVER_LOG_MIRROR_DIR from serveServerLog so the
mirror can be enabled in either mode. Useful for deployments that
opt out of the in-container /root/.sky/api_server/server.log (to skip
its disk overhead and rely on k8s pod logs) but still want a durable
copy on shared storage for cross-replica debug collection.

* Resolve the mirror sink path before the serveServerLog branch so
  both renders can use it.
* serveServerLog=false + mirror set: still spin up the FIFO + a tee
  that only writes to the mirror file. tee's stdout is inherited
  from the shell — i.e. the container's stdout — so k8s pod logs
  continue to work exactly as the no-FIFO direct-exec path.
* serveServerLog=false + mirror unset: unchanged direct-exec path.
* Add two helm unit tests covering the new combinations.

subject: [Kubernetes] Respect configured pod tolerations in node-health display (#9750)
message:
[Kubernetes] Respect configured pod tolerations in node-health display (#9750)

* [Kubernetes] Respect configured pod tolerations in node-health display

Today the dashboard's Infra page, `sky show-gpus`, and any caller of
`get_kubernetes_node_info()` treats *any* node taint (after the existing
PreferNoSchedule / cordon / not-ready / handled-key / role-prefix
filtering) as unschedulable. That's wrong for the common case where a
user has configured `kubernetes.pod_config.spec.tolerations` to tolerate
a custom taint on their nodes: jobs schedule fine, but the dashboard
shows the nodes as not-ready and `show-gpus` reports 0 available GPUs.

Add a thin layer that respects those configured tolerations when
deciding whether a remaining taint makes a node unschedulable for the
user's workloads:

- New `get_configured_tolerations(context)` reads
  `kubernetes.pod_config.spec.tolerations` via the existing
  `get_effective_region_config` plumbing (so per-context overrides Just
  Work). Returns `None` when nothing is configured, which makes
  downstream call sites byte-identical to today.
- New `taint_is_tolerated(taint, tolerations)` implements standard K8s
  toleration semantics (Equal vs. Exists; empty effect matches all;
  empty key + Exists is a wildcard).
- `V1Node.get_taints()` gains one optional `tolerations=` kwarg. When
  passed (a list, possibly empty), each retained taint dict gets a
  `'tolerated': bool` key. Existing `exclude_*` filtering is unchanged.
  Omitted / None preserves today's exact wire shape.
- `get_kubernetes_node_info()` and `_get_total_accelerators()` thread
  the configured tolerations through and recompute `node_is_tainted` as
  `any(not t.tolerated for t in node_taints)`. The separate `is_ready`
  / `is_cordoned` gating is untouched.
- Infra page dashboard: narrow the existing gray taint chip to
  un-tolerated taints; tolerated-only nodes fall into the existing
  green "Healthy" rendering. No new chip type.

Tested:
- Added 23 unit tests in
  `tests/unit_tests/kubernetes/test_kubernetes_utils.py` covering
  `taint_is_tolerated` (14 K8s-semantics rows), `get_configured_tolerations`
  (None / configured / empty / malformed), and
  `V1Node.get_taints(tolerations=...)` (no-tolerations is byte-identical;
  empty list marks all tolerated=False; matching toleration marks
  tolerated=True; exclude_* filtering still applies).
- Full kubernetes_utils unit-test file passes (165 tests).
- Dashboard builds clean with `npm run build` in `sky/dashboard`.
- Manual e2e verification on a live Kubernetes cluster (taint a node +
  configure a matching toleration + confirm `sky show-gpus` and Infra
  page reflect the node as Healthy) is planned before merge.

* Flatten show-gpus taint-status nesting

Hoist the un-tolerated-taint computation above the `if taints:` guard
since an empty/None taints list already produces an empty list
comprehension, then drop the inner `if untolerated_taints:` since the
outer one already gates rendering. Equivalent behavior, one less level
of nesting.

Addresses review comment skypilot-org/skypilot#9750 (discussion_r3321369713).

* Preserve falsy taint values (0, False) in toleration matching

The previous `str(x or '')` idiom collapses Python-falsy values to
'' — `str(0 or '')` → `''`, `str(False or '')` → `''`. A YAML-parsed
`value: 0` toleration would therefore fail to match a K8s taint whose
value is the string `'0'`, falsely marking the node un-tolerated.

Switch to `'' if v is None else str(v)` (via a local helper) which
distinguishes 'absent' from 'set to a falsy value'. The Equal operator
default keeps its `or 'Equal'` since '' is not a valid operator.

Added regression tests for `value: 0` (int) and `value: false` (bool),
plus an inverse-collapse case (value-less taint, '0' toleration must
NOT match).

Addresses review comment skypilot-org/skypilot#9750 (discussion_r3321364550).

* Simplify: extract shared helpers, reuse resolve_effective_pod_config

Applied 5 cleanups from a /simplify pass:

1. Extracted `has_untolerated_taint(taints)` helper in
   `sky/provision/kubernetes/utils.py`. The
   `any(not t.get('tolerated', False) for t in taints)` predicate was
   copy-pasted in 3 Python sites (catalog `_get_total_accelerators`,
   utils `get_kubernetes_node_info`, CLI `_count_not_ready_gpus`) —
   collapsed to a single call. Added a parametrized unit test.

2. `get_configured_tolerations` now delegates to the existing
   `resolve_effective_pod_config(...)` instead of reimplementing the
   same `get_effective_region_config(keys=('pod_config',))` + dict
   lookup chain. Same K8s-specific dict-merge for per-context
   tolerations; fewer lines of duplication; relies on the canonical
   reader.

3. Moved `_str_or_empty` from a closure inside `taint_is_tolerated`
   to module scope. Avoids constructing a function object on every
   matcher call.

4. Parametrized the 5 `*_coerces_*` unit tests into one
   `test_taint_is_tolerated_str_coercion` with 5 ids
   (yaml-int / yaml-bool / yaml-int-zero / yaml-bool-false /
   inverse-collapse). Same regression coverage, ~40 LOC less.

5. Extracted `isNodeNotReadyForGpus(nodeData)` helper in
   `sky/dashboard/src/data/connectors/infra.jsx`. The
   isReady/isCordoned/isTainted/isNodeNotReady block was duplicated
   across two near-identical loops — both call sites now share one
   helper, eliminating drift risk.

178 unit tests pass; dashboard build clean.

* Address review: SSH-context support + resolve None to current kube context

Two fixes from @hdf67fd849db16fcd:

1. `get_configured_tolerations` now passes `cloud=clouds.SSH()` to
   `resolve_effective_pod_config` for `ssh-<pool>` contexts.
   Previously it always passed `cloud=None`, which made
   `resolve_effective_pod_config` read the `kubernetes.*` config
   namespace and skip the `ssh-` prefix-stripping. For an SSH-pool
   context that meant SSH-scoped tolerations would be missed and a
   global `kubernetes.pod_config` toleration would leak onto SSH node
   health. Auto-detect via `context.startswith('ssh-')` to keep the
   helper's signature unchanged.

2. `get_kubernetes_node_info` direct-path branch now resolves
   `context=None` to `get_current_kube_config_context_name()` before
   reading tolerations. `get_kubernetes_nodes(context=None)`
   internally resolves to the current kube context, but
   `get_configured_tolerations(None)` would have skipped
   `context_configs` overrides — so a user with a per-context
   toleration on the current context would not see those nodes
   honored. The plugin branch above already resolves the same way.

Added two regression tests: `*_ssh_context_uses_ssh_namespace`
asserts the underlying `get_effective_region_config` is called with
`(cloud='ssh', region='cluster1')` for an `ssh-cluster1` context.

Addresses skypilot-org/skypilot#9750 (discussion_r3322597523 + r3322597524).

subject: [Kubernetes] Coerce Python bool tolerations to lowercase for taint match (#9756)
message:
[Kubernetes] Coerce Python bool tolerations to lowercase for taint match (#9756)

`_str_or_empty` already coerces non-string toleration / taint values to
string so YAML-parsed scalars (`value: 0`, `value: 1.5`, `value: true`)
match against the K8s API's always-string taint fields. But `str(True)`
yields the Python-cased `'True'`, while K8s stores taint values as
whatever Go's YAML serializer emits — always lowercase (`'true'` /
`'false'`). A `kubectl taint nodes X foo=true:NoSchedule` ends up with
`value: "true"` on the node.

That silent mismatch means a config

    tolerations:
      - key: foo
        operator: Equal
        value: true       # unquoted YAML → Python True → 'True'
        effect: NoSchedule

would never match a real K8s taint with `value: "true"` — the operator
sees `'True' != 'true'` and the taint reads un-tolerated. The user has
to quote the value (`value: "true"`) to work around it.

Special-case `bool` inside `_str_or_empty` to lowercase. Mirrors what
Go's `strconv.FormatBool` / `fmt.Sprintf("%t", ...)` produce, so the
matcher stays in lockstep with how K8s actually stores taint values.

Tests:
- Updates `yaml-bool` / `yaml-bool-false` parametrize cases to use
  `'true'` / `'false'` taint values (the realistic K8s shape).
- Adds two `python-cased-bool-no-match` cases to assert strictness:
  a hypothetical taint stored as Python-cased `'True'` / `'False'`
  must NOT match a Python-bool toleration — the lowercase coercion
  is one-directional, not a case-insensitive compare.

subject: [Kubernetes][Jobs] Surface pod OOM and eviction reasons for jobs and clusters (#9758)
message:
[Kubernetes][Jobs] Surface pod OOM and eviction reasons for jobs and clusters (#9758)

* [Jobs][Kubernetes] Surface pod OOM and fail managed jobs as FAILED_SETUP

When a managed job's K8s pod is OOM-killed during cluster/runtime setup,
SkyPilot previously surfaced only the bare kubectl error ("cannot exec
into a container in a completed pod") and retried the launch forever, so
the job hung in STARTING with no failure reason.

Two layers:

- Surface: KubernetesCommandRunner enriches a failed `kubectl exec`'s
  stderr with the pod's termination reason (e.g. "OOMKilled (exit code
  137)") plus a remediation hint, gated on "pod gone" signatures so
  ordinary command failures (e.g. exit 127) don't trigger an extra API
  read. Reason extraction (`get_condensed_pod_reason`) is lifted from
  instance.py into kubernetes/utils.py and shared.

- Terminal: recovery_strategy detects an OOM launch failure and raises
  the (previously unused) ClusterSetUpError instead of retrying;
  controller maps it to ManagedJobStatus.FAILED_SETUP with the OOM
  reason written to failure_reason (shown in the CLI and the
  dashboard).

Also unifies the duplicate K8s failure-hint tables: the canonical
KUBERNETES_FAILURE_HINTS now lives in kubernetes/utils.py and is consumed
by both the provision-failure formatter (cloud_vm_ray_backend) and the
pod-OOM diagnosis path.

Tested:
- Added unit tests (26): get_condensed_pod_reason, _pod_terminated_abnormally,
  diagnose_terminated_pod, match_kubernetes_failure_hint (kubernetes utils);
  KubernetesCommandRunner._diagnose_dead_pod + run() stderr enrichment;
  recovery_strategy._is_oom_failure. All pass.
- Manual e2e on a Kubernetes cluster: a job whose pod OOMs during setup
  now reaches FAILED_SETUP in ~45s with failure_reason containing
  "OOMKilled (exit code 137)" + the memory hint, vs. hanging in STARTING.
- format.sh clean on all changed source files (mypy ok, pylint 10.00/10).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Surface pod OOM in cluster-abnormal reason during run phase

When a managed job's pod is OOMKilled mid-run, the container restarts and
the cluster briefly goes INIT (ray unhealthy), so the controller treats it
as a preemption and recovers. The recovery event showed only the generic
"ray cluster is unhealthy" message, with no indication of the OOM on the
dashboard.

The OOM reason survives in the container's last_state.terminated after the
restart, but _get_pod_health_issues only inspected the current state. Now,
for a not-ready container, it also surfaces a non-zero last_state
termination (e.g. "OOMKilled (exit code 137)"). This reason flows through
query_instances -> node_statuses -> _summarize_pod_reasons -> the cluster
STATUS_CHANGE event -> the controller's cluster_event_reason -> the
RECOVERING job event, making the OOM visible on the dashboard/CLI.

Visibility only: no change to recovery behavior. Scoped to not-ready
containers, so a fully-recovered (Ready=True) pod does not surface a stale
prior OOM.

* [Jobs] Surface recovery reason in managed-job details

`job['details']`, which was empty during RECOVERING. The reason was only in
the job_events audit log and controller logs.

RECOVERING event reason for recovering jobs (one query, scoped to the
RECOVERING subset to stay off the per-job path) via the new
state.get_latest_recovery_reasons(), and _format_job_details renders it as
"Recovering: <reason>" when there's no higher-priority detail (backoff /
waiting / terminal failure still take precedence). Pod-termination reasons
can be multi-line, so whitespace is collapsed to a single line for the
details column (the controller-log multi-line format is unchanged).

Also clarifies the FAILED_SETUP docstring to note it now covers
deterministic cluster/runtime setup failures (e.g. an OOMKilled pod before
the job starts), not just the user's setup script.

No schema change (the spot_jobs DB migrates via Alembic); the reason is
read from the existing job_events table.

The pod-reason extractors only inspected pod conditions and container

/ disk / memory pressure -- degraded to the generic "Terminated
unexpectedly". The kubelet records such evictions as an Event
(reason='Evicted', message e.g. "Pod ephemeral local storage usage exceeds
the total limit of containers 2Gi"); this is NOT reflected in
pod.status.reason, and the container's exit ('Error') is only a side effect
of the kill, so the event is the authoritative cause.

An ephemeral-storage (and disk / memory pressure) eviction is recorded in

the cluster as abnormal and reads the pod inside that window, so the
status-derived reason degraded to a generic "Terminated unexpectedly. ...
Container errors: Error", losing the eviction cause.

(currently 'Evicted') when a flagged pod's status-derived reason is generic
(lacks a specific cause). The eviction reason -- which includes the
"...ephemeral local storage usage exceeds..." message -- is appended, so it
flows into the cluster-abnormal reason / recovery details and matches the
`ephemeral` hint.

healthy pods incur no extra events API call.

* [Kubernetes] Surface pod eviction reason at cluster-abnormal detection

event but pod.status has not caught up. At that instant all nodes are UP and
the per-pod status_reason is empty, so _update_cluster_status fell through to
the generic "ray cluster is unhealthy (0/1 ready)".

subject: [Storage] Add Hugging Face Buckets and repos as a storage backend (#9698)
message:
[Storage] Add Hugging Face Buckets and repos as a storage backend (#9698)

* [Storage] Add Hugging Face Buckets and repos as a storage backend

Adds a new hf storage type that wraps Hugging Face Buckets
(Xet-backed S3-like object storage, read-write) and, via the same
handle, also supports mounting HF model/dataset/space repos read-only.

All bucket lifecycle operations (create/upload/download/delete) go
through huggingface_hub (>=1.10). MOUNT/MOUNT_CACHED modes install
and invoke hf-mount (https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mount) with
its FUSE backend, which aligns with SkyPilot's existing FUSE-based
mount infrastructure (gcsfuse/blobfuse2/rclone mount/goofys).

Note: the published v0.3.1 hf-mount Linux binaries are linked against
glibc >= 2.32, so MOUNT-mode tasks on the default SkyPilot k8s image
(Ubuntu 20.04, glibc 2.31) need an explicit newer base image via
resources.image_id (e.g. docker:mirror.gcr.io/ubuntu:22.04). COPY
mode works on any image. See docs/source/reference/storage.rst.

- URL formats:
    hf://buckets/<ns>/<bucket>[/<sub>]           (bucket, rw)
    hf://<ns>/<model>[@<rev>][/<sub>]            (repo, ro)
    hf://datasets/<ns>/<ds>[@<rev>][/<sub>]      (repo, ro)
    hf://spaces/<ns>/<sp>[@<rev>][/<sub>]        (repo, ro)

- Auth: reads HF_TOKEN from env or the HF CLI token file and propagates
  it to clusters via the existing credential-file-mounts pipeline.

- Uploading to a repo with a local source raises StorageUploadError
  instead of silently no-op'ing, so misconfigurations fail loud.

Tested:
- Unit tests covering URL parsing, name validation, classify/upload
  guards, public Storage construction paths, COPY-mode translation,
  credential propagation, cloud-store download command generation, and
  the hf-mount command generator (including --fuse and fuse3 bootstrap
  assertions).
- Focused HF test pass:
    uv run --with-editable .[huggingface] --with pytest --with pytest-xdist
      --with pytest-env --with buildkite-test-collector --with boto3
      pytest tests/unit_tests/test_sky/storage/test_huggingface.py -q -n 0
- git diff --check, yapf --diff, isort --diff.
- End-to-end on a Kubernetes cluster:
    * create bucket -> upload dir+files (COPY mode via HfApi.sync_bucket)
    * pod starts, HF token file propagated to pod at ~/.cache/huggingface
    * pod lists bucket via huggingface_hub, downloads hello.txt
    * pod writes pod-wrote.txt back via batch_bucket_files
    * re-list shows pod-written file, re-download confirms content
    * clean teardown (sky down + HfApi.delete_bucket)
    * MOUNT mode via hf-mount --fuse on Ubuntu 22.04

* [Storage] Address PR review feedback

- Broaden Python support: relax huggingface_hub>=1.10 (Python 3.10+) to
  >=1.5 (>=1.5,<1.9 on Python 3.9). 1.5 is the first release with the
  full Buckets API and still supports Python 3.9; 1.9+ drops 3.9.
  This fixes the CI unit-test job (runs on 3.9) that was failing with
  ModuleNotFoundError.
- cloud_stores.HFCloudStorage.is_directory: use list_repo_tree instead
  of repo_info().siblings for repo-path checks. repo_info fetches
  metadata for every file in the repo; list_repo_tree(path_in_repo=p)
  only fetches the specified path (and raises EntryNotFoundError for
  file paths, which is how we now distinguish file vs directory).
- HuggingFaceStore.mount_cached_command: propagate MountCachedConfig
  read_only to hf-mount via --read-only instead of silently dropping
  the config. Other (rclone-specific) fields still have no hf-mount
  equivalent; documented in the docstring.
- Doc nits from review: shorten HF mention in intro, drop the full
  hf:// URL enumeration from the example (users can refer to the HF
  CLI docs), single hf:// example in the Storage YAML reference.
- Add unit tests covering the list_repo_tree optimization and
  mount_cached_command propagation.

Tested:
- Full HF test suite passes on Python 3.9 (278) and 3.11 (310).
- bash format.sh clean (black, yapf, isort, mypy, pylint 10.00/10).

* [Storage] Bump hf-mount to v0.6.5 for unprivileged k8s

v0.3.1 cannot mount in unprivileged k8s pods (the default SkyPilot
Kubernetes execution context). Two bugs blocked it:

1. fuser's direct /dev/fuse open path didn't fall back to fusermount
   when the device wasn't openable, so the mount failed before the
   setuid fusermount-shim could ever be invoked. Fixed in hf-mount
   v0.6.3 (huggingface/hf-mount#173, picking up huggingface/fuser#1).

2. After the initial mount succeeded via fusermount-shim, fuser's
   session loop opened /dev/fuse N-1 more times to clone per-thread
   fds. Those direct opens hit EPERM in the unprivileged pod and
   the daemon crashed with 'FUSE session error: Operation not
   permitted (os error 1)' immediately after the FUSE_INIT
   handshake, tearing the mount down (visible to the pod as
   'mountpoint /data' returning 'not a mountpoint'). Fixed in
   hf-mount v0.6.4 (huggingface/hf-mount#174): probe /dev/fuse
   openability once at startup and disable clone_fd if denied.

v0.6.5 is a maintenance release on top of v0.6.4.

Verified end-to-end on a private sandbox Kubernetes cluster with the
fusermount-shim/fusermount-server setup from this PR: mount, list,
and read of a dataset repo all succeed.

Also corrects the comment's glibc minimum (the actual binaries
require 2.34, not 2.32; verified with 'strings ... | grep GLIBC_'
against the published release).

* [Storage] Address PR review feedback from bots

Devin findings:
- Fix attribute name bug in HuggingFaceStore._classify/_validate: the sub-path
  was being assigned to `self.bucket_sub_path` (no leading underscore), but
  every consumer reads `self._bucket_sub_path`. The assignment silently
  created a dead attribute. Masked in the common flow (Storage.add_store
  injects _bucket_sub_path at the parent level), but corrupted state if
  HuggingFaceStore is constructed directly with a sub-path URL.
- Update docs/source/reference/storage.rst FAQ to reference hf-mount v0.6.5
  and glibc >= 2.34 (was still pointing at v0.3.1 / glibc 2.32 after the
  version bump).

Gemini findings:
- Harden HF token cache directory permissions: os.makedirs(mode=0o700)
  ignores the mode flag for pre-existing dirs, and the prior code swallowed
  any chmod failure. Now we raise StorageSpecError on chmod failure and
  verify the final mode before writing the token; we refuse to write if the
  dir is group- or world-accessible.
- Remove `eval echo` from the hf-mount token-file path expansion. Expand a
  leading `~/` to `$HOME/` in Python instead so the generated shell command
  never invokes eval.
- Improve StorageSpecError wording when an HF repo source disagrees with the
  storage name ('Hugging Face' instead of the cryptic 'HF').
- Parallelize multi-source bucket uploads with a small ThreadPoolExecutor
  (max 4 workers). Each sync_bucket call is already internally parallel, so
  the pool just overlaps I/O between distinct source dirs. Also classifies
  all sources up front so missing paths fail loud before any upload starts.

* [Storage] Don't mask StorageSpecError as a connection failure

Devin finding: HuggingFaceStore._get_bucket() wrapped both bucket_info()
and _validate_existing_bucket() in a single try/except Exception block,
so a StorageSpecError raised by _validate_existing_bucket (e.g. when a
user tries to mount an externally-created bucket without ``source:``)
was caught by the broad handler and re-raised as a misleading
StorageBucketGetError. Move the validation out of the try block so the
spec error surfaces its actionable message.

* [Storage] Fix doubled sub-path on HF repo COPY-mode downloads

Devin finding: ``snapshot_download`` preserves repo-relative paths under
``local_dir``, so passing ``allow_patterns=['<sub_path>/*']`` places
files at ``<destination>/<sub_path>/<files>`` rather than
``<destination>/<files>``. For a source like
``hf://openai-community/gpt2/onnx`` mounted at ``/data/onnx``, files
ended up at ``/data/onnx/onnx/model.onnx`` instead of
``/data/onnx/model.onnx``.

Both COPY-mode paths are affected:

- ``HFCloudStorage.make_sync_dir_command`` (remote heredoc).
- ``HuggingFaceStore.download_remote_dir`` (in-process).

Fix: when a sub-path is present, stage ``snapshot_download`` into a
temporary directory and move only the sub-path contents up to the
real destination. The no-sub-path path is unchanged.

Added an assertion to ``test_repo_dir_download_command`` plus a new
``test_repo_dir_download_command_no_sub_path`` to lock in the
behavior.

* [Storage] HF: strip URL sub-path before appending via get_bucket_sub_path_prefix

Devin finding: when ``storage.source`` is an HF URL with a sub-path, the
sub-path was relied upon entirely from the source URL, while every other
store type also runs the constructed blob path through
``get_bucket_sub_path_prefix``. This left a gap when ``_bucket_sub_path``
is set independently of the source URL (e.g. constructed via the
internal API or restored from a handle that no longer carries the sub-
path in ``source``).

Naively always calling ``get_bucket_sub_path_prefix`` would double the
sub-path in the common case (``hf://buckets/ns/bucket/sub`` →
``hf://buckets/ns/bucket/sub/sub``). Instead, parse the source URL,
drop any embedded sub-path to recover a canonical base URL, then run
that through ``get_bucket_sub_path_prefix`` — symmetric with the other
``StoreType`` branches.

* [Storage] HF adaptor: use LazyImport handle in api() instead of re-importing

Devin / AGENTS.md: ``huggingface_hub`` is already exposed at module level
via ``common.LazyImport``, so the in-function ``from huggingface_hub
import HfApi`` was redundant. Drop the local import and call
``huggingface_hub.HfApi()`` directly — the LazyImport defers loading
until first attribute access, so ``sky`` import cost is unchanged.

* [Storage] HF: address review (docs entry, sky check hints, COPY-mode ~ expansion)

Addresses the review feedback from PR #9418 (referenced on #9698):

- installation.rst: add a Hugging Face storage backend section with the
  _huggingface-installation anchor (pip extras, hf auth login / HF_TOKEN,
  sky check huggingface).
- check.py: include HuggingFace in the storage-only clouds comment.
- adaptors/huggingface.py: add a "For more info:" docs link to the
  token-not-set hint, like the other storage-only clouds. On whoami()
  failure, stop unconditionally blaming the token: surface the underlying
  error on a separate "Details:" line and make the refresh advice
  conditional (a missing httpx[socks], network errors, etc. are not token
  problems).
- cloud_stores.py: wrap every COPY-mode download destination with
  os.path.expanduser. We invoke huggingface_hub directly (no shell), so a
  wrapped "~/.sky/file_mounts/..." destination was treated as a literal
  "~" directory and files never reached the mount point.
- Add unit tests for the new hint behavior and the ~ expansion.

* [Docs] Allowlist "Hugging Face" in heading-case linter

The doc-build job treats Sphinx warnings as errors. The new "Hugging Face"
section heading tripped the sentence-case linter ("Unexpected capitals:
Face"). Add it to MULTI_WORD_TERMS, like "Prime Intellect".

* [Storage] HF: fix repo-file COPY temp-dir leak + harden bucket COPY

Addresses review follow-ups on #9698:
- cloud_stores: wrap the HF repo file-download (hf_hub_download) in
  try/finally so the staging temp dir is always removed, mirroring the
  dir-download path (Devin review, otherwise leaks a temp dir per COPY).
- cloud_stores: pass raise_on_missing_files=True to download_bucket_files
  so a COPY of a missing bucket file fails loud instead of silently
  producing nothing.
- storage: replace assert with StorageSpecError for the bucket

[Test] Fix test_volume_env_mount_kubernetes teardown race with managed job cluster (#9667)

* [Test] Fix test_volume_env_mount_kubernetes teardown race with managed job worker cluster

The teardown ran `sky volumes delete` 5 seconds after `sky jobs cancel -a -y`,
but the managed job's worker cluster is torn down asynchronously by the jobs
controller after the job completes. When the cluster is still alive,
volume_delete rejects with `ValueError: Volume X is used by cluster Y`.

Replace the fixed 5s sleep with a retry loop on the delete (up to ~5 minutes)
that only retries while the error indicates the volume is in use, and fails
fast on any other error. Also fix a stray non-f-string on the success-echo
line so the actual PVC name is printed instead of a literal `{full_pvc_name}`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Also poll volume listing after delete in test_volume_env_mount_kubernetes teardown

After the previous fix, `sky volumes delete` succeeds once the worker cluster
is torn down, but `sky volumes ls` can still list the volume briefly while the
deletion propagates server-side. Add a second polling loop on the listing so
the teardown waits for the volume to actually disappear before declaring it
deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Test] Wait for managed job schedule_state=DONE before deleting volume

The previous fix replaced sleep+delete with retry-on-delete + retry-on-ls,
but that's fighting the symptom. The actual contract is: the controller
sets schedule_state=DONE in its `finally` block, AFTER `_cleanup_cluster`
runs and the worker cluster is gone. So DONE strictly implies the PVC is
no longer in use, regardless of whether the per-task status ended up
SUCCEEDED, CANCELLED, or FAILED.

Poll `sky jobs queue -v -a --format json` for the test's managed job and
wait until its schedule_state is DONE, then do a single volume delete and
existence check.

subject: [Storage] HF: pin click<8.3.0 when installing huggingface_hub on the runtime (fixes ray status / stuck INIT) (#9763)
message:
[Storage] HF: pin click<8.3.0 when installing huggingface_hub on the runtime (fixes ray status / stuck INIT) (#9763)

* [CI] Fix helm publish workflow by allowing flexible separator length in README

* [Storage] HF: pin click<8.3.0 when installing huggingface_hub on runtime

The COPY-mode HF download installs `huggingface_hub>=1.5` into the remote
runtime venv. huggingface_hub>=1.5 declares `click>=8.4` (core dep + typer),
which upgrades click past the runtime's `ray==2.9.3` ceiling. ray 2.9.3's CLI
crashes at import under click>=8.3 (deepcopy of click Sentinel values,
ray-project/ray#56747), so `ray status` exits non-zero, SkyPilot marks the
cluster "abnormal", and it gets stuck in INIT (CLI can no longer tail logs /
read the queue even though the job ran).

Pass a uv `--overrides` file pinning `click<8.3.0` when installing
huggingface_hub so click stays below the ray-breaking version while still
pulling huggingface_hub's other deps. The bucket API works fine with the
older click. A plain `click<8.3.0` constraint would be unsatisfiable against
the declared `>=8.4`, hence an override rather than a constraint.

Tested:
- Repro in a py3.10 venv: `ray[default]==2.9.3` + `huggingface_hub>=1.5`
  upgrades click to 8.4.1 and `ray status` crashes with the Sentinel error.
- With the override: click resolves to 8.2.1, `ray status` no longer crashes
  (reaches the connection step), and `huggingface_hub` + `HfApi().sync_bucket`
  import cleanly.
- Added a regression unit test; full HF suite: 84 passed.

subject: [Volume] Don't rewrite region to 'in-cluster' when in-cluster auth unavailable (#9743)
message:
[Volume] Don't rewrite region to 'in-cluster' when in-cluster auth unavailable (#9743)

* [Volume] Don't rewrite region to 'in-cluster' when in-cluster auth unavailable

refresh_volume_config previously rewrote volume.region=None to the literal
string 'in-cluster' unconditionally. That string is only valid when the API
server is actually running with in-cluster service-account auth; when the
server authenticates via kubeconfig (the common case for buildkite kind
agents, dev workstations, etc.), the optimizer compares 'in-cluster'
against the kubeconfig context names and raises ResourcesUnavailableError
on every sky launch that references such a volume.

The bug surfaces as a race against the 60s volume-refresh daemon:
1. `sky volumes apply` (no infra: field) inserts the volume with region=None.
2. If the next daemon tick fires before `sky launch`, the row is rewritten
   to region='in-cluster' and the launch fails.
3. If `sky launch` beats the tick, the launch succeeds because region=None
   falls back to the task's --infra.

Surfaced as flaky failures in nightly smoke-test builds — same args
passed yesterday on the previous commit and again on retry today; no
volume/task/optimizer code was touched between those runs.

Fix: only rewrite region when is_incluster_config_available() returns True
(i.e. /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token exists). Otherwise
leave region=None so the launch resolves the context from --infra at task
time. The backward-compat path described in the original comment (PR #8386)
is preserved: volumes created with in-cluster auth still get their region
populated on the first refresh.

Added a regression unit test covering both branches.

When this test fires on the unfixed code, the assertion message now spells
out the exact ResourcesUnavailableError that surfaces in production
(verified by reverting the volume.py change and running the test — fails
with the named error chain). Adds a docstring that walks the daemon-tick
race step by step with file:line citations.

subject: [Jobs] Retry transient DB errors in controller monitor loop and cleanup (#9748)
message:
[Jobs] Retry transient DB errors in controller monitor loop and cleanup (#9748)

* [Jobs] Retry transient DB errors in controller monitor loop and cleanup

The managed-jobs controller had no retry on transient psycopg2 / SQLAlchemy
OperationalErrors during routine status polling and failure marking. A brief
DB outage (RDS failover, DNS hiccup, network blip) would propagate to the
run() catch-all and mark a healthy job FAILED_CONTROLLER -- or, for outages
that outlast the catch-all itself, leave the job as a RUNNING zombie with
leaked worker pods.

Add sky/utils/db/retries.py with thin sync + async wrappers using the
existing common_utils.Backoff (no new deps). Wrap four call sites in
sky/jobs/controller.py:
- _monitor_one_task: get_job_status (does DB read for cluster handle)
- _monitor_one_task: refresh_cluster_status_handle (DB write)
- _update_failed_task_state: set_failed_async
- finally block: set_cancelling_async / set_cancelled_async

Catches sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError, sqlalchemy.exc.InterfaceError,
psycopg2.OperationalError (raw -- used by PostgresLock via raw_connection),
and Python builtin ConnectionError (asyncpg's "connection_lost" path).

5 attempts, exponential backoff capped at 5s (~10s total budget). Covers
brief outages; very long outages (e.g. multi-second RDS failover) still
surface as failures, but with a clean FAILED_CONTROLLER instead of a zombie.

Tested:
- Unit tests in tests/unit_tests/test_sky/utils/test_db_retries.py (19 tests, all pass).
- Local end-to-end: postgres + toxiproxy + 2-node managed job on Kubernetes.
  7-second proxy outage on master produces a RUNNING zombie (controller
  dies, pods leak). Same outage on this branch triggers 3 retry warnings,
  succeeds on the 4th attempt; job stays RUNNING with the controller never
  noticing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] drop Airflow reference in retries docstring

* [Jobs] drop redundant retry-justification comments

* [Jobs] Address review feedback on retry helper

- Add socket.gaierror to RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS. asyncpg.connect() lets DNS
  resolution failures propagate as socket.gaierror unwrapped; SQLAlchemy
  does not wrap them when going through async_creator. Without this, the
  async path failed immediately on DNS hiccups.
- Add psycopg2.InterfaceError to the catch tuple. Covers "connection
  already closed" raised from raw_connection paths (e.g. PostgresLock)
  on a stale connection during an outage.
- Raise ValueError on max_retries < 1 instead of falling through to the
  unreachable AssertionError. Clearer signal for caller misuse.
- Expand test coverage: parametrize the retryable-exception tests to
  include the two new entries; add invalid-max_retries tests for both
  sync and async helpers across [0, -1, -100]. 28 tests total.

* [Jobs] make summarize and RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS public

* [Jobs] Push DB retries down into state.py and global_user_state.py

Move the transient-DB-error retry wrap from the controller call sites
into the direct-DB functions themselves. This way every controller path
that touches `managed_job_state` or `global_user_state` is covered, not
just the five call sites that had explicit `with_db_retries_async`
wraps. Per-review feedback that wrapping should live at the DB-touching
layer.

Two patterns used:

- `@db_retries.retry` / `@db_retries.retry_async` decorators for pure
  leaves (single session, no non-DB side effects).
- `_retry_session(_op)` inner-closure pattern for the `set_*_async`
  functions in `state.py` that interleave session work with non-DB side
  effects (`add_job_event_async` prologue, `callback_func` epilogue) —
  only the session block retries, side effects run exactly once.

Coverage: 18 controller-reachable direct-DB functions in
`sky/jobs/state.py` and 5 in `sky/global_user_state.py`. The five
outer wraps in `sky/jobs/controller.py` (plus the `db_retries` import)
are removed since the work now lives downstream.

* [Jobs] Close async DB connect-timeout retry escape

Two related fixes that together let the retry helper actually cycle on
TCP black-hole outages (e.g. RDS failover):

1. `asyncpg.connect()` raises `asyncio.TimeoutError` (= builtin
   `TimeoutError` on 3.11+) on its internal `asyncio.wait_for(...)`
   connect-timeout. SQLAlchemy does NOT recognize it as a DBAPI error,
   so it propagates unwrapped through the `async_creator` path —
   bypassing `RETRYABLE_EXCEPTIONS` entirely. Add both names so 3.8–3.10
   (where they are distinct classes) is also covered.

2. asyncpg's default connect timeout is 60s — far longer than the
   ~10s backoff budget in the retry helper. Pass `timeout=15` to
   `asyncpg.connect()` in `_make_asyncpg_creator` so each retry attempt
   surfaces failure within the expected budget.

* [Jobs] Wrap cluster-event/status/remove DB writes for controller hot path

The managed-job controller's monitor loop calls `refresh_cluster_status_handle`
on every 15s poll iteration. That chains into `backend_utils._update_cluster_status`,
which calls these three direct-DB functions in `global_user_state.py`:

- `add_cluster_event` — fires on every refresh to log "All nodes up; SkyPilot
  runtime healthy" (and on every status transition).
- `set_cluster_status` — fires when transitioning to AUTOSTOPPING.
- `remove_cluster` — fires if the cluster YAML is missing.

None of these have decorator-level retry, and the `refresh_cluster_status_handle`
call site in `sky/jobs/controller.py` is NOT in a try/except — so any transient
DB error here propagates straight to the controller catch-all and the job is
marked FAILED_CONTROLLER. Decorate all three with `@db_retries.retry` so the
retry budget actually covers the hot path.

Recovery-strategy DB call sites are already defensively wrapped in
`try/except Exception` with `continue`, so they don't need the same treatment.

* [Jobs] Wrap remaining controller-reachable state writes on launch/recover/done paths

Found via systematic audit of every controller-reachable DB call site
outside of try/except. Adds retry coverage to the following functions in
`sky/jobs/state.py`:

- `get_pool_from_job_id`: called by `event_callback_func`'s closure, which
  fires on every `set_*_async` epilogue during state transitions in the
  monitor loop.
- `scheduler_set_launching_async`, `scheduler_set_alive_async`: called by
  `scheduler.scheduled_launch`, entered from `recovery_strategy._launch`
  (which the monitor loop reaches via `executor.recover()`).
- `scheduler_set_done_async`: called by `scheduler.job_done_async` from
  the FAILED_CONTROLLER catch-all (`controller.py:2306`) — if this fails,
  the catch-all itself fails and the controller dies silently (RUNNING
  zombie).
- `set_job_infra`: called by `FailoverStrategyExecutor._launch` to
  persist cloud/region/zone after a successful launch; not in any
  try/except in the subclass, propagates to controller catch-all.
- `set_backoff_pending_async`, `set_restarting_async`: refactored to the
  `_retry_session(_op)` inner-closure pattern (rather than a
  function-level decorator) because they have a non-idempotent
  `add_job_event_async` prologue.

* [Jobs] Fix decorator ordering on get_handle_from_cluster_name

Match the convention used elsewhere in this PR: `@db_retries.retry`
outermost, `@metrics_lib.time_me` inner. With the prior order, each
retry attempt's wait was rolled into a single time_me sample; with
this order, time_me records each attempt's per-call duration the same
way it does for every other retry-decorated function in this file
(add_or_update_cluster, add_cluster_event, remove_cluster,
set_cluster_status, get_cluster_from_name, delete_service_account_token).

* [Jobs] Make scheduler_set_{alive,done}_async idempotent under commit-lost retry

Per review: both functions had a state-checking WHERE + hard `assert
rowcount == 1` that fires incorrectly on a retry replay after commit-lost
(server committed the UPDATE but the client never saw the ack — possible
during PostgreSQL/RDS failover). On retry, the strict WHERE matches 0
rows and the assert fires with `AssertionError: (job_id, 0)`.

Approach: thread the attempt index through `with_db_retries[_async]`
instead of via ContextVar — `Callable[[int], T]` for the wrapped fn,
attempt 0 = first call, 1+ = retry. The two decorators (`retry` /
`retry_async`) discard the arg, so the common pure-leaf case is
unaffected. Drop the decorator on the two scheduler-state functions
and call `with_db_retries_async(_op)` inline so `_op` can see attempt.

Inside each function, keep the strict WHERE on every attempt, and use
a closure-scoped `prior_update_matched` flag (set BEFORE commit, only
when WHERE matched) to gate the retry tolerance:

  - On attempt 0, behave exactly as before — strict assert on 0 rows.
  - On attempt > 0 with `prior_update_matched == True`, accept a 0-row
    UPDATE if a SELECT confirms state is already the target (the only
    case where commit-lost could have produced this). Real caller bugs
    (calling the function when state was already in the target before
    THIS call) still trigger the assert because the flag stays False.

Updates one test that passed a no-arg lambda to `with_db_retries_async`.

* [Jobs] Fix non-idempotent state writes in set_recovering_async / set_recovered_async

set_recovering_async: with `force_transit_to_recovering=True`, the WHERE
clause matches every processing status (including RECOVERING itself, for
controller resume), and the inner `_retry_session` may replay the op
after a commit-lost. On replay, the row is already RECOVERING but the
case `last_recovered_at >= 0` still fires, double-counting `current_time
- last_recovered_at` into `job_duration`. Gate the accumulation on
`status == RUNNING` so only the actual RUNNING → RECOVERING transition
contributes runtime; replay and resume from non-RUNNING states are no-ops.

set_recovered_async: strict WHERE `status == RECOVERING` plus `assert
count == 1` fired `ManagedJobStatusError` on commit-lost replay (status
is now RUNNING, WHERE matches 0). Same pattern used elsewhere:
`prior_update_matched` closure flag set before commit, attempt-aware
inline retry via `with_db_retries_async`, and on `attempt > 0` with
the flag set, accept already-RUNNING state via a verification SELECT.

* [Jobs] Extract commit-lost-safe retry helpers, apply to all task/schedule state writes

Adds two helpers in sky/jobs/state.py:

- `_retry_task_status_update(job_id, task_id, target_status, update,
  failure_prefix)`: wraps a one-row UPDATE on `spot_table` with the
  `prior_update_matched` + attempt-aware retry pattern. On `count != 1`,
  walks the same three branches the call sites used to inline: count == 1
  → success; commit-lost retry path (attempt > 0 + prior_update_matched
  + target reached) → success; otherwise raise
  `ManagedJobStatusError(f'{failure_prefix} ({count} rows updated. {details})')`,
  preserving the original error format byte-for-byte.

- `_retry_schedule_state_update(job_id, target_state, update, idempotent)`:
  same pattern for one-row UPDATEs on `job_info_table`. `idempotent=True`
  short-circuits past the assert chain (matches the prior
  `scheduler_set_done_async` semantics where the assert was guarded by
  `if not idempotent`).

Refactors through the helpers:

- `set_backoff_pending_async`, `set_starting_async`, `set_started_async`,
  `set_recovering_async`, `set_recovered_async`, `set_succeeded_async`,
  `scheduler_set_alive_async`, `scheduler_set_done_async`.

Each function's WHERE clause and SET values are unchanged. Failure
messages preserved (`'Failed to set the task to {x}.'` formats round-trip
through `failure_prefix`). For `set_recovering_async`, `should_accumulate_duration`
now allows `WINDING_DOWN` in addition to `RUNNING` (both are "still doing
job work" per `set_succeeded_async`'s acceptance set; the
`set_winding_down` transition itself doesn't accumulate, so excluding
WINDING_DOWN here would drop the preceding RUNNING segment from
`job_duration` on a force-transit-to-recovering controller resume).

`set_restarting_async` left on `_retry_session` (WHERE has no source-state
filter so it's already idempotent under retry). Sync `scheduler_set_done`
unchanged (not in controller retry scope).

* [Jobs] PostgresLock.release: catch DatabaseError, not just OperationalError

psycopg2 raises bare DatabaseError (parent of OperationalError) for some
connection-closed cases like "server closed the connection unexpectedly",
which the narrower OperationalError catch misses. The exception then
propagates from `release()` to the controller catch-all and marks the
job FAILED_CONTROLLER.

Reproduced under chaos testing (failover + simulate-maintenance every
60s against an HA postgres instance): after the first round of retries
recovers, a subsequent release() on a stale advisory-lock connection
raises bare DatabaseError. Broadening the catch handles this case while
still being scoped to psycopg2 DB-state errors (DatabaseError is a
proper subclass of psycopg2.Error).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Retry get_cluster_yaml_str on transient DB errors

Cluster YAML reads happen on every monitor-loop iteration via
ssh_credential_from_yaml → get_cluster_yaml_dict → get_cluster_yaml_str.
On a control-plane DB blip during failover/maintenance, the raw
session.query() raises psycopg2.OperationalError. That propagates up
through run_ray_status_to_check_ray_cluster_healthy's broad except,
gets converted to "ray cluster is unhealthy" with the DB error text
attached, and triggers a full worker-cluster teardown + recreate for
what is actually just a control-plane blip.

Wrapping the leaf with @db_retries.retry keeps the failure isolated to
the leaf and makes the transient error self-recover without changing
any caller behavior.

Decorator order matches the rest of the file: @db_retries.retry outer,
@metrics_lib.time_me inner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Retry PostgresLock._get_connection on transient DB errors

PostgresLock.acquire() calls _get_connection() which does
engine.raw_connection() on the QueuePool. During a Cloud SQL maintenance
event or RDS failover, raw_connection() raises psycopg2.OperationalError
mid-acquire — and because the caller (refresh_cluster_record at
backend_utils.py:3240) wraps acquire in `with lock.acquire(blocking=False):`
without a retry, the exception propagates straight to the controller
catch-all and marks the job FAILED_CONTROLLER.

The leaf is safe to retry: raw_connection() either returns a checked-out
conn or raises with nothing taken — no partial state, no leaked pool
slot. pool_pre_ping=True already handles stale pool entries on each
checkout, and our retry catches the resulting OperationalError if a
fresh connect still fails.

Validated with a deterministic stress test that hammers
PostgresLock.acquire from 8 worker threads while a simulate-maintenance
event fires against the same Cloud SQL instance:
  - With  this retry: 15,870 acquires, 0 failures
  - Without (control): 15,732 acquires, 99 failures
Both runs identical throughput (~33/s); the only difference is the
decorator catching transient connection-refused on the maintenance
window.

subject: [Debug] Break same-type cross-link cycles in debug-dump (#9753)
message:
[Debug] Break same-type cross-link cycles in debug-dump (#9753)

* [Debug] Break same-type cross-link cycles in debug-dump

`sky debug-dump -j 66684` brought in 7 unrelated jobs (66596, 66610,
66611, 66677, 66683, 66691, 66692) because `_get_requests_from_managed_jobs`
matches `sky.jobs.launch` requests by `body.name` (the task name), and
then `_get_managed_jobs_from_requests` reads each matched launch's
`return_value.job_id` back into `managed_job_ids` — so every sibling
launch of the same `sb-sweep-8` task got pulled in.

Track linkage provenance via two sidecar sets on DebugDumpContext:
`request_ids_via_job` and `request_ids_via_cluster`. When a cross-link
helper iterates `request_ids` to expand into another resource, it
skips requests that were themselves added by the same resource type.
This breaks the job→request→job and cluster→request→cluster cycles
without restricting expansion from user-seeded or recent-context
requests, and covers all three over-broad matchers (`body.name`,
`body.all_users`, `body.all`) in one shot.

* [Debug] Don't tag pre-existing request IDs with cross-link provenance

Gemini and Devin both flagged that the sidecar-tagging in
_get_requests_from_clusters and _get_requests_from_managed_jobs was
unconditional. A request ID that was already in `request_ids` from
user input (`sky debug-dump -r <id>`) or `_populate_recent_context`
would also pick up via_cluster/via_job, then get skipped by the
inverse-direction helper — losing exactly the expansion the user
explicitly asked for. This violated the invariant in the comment at
create_debug_dump.

Only tag IDs that were not already present in `request_ids` before
the helper ran. Add two regression tests covering the pre-existing
case for both helpers.

subject: [Jobs] Scope debug-dump controller_system logs to the relevant controllers (#9752)
message:
[Jobs] Scope debug-dump controller_system logs to the relevant controllers (#9752)

* [Jobs] Scope debug-dump controller_system logs to the relevant controllers

`_collect_controller_system_log_paths` previously globbed every
`~/sky_logs/jobs_controller/controller_*.log` regardless of which jobs
the dump targeted. On a controller with ~25 days of accumulated
processes that meant ~8.5k files / ~3.5 GB rsynced and ~19 minutes of
SSH overhead for a single-job dump, with ~99% of the bytes irrelevant.

Each managed-job controller writes `From controller <UUID>` at the head
of its `<jobid>.log` when it claims the job. Parse that line in
`_collect_job_debug_manifest`, aggregate UUIDs across requested jobs in
`collect_debug_dump_manifest`, and have `_collect_controller_system_log_paths`
look up `controller_<uuid>.log` directly instead of globbing.

If no requested job has emitted the marker yet (e.g. PENDING jobs that
never started), no controller_system files are included; we do not fall
back to globbing.

* [Jobs] Stream <jobid>.log when extracting controller UUIDs

Devin's review on #9752 caught a real HA-recovery gap: the per-job log
is opened in append mode (sky/utils/context.py:146), so when a second
controller takes over after a recovery it writes its
"From controller <UUID>" line *after* all of the previous controller's
output. A 16 KB head read can easily miss it on long-running jobs and
silently omit the most relevant controller_system log from the dump.

Scan the per-job log line by line instead. Bounded memory, catches
every "From controller …" line regardless of where it lands, and these
files are small (KB to a few MB on production controllers). Drops the
now-unused _CONTROLLER_UUID_LOG_HEAD_BYTES constant and adds a
regression test where the second UUID sits 200 KB into the file.

The two Gemini comments about case-insensitive UUID matching are not

subject: [Jobs] Show provisioning spinner during sky jobs launch (#9761)
message:
[Jobs] Show provisioning spinner during sky jobs launch (#9761)

* [Jobs] Show provisioning spinner during sky jobs launch

Managed job launches previously showed no provisioning progress: the
cluster launch runs asynchronously inside the jobs controller, whose
rich-status spinner codes were consumed (and dropped on a worker thread)
there and never reached the client. Users only saw a generic "Waiting
for task to start" message until the job began running.

Bridge the spinner from the controller to the client:

- Add a relay mode (`relay_rich_status`, default off) to
  `decode_rich_status` / `stream_response` / `stream_and_get` that
  forwards encoded rich-status payloads verbatim instead of rendering or
  dropping them.
- The jobs controller's `_launch` now streams the inner cluster launch
  with relay enabled, so the provisioning spinner codes are preserved in
  the per-job controller log.
- `stream_logs_by_id` follows that log during the pre-RUNNING phase and
  drives the single existing status spinner with the live provisioning
  messages (e.g. "Preparing SkyPilot runtime (1/3)"), matching the
  `sky launch` experience, then switches to job logs once running.

Falls back to the generic waiting message when no spinner is available
(old controllers, pool jobs), so behavior is backward compatible.

Tested:
- Unit: relay forwards payloads / drops heartbeats
  (test_rich_utils.py); controller-log spinner decoding incl. partial
  lines and STOP/EXIT clearing (test_utils.py).
- format.sh clean (mypy, pylint 10/10); affected unit suites pass.
- Manual: `sky jobs launch` shows the provisioning spinner with step
  counters before streaming job logs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* simplify message

* [Jobs] Address review feedback on provisioning spinner relay

- rich_utils: yield None for heartbeats in relay mode so stream_response
  keeps advancing progress_count (retry decorator sees forward progress)
  instead of dropping them entirely.
- read_provision_status_from_log: only INIT/UPDATE update the live message
  and only EXIT clears it; START/STOP no longer mutate msg, so a nested
  status enter (UPDATE(nested) then START(original)) doesn't revert the
  headline to stale text. Also reset the read offset when the log is
  truncated/recreated so following doesn't get stuck past EOF.
- _provision_status_headline: strip the trailing dim hint then peel the
  outer [bold cyan] wrapper with a greedy capture, preserving nested markup.
- stream_logs --controller: hide relayed <sky-payload> lines from the
  human-readable controller log output.
- Tests for all of the above.

subject: [Jobs] Fix provisioning headline extraction regression in sky jobs launch (#9770)
message:
[Jobs] Fix provisioning headline extraction regression in sky jobs launch (#9770)

[Jobs] Fix provisioning headline extraction regression

The previous review-feedback commit rewrote _provision_status_headline
with a regex anchored at `[/]$` and a `[dim]`-stripping pass. But real
spinner messages from ux_utils.spinner_message append the log hint with
raw ANSI (colorama) codes, not rich `[dim]...[/]` markup -- so the message
does not end at the headline's `[/]` and contains no literal `[dim]`. The
anchored regex therefore matched nothing and the provisioning detail line
under "Waiting for task to start" disappeared during `sky jobs launch`.

Replace it with a depth-aware scan from the `[bold cyan]` open tag to its
matching `[/]`: this keeps nested markup intact (the original review nit)
and ignores the trailing ANSI hint (the common real case). Add regression
tests using real ux_utils.spinner_message output (log-path and provision
hint variants).

- check_user_role_demotion() called safe_reload_config() + fetched all
  clusters + all managed jobs PER user -> O(N * (C+J)) for /users/batch_update.
- _validate_workspace_config_changes() fetched active resources PER
  workspace -> O(W * (C+J)) for /workspaces/batch_remove_users.
- preferred_identifier_for_user() / entries_for_user() rebuilt the
  username->ids map PER call -> O(M) every call.

Pre-fetch once, plumb through optional kwargs:

  build_username_to_ids_map; preferred_identifier_for_user and
  entries_for_user accept an optional pre-built map.

  active_resources ONCE for the demotion path, and passes both to each
  per-user check_user_role_demotion call. Promotion path (target=admin)
  skips the pre-fetch entirely.

    instead of re-resolving preferred_identifier_for_user per workspace.
  - batch_remove_users_from_workspaces fetches active resources for the

    per-workspace slice through _validate_workspace_config_changes_with_lock

test cases and _get_active_resources_for_workspaces in the batch remove

This is a hygiene cleanup of code introduced earlier in this PR. No
behavior changes; the goal is to collapse the ad-hoc kwarg sprawl that
each batch entrypoint had to thread through workspaces helpers.

UserResolver

Introduces sky/users/resolver.py with a UserResolver class that wraps
a user-table snapshot plus its derived lookup maps (id -> User,
name -> [ids]) and a lazily-fetched admin user_id set. Batch callers
build one resolver at the top and pass it through helpers; per-user
lookups become O(1) and the "did I remember to pass name_to_ids?"
footgun goes away.

resolve_allowed_entries / resolve_workspace_users /
resolve_workspaces_allowed_users. Lives in sky/users/ (not
sky/workspaces/) because the snapshot itself is user-domain; the
workspace-allowed_users methods only operate on plain Dict configs.

- sky/workspaces/utils.py: trimmed to just get_workspace_users(config,

    now lazy on first access via the resolver property.

  resolver and derives all_users_map from it; promotion branch uses
  global_user_state.get_users(set(user_ids)) (smaller targeted IN
  query) since it doesn't need the full table.

a remaining_admin_user_ids kwarg, intending to skip workspaces where
the demoted user "is still admin". Because every caller constructs the
set as all_admins minus the user being demoted, the check
"user_id in remaining_admin_user_ids" is structurally always False.

subject: [Kubernetes] Treat pods as scheduled on binding, not on container status (#9766)
message:
[Kubernetes] Treat pods as scheduled on binding, not on container status (#9766)

* [Kubernetes] Treat pods as scheduled on binding, not on container status

`_wait_for_pods_to_schedule` (bounded by `provision_timeout`, which defaults
to ~10s) decided a pod was scheduled by checking
`pod.status.container_statuses is not None`. However, `container_statuses` is
populated by the kubelet only after it picks the pod up and starts the
sandbox -- well after the kube-scheduler has already bound the pod
(`spec.nodeName` set / `PodScheduled` condition True).

When the control plane is slow to propagate the binding to the kubelet, a pod
can be fully bound to a node at the `provision_timeout` deadline yet still
have `container_statuses == None`. The function then raised
`KubernetesError: Timed out while waiting for nodes to start. Cluster may be
out of resources or may be too slow to autoscale`, SkyPilot tore the cluster
down, and failover surfaced a misleading `ResourcesUnavailableError` -- even
though capacity had been found and the pods were placed on free nodes.

Treat a pod as scheduled once the scheduler has bound it (phase != Pending,
`spec.nodeName` set, or `PodScheduled == True`), so provisioning hands off to
`_wait_for_pods_to_run`, which waits for containers to come up without the
short `provision_timeout`. Genuinely unschedulable pods keep `PodScheduled`
False and no `nodeName`, so they remain in the scheduling wait loop and the
out-of-resources / autoscaler-detection behavior is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Default pending reason to "container creation" while waiting for kubelet pickup

After a pod is bound to a node it can sit Pending with no container status
and no event for the whole kubelet-pickup window (and the uninformative
ContainerCreating state has no reason either), so the launch spinner showed a
bare "Launching" with no detail. Default the pending reason to "container
creation" in _inspect_pod_status's Pending branch so the spinner shows
"Launching (N pod(s) pending due to container creation)" during that wait.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Only default pending reason to "container creation" for bound pods

Gate the 'container creation' default on _pod_is_scheduled so an unbound
pod still waiting for capacity (reason genuinely None) is not mislabeled
as creating a container. Restore the prior guard that skips the pending
log line when there is no reason.

subject: ci(nightly): trigger a downstream workflow after PyPI publish (#9738)
message:
ci(nightly): trigger a downstream workflow after PyPI publish (#9738)

* ci(nightly): emit optional repository_dispatch after PyPI publish

Add a `notify-downstream` job that fires a `repository_dispatch` event
to a configurable downstream repository immediately after a successful
nightly publish to PyPI. This lets external pipelines react to a fresh
nightly without polling the PyPI JSON API.

The dispatch is gated on two repo-level secrets so forks and the
default upstream config are unaffected:

  - NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_REPO   (e.g. "owner/repo")
  - NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_TOKEN  (PAT with contents:write on the target)
  - NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_EVENT_TYPE  (optional repo variable; default
    "skypilot-nightly-published")

When either secret is unset, the step exits silently. The payload
includes the published `skypilot-nightly` version so downstream jobs
can pin their base image / install line.

* ci(nightly): use GitHub App token for downstream dispatch

Replace the long-lived NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_TOKEN PAT with a short-lived
installation token minted at runtime via actions/create-github-app-token,
scoped to just the downstream repository.

Configuration:
  - vars.NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_REPO  (e.g. "owner/repo") — gates the job
  - secrets.CI_APP_ID
  - secrets.CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
  - vars.NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_EVENT_TYPE  (optional; default
    "skypilot-nightly-published")

When NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_REPO is unset (forks, default upstream config),
the entire notify-downstream job is skipped.

* ci(nightly): trigger downstream via workflow_dispatch

Switch the optional downstream notification from repository_dispatch to
workflow_dispatch so the dispatch token only needs Actions: write (it can
trigger a workflow but cannot write repository contents), rather than the
Contents: write that the repository_dispatch endpoint requires.

The target workflow file and git ref are configurable via repo-level
variables (NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_WORKFLOW, NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_REF, default
main); the published nightly version is passed through as a workflow input.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(nightly): pin create-github-app-token to commit SHA

Pin actions/create-github-app-token to its v3.2.0 commit SHA, matching
how every other third-party action in this workflow is pinned. This
action receives the app credentials, so an unpinned mutable tag is an
unnecessary supply-chain risk.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* ci(nightly): use downstream dispatch secrets and fail loud on dispatch errors

The downstream dispatch config is provisioned on the upstream repo as
secrets (NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_CI_APP_ID, NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_CI_APP_PRIVATE_KEY,
NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_REPO, NIGHTLY_DOWNSTREAM_WORKFLOW), not variables. Read
them from the secrets context with the matching names.

The secrets context is not allowed in job-level `if:`, and gating on it
would let a missing/typo'd secret silently skip the job and report green.
Instead the job is fail-loud: it runs whenever publish-and-validate-both
succeeds, and a missing secret, bad App credentials, or a non-204 dispatch
all fail the job with a `::error::` annotation so the nightly run goes red.
