message:
[GCP] Set provisioningModel=RESERVATION_BOUND for DENSE reservations (#9779)

GCP DENSE reservations (used for large GPU blocks like A100/H100)
require instances to set provisioningModel=RESERVATION_BOUND. Without
this, the GCE API rejects the insert call with a 400 error.

This change:
- Adds _is_reservation_bound() which queries the reservation metadata
  via compute.reservations().list() (already in SkyPilot's required
  permissions) to check deploymentType
- Uses a deep copy of config per reservation iteration to prevent
  RESERVATION_BOUND leaking to subsequent non-DENSE reservations
- Adds num_retries for resilience against transient API errors
- Sets RESERVATION_BOUND + onHostMaintenance=TERMINATE when the
  reservation is DENSE
- Falls back gracefully on API errors (assumes standard reservation)
- Adds 6 unit tests covering DENSE, standard, missing field, not found,
  API failure, and full URI parsing

subject: [Workspaces] Auto-select / persist per-user default workspace (#9755)
message:
[Workspaces] Auto-select / persist per-user default workspace (#9755)

* [Workspaces] Auto-select / persist per-user default workspace

Add per-user `preferred_workspace` so users with access to multiple
workspaces don't get cryptic "permission denied to default" errors on
launch, and can persist a default once via the CLI instead of editing
`~/.sky/config.yaml` on every machine.

What it does
------------
* New column `users.preferred_workspace` (migration 019, additive,
  default null).
* New resolver `sky/workspaces/core.py:resolve_workspace_for_user()` with
  documented precedence:
  1. explicit (--workspace flag / active_workspace in merged config)
  2. preferred_workspace (if still accessible — re-validated at use)
  3. 'default' if accessible (back-compat safety net for legacy
     multi-workspace users and admins; without this, every existing
     multi-ws user would AMBIGUOUS on upgrade)
  4. exactly one accessible workspace — auto-select
  5. zero accessible — NoWorkspaceAccessError
  6. multiple, no preference, no 'default' access —
     WorkspaceAmbiguousError (returns guidance, never silently picks)
* Resolver wired into `override_request_env_and_config` with three skip
  gates: daemon requests, old clients
  (MIN_PREFERRED_WORKSPACE_API_VERSION), and explicitly-set
  active_workspace. Reads preferred from the User dataclass already
  loaded by `add_or_update_user(return_user=True)` — no extra DB read
  per request.
* Endpoint `POST /users/me/workspace { preferred: str|null }` echoes
  the persisted value back. No GET — preferred ships inline on the User
  row returned by `/api/health`.
* CLI:
  - `sky workspace use <name>` / `sky workspace use --clear`
  - `--workspace/-w` on `sky launch` and `sky jobs launch` (sugar over
    `--config active_workspace=X` via a thin click callback)
  - `sky api info` shows `Preferred workspace: 'X'` (or `(not set)`),
    read from the existing `/api/health` payload
* D8 relaxation: cluster-op workspace check now uses RBAC access, not
  active-workspace equality — without this, switching preferred would
  lose ability to manage previously-launched clusters.
* `WorkspaceAmbiguousError` carries an optional `note` for RBAC drift
  ("preferred 'team-x' not accessible") so users understand why their
  preference wasn't honored.

What it does NOT include
------------------------
* No dashboard UI for setting preferred. First iteration shipped a
  user-menu picker; dropped because (a) the OSS sidebar is replaced
  wholesale by feature-plugin's Sidebar.tsx in enterprise installs, so
  the picker code is dead there, and (b) a flat list of N workspaces
  in the user menu is the wrong density for a setting users touch
  once. CLI-only entry point is sufficient. A future `/settings`-page
  surface can read the same `/api/health` field and POST to the same
  endpoint with no server change.
* Sky Serve workspace-awareness is not touched (separate scope).
* Admin assignment (SKY-4210) deferred — additive follow-up on the
  same column.

Test plan
---------
Unit tests (55 pass):
* `test_resolve_workspace_for_user.py` — every precedence branch +
  RBAC drift + admin case + exception class signatures
* `test_resolver_compat_matrix.py` — 41-case parametric matrix
  asserting the back-compat invariant: every case where the legacy
  server succeeded still succeeds on the new resolver with the same
  workspace pick, when the user has not opted in
* `test_preferred_workspace_endpoints.py` — POST happy path, 401/403/
  404 surfaces, version-gate constant, daemon/old-client/explicit
  skip gates on the executor
* `test_cli_workspace.py` — `sky workspace use`, `--workspace` flag
  callback, AMBIGUOUS message round-trip via CLI
* `test_viewer_route_coverage.py` — POST registered as viewer-denied

Smoke (`test_workspace_e2e_via_cli`): end-to-end CLI →
`/users/me/workspace` → resolver → cluster.workspace recording, with
three resolver branches exercised (preferred, explicit, default-
fallback) and `sky api info` round-tripping the persisted value.

The smoke test `test_workspace_switching` is updated for D8 (no
mismatch error on cross-workspace cluster ops; access check only).

Local: `bash format.sh` clean on changed files (pylint 9.94/10).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Update test_cli_api_info for new Preferred workspace line

`sky api info` now prints a `Preferred workspace: (not set)` line between
the `User:` and `Endpoint` lines (reads `preferred_workspace` from the
/api/health user row). The existing test asserted indexes against the
pre-change layout and broke in CI:

  Python Tests - CLI Tests / Limited Deps - Jobs, Serve & CLI (3.9)
  tests/test_cli.py::TestWithNoCloudEnabled::test_cli_api_info
  AssertionError: assert '├── Preferre...ce: (not set)' == '└── Endpoint...'

Shift indexes: Endpoint line moves from output[4] to output[5], total
length 6 → 7. Add an explicit assertion on the new line so future
formatting changes catch their own regression.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Address PR review feedback on per-user default workspace

Five fixes prompted by Gemini and Devin review comments on the PR, plus
their regression tests:

1) ContextVar does not propagate to worker processes — resolver gate
   never fires (Devin)
   `_should_apply_workspace_resolver` read the client API version via
   `versions.get_remote_api_version()`, a `contextvars.ContextVar` set
   by `APIVersionMiddleware` in the FastAPI dispatch process. Request
   execution actually runs in a worker spawned by `BurstableExecutor`
   (a `ProcessPoolExecutor`); ContextVar values do not propagate
   across process boundaries, so the worker always saw `None` and the
   gate treated every request as "old client" — silently disabling
   the new resolver.
   Fix: add `client_api_version: Optional[int]` to `RequestBody`
   defaulting to `server_constants.API_VERSION` at client construction
   time. The field is serialized to the request DB and read back in
   the worker, so the gate has the real value without depending on
   ContextVar propagation. The gate signature becomes
   `(is_daemon, client_api_version)`. Old clients (pre-this-PR) do not
   set the field; Pydantic defaults to None and the gate treats them
   as "old client" — same legacy semantics as before. Drops the now
   unused `versions` import from `executor.py`.

2) `set_preferred_workspace` SDK method missing
   `@versions.minimal_api_version(...)` decorator (Devin)
   New client talking to an older server hit a confusing HTTP 404 on
   the unknown `/users/me/workspace` route instead of a clean
   `APINotSupportedError`. Added the decorator pointing at
   `MIN_PREFERRED_WORKSPACE_API_VERSION` so the version-skew error
   surfaces with the SDK method name.

3) `WorkspaceAmbiguousError` corrupted by pickle round-trip (Devin)
   The exception's executor-side pickle path
   (`sky/server/requests/serializers/encoders.py`) reconstructs it on
   the client. Python's default exception pickle calls
   `cls(*self.args)` where `self.args` is the formatted message
   string — `sorted(message_string)` then sorted individual
   characters into `accessible`, and `super().__init__` rebuilt a
   garbled guidance message. Added `__reduce__` returning
   `(cls, (self.accessible, self.note))` so the original constructor
   arguments survive the round-trip. (Matches the pattern used by
   `ExecutionRetryableError`.)

4) Drop dead `get_user_preferred_workspace` from `global_user_state.py`
   (Gemini)
   Gemini suggested `.scalar()` over `filter_by(...).first().attr`,
   but the function had no remaining callers — resolver now reads
   `user.preferred_workspace` directly from the `User` dataclass
   already loaded by `add_or_update_user(return_user=True)`. Deleted
   the function entirely (also moots the `.scalar()` suggestion).

5) `tests/unit_tests/test_lifecycle_hooks.py` was brittle
   (incidental — surfaced when this PR bumped API_VERSION)
   `test_tail_hook_logs_minimal_api_version_required` mocked the
   remote version to `server_constants.API_VERSION - 1`. That formula
   only fires the `tail_hook_logs` decorator (`@minimal_api_version
   (52)`) when API_VERSION is exactly 52; this PR bumped it to 53, so
   `53 - 1 = 52` no longer trips the gate and the test fell through
   to a real cluster lookup. Pinned the mock to `51` (one less than
   the function's own minimum) so the test is not coupled to global
   API_VERSION bumps.

Regression tests added:
* `TestSetPreferredWorkspaceSdkVersionGate` — exercises the
  decorator chain on the SDK function with a pinned old remote
  version.
* `TestRequestBodyCarriesClientApiVersion` — three tests covering
  default population, explicit override, and Pydantic JSON round-trip
  of the new field.
* `TestWorkspaceAmbiguousErrorSignature.test_pickle_roundtrip...` —
  pickles the exception with accessible + note, asserts both
  attributes and `str(e)` survive intact.

Validation:
* 60+ UTs pass locally; `bash format.sh` clean (pylint 9.94/10).
* Pickle round-trip verified empirically with `python -c` repro
  before/after the `__reduce__` fix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Docs] Regenerate agent reference docs for --workspace flag and SDK

`reviewable` CI job runs `git diff --exit-code
agent/skills/skypilot/references/` after `agent/scripts/generate_references.py`
and was failing on this PR because the new surface (--workspace flag on
sky launch / sky jobs launch, sky.set_preferred_workspace SDK) was not
reflected in the auto-generated reference docs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Make local_active_workspace_ctx exception-safe

Devin review caught that `local_active_workspace_ctx` in
sky/skypilot_config.py does not wrap its `yield` in try/finally, so a
caller whose `with` block raises leaks the new thread-local workspace
value into subsequent code paths in the same worker process
(ProcessPoolExecutor reuses workers).

This is a pre-existing latent bug, not introduced by this PR — but
this PR's new executor caller in `override_request_env_and_config`
deliberately raises PermissionDeniedError from
`reject_request_for_unauthorized_workspace` for workspace-rejection,
making the leak path part of normal flow rather than an edge case.

The practical impact on the resolver gate is masked because
`override_skypilot_config` already rebinds the global
`_active_workspace_context` to a fresh `threading.local()` at the
start of every request, so the leak does not actually corrupt the
next request's gate. But the function itself should be correct
contextmanager shape, and the other ~10 callers (sky check, core
launch, jobs server, serve server, backend_utils) also benefit.

Fix: wrap the yield in try/finally so the original workspace is
restored even when an exception escapes.

Regression test added: TestIsActiveWorkspaceSet
.test_local_active_workspace_ctx_cleanup_on_exception — uses a
synthetic exception inside `with local_active_workspace_ctx(...)`
and asserts the post-condition equals the pre-condition value.
Verified the test fails when the try/finally is removed (revert
check via standalone repro).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Fix two PR-review-found exception+payload bugs

Two related bugs caught by Devin's review on the previous push, both
guarded by new regression tests.

1) WorkspaceAmbiguousError fails JSON deserialization (multiple values
   for 'accessible')

   The request executor's exception transit is NOT direct pickle — it
   is `serialize_exception` -> dict {args, attributes, ...} ->
   `pickle_and_encode(dict)` -> request DB -> `decode_and_unpickle`
   -> `deserialize_exception` which reconstructs via
   `cls(*args, **attributes)`. For this exception:

     args        = (formatted_message,)  # from super().__init__(msg)
     attributes  = {'accessible': [...], 'note': ...}  # from __dict__
     ctor        = (accessible, note=None)

   `cls(formatted_message, accessible=[...], note=...)` -> TypeError:
   __init__() got multiple values for argument 'accessible'. Result:
   instead of the helpful "You belong to multiple workspaces… run
   `sky workspace use`" guidance, the affected client sees a TypeError
   — the feature is unusable for the exact users it targets.

   The previous `__reduce__` override I added only fixed the direct
   pickle path; the JSON serialize path runs through
   `serialize_exception` which ignores `__reduce__` entirely.

   Fix: extend SkyPilotExcludeArgsBaseException (existing marker in
   sky/exceptions.py) so `serialize_exception` zeros out `args`. Then
   deserialize calls `cls(**attributes)` cleanly. The `__reduce__`
   override is kept for the direct-pickle path (defense in depth).

   Regression test
   `test_serialize_deserialize_roundtrip_via_request_executor_path`
   exercises the actual serialize_exception → deserialize_exception
   path and asserts args==() + full str(e) round-trips.

2) `client_api_version` server-side default-fill bypasses the gate
   for old clients

   `RequestBody.__init__` unconditionally filled `client_api_version`
   with `server_constants.API_VERSION` if absent. Correct on the
   CLIENT side (the client stamps its own version). WRONG on the
   SERVER side: when an OLD client (pre-this-PR) sends a body
   omitting the field, Pydantic deserialization calls `__init__`
   again on the server, and the server's API_VERSION (53) gets
   stamped — making the executor gate think it's a new client. The
   resolver runs and may raise `WorkspaceAmbiguousError`, which the
   old client cannot deserialize.

   Fix: only apply the default-fill when `annotations.is_on_api_server`
   is False (i.e., inside a `@client_api` SDK wrapper). On the server
   side the field stays at its Pydantic-declared `None` default for
   missing input, which the executor gate correctly interprets as
   "old client → skip resolver".

   Regression tests
   `test_server_side_parse_of_old_client_body_leaves_field_none` and
   `test_server_side_parse_of_new_client_body_preserves_field` cover
   both legs of the wire format (missing field stays None; present
   field is preserved). `test_default_construction_populates_local_api_version`
   was renamed to `test_client_construction_stamps_local_api_version`
   and now explicitly flips `is_on_api_server` to False to mimic the
   `@client_api` runtime context.

Validation:
* 62 UTs pass locally (60 + 2 new server-side parse tests).
* Empirical repro before/after both fixes verified with `python -c`
  scripts driving `serialize_exception/deserialize_exception` and
  `RequestBody.model_validate_json` with the old-client JSON shape.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Header-driven client version + thread-local + CLI/SDK gaps

Three related fixes uncovered while taking the dashboard end-to-end
through `test00` (a user with no 'default' workspace access).

1) Header-driven client version (replaces in-body client-side stamping)

Previously `RequestBody.__init__` stamped `client_api_version` on
the client side (gated by `annotations.is_on_api_server`). That
worked for the Python SDK but left the dashboard out — dashboard
JS does not construct `RequestBody`. Dropping the guard would not
help either, because server-side Pydantic deserialization of an
old client's body would then silently populate the field with the
server's own API_VERSION.

Single-source-of-truth design: the SDK already sends
`X-SkyPilot-API-Version` / `X-SkyPilot-Version` headers on every
request; `APIVersionMiddleware` parses them and sets the
`_remote_api_version` ContextVar in the FastAPI dispatch context.
`prepare_request_async` now reads that ContextVar and stamps it
onto the request body before persisting — one place, every
transport. Client-side `__init__` stamping is removed.

For the dashboard, the same two version headers are added to all
outgoing requests through `apiClient` plus three direct-fetch
sites that bypass apiClient and POST to queued routes
(`/jobs/download_logs`, `ssh_node_pools/{deploy,down}`).
`_check_version_compatibility` requires BOTH headers, so the
dashboard sends a placeholder readable version (`'dashboard;'`)
alongside `CLIENT_API_VERSION`.

2) Thread-local restoration in `local_active_workspace_ctx`

The previous try/finally fix still restored the wrong value on
exit: `get_active_workspace()` falls back to the literal
`SKYPILOT_DEFAULT_WORKSPACE` ('default') when nothing is set, so
a worker that handled one request entered the ctx with no
attribute and exited with the attribute SET to 'default'. The
next request from the same worker (especially dashboard requests
with empty `override_skypilot_config`, which short-circuits the
global rebind in `override_skypilot_config`) saw
`is_active_workspace_set()` == True, skipped the resolver, and
rejected users without 'default' access.

Now restores the thread-local attribute's STATE (had / didn't
have), not the resolved string. Downstream `get_active_workspace`
still chains to layer-2 / layer-3 fallbacks correctly.

3) CLI / SDK no longer hard-code 'default' into outgoing requests

`sky status` (cli/command.py) and `sdk.enabled_clouds` read
`get_active_workspace()` client-side and passed the result as an
explicit `?workspace=...`. With nothing set on the client this
resolved to the literal 'default' and was stamped on the wire as
explicit intent — which the server's resolver gate (c) honors,
skipping the resolver and rejecting users without 'default'
access. Both sites now send the workspace only when
`is_active_workspace_set()` is True; otherwise None and the
server-side resolver picks. `_show_enabled_infra` accepts
`Optional[str]` and skips the `(workspace: 'X')` annotation when
None, since the resolved workspace happens server-side.

Regression tests
* `test_local_active_workspace_ctx_removes_attr_when_originally_unset`
  — enter with no prior attribute, exit, assert the attribute is
  GONE and `is_active_workspace_set` reports False.
* `TestPrepareRequestAsyncStampsClientApiVersion` — exercises the
  ContextVar -> body stamping with header-present and -absent.
* Rewrote `TestRequestBodyCarriesClientApiVersion` to assert no
  client-side stamping happens in `__init__`.

Validation
* 65 UT pass locally.
* End-to-end: `sky status` and the dashboard at

* [Workspaces] Fix managed-job job_info.workspace for users without 'default' access

When a managed job is submitted, the recorded `workspace` was read via
`get_active_workspace(force_user_workspace=True)`, which deliberately
bypasses the per-thread workspace context and falls back to the
config-side value (or the literal `'default'` when nothing is set).
That hack predates the per-user workspace resolver introduced by this
PR: the resolver now sets the thread-local at the request boundary
to whichever workspace the user actually intends for this request, so
force-bypassing it instead records the legacy `'default'` literal —
silently breaking users who have no access to the `'default'`
workspace (the exact scenario SKY-5468 targets).

Concretely, a user with access only to `'pub'` would submit a
managed job and see:
  cluster_table.workspace  = 'pub'    (recorded via the resolver-set
                                       thread-local)
  job_info_table.workspace = 'default' (recorded via
                                        force_user_workspace=True)
and the controller would then reject the job at the
`reject_request_for_unauthorized_workspace` check.

Fix: drop `force_user_workspace=True` at the two job-submission sites
that write `job_info.workspace`:

* `_maybe_submit_job_locally` (consolidation mode, jobs/server/core.py).
  The call point is before any nested
  `local_active_workspace_ctx(...)` is entered, so the thread-local
  here is the resolver's pick.
* `_submit_remotely` (non-consolidation mode, jobs/server/core.py).
  `_ensure_controller_up` has already entered AND exited its own
  controller-provisioning workspace ctx by this line, so the
  thread-local is restored to the outer (resolver-set) workspace.

`_exec_code_on_head` also reads `force_user_workspace=True` to populate
`ManagedJobInfo.workspace` on the gRPC `QueueJobRequest`, but the
skylet-side handler in `services.py::QueueJob` does not currently
read `request.managed_job` at all — the protobuf field is defined for
future use but is dead on the wire today. Left untouched aside from a
short comment so a future skylet that wires it up can find the
context.

Validation
* Existing UTs pass (65).
* `sky status` for a `test00` user with no `default` workspace access
  succeeds end-to-end against the local API server, where it
  previously hit
  `PermissionDeniedError: User test00 does not have permission to
  access workspace 'default'` on the managed-jobs view path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Refresh /api/health user from DB so preferred_workspace surfaces

Auth middlewares (BasicAuth, AuthProxy, BearerToken, plugin-supplied)
populate request.state.auth_user from headers/JWT/credentials. The
header-only paths (AuthProxy and BearerToken) build the User from id +
name + type and never load the persisted preferred_workspace column.

Worker-side reads were already fine — executor.prepare_request_async
runs add_or_update_user(return_user=True) before the resolver sees the
user — but /api/health is synchronous and returned the middleware-
built User verbatim, which made `sky api info` print "(not set)" even
right after `sky workspace use <name>` succeeded.

Refresh the User from the DB inside health() so the response reflects
the persisted preference regardless of which middleware authenticated
the request.

Tests: 3 new tests in test_server.py covering the refresh, the
DB-miss fallback, and the unauthenticated path's skip of the lookup.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Workspaces] Helper for plugin sync handlers to refresh workspace state

The executor's reload_for_new_request pipeline refreshes config and the
request-scoped lru cache on every queued worker request, but plugin
endpoints that respond as sync FastAPI handlers (i.e. not queued via
executor.schedule_request_async / prepare_request_async) bypass it.

Their process-cached workspace config snapshot can therefore lag behind
a worker process that just ran sky workspace create/update — a sync
handler filtering by accessible_workspaces will exclude newly-created
workspaces and include workspaces that have since been removed.

Add a refresh_workspace_state_for_sync_handler() helper next to
reload_for_new_request that plugin sync handlers call before reading
workspace/RBAC state. It does the minimum subset of the executor's
reload: safe_reload_config() to pick up new YAML/DB state, plus
clear_request_level_cache() to flush the per-request _load_workspaces
lru cache so the fresh config is observed.

Casbin's in-memory enforcer is refreshed lazily by
permission_service.get_user_roles (called inside
get_accessible_workspace_names), so it doesn't need a separate refresh
here.

Companion fix in feature-plugin wires this into the pagination and
secrets-manager plugins; both have sync handlers that read
workspaces_core.get_workspaces() / check_workspace_permission and were
returning stale lists post-workspace-update.

message:
[Image] Bump GPU image to NVIDIA 580 open + CUDA 13 for Blackwell (#9639)

* [GCP] Bump GPU image to NVIDIA 580 open + CUDA 13 for Blackwell

The published skypilot:custom-gpu-ubuntu-2204 image installs NVIDIA
driver 535 + CUDA 12.4 via this provisioner. That driver branch does
not support Blackwell parts (B200 and the newly added RTX PRO 6000
Blackwell on G4), so `nvidia-smi` fails on those VMs at first boot
when using the default image.

Changes:
- Install the 580-open driver. NVIDIA's open kernel module is the only
  flavor supported on Blackwell data-center GPUs (B200,
  RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server); the proprietary module is rejected.
  The open module also works on every previously supported GPU
  (Turing and later), so one image continues to cover the full matrix.
- Bump CUDA toolkit to 13.0 and cuDNN to libcudnn9-cuda-13. This pairs
  with driver 580 per NVIDIA's compatibility matrix.
- Install gcc-12 (+ matching g++-12 and linux-headers) and set it as
  the default compiler before driver install. The DKMS rebuild of the
  NVIDIA kernel module on GCP's 6.8.x kernels needs gcc >= 12 because
  the kernel Makefile passes `-ftrivial-auto-var-init=zero`, which
  gcc-11 (Ubuntu 22.04 default) does not understand. Without this the
  module silently fails to build and the image ships with no working
  driver.
- Collapse the arm64 / x86 split: same driver/toolkit packages work
  on both architectures with the open module; only `nvidia-modprobe`
  is kept arm64-only (existing behavior).
- Add `set -euxo pipefail` so a future silent failure in the build
  surfaces immediately instead of producing a broken image.

This script is consumed by `sky/catalog/images/skypilot-gcp-gpu-ubuntu.pkr.hcl`
(and the equivalent AWS / Azure builders). Maintainers need to rerun
Packer in the `sky-dev-465` GCP project and ship the new image via a
PR to `skypilot-org/skypilot-catalog` for users to see it. The script
change alone has no runtime effect until that image is rebuilt.

Tested:
- `bash -n cuda.sh` syntax check passes.
- This script (identical content) has been baked into a Blackwell image
  in our internal GCP project and used to launch RTX PRO 6000 (G4)
  workloads; `nvidia-smi` reports driver 580.xx, CUDA 13.0.

Companion to skypilot-org/skypilot#9634 ([GCP] Add RTX PRO 6000
Blackwell (G4) support), which adds the catalog/launch-path metadata.
This PR addresses the image-content side; the two are independent and
can be reviewed / merged in either order.

* [Image] Address review: apt-get update + install nvidia-modprobe on x86_64

subject: [Core] Fix set_pod_resource_limits silently ignored in task-level config (#9786)
message:
[Core] Fix set_pod_resource_limits silently ignored in task-level config (#9786)

* [Core] Fix set_pod_resource_limits silently ignored in task-level config

`set_pod_resource_limits` set in a task-level `config:` block was silently
dropped before reaching the pod spec. `Task.from_yaml` parsed it correctly
into `Resources._cluster_config_overrides`, but `Resources.copy()` (invoked
during the launch/optimize flow) rebuilds the overrides using the allow-list
`OVERRIDEABLE_CONFIG_KEYS_IN_TASK`, which was missing this key. The pod thus
ended up with no CPU/memory limits and QoS class `Burstable` instead of
`Guaranteed`. `pod_config` worked because it is in the allow-list.

Fix: add `('kubernetes', 'set_pod_resource_limits')` to the allow-list. SSH
Node Pools reuse the Kubernetes backend and read this under the `kubernetes`
config key, so the single entry covers both.

Fixes #9785

Tested:
- Added a regression unit test in tests/unit_tests/test_resources.py
  (parametrized over `True` and a numeric multiplier) that fails before the
  fix and passes after.
- End-to-end on a real Kubernetes cluster, controlled before/after with
  `sky launch` of a task containing
  `config.kubernetes.set_pod_resource_limits: true`:
    - Without fix: container resources `{"requests": {...}}`, QoS `Burstable`.
    - With fix: `{"limits": {"cpu": "2", "memory": "8G"}, "requests": {...}}`,
      QoS `Guaranteed`.

subject: [API] Reconcile internal daemon rows on API server boot (#9668)
message:
[API] Reconcile internal daemon rows on API server boot (#9668)

* [API] Reconcile internal daemon rows on API server boot

Persisted daemon request rows (status, env_vars, schedule_type, etc.) can
drift from what the current process intends them to be — for example,
across deployment generations on a HA backend with a persistent task
queue, or when a daemon is added / removed / renamed in code. Today the
lifespan handler enqueues each daemon via `schedule_request_async` →
`create_if_not_exists_async`, which both backends implement with
`ON CONFLICT(request_id) DO NOTHING`; the new process's env_vars are
silently discarded if a row already exists.

Add `RequestBackend.reconcile_internal_daemons_async` that runs in the
parent server process between `setup_consolidation_mode_on_startup` and
`executor.start(config)` — before any RequestWorker thread starts
dequeuing — and:

- DELETEs daemon-shaped rows whose id is no longer in
  `INTERNAL_REQUEST_DAEMONS`, along with any task_queue entries.
- UPSERTs each current daemon's row to PENDING with the current
  process's `RequestBody()` (env_vars from current os.environ),
  pid cleared.
- Preserves rows that are RUNNING with a live local pid (SQLite) or
  RUNNING on a live replica (PG): refreshes request_body / name /
  schedule_type only — does not yank `status`, `pid`, or `entrypoint`.

The OSS SQLite implementation lives in `SqliteRequestBackend`; the PG
implementation in a follow-up that ships separately. The OSS path
returns the list of `Request` objects that the caller must enqueue (the
SQLite path's multiprocessing queue is in-memory and freshly created by
`executor.start`); a persistent task_queue backend can write the queue
inline inside its own transaction and return [].

Reconcile is guarded by a filelock at `~/.sky/locks/` (outside the
`REQUEST_LOG_PATH_PREFIX` tree that `reset_db_and_logs` wipes), making
it safe to call concurrently across processes.

Tested:
- New unit tests in
  `tests/unit_tests/test_sky/server/requests/test_reconcile_internal_daemons.py`
  cover the insert / refresh / delete / terminal-reset /
  preserve-running / should_skip-preserve-running / enqueue-list
  paths.
- Existing `tests/unit_tests/test_sky/server/requests/test_requests.py`
  still passes (48/48).
- Manual e2e: bootstrap a daemon row with `SKYPILOT_REPRO_TAG=v1` in
  its env_vars, change current process env to `v2`, run reconcile —
  row's env_vars[SKYPILOT_REPRO_TAG] flips from `v1` to `v2`. A
  pre-seeded `fake-legacy-daemon` row gets deleted.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [API] Simplify SQLite reconcile to inherit default (DB is wiped on boot)

Address review feedback: the OSS SQLite request DB is wiped on every
`sky api start` via `reset_db_and_logs` -> `clear_local_api_server_database`,
so there are no persistent stale rows for the SQLite backend to
reconcile. Move the trivial "create_if_not_exists for each non-skip
daemon" logic into the base `RequestBackend` class as a concrete
default. Remove the SQLite-specific override along with its filelock,
psutil dependency, running-on-live-pid preserve logic, and stale-row
delete path — none of which are exercised when the DB is empty at boot.

The PG backend in feature-plugin keeps its real reconcile override (PG
DB is persistent across pod restarts, so stale rows can survive).

Simplify the unit tests accordingly: keep three tests covering the
default's contract (insert each non-skip daemon, skip-true is omitted,
idempotent on repeat). Drop the running-on-live-pid / preserve /
should-skip-deletes / orphan-deletes tests, which exercised behaviour
that no longer exists in the base default.

* [API] Preserve daemon submission semantics; refresh env_vars in-place

Replace the parent-process reconcile call site with two narrower hooks
on the existing per-daemon submission path:

- New `RequestBackend.create_or_refresh_internal_daemon_async(request)`
  mirrors `create_if_not_exists_async`: returns True if the insert won
  the conflict race (caller enqueues onto task_queue, exactly as
  before), False otherwise. Losing callers additionally UPDATE
  `request_body`, `name`, and `schedule_type` on the existing row so
  the persisted env_vars reflect this process's `os.environ` rather
  than whatever the original creator captured.
- New `RequestBackend.delete_orphan_internal_daemons_async(daemons)`
  removes daemon-shaped rows whose ids are not in the current code's
  INTERNAL_REQUEST_DAEMONS (daemon renamed / removed).

`executor.schedule_internal_daemon_async(daemon)` wraps create_or_refresh
+ schedule_prepared_request and is the new submission path used by
lifespan. The dedup contract is unchanged (exactly one concurrent caller
enqueues onto task_queue); the only new behaviour is the env-vars
refresh on losing callers.

Lifespan stays in its existing shape: it calls
`delete_orphan_internal_daemons_async` once at startup, then iterates
`INTERNAL_REQUEST_DAEMONS` and calls `schedule_internal_daemon_async`
per daemon. The submission timing (per-uvicorn-worker, after
executor.start) is identical to today — no asyncio.run in start(), no
parent-process call site, no change to when daemons enter the queue.

The SQLite default implementation uses INSERT-OR-IGNORE-then-UPDATE
under `create_if_not_exists`-style dedup. The PG-backed implementation
in the HA plugin uses `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ...
RETURNING (xmax = 0)` to atomically distinguish insert vs update.

Tested:
- Renamed unit tests to test_internal_daemon_submission.py:
  - test_create_or_refresh_inserts_new_row
  - test_create_or_refresh_existing_row_returns_false_and_refreshes_env
  - test_delete_orphan_removes_rows_not_in_current_set
  - test_delete_orphan_ignores_non_daemon_request_ids
- Existing test_requests.py still passes (48 / 48).
- Manual: `sky api start` boots and queues 6 daemons in the same order
  as today; the `Queuing request:` log lines are unchanged.

subject: [Dashboard] Don't block managed-jobs table on /status when controller is up (#9645)
message:
[Dashboard] Don't block managed-jobs table on /status when controller is up (#9645)

[Dashboard] Don't block jobs table on /status when controller is up

The managed-jobs page calls getClusters (POST /status) after every
pagination/jobs fetch to decide whether to show a "controller stopped"
or "controller launching" banner. The await is sequential: the table
tbody stays in its "Loading..." state until /status returns, even though
the row data is already in component state.

On a 50K-job PG deployment we measured row-visible going from ~2.7 s to
~1.5 s by skipping /status — and the periodic 5-second refresh now skips
it too. Larger improvements expected over remote-DB latency.

Logic: the pagination/jobs endpoint already catches ClusterNotUpError
and returns controller_stopped=true for both STOPPED and INIT-without-
head_ip (LAUNCHING) cases. /status is only needed to disambiguate which
banner to show. When controller_stopped is false the controller is
reachable, so there's no banner to show and /status can be skipped.

Tested with playwright against a tilt-up dev stack seeded with 50K
managed jobs:
- Happy path (controllerStopped=false): /status NOT requested, real
  rows visible at t=1.5 s (was t=2.7 s).
- Stopped path (controllerStopped=true, mocked via route-fulfill):
  /status IS requested right after pagination/jobs returns, banner
  resolution path intact.
- Works for both consolidation and non-consolidation modes — the queue
  endpoint's controller_stopped flag is set in both.

subject: [Core] Let packages expose client SDKs under the sky namespace (#9784)
message:
[Core] Let packages expose client SDKs under the sky namespace (#9784)

* [Core] Let packages expose client SDKs under the sky namespace

Add a lazy loader so an installed package can surface a client SDK as
`sky.<name>` by registering an entry point in a new `sky.client_sdks`
group whose value is the dotted path of the module to expose. With that,
`sky.<name>`, `from sky import <name>` and `import sky.<name>` all resolve
to the registered module, letting add-on packages extend the `sky`
namespace without SkyPilot knowing about them at build time. This mirrors
the other entry-point hooks SkyPilot already exposes.

Resolution is fully lazy (a PEP 562 module `__getattr__` for attribute
access plus a `sys.meta_path` finder for the dotted-import form) and adds
no import-time cost when no such SDK is installed. The finder is appended
to `sys.meta_path`, so real `sky` submodules always take precedence.

Tested:
- tests/unit_tests/test_client_sdks.py: attribute / dotted / from-import
  resolution and module identity, unknown-name errors (AttributeError and
  ModuleNotFoundError), the underscore short-circuit, and the Python <3.10
  `entry_points()` mapping fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] client SDK loader: cache entry-point scan; scope to single module

Address review feedback:
- Cache the sky.client_sdks entry-point scan with functools.lru_cache so
  attribute misses and unresolved sky.* imports are O(1) instead of
  re-scanning every installed distribution on each lookup.
- Make the single-module contract explicit: the meta-path finder stays
  appended (real sky submodules keep precedence) and sky.<name>.<sub> is
  intentionally not aliased (clean "not a package" error for a module target).
- Tests: autouse fixture clears the cache around each test so monkeypatched
  entry points take effect; add a contract test for the submodule behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Core] client SDK loader: preserve target __spec__; test error propagation

Address second-pass review feedback:
- The alias loader returned the target module from create_module, so
  module_from_spec() overwrote the target's __spec__ (name -> sky.<name>,
  loader -> the alias loader). That broke the __name__/__spec__.name
  invariant and made importlib.reload() on the target a silent no-op.
  Capture the target's real spec in create_module and restore it in
  exec_module.
- Tests: assert the resolved alias preserves the target's
  __name__/__spec__.name; assert a registered-but-missing target surfaces
  ModuleNotFoundError (not AttributeError); build test EntryPoints with

message:
[AWS] Fix false MISMATCH error when subnet_names span multiple AZs (#9791)

When user-specified subnets span multiple Availability Zones, AZ
filtering naturally reduces the subnet count. The existing

subject: [Jobs] Optionally merge cluster launch-progress events into job events (#9804)
message:
[Jobs] Optionally merge cluster launch-progress events into job events (#9804)

* [Jobs] Optionally merge cluster launch-progress events into job events

Managed job events currently record only high-level status transitions
(submitted, starting, started, ...). The underlying cluster, however,
already records fine-grained launch/setup events: the milestone sequence
(provisioning, runtime setup, file-mount syncing, ...) as STATUS_CHANGE
events, and sub-status such as pods pending due to image pulling as
LAUNCH_PROGRESS events. These explain what a job is doing while it sits
in STARTING, but are not visible in the job's event timeline today.

This adds an opt-in `include_cluster_events` flag to the get-job-events
endpoint. When set, the server reconstructs the job's underlying cluster
name(s) (the same deterministic naming used elsewhere) and merges those
clusters' STATUS_CHANGE and LAUNCH_PROGRESS events into the returned
timeline, ordered by timestamp.

- New `global_user_state.get_cluster_events_by_name`, which looks events
  up by the persisted cluster name rather than resolving name->hash via
  the clusters table, so events remain queryable after the cluster has
  been torn down (e.g. for a finished job).
- Merged cluster events adopt the timezone of the job events (tz-aware on
  Postgres, naive on SQLite) so the combined list serializes consistently.
- Pool clusters are skipped, since they are shared across jobs and their
  events are not attributable to a single job.
- The merge is best-effort: a failure to read cluster events never fails
  the job-events request. The flag defaults to False, so existing
  behavior is unchanged.

Also extend `get_cluster_events` to accept multiple event types (a list,
or a comma-separated string at the API layer, e.g.
'STATUS_CHANGE,LAUNCH_PROGRESS'), merged and ordered in a single query,
so a single call can return more than one event type.

subject: [Kubernetes] Record autostop via a durable Event breadcrumb (#9810)
message:
[Kubernetes] Record autostop via a durable Event breadcrumb (#9810)

On Kubernetes, autostop is implemented as autodown (pod termination). The
server only attributes a stop to autostop if a status refresh catches the
cluster in AUTOSTOPPING via the IsAutostopping gRPC while the head pod is
alive. If skylet completes the autodown between two refreshes, the server
never observes AUTOSTOPPING and records only a generic "All nodes
terminated, cleaning up the cluster." event.

This adds a robust, k8s-only fallback:

- Skylet emits a custom Kubernetes Event (reason=SkyPilotAutodown) on the
  head pod from the autostop code path, before terminating the pods. The
  event outlives the deleted pods for the namespace's event TTL (~1h).
- The status-refresh terminal-cleanup path reads the event back and, when
  found, records an attributed "Cluster was autodowned (idle timeout)."
  cluster event stamped with the event's timestamp. nop_if_duplicate keeps
  the timeline clean when AUTOSTOPPING was already observed.

Also adds `events: create` to the documented minimal RBAC role (the default
wildcard role already permits it) and unit tests for the event reader.

subject: [Core] tolerate unaccessible PID during child processes walk (#9806)
message:
[Core] tolerate unaccessible PID during child processes walk (#9806)

* [Core] subprocess_utils: tolerate per-PID EACCES during /proc walk

psutil.Process.children(recursive=True) builds the global {pid: ppid}
map by reading /proc/<N>/stat for every visible PID and aborts on the
first PermissionError. On hardened-host substrates where some
/proc/<N>/stat reads return EACCES (custom SELinux modules, eBPF LSM
agents like Falco/Tetragon), this turns into a hard failure of
kill_process_daemon (called from log_lib.run_with_log) and
kill_children_processes (called from teardown / recovery paths),
which then propagates and:
  - fails managed-job controller polls as FAILED_CONTROLLER, and
  - skips the subsequent proc.wait()/kill calls, leaking zombies and
    leaving cloud resources unkilled during cleanup.

Walk /proc directly with per-PID error tolerance: PIDs that fail with
PermissionError are skipped, their descendants are unreachable and not
killed, but every PID we could enumerate is still cleaned up. One
aggregated warning per call captures pid/comm/SELinux-label of the
denied entries to aid future diagnosis. Existing behaviour
(NoSuchProcess swallowed via FileNotFoundError/ProcessLookupError) is
preserved. Non-Linux platforms fall back to psutil.

Tested:
  - Added unit tests covering: clean tree enumeration, EACCES on a
    mid-tree PID (sibling subtrees still enumerated, denied PID captured
    in the diag list), and PID that vanishes mid-walk.
  - Integration check that kill_process_daemon does not raise and that
    kill_children_processes still SIGKILLs the explicit parent when the
    /proc walk yields no children.
  - All 17 existing subprocess_utils tests pass.

* [Core] subprocess_utils: correct DFS comment, broaden fallback catch

Addressing review feedback on _fallback_children:

  - The comment claimed BFS but the stack.pop() loop is DFS. Update the
    comment to call this out and clarify that it matches upstream
    psutil.Process.children(recursive=True), which uses the same
    stack-based pattern. Order does not matter for the callers
    (kill_process_daemon / kill_children_processes both walk the whole
    subtree to kill it).

  - Broaden the catch around psutil.Process(child_pid) from
    psutil.NoSuchProcess to psutil.Error. We only enter this fallback
    because the host LSM is actively denying introspection; the per-PID
    instantiation can plausibly hit AccessDenied or ZombieProcess too.
    Dropping the offending PID and continuing the walk is better than
    propagating and aborting cleanup of the rest of the subtree.

Tested: existing 19 unit tests in test_subprocess_utils.py still pass.

* Address review comments

subject: [API] Run user-management sync handlers in their own request context (#9816)

[API] Run user-management sync handlers in their own request context (#9816)

The sync handlers in sky/users/server.py (get_user_workspace, user_update,
user_batch_update, user_delete) bypass the executor framework, which would
normally establish a per-request context. They call set_current_user()
directly, but with no active context that write lands in a process-global
fallback shared across worker threads. As a result concurrent requests can
clobber each other's current user, and a request's identity leaks to later
requests on the same worker -- making get_accessible_workspace_names() /
get_workspaces() resolve the wrong user's accessible workspaces.

Wrap these handlers in @context.contextual so set_current_user() writes to a
per-request SkyPilotContext that is torn down afterwards (no leak, no race).
Add a regression test asserting the user is visible inside the handler and
not leaked after it returns.

subject: [Jobs] Pin active_workspace to cluster row in terminate_cluster (#9808)
message:
[Jobs] Pin active_workspace to cluster row in terminate_cluster (#9808)

* [Jobs] Pin active_workspace to cluster row in terminate_cluster

The jobs controller's `terminate_cluster` (used by both cancel and
recovery-teardown paths) calls `core.down` directly. `core.down` →
`backend.teardown` → `_teardown` does a RAW
`backend_utils.check_owner_identity` (cloud_vm_ray_backend.py:4519,
not auto-wrapped). The controller runs in the system/daemon process —
the executor's per-request resolver doesn't fire here (skipped by the
daemon gate in `_should_apply_workspace_resolver`), so
`skypilot_config.get_active_workspace()` falls back to 'default' and
the owner-identity check raises for any cluster whose recorded
workspace is not 'default':

    ClusterOwnerIdentityMismatchError: The cluster 'e82-X' is in
    workspace 'pub', but the active workspace is 'default'.

Pre-existing latent bug, surfaced more often after #9755 (per-user
preferred workspace) because users no longer need an explicit
`active_workspace:` in `~/.sky/config.yaml` to land on a non-default
workspace.

Fix: in `terminate_cluster`, look up the cluster row once before the
retry loop and wrap `core.down` in
`local_active_workspace_ctx(cluster.workspace)` — the same pattern
`_update_cluster_status_no_lock` already uses for its owner check.
Falls back to `nullcontext()` when the cluster row is gone (core.down
will raise `ClusterDoesNotExist` immediately and we return — no
workspace to pin).

Scope:
* Only `terminate_cluster` is fixed because it's the only controller-
  side caller that goes through a RAW (non-auto-wrapped) owner check.
* `controller.py:1935 core.status` and `:1947 core.cancel` route their
  owner check through `_update_cluster_status_no_lock`, which already
  auto-wraps in `local_active_workspace_ctx(record['workspace'])`.

subject: [CI] Tune nightly Buildkite wait timeouts to measured p95 (#9821)
message:
[CI] Tune nightly Buildkite wait timeouts to measured p95 (#9821)

The nightly fans out ~10 Buildkite builds and the GitHub `wait-for-buildkite`
jobs were timing out below the builds' actual run time, turning the nightly red
even though Buildkite passed. The fix until now was a manual "re-run failed
jobs" once Buildkite finished, which let publish proceed.

Measured 28 scheduled nights (May-Jun 2026) from the Buildkite API. On a quiet
01:00 UTC night per-job queue wait is small (~7-18m); the long builds are long
because the `kind` queue is a hard cap of ~50 agents, saturated ~2h with a
~900-job backlog (throughput-bound). So several timeouts sat below the median
runtime:

  remote-server      p50 134m  p90 225m  -> failed 23/28 nights (t/o was 120)
  backward-compat-nightly p50 104m p90 130m -> failed 18/28 (t/o was 60)
  jobs-consolidation p50  94m  p90 146m  -> failed 17/28 (t/o was 90)

Timeouts raised to clean-p95 + margin (hang outliers >400m dropped):

  smoke-tests-aws                 90 -> 180
  backward-compat-test-nightly    60 -> 240
  backward-compat-test-stable     60 ->  90
  resource-heavy                 100 -> 150
  no-resource-heavy              180 -> 270
  no-resource-heavy-limit-deps   120 -> 270
  remote-server-kubernetes       120 -> 300
  jobs-consolidation              90 -> 210
  shared-gke-api-server          180 -> 300
  slurm-minimal                   60 ->  90

All stay <340m, under the GitHub job 6h cap (wait job has no timeout-minutes).

Also removed `sleep_seconds: 600` on remote-server. It was meant to "reduce
buildkite resource usage", but `kind` is throughput-bound (hard cap), so the
delay only pushed those jobs to the back of an already-full queue, making
remote-server finish last. Staggering cannot help a saturated fixed-size queue;
capacity can (cf. #7486 which scaled kind and dropped the original staggers).

Test plan:
- YAML validated: python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/nightly-build.yml'))".
- Values derived from finished_at-created_at across 28 scheduled nightly builds
  per variant; new timeout >= clean p95 for every variant.
- Next scheduled nightly should complete one-shot without a manual re-run; the
  rare multi-hour starvation incidents (8/28 nights) are an autoscaler/capacity
  issue tracked separately, not addressed here.

* [Test] Fix flaky test_backoff_progression from cross-thread sleep mock

test_backoff_progression patched time.sleep process-wide and asserted the
number of recorded sleeps == 3. mock.patch('time.sleep') replaces sleep for

patched window turns into a busy loop and floods the shared sleep_times list.

another thread, failing `assert len(sleep_times) == 3`.

synchronously on it), so concurrent threads can no longer pollute the count.

subject: [Jobs] Persist managed-job log path before slow log re-stream (#9827)
message:
[Jobs] Persist managed-job log path before slow log re-stream (#9827)

* [Jobs] Persist managed-job log path before slow log re-stream

When a managed job finishes, the controller syncs down the worker's
run.log and then re-streams it into the controller log before recording
local_log_file. For multi-GB logs full of carriage-return progress
output (e.g. `aws s3 cp`), that re-stream takes minutes: text-mode
iteration splits on every '\r', turning a ~160MB / 139K-line log into
~2M flushed writes. During that whole window local_log_file is NULL, so
the dashboard "Logs" tab shows "Job is already in terminal state ...
run sky jobs logs --controller" instead of the logs.

- Persist local_log_file as soon as the log is synced down, via a new
  on_downloaded callback, before the re-stream. The dashboard can serve
  logs in ~sync time instead of sync + re-stream.
- Open the log with newline='\n' and flush once instead of per line, so
  carriage-return progress no longer explodes the line count / runtime
  (measured 348s -> 5.5s, 1.96M -> 139K lines) and the controller log no
  longer bloats. Shared by managed jobs and sky serve replica logs.

Tested:
- tests/unit_tests/test_controller_utils.py: 3 new tests (callback fires
  before the re-stream; '\r' preserved verbatim; no-logs returns None),
  revert-checked so each fails when its fix is reverted.
- Live large managed job: set_local_log_file now fires ~5.4s after
  success (before the re-stream); re-stream 348s -> 5.5s.

* [Jobs] Decode the log re-stream with errors='replace'

A stray invalid-UTF-8 byte in the user program's log would otherwise
raise UnicodeDecodeError mid-iteration and truncate the controller-log
copy. Match log_lib's decode handling so the copy is best-effort.

subject: [Kubernetes] Don't schedule a -80GB GPU request onto a smaller-memory node (#9819)
message:
[Kubernetes] Don't schedule a -80GB GPU request onto a smaller-memory node (#9819)

* [Kubernetes] Don't schedule a -80GB GPU request onto a smaller-memory node

A request for a high-memory GPU variant (e.g. `A100-80GB`) could be
scheduled onto a node with a smaller-memory sibling (e.g. a 40GB `A100`),
causing the workload to OOM at runtime. The matcher
`_accelerator_name_matches` treats any `-`-separated prefix as a match for
GPU-name backward compatibility, so a bare `A100` (40GB) was accepted for an
`A100-80GB` request.

Add a per-device-memory map for canonical GPU names that have memory-variant
siblings and guard the prefix match: reject only when the requested GPU needs
strictly more memory than the candidate node provides. The benign reverse
direction (a smaller request landing on a larger node) and same-hardware
renames (e.g. `H100` == `H100-80GB`) keep matching.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Kubernetes] Handle non-canonicalized memory-variant names in GPU matcher

On a Kubernetes-only cluster, a user-typed accelerator like `A100-80G`
(missing the trailing `B`) is not canonicalized to `A100-80GB`, so the
previous exact-name memory map did not recognize it and the request could
still be scheduled onto a 40GB A100 node.

Generalize the memory lookup: resolve a GPU name's device memory from the
bare-name map, or by parsing a trailing memory suffix (e.g. `-80GB`, `-80G`).
Parsing is scoped to the GPU families already tracked in the map (A100,
V100) -- the suffix is only honored when the part before it is a tracked
bare name -- so matching for any other GPU is unchanged and the blast radius
stays limited.

RuntimeClass exists in the API but the runtime handler is not
configured on nodes (e.g. CRI-O clusters with hook-based GPU operator

empty'.

every pod, and treat an explicit falsy override as user intent to
disable the runtime class (suppressing the automatic 'nvidia'
assignment). Non-empty values and default behavior are unchanged.

message:
[Storage] Support OCI Object Storage via the S3-compatible API (#9831)

* [Storage] Support OCI Object Storage via the S3-compatible API

OCI Object Storage exposes an Amazon S3 Compatibility API authenticated
with a Customer Secret Key (access/secret key pair):
https://docs.oracle.com/en-us/iaas/Content/Object/Tasks/s3compatibleapi.htm

This adds OciS3CompatibleStore(S3CompatibleStore), selected for
StoreType.OCI instead of the native OciStore when the S3-compatible
credential files (~/.oci/s3.credentials + ~/.oci/s3.config) are present.
Without those files, behavior is unchanged: the native OCI SDK/CLI path
is used, so existing OCI users are unaffected.

In S3-compatible mode, remote nodes only need the AWS CLI and the
mounted credential files (no OCI CLI or native API key):
- sky/adaptors/oci_s3.py: boto3 session/client/resource against the
  tenancy endpoint, path-style addressing, credential checks, file
  mounts.
- storage.py: OciS3CompatibleStore + dispatch gating in add_store and
  _add_store_from_metadata. The class is intentionally not registered
  via @register_s3_compatible_store, since the registry is consulted
  before the StoreType.OCI branches and would bypass the gate.
- cloud_stores.py: OciS3CloudStorage (aws s3 sync/cp) for oci:// file
  mounts.
- clouds/oci.py: storage credential check passes on the S3 credential
  files alone in S3-compatible mode; credential file mounts include the
  S3 files.
- data_utils/mounting_utils: client/verify helpers, goofys/rclone mount
  and rclone cached-mount support.

The <bucket>@<region> suffix is not supported in S3-compatible mode
(the endpoint pins a single region) and raises a clear error.

tests/unit_tests/test_sky/adaptors/ (229 passed; includes new dispatch,
adaptor, and command-generation tests). Not yet exercised against a

* [Storage] Drop redundant addressing_style from OCI S3 setup steps

boto3 and the AWS CLI default to path-style addressing whenever a custom
endpoint_url is configured, and the adaptor's own clients force it in
code, so the extra `aws configure set s3.addressing_style path` step is
unnecessary. Remove it from the installation docs and the sky check
hint, and document in the adaptor why path-style is the right mode for

[Dashboard] Feed External Links extraction from plugin-owned log panels (#9838)

* [Dashboard] Feed External Links extraction from plugin-owned log panels

External link extraction (e.g. W&B run URLs) only scanned lines from the
built-in log streamer on the managed job page. When a dashboard plugin
registers a component into the jobs.detail.logs slot, that streamer is
disabled, so the External Links row always showed "-" even when a
matching URL was visible in the plugin's log panel.

- Extract the scan-and-accumulate logic into a shared useLogLinkExtractor
  hook and reuse it on both the managed job page and the cluster job
  page, removing the duplicated inline implementations.
- Pass the hook's stable scanLines callback into the jobs.detail.logs
  slot context as onLogLines so a plugin that owns the log panel can
  forward its visible lines for extraction, mirroring the existing
  onNodesExtracted plumbing.

* [Dashboard] Fix Users page per-user GPU count exceeding cluster capacity

The per-user GPU total on the Users page summed accelerators over all active
managed-job statuses. A job's accelerators are derived from its live cluster
handle, so a STARTING job (cluster still provisioning, e.g. a k8s pod sitting

previously-running job re-acquiring the same resources), and CANCELLING (the
cluster still holds GPUs until teardown). Job counts are unchanged.

Extract the GPU-summing logic into a pure getJobGpuCount() helper and use it at
all three aggregation sites (filter lookup, Users table, Service Accounts

message:
[Backend] Default a new cluster handle to no runtime set up (#9845)

Default a new cluster handle to no runtime set up

CloudVmRayResourceHandle is constructed before provisioning runs (the
backend records it while the cluster is still INIT, so a crash or
recovery mid-provisioning still leaves a row that `sky status` and
teardown can see). Its `__init__` defaulted `provision_runtime_metadata`
to `ProvisionRuntimeMetadata()`, which claims `has_ray=True` — but the
SkyPilot runtime (Ray, skylet, job queue, SSH) is not set up until
provisioning completes. Teardown of a cluster that never finished
provisioning then read that default and attempted `ray stop` on a cluster
where Ray never started.

Default the constructed handle to nothing set up (`has_ray=False`, etc.)
instead. `bulk_provision()` overwrites it with the real record on
completion, so a fully-provisioned cluster is unchanged. Handles
reconstructed from the DB via `from_dict()` / `__setstate__` skip
`__init__` and keep their persisted metadata, so existing clusters are
unaffected.

subject: [Test] Enumerate routes via OpenAPI in viewer-coverage test (#9872)
message:
[Test] Enumerate routes via OpenAPI in viewer-coverage test (#9872)

FastAPI 0.137.0 reworked router inclusion so that ``app.routes`` is a
nested tree of private ``_IncludedRouter`` objects instead of a flat
list of fully-prefixed ``APIRoute``s. A sub-router included with a
``prefix=`` no longer surfaces its routes at the top level, so the
viewer-route-coverage test's flat ``app.routes`` scan silently dropped
every prefixed endpoint (``/jobs/*``, ``/serve/*``, ``/users/*``,
``/workspaces``, ``/volumes``, ``/recipes``, ``/ssh_node_pools``).
``test_allowlist_entries_match_real_routes`` then failed because those
allowlist entries no longer matched any enumerated route.

Enumerate the visible surface from the public ``app.openapi()`` schema
instead. It is a documented, version-stable API that flattens router
prefixes into full ``{name}`` path templates -- the form
``_fastapi_path_to_casbin`` already expects -- and behaves identically
on older FastAPI releases, so the full security surface stays covered
even if FastAPI reshapes its private routing internals again.

Routes with ``include_in_schema=False`` are absent from the schema, so
fold them back in via ``_iter_api_routes``, a defensive recursive walk
that descends the >=0.137 router tree (children/prefix off the private
``include_context``, every access guarded) and degrades gracefully on
older FastAPI where the tree is already flat. This catches hidden
routes at any nesting depth, not just at the app root.

Tested: ran the test against both fastapi 0.116.1 and 0.137.0; both
pass. Without this change, 0.137.0 fails
test_allowlist_entries_match_real_routes. Separately verified the
hidden-route backstop surfaces a route injected into the real /jobs
sub-router under 0.137.

subject: Set request to PENDING before retry backoff wait (#9874)
message:
Set request to PENDING before retry backoff wait (#9874)

* [Server] Set request to PENDING before retry backoff wait

When a request raises ExecutionRetryableError, the worker reset the
request to PENDING only *after* sleeping for retry_wait_seconds. During
that wait the request stayed RUNNING even though it was no longer
executing, just parked waiting to be rescheduled.

Set the status to PENDING (with a 'Retrying in Ns' status message)
before the wait instead. This reflects the request's true state during
the backoff and lets any request-recovery mechanism re-enqueue it if the
server is interrupted mid-wait, rather than treating it as a crashed
in-flight task. The request is not put back on the queue until after the
wait, so no worker picks it up early.

* [Server] Address review: guard negative wait, clear stale status_msg

- Clamp the backoff to max(0, retry_wait_seconds) so an unexpected
  negative value can't raise ValueError in time.sleep() and strand the
  request in PENDING without re-enqueuing it.
- Clear status_msg when the request transitions back to RUNNING in
  _request_execution_wrapper, so the 'Retrying in Ns' message doesn't
  linger while the request is actually running.

* [Server] Include retry reason in backoff status message

A client attaching during the retry backoff previously only saw
'Retrying in Ns' with no explanation. Surface the retry reason (the
exception message, color-stripped, whitespace-collapsed and truncated)
so the status message reads e.g. 'Failed to provision ... (retrying in
30s)'. Falls back to 'Retrying in Ns' when there is no message.

* [Server] Trim comments in retry backoff handling

message:
[Helm] History dashboard: cap GPU allocation at per-node capacity (fix >100%) (#9877)

* [Helm] History dashboard: cap GPU allocation at per-node capacity (fix >100%)

The "Allocation & Utilization Over Time" panel computed GPU allocation as
sum(requests) / sum(allocatable), which can exceed 100%. Two independent
causes: (1) a node can briefly carry GPU requests above its own capacity
when a terminating pod and its replacement are both counted, and (2) when
a node drops out of kube_node_status_allocatable, its pods' requests still
inflate the numerator while the denominator shrinks. Allocation as a
fraction of capacity should never exceed 100%.

Cap each node's counted requests at that node's allocatable before summing:

  sum( min(requests_per_node, allocatable_per_node) ) / sum(allocatable)

expressed in PromQL as req - clamp_min(req - alloc, 0) joined per
(cluster, node). Because the per-node min join only keeps nodes present in
both the request and allocatable sets, the numerator and denominator are
computed over the same node set, and each node contributes at most its
capacity. The result is bounded to [0, 100] by construction.

Verified against live data over a 7-day range (10-minute resolution): min
0.39%, max 100.00%, zero points outside [0, 100] (the previous query
peaked at 178%).

The "Avg GPU Allocation" reference line reuses the same expression, so it
stays consistent with the corrected series and is likewise bounded.

subject: Support execution wait on external condition (#9875)
message:
Support execution wait on external condition (#9875)

* [Core] Add ExecutionPausedError to pause provisioning without teardown

Provisioning can block on an external decision (e.g. admission or quota
approval) that takes arbitrarily long. Today the request holds an executor
worker for the whole wait, which can exhaust the worker pool. As a first
step toward letting such a wait release its worker and resume later, add a
way to pause an in-progress provisioning attempt while keeping the
partially provisioned resources intact.

- Add exceptions.ExecutionPausedError, a subclass of ExecutionRetryableError
  that signals "keep the resources, do not tear down, resume later". It can
  optionally carry a (picklable) continue condition; retry_wait_seconds is
  the fallback wait.
- Re-raise it past the two teardown layers (provisioner.bulk_provision and
  RetryingVmProvisioner._retry_zones) so the kept resources survive the pause
  instead of being cleaned up / failed over.

Also pin the reattach-safety contract this relies on: relaunching onto pods
that already exist computes to_start_count == 0 and creates nothing, and a
running+pending count above the requested count trips the resource-leak
guard.

* [Server] Wait on a continue condition during retry backoff

When a retry carries a continue condition (set on ExecutionPausedError), the
request scheduler calls ``condition.wait()`` instead of waiting a fixed backoff
and re-checking blindly. The wait runs in the request's monitor thread, not an
executor worker, so a paused request releases its worker for the whole wait and
resumes via whatever signal the condition watches for.

- Add sky/server/requests/continue_condition.py: a ``ContinueCondition`` base
  class exposing ``wait(is_cancelled, fallback_wait_seconds) -> bool``. The
  base does a single fixed wait; components that know how to watch the external
  state (e.g. a server plugin) subclass it and own the polling interval,
  backoff, deadline, and fallback policy. The instance is pickled onto the
  exception to cross the worker/scheduler boundary, so subclasses must be
  importable in the scheduler process and hold only picklable state.
- In RequestWorker.handle_task_result, call ``condition.wait()`` and reschedule
  on True / drop on False; without a condition, fall back to the fixed backoff.
  Builds on the existing "set PENDING before the wait" ordering so an
  interrupted server can still recover the request.

* comment changes

* [Server] Mark executor free when future completes, before retry wait

The free-executor gauge was only incremented in a post-wait finally block,
so during a long-lived pause (ExecutionPausedError) it under-reported idle
executors for the entire wait, even though the worker process had already
returned and was back in the pool.

Account for the released process the instant the future completes - via an
inner try/finally around fut.result() - so the gauge stays accurate during
any retry/pause wait. This covers success, ordinary retry backoff, and
pauses uniformly, and the structural finally guarantees exactly one
increment per request without a manual flag.

Add a unit test that snapshots the gauge's inc() count at the moment
condition.wait() is entered; it would read 0 on the old post-wait code.

* [Server] Add WAITING request status for parked retries

A request that releases its executor worker during a retry/pause backoff
was marked PENDING for the duration of the wait, making it
indistinguishable from a request that has never been scheduled. Add a
distinct WAITING status (ordered between PENDING and RUNNING so existing

file-mount blob GC, launch precondition) so a parked request stays
visible, cancellable, and keeps its uploaded artifacts.

the wire for clients whose API version predates the new status, so older

subject: [Core] Add per-cluster time-in-state metric for stuck-in-state alerting (#9891)
message:
[Core] Add per-cluster time-in-state metric for stuck-in-state alerting (#9891)

* [Core] Add per-cluster time-in-state metric for stuck-in-state alerting

Adds sky_cluster_time_in_state_seconds{workspace, status, cloud, kind,
cluster_name} — a per-cluster gauge of seconds since the cluster
entered its current status. Emitted only for transient statuses
(INIT, AUTOSTOPPING); UP / STOPPED never emit so steady cardinality
is bounded by the number of clusters currently in flight.

Source is the cluster_events STATUS_CHANGE log, not the cluster row's
status_updated_at. status_updated_at is rewritten on every
_add_or_update_cluster call (refresh path included), so a cluster
that has been stuck in INIT for 30 min looks freshly-entered after
every refresh cycle. STATUS_CHANGE rows are written only on actual
transitions (the refresh path explicitly skips event writes for
already-INIT clusters), making transitioned_at the canonical
"entered this state at" timestamp.

Implements get_last_status_change_times() as a batched DB helper that
returns the latest STATUS_CHANGE timestamp per cluster_hash for a
given ending_status. Mirrors the row_number/partition_by pattern
already used by get_last_cluster_event_of_type_multiple().

* Apply Gemini suggestions: chunk cluster_hash IN + fix outdated docstring

- get_last_status_change_times: chunk the cluster_hash IN predicate by
  _CLUSTER_IN_QUERY_CHUNK_SIZE (500) to stay under SQLite's
  999-parameter cap. Mirrors the chunking already used elsewhere in
  this file (get_clusters / get_managed_jobs).
- WorkspaceUsageCollector docstring: update the
  sky_cluster_time_in_state_seconds bullet to reflect the per-cluster
  (not aggregated) shape and the cluster_name label.

* Address review: cap sky_cluster_time_in_state_seconds at top 100

Per aylei's review: INIT / AUTOSTOPPING may not be backed by real compute
(e.g. a tenant in a launch-retry storm, or many fail-fast launches),
so the cluster_name-keyed series can grow much larger than expected.

Cap rows at _TIME_IN_STATE_MAX_SERIES (100) per scrape, sorted by age
descending so the clusters most likely to be stuck (and therefore most
likely to be alertable) always survive the cap. Emit a WARNING log when
the cap engages so ops can spot pathological churn.

Threshold rationale: 100 is well above any plausible normal-operation
count (typical tenants have <50 simultaneous in-flight transitions) but
small enough to bound a single misbehaving tenant's contribution to
Prometheus's series budget.

subject: [metrics] Fix /gpu-metrics scrape-timeout vs per-context-timeout invariant (#9898)

[metrics] Fix /gpu-metrics scrape-timeout vs per-context-timeout invariant (#9898)

* [metrics] Fix /gpu-metrics scrape-timeout vs per-context-timeout invariant

The default Prometheus scrape config for the API server's /gpu-metrics
endpoint ships with scrape_timeout=10s, while the endpoint's own
_PER_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is 20s. The code comment requires the
per-context timeout to be shorter than the upstream scrape_timeout, but
the shipped defaults are the reverse (10s < 20s) -- so once federating a
context takes more than 10s (common as DCGM series grow with GPU count),
the scrape times out and marks /gpu-metrics down, dropping GPU metrics
even though the endpoint would have answered within its budget.

Restore the invariant and add headroom for large fleets:
- charts: skypilot-api-server-gpu-metrics scrape_interval 15s->60s,
  scrape_timeout 10s->45s
- server: _PER_CONTEXT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 20->30

Ordering is now consistent: port-forward 5s << per-context 30s <
scrape_timeout 45s <= scrape_interval 60s. The scrape_interval increase
trades GPU-metric resolution (15s->60s) for reliability at scale.

subject: [Buildkite] Fix pipeline generator silently producing empty pipelines on unrecognised pytest args (#9900)
message:
[Buildkite] Fix pipeline generator silently producing empty pipelines on unrecognised pytest args (#9900)

* [Buildkite] Fix pipeline collection silently producing empty pipelines

Pass only conftest-registered flags to `pytest --collect-only` instead of
the raw ARGS string.  The ARGS string includes flags that are only parsed by
generate_pipeline.py (--concurrency, --submodule-base-branch, --dependency,
--generic-cloud, --base-branch); when a build pins an older submodule whose
conftest does not yet register those flags pytest exits with code 4
("unrecognized arguments"), subprocess.run captures the output without
checking the return code, no "Collected" lines are matched, and every test
file yields 0 steps — the pipeline is silently a no-op.

Fix has two parts:
1. Use clean args for pytest --collect-only.  _parse_args already separates
   known flags (parsed_args) from pytest-native unknowns (pytest_native via
   parse_known_args remainder).  Build pytest_collect_args from extra_args
   (conftest-registered flags explicitly reconstructed from parsed_args) plus
   pytest_native (conftest-registered flags the pipeline parser doesn't know,
   e.g. --no-resource-heavy).  Cloud flags (--kubernetes, --aws, …) are also
   added to extra_args so collection still respects the cloud filter.
   --concurrency and other pipeline-only flags are excluded by construction.

2. Fail loudly when pytest --collect-only exits with a non-zero code other
   than 5 (exit 5 = "no tests collected", which is normal for files with no
   matching tests).  Previously any collection error silently produced an
   empty pipeline; now generate_pipeline.py propagates the exit code so the
   Buildkite step is visibly broken.

* Address review: shlex.join, flat extra_args tokens, print stdout+stderr on error

* fix: use shlex.split for input parsing (consistent with shlex.join output)

* style: apply yapf formatting

subject: [Test] chaos_proxy: rewrite Host header so it works behind a reverse proxy (#9899)
message:
[Test] chaos_proxy: rewrite Host header so it works behind a reverse proxy (#9899)

chaos_proxy raw-forwards TCP bytes, so every request keeps
Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>. Behind a Host-routing reverse proxy (e.g. an
nginx virtual host) that authority isn't recognized and the request
gets a 404, surfaced as ApiServerConnectionError. A 404 is not retried,
so test_cli_auto_retry fails immediately on such a server even though
the server is healthy.

Make the client->server direction HTTP/1.1-aware: rewrite the Host
header per request to the upstream host, framing bodies via
Content-Length (chunked bodies are forwarded verbatim). The
server->client direction stays a raw byte forward, so log streaming is
unchanged.

subject: [k8s] generate_kubeconfig.sh: mirror current-context CA, not SA secret CA (#9893)

[k8s] generate_kubeconfig.sh: mirror current-context CA, not SA secret CA (#9893)

* [k8s] generate_kubeconfig.sh: mirror current-context CA, not SA secret CA

The script always wrote the ServiceAccount secret's ca.crt (the cluster's
internal CA) into the generated kubeconfig's certificate-authority-data. That
CA only verifies the API server's own serving cert; for clusters whose
external endpoint terminates TLS at a CDN/proxy presenting a different,
often publicly-trusted certificate (e.g. CoreWeave behind Cloudflare), it does
not match what the endpoint serves, so every request fails with
"x509: certificate signed by unknown authority".

Mirror the TLS trust config from the user's current kubeconfig context
instead: it is the config kubectl already uses successfully against the same
server URL, so reusing it is guaranteed to verify. Inline
certificate-authority-data is copied, a certificate-authority file is
base64-inlined for portability, insecure-skip-tls-verify is preserved, and
when the source pins no CA the generated kubeconfig relies on the system CA
store.
